America.title: CONTINUATION: Explosion and tank fire at the Clean Harbors hazardous-waste incineration facility near Deer Park / La Porte, Texas
America.location: La Porte / Deer Park, Texas (Houston area)

Residents reported a loud boom and shaking homes, with some saying it was felt as far as downtown Houston; Deer Park officials describe a tank fire. America.status: Fire ongoing as of about 11:00 PM ET; La Porte Fire Department assisting Deer Park; Harris County Pollution Control and third-party air monitoring teams en route. Cause and any injuries not reported; About 11:49 PM ET Nov. 17: KHOU reports the fire at Clean Harbors is out; officials say air monitoring continues with no detectable readings and no protective actions are needed for nearby residents. KHOU also published home video of the explosion. Cause and any injuries still not reported; About 12:20 AM ET Nov. 18: the City of Deer Park says the fire is extinguished and crews are blanketing the open tank with foam through the night; one onsite worker was injured, taken for medical care and is in stable condition. Clean Harbors says the tank held an industrial wastewater stream (water and suspected hydrocarbons); the cause remains under investigation; About 1:56 PM ET Nov. 18: reporter Zach Bitango, citing the Harris County Fire Marshal's Office, says hydrocarbon vapors ignited inside a hazardous liquid waste tank, triggering the explosion; the tank had a pressurized nitrogen system and an incinerator connection meant to prevent ignition, the facility had two minor fires in the same treatment process over the past week, and officials are still investigating why the safety systems failed; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FBI FLASH warns cybercriminals and state-aligned hackers are using ARTEX, an AI-driven autonomous hacking framework, to automate attacks on organizations worldwide
America.summary: FBI FLASH-20261113-001, dated Nov. 13, 2026, warns that cybercriminals and state-aligned actors are using ARTEX, an open-source, LLM-driven agentic penetration-testing platform, against financial, government, technology, defense, energy, healthcare, telecom and other sectors since at least August 2026, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours. Campaigns it cites include attacks on South Korean financial institutions (data on about 67,000 people exfiltrated) and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise (more than 2,250 downstream tenants). The developer pulled the GitHub repository on Oct. 8, 2026, but forks, archived copies and a commercial ARTEX PRO still circulate, and more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles were found in early November. BleepingComputer and The Record covered the advisory; today's X coverage comes from viral relays of the Nov. 13 FLASH.
America.status: Official statement issued (FBI FLASH, Nov. 13, 2026, ic3.gov); renewed media and viral coverage Nov. 17; no new FBI or CISA post on ARTEX found on X in this sweep; Nov. 17, about 3:24 PM ET: the FBI says the ARTEX cyber advisory was released Friday, Nov. 13, is not a new announcement, and no additional warning has been issued since; the guidance remains current. Stabilized; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Apple confirms an iCloud sign-in issue as users report problems with Apple Pay, the App Store, Gmail, Outlook/Microsoft 365 and Marriott; no evidence of a cyberattack
America.location: United States and global (consumer online services)
America.summary: Starting late Tuesday morning, Nov. 17, Downdetector logged user reports of problems with Apple Support from 11:45 AM ET and Apple Pay from 11:48 AM ET, and Breaking911 reported at 12:30 PM ET that users were also reporting outages at Gmail, Marriott, Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft 365. Apple's official system status page lists an ongoing 'iCloud Account & Sign In' issue ('This service may be slow or unavailable') that began at 8:45 AM PT (11:45 AM ET); as of about 1:00 PM ET no other Apple service, including Apple Pay, Wallet and the App Store, showed an event. Google's Workspace Status Dashboard shows no incident on Nov. 17, and no @MSFT365Status post about a new incident was found. Reuters reports President Trump shrugged off the spate of US outages, saying 'things like that happen'.
America.status: Apple confirms only the iCloud sign-in issue; other services rest on user reports and Downdetector spikes; cause unknown; no evidence of a cyberattack (posts tying this to the FAA, NSA and bank outages as a coordinated attack are unsupported and not logged); consumer services, not critical infrastructure. Re-check Apple status, MSFT365Status, Google dashboard and Downdetector; Nov. 17, about 1:11 PM ET: Al Arabiya English reports Downdetector user reports of problems with iCloud, Apple Pay, the Apple Store, App Store and Apple Business Manager. Apple's system status page checked at 2:03 PM ET lists 'iCloud Account & Sign In' as an ongoing issue since 08:45 PST, 'AppleCare on Device' purchases temporarily unavailable since 08:15 PST, and Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork as possibly slow or unavailable since 10:40 PST (1:40 PM ET); Apple Pay, App Store and Apple Music show no issue. Google's Workspace status feed shows no Nov. 17 incident. No evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 2:50 PM ET: an Apple spokesperson says many of its systems are back up after an internal update caused some outages this morning and it is working to restore the remaining systems. Apple's status page checked at 3:01 PM ET: iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, Apple Business, Apple School Manager, Schoolwork and AppleCare on Device still ongoing; App Store and Volume Purchase Program issues ongoing since 11:27 PST; iCloud Mail resolved. Apple attributes the disruption to an internal update; no evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 3:10 PM ET: NBC News reports Apple said it was having tech issues affecting several consumer services. Apple's status page checked at 3:58 PM ET: App Store and Volume Purchase Program issues resolved (ended 12:00 PST), AppleCare on Device resolved (12:39 PST); iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork still listed as ongoing. Apple attributes the disruption to an internal update; no evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 4:15 PM ET: Fox News reports Apple is ruling out a cyberattack, saying an internal update triggered the disruptions and most services are restored. Apple's status page checked at about 5:03 PM ET: iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, iCloud Mail and Schoolwork now resolved; Apple Business and Apple School Manager still ongoing, and a new intermittent Volume Purchase Program issue listed (from 1:11 PM PST). Largely stabilized; About 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: CBS News reports Apple has restored services after an internal update caused the outages. Resolved; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: NSA's classified internal communications network (NSA Net) is down, CNN reports; sources say no evidence of a cyberattack

Sources told CNN there is no evidence of a cyberattack so far, and accounts summarizing the report say the agency staggered employee arrivals while it works out the scope of the outage. CNN says it has asked the NSA for comment. The outage follows the week's FAA, United, banking and Microsoft disruptions already in this log, none of which has been tied to a cyberattack.

Still no NSA statement on cause or restoration found as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 1:14 PM ET: CBS News, citing multiple US officials, reports the NSA's internal classified network went offline Tuesday, prompting the agency to stagger arrival times for some personnel at Fort Meade. About 1:57 PM ET: Al Jazeera, citing CNN and a US official, reports the outage will not prevent urgent intelligence from reaching President Trump in Asia. Still no NSA statement and no evidence of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17, about 2:44–2:49 PM ET: Senate Majority Leader Thune says on the tech outages that 'a lot of bad actors' would love to damage the US; Al Jazeera reports the top House Democrat said it is not clear whether the outages are tied to infrastructure or malicious activity and that Congress needs a briefing. Reuters: as the string of tech outages raises alarm, President Trump says everything is 'fine'. No evidence of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17, about 4:56 PM ET: the White House posts DNI Jay Clayton saying 'This is not a cyberattack and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation-state' about the string of outages. Still no NSA statement on restoration found; About 9:10 PM ET Nov. 17: Reuters reports the week's technology outages 'extended to the US National Security Agency' as the Trump administration downplayed concerns about a broader problem. America.title: CONTINUATION: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)
America.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme reported malicious JavaScript being served through the Optimizely web experimentation platform to the websites of about 178 organizations, including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax and Ledger. He and security firm Coinspect say the payload included a crypto address swapper, a card skimmer, cookie theft and iOS exploit code; Helme says about $7,000 in crypto had been diverted. Optimizely says it identified and contained a security incident affecting some Web Experimentation customers, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the injected code and contacted customers. BleepingComputer reports the attack.
America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known; Nov. 17: Optimizely's notice says an 'unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation' (Infosecurity Magazine). Reuters (via the New York Post, about 9:30 AM ET) cites researcher Scott Helme and says it could not independently establish whether every affected site was successfully exploited; AFP (about 12:45 PM ET) says nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted. Report URI names the iOS exploit kits as Coruna and DarkSword and advises updating to iOS 18.7.3+ or 26.3+; Mediaite, citing Reuters, says Salesforce disabled the scripts, Equifax stopped using the platform and found no compromise, and IKEA is investigating. Report URI says all infected files were clean by 23:11 UTC Nov. 16 (6:11 PM ET). STABILIZED: contained; moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Peoria, Illinois — FBI arrests and a grand jury indicts a man over the emailed bomb threat to the BioUrja ethanol plant; evacuation order lifted earlier
America.location: Peoria and East Peoria, Illinois, US
America.summary: Peoria police ordered a mandatory evacuation within about one mile of the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant (the former ADM plant) after a bomb threat on Friday, the Peoria Journal Star reports. WCIA reports officials said there is a bomb, with Homeland Security monitoring, the Coast Guard holding river traffic, bridges shut and downtown businesses closed. Lookner, relaying Peoria Police, says bomb technicians rendered a suspicious package safe around 9:12 PM CT and that it had been determined to be a threat; the search was not complete and the evacuation order was still in effect.
America.status: Official all-clear relayed: CBS News reports the evacuation order was lifted Saturday and residents allowed home; KMOX reports the Coast Guard reopened the river and that Saturday's searches were negative after one bomb was found Friday; suspect and motive not stated. Situation has stabilized; can move to routine coverage; WPXI and other Hearst stations report police lifted the evacuation after a bomb was found near the ethanol plant; Nov. 16: CBS Chicago says Peoria police report a person is in custody in connection with the bomb threat and explosive device found at the ethanol plant; Nov. 16: NewsNation and WCCB say Peoria Mayor Rita Ali said a suspect is in custody in connection with the bomb found at the BioUrja ethanol plant; EODWX5 says Peoria police retracted their statement that a person of interest was taken into custody and that the FBI continues to lead the investigation. Custody status is conflicting in posts checked; Nov. 16, about 11:00 PM ET: Mario Nawfal, citing NBC Chicago, reports federal authorities say a 10-month trainee at the plant named Kozak was arrested for allegedly leaving the device and sending the bomb threat. This clears up the earlier conflicting custody reports, but it comes through a relay of NBC Chicago, not an official post. Evacuation remains lifted; stabilized; Nov. 17, about 1:29–1:30 PM ET: KPLR 11 reports an Illinois man has been indicted over the Peoria ethanol-plant bomb threat; a watch-floor account citing CBS News and NBC Chicago names him as Andrew M. Kozak, charged with one count of threats regarding explosives and one count of interstate communications. Stabilized; About 6:14 PM ET Nov. 17: FBI Director Kash Patel says the FBI arrested one person who allegedly sent the Nov. 13 email claiming explosive devices had been placed at the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant, and that a grand jury indicted him today on charges including making threatening interstate communications and threatening to damage or destroy property with an explosive device; no one was injured and the investigation is ongoing. OSINTdefender names him as BioUrja employee Andrew Kozak, arrested at the facility when he reported for work, and notes the indictment does not allege he placed the device found at the plant; About 10:20 PM ET Nov. 17: NBC News reports the Illinois man, a trainee at the Peoria ethanol plant, is charged by a federal grand jury with two felonies related to the bomb found at the facility; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; About 6:40 AM ET Nov. 18: ABC News says Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is due on Capitol Hill on Wednesday for a hearing on worldwide threats and is likely to face questions about the technology disruptions of the past week; About 11:42 AM ET Nov. 18: at the House Worldwide Threats hearing, DNI Jay Clayton said that, based on what is known today, the recent outages are separate service outages tied to maintenance and technical changes and 'not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack,' while the intelligence community keeps monitoring (House Homeland Security Committee GOP clip); About 1:38 PM ET Nov. 18: CBS News says top US national security officials told Congress they have found no evidence that the string of outages affecting airlines, banks, Microsoft services and national security communications systems were connected or caused by malicious cyberattacks. About 1:52 PM ET: CBS News, citing a person familiar with the investigation, reports the contractor that owns the network running the air traffic control system took several hours to pinpoint the source of the outage behind Friday's ground stop, delaying its lifting; About 2:35 PM ET Nov. 18: Reuters reports experts say a surge in software patches is likely behind the recent string of tech outages. Consistent with officials' testimony that no cyberattack link has been found; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Court websites and e-filing portals offline in California and other states after a security incident at vendor Journal Technologies
America.location: California (incl. Sacramento, Alameda and Kern counties), Las Vegas, Nevada, and Spokane, Washington
America.summary: Online court portals for courts across California and in other states were taken offline after court technology vendor Journal Technologies reported a security incident, FOX40 and KTLA report. The Lynnwood Times says the vendor detected suspicious automated activity targeting its public-facing court portals on Nov. 13 and advised courts to suspend access while security measures were put in place; the company says it has found no evidence so far that criminal justice information was exposed. Affected courts include several California counties and municipal courts in Las Vegas and Spokane, where people are told to contact the court directly.
America.status: Portals offline since Nov. 17 (first reported about 5:20 PM ET); vendor investigation ongoing; restoration timing varies by court; About 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: OSINT account Osint613 reports court online services in California 'and several other states' are out after the potential cybersecurity threat at Journal Technologies, naming courts in Sacramento, Alameda and Kern counties, Las Vegas and Spokane. Many relays repeat the same report; no vendor or court confirmation of ransomware, data theft or a wider scope found as of about 9:55 PM ET. Remains MEDIUM; As of about 11:10 PM ET Nov. 17: relays add Fresno, Marin and Los Angeles counties to the list of affected California courts (unconfirmed); still no vendor or court confirmation of ransomware, data theft or a wider scope. Remains MEDIUM; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Logan Circle mass shooting in Washington, D.C. — police now count six victims (one killed, five wounded) at and outside a VIDA Fitness gym; suspect dead after shooting himself while barricaded
America.location: 1500 block of 15th Street NW (15th and P Streets NW), Logan Circle, Washington, D.C.
America.summary: D.C. police say one person was killed and four wounded Thursday morning (Nov. 12) in a shooting at and outside a VIDA Fitness gym near 15th and P Streets NW in Logan Circle. The suspect barricaded himself in an apartment on the 1500 block of 15th Street NW and shot himself; MPD later said the barricade had concluded and the scene was safe, and the Washington Post says police report the suspect was pronounced dead. Interim police chief Jeffery Carroll described a conflict between the suspect and the building's homeowners association, and FOX 5 DC cites Councilmember Brooke Pinto saying the suspect allegedly targeted and killed the building's owner, with whom he was in litigation. A reporter relaying the chief's briefing says one of the wounded is in critical condition; WUSA9 says 13 nearby schools were placed on alert status.
America.status: Official statement issued (MPD): barricade concluded, suspect dead of a self-inflicted gunshot wound; MPD interim chief Jeffrey Carroll gave an update; a 7News reporter, citing MPD, says police have publicly identified the suspect and that the victim who died was 46; WGME, citing D.C. police, counts two dead including the gunman and four injured; situation stabilized, moving to routine coverage; police now count a sixth victim, whose injuries are not considered life-threatening (AP-sourced posts relayed by KVUE and WFAA), bringing the toll to one killed and five wounded; police identified the man killed as 46-year-old James Stuart, a manager at the condo building where the suspected shooter lived; CBS Mornings says police report the gunman had posted complaints about mold and water problems at his apartment before the shooting; Washington Post reports police say one person was killed and five injured and the shooter died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound; a DC reporter quotes Police Chief Jeffery Carroll as saying one victim remains in critical but stable condition; FOX 5 DC reports police say the suspect, identified by outlets as 55-year-old doctor Matt Lambert, waited inside the gym for nearly an hour before shooting the building manager; incident is over and moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; About 2:00–2:40 AM ET Nov. 18: AFP reports Ukraine released images of the strike; Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says its special operation with the defence forces destroyed one of the bridge's arches and a road span, and Zelensky called the strike 'unprecedented'. New video of the destroyed road section is circulating; About 3:30 AM ET Nov. 18: footage filmed from a train crossing the bridge shows the missing road arch and adjacent span; trains appear to be running on the rail section, indicating rail traffic has resumed (OSINT reading of video). No confirmed new strikes; About 4:48 AM ET Nov. 18: Russia says rail traffic across the bridge is running on schedule despite the damage; its Transport Ministry is adding passenger trains and says the Kerch ferry crossing could be activated for cargo and passengers if necessary (via NOELreports). No confirmed new strikes; About 6:33 AM ET Nov. 18: the Kyiv Independent shares new video (from the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+) apparently filmed from a train crossing the bridge. It shows a large section of the motorway fully collapsed with the arch missing and debris in the water, and suggests the railway across the rest of the bridge is still working; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight
Russia.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Sunday that its forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield, home to the 929th State Flight Test Center and a Su-34 base, and a drone launch site at Tsymbulova in Oryol region overnight. Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry says Russian strikes left some consumers in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions without power and forced emergency outages there (via Flash). Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian attack on Zhytomyr region reportedly hits energy infrastructure and homes
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports Russian Geran-4 jet-powered drones attacked a locomotive depot in Dnipro overnight, with a fire visible after the attack. No casualty figures or official confirmation were available.
Russia.status: Single OSINT source; no Ukrainian Railways or regional official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts; no Ukrainian Air Force tally, regional administration statement or damage reports found yet; AMK Mapping reports a large fire in Chornomorsk after the attack and says NASA FIRMS data shows a large fire at the impact area; it says a likely target was a freight-logistics company or the Chornomorsk Automobile Plant; still no official Ukrainian damage or casualty report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays a Russian Defense Ministry claim that the targets were a ferry terminal, the Chornomorsk port administration and a nearby electrical substation; this is a Russian military claim, not independently confirmed, and no official Ukrainian damage report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays Ukrainian energy company DTEK confirming a substation in Chornomorsk was hit by multiple drones, leaving about 41,000 homes without power; Gerashchenko and Flash report six people injured in Chornomorsk and damage to energy infrastructure, an administrative building, a gas pipeline and nearby homes; the same overnight wave injured six in Zaporizhzhia (12 strikes, per Flash) and three in a drone hit on a Kropyvnytskyi residential building; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. The Russian Defense Ministry says it downed 533 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and seas between 8 PM Nov 14 and 8 AM Nov 15 Moscow time, and SOTA and Charter 97 report Rosaviatsia restrictions at about 12 airports including Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Samara, Sochi and Volgograd. An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian double-tap drone strike in Hlukhiv, Sumy region, wounds a grandmother, her grandson and a police officer
Russia.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential area in Hlukhiv on the morning of Nov. 14, wounding a woman; a second drone hit while police were evacuating her and her 9-year-old grandson. NOEL Reports names officers Mykola Savchenko and Ihor Voloshko and says Voloshko was wounded; Ukraine's United24 says the officer and the boy were both injured and all survived.
Russia.status: Reported by Ukrainian government fundraising account United24 and multiple Ukrainian outlets with bodycam footage; final casualty details not confirmed by Sumy regional officials on X; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone strike on a house in Proletarsky, Belgorod region, kills three, Russian regional officials say
Russia.location: Proletarsky, Rakitnoye district, Belgorod region, Russia
Russia.summary: SOTA, citing the Belgorod regional operational headquarters, reports a drone hit a private house in the settlement of Proletarsky, killing a married couple and their 24-year-old daughter and injuring another man. It also reports injuries from drone attacks in Shebekino and the village of Rzhevka.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Russian regional authorities, relayed); not independently verified; no Ukrainian comment found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone strike sets warehouses on fire in Vyshhorod, just north of Kyiv
Russia.summary: WarTranslated reports a large fire in Vyshhorod near Kyiv after a drone strike on Saturday morning. A second account reports warehouses are on fire after the strike as attacks continued into the morning.
Russia.status: Early reports; casualties and official Ukrainian regional statement not found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, injure more than 50, including eight children; a rescuer clearing rubble is killed
Russia.summary: A Russian strike on Friday damaged two five-storey apartment buildings in Zaporizhzhia, causing fires, and rescuers freed people trapped in their apartments. Ukraine's State Emergency Service says 30 people were injured, including six children. Kyiv Post reports Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed two people on Friday, including a 17-year-old boy.
Russia.status: Official figures issued (Ukraine's State Emergency Service, as relayed by United24); search-and-rescue reported completed; a CGTN Europe post citing Ukrainian reports puts the injured at 50, which is not confirmed; Kyiv Independent now reports 50 injured, including eight children, and says a Cobra emergency-service rescuer was killed when a concrete slab fell on him while clearing debris, citing local authorities; Euromaidan Press, citing the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration, says the Nov. 13 strikes killed two people and injured more than 50, and Anton Gerashchenko puts the dead at three including the rescuer; death counts differ slightly between sources; Ukraine Review reports 29 of those injured remain under medical care, six in serious condition, including six children aged 10 to 17; Angurintel, relaying the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration, reports a new Russian strike on the Voznesenivskyi district today injured 15 people, including two children, and damaged a residential building and nearby educational institution; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Ukrainian drone attacks hit Rostov region and the Samara oil pumping station; Rostov-on-Don declares an emergency regime
Russia.location: Rostov-on-Don and Aksay district (Rostov region); Samara region, Russia
Russia.summary: NEXTA reports more than 120 drones attacked Russia's Rostov region on the night of Nov. 13, sparking a fire at a 1,500-square-metre warehouse in Aksay district and setting an industrial facility and three cars on fire in Rostov-on-Don. Sota reports Rostov-on-Don's mayor declared an emergency regime on streets where homes were damaged, saying nine apartment buildings were damaged and 114 houses were left without heat. The Insider reports the Samara regional governor confirmed a drone attack on an industrial enterprise, which monitoring channels identify as the Transneft-operated Samara oil pumping station (LPDS).
Russia.status: Official regional statements reported (Rostov governor and mayor, Samara governor); extent of damage at the Samara station not confirmed; separate from the Volgograd refinery strike logged below; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones strike the Volgograd oil refinery, setting fires; governor says four killed and two injured
Russia.summary: Multiple posts with video, including Liveuamap, report a drone attack on the Lukoil-operated Volgograd oil refinery on the evening of Nov. 12, with fires on the plant's grounds; one post says the extent of damage remains unconfirmed. A separate post relays Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as saying more than 50 drones headed for Moscow were destroyed in about 90 minutes. Middle East.summary: India's Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker MT NAVIG8 MESSI, carrying three Indian seafarers, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf on Nov. 18 while approaching the Strait of Hormuz. He says all three Indians and the entire crew are safe and accounted for with no serious injuries; one Indian officer was taken to hospital for first aid. Maritime-risk analyst Martin Kelly says NAVIG8 MESSI was struck this morning after a recent strike on its sister ship NAVIG8 MACALLISTER, and Osint613 says Kelly linked it to the tanker ADNOC reported struck. The attacker has not been officially named.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by India's shipping minister about 7:24 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker not named; how this relates to the ADNOC vessel and UKMTO 211-26 reports (which mention injured or missing crew) is not confirmed by ADNOC or UKMTO; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Car-ramming in Kafr Qasim, Israel, injures eight; local leaders call it terrorism and a Jewish driver is arrested
Middle East.location: Kafr Qasim, central Israel
Middle East.summary: Eight people, including women leaving a wedding hall, were struck at several locations in the Arab town of Kafr Qasim; local authorities called it an act of terrorism and the driver, a Jewish man, was arrested (journalist Noga Tarnopolsky). United Hatzalah said it treated three pedestrians struck near the country club, a 25-year-old woman seriously injured and a couple in their 50s lightly injured. Motive not officially established; some posts say police are examining whether the driver was under the influence.
Middle East.status: About 1:43–1:57 PM ET Nov. 18: driver arrested; police investigation ongoing; no official police statement on motive found; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli military announces an operation in three blocks of central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and closes Salah al-Din Road, despite the ceasefire
Middle East.location: Central Gaza Strip (north of Bureij and Nuseirat camps), Palestinian Territories
Middle East.summary: Israel's coordinator of government activities in the territories (COGAT) said the Israeli military began an operation in three blocks of central Gaza and would close Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south road, to traffic there, Al Jazeera reports. The Israeli military said its forces began concentrated activity in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and called Hamas infrastructure threatening its troops a breach of the agreement. Anadolu calls it a new offensive despite the ceasefire, and Roya News says tanks were approaching Salah al-Din Road. A source at Al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera one person was killed and others injured in an Israeli strike on al-Maghraqa, north of Nuseirat.
Middle East.status: Announced about 6:00–6:55 AM ET Nov. 18; operation under way; casualty figures early and from one hospital source; no Hamas or mediator response found yet; About 7:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Al Jazeera, citing Israeli media, says the army has begun its first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire agreement. No updated casualty figures or Hamas or mediator response found; About 2:46–2:52 PM ET Nov. 18: the IDF says IDF and ISA (Shin Bet) personnel began a targeted operation to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to troops; civilians were warned to avoid the area and told of a road closure; the IDF says troops remain deployed in accordance with the ceasefire agreement. Times of Israel's Emanuel Fabian notes COGAT issued an evacuation warning to civilians in the Hamas-controlled area. No casualty figures in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 211-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; fire put out, one crew member missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, 13 nm north of Khasab, Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued warning 211-26 at about 4:53 AM ET Nov. 18 after a time-late report of an incident 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Local authorities report a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile within the Strait of Hormuz; a fire broke out on board and has since been extinguished. Search and rescue efforts are under way for a missing crew member. UKMTO did not name the vessel or the attacker, and it is not clear whether this is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel attack reported on Nov. 17 (also one crew member missing), which is logged separately.
Middle East.status: Time-late report; vessel damage and environmental impact unknown; UKMTO advises vessels to transit with caution. Vessel name and attacker not stated as of about 6:00 AM ET; About 6:42 AM ET Nov. 18: the maritime-tracking account live_ais_com says the time-late UKMTO report followed ADNOC's press statement, suggesting the struck tanker is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel (logged separately). This link is the account's assessment; neither UKMTO nor ADNOC has said publicly that they are the same incident, and the vessel name and attacker are still not stated; carried forward from 3:15 PM ET, no newer change found
