Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, as the search ends
Russia.summary: NEXTA, citing Ukraine's Interior Ministry, says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha and that the search operation is complete. Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; About 2:00–2:40 AM ET Nov. 18: AFP reports Ukraine released images of the strike; Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says its special operation with the defence forces destroyed one of the bridge's arches and a road span, and Zelensky called the strike 'unprecedented'. New video of the destroyed road section is circulating; About 3:30 AM ET Nov. 18: footage filmed from a train crossing the bridge shows the missing road arch and adjacent span; trains appear to be running on the rail section, indicating rail traffic has resumed (OSINT reading of video). No confirmed new strikes; About 4:48 AM ET Nov. 18: Russia says rail traffic across the bridge is running on schedule despite the damage; its Transport Ministry is adding passenger trains and says the Kerch ferry crossing could be activated for cargo and passengers if necessary (via NOELreports). No confirmed new strikes; About 6:33 AM ET Nov. 18: the Kyiv Independent shares new video (from the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+) apparently filmed from a train crossing the bridge. It shows a large section of the motorway fully collapsed with the arch missing and debris in the water, and suggests the railway across the rest of the bridge is still working; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine

Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.

Middle East.location: Saudi Arabia / Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters' chief Saudi correspondent Timour Azhari posted that Saudi Arabia is preparing for its war against Yemen's Houthis to last well into next year, citing two Western officials briefed by Saudis. He reports Saudi officials have briefed the campaign could run up to six months, and that Riyadh has postponed major global events it was set to host to autumn/winter 2027.
Middle East.status: Single-journalist report citing two unnamed Western officials, posted about 8:46 AM ET Nov. 18; no official Saudi statement found. Escalation signal, not a new attack; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: India's shipping minister says the Liberia-flagged tanker NAVIG8 MESSI was hit by a projectile in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz; all crew safe
Middle East.location: Persian Gulf, approaches to the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: India's Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker MT NAVIG8 MESSI, carrying three Indian seafarers, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf on Nov. 18 while approaching the Strait of Hormuz. He says all three Indians and the entire crew are safe and accounted for with no serious injuries; one Indian officer was taken to hospital for first aid. Maritime-risk analyst Martin Kelly says NAVIG8 MESSI was struck this morning after a recent strike on its sister ship NAVIG8 MACALLISTER, and Osint613 says Kelly linked it to the tanker ADNOC reported struck. The attacker has not been officially named.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by India's shipping minister about 7:24 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker not named; how this relates to the ADNOC vessel and UKMTO 211-26 reports (which mention injured or missing crew) is not confirmed by ADNOC or UKMTO; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: Car-ramming in Kafr Qasim, Israel, injures eight; local leaders call it terrorism and a Jewish driver is arrested
Middle East.location: Kafr Qasim, central Israel
Middle East.summary: Eight people, including women leaving a wedding hall, were struck at several locations in the Arab town of Kafr Qasim; local authorities called it an act of terrorism and the driver, a Jewish man, was arrested (journalist Noga Tarnopolsky). United Hatzalah said it treated three pedestrians struck near the country club, a 25-year-old woman seriously injured and a couple in their 50s lightly injured. Motive not officially established; some posts say police are examining whether the driver was under the influence.
Middle East.status: About 1:43–1:57 PM ET Nov. 18: driver arrested; police investigation ongoing; no official police statement on motive found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Israeli military announces an operation in three blocks of central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and closes Salah al-Din Road, despite the ceasefire
Middle East.location: Central Gaza Strip (north of Bureij and Nuseirat camps), Palestinian Territories
Middle East.summary: Israel's coordinator of government activities in the territories (COGAT) said the Israeli military began an operation in three blocks of central Gaza and would close Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south road, to traffic there, Al Jazeera reports. The Israeli military said its forces began concentrated activity in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and called Hamas infrastructure threatening its troops a breach of the agreement. Anadolu calls it a new offensive despite the ceasefire, and Roya News says tanks were approaching Salah al-Din Road. A source at Al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera one person was killed and others injured in an Israeli strike on al-Maghraqa, north of Nuseirat.
Middle East.status: Announced about 6:00–6:55 AM ET Nov. 18; operation under way; casualty figures early and from one hospital source; no Hamas or mediator response found yet; About 7:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Al Jazeera, citing Israeli media, says the army has begun its first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire agreement. No updated casualty figures or Hamas or mediator response found; About 2:46–2:52 PM ET Nov. 18: the IDF says IDF and ISA (Shin Bet) personnel began a targeted operation to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to troops; civilians were warned to avoid the area and told of a road closure; the IDF says troops remain deployed in accordance with the ceasefire agreement. Times of Israel's Emanuel Fabian notes COGAT issued an evacuation warning to civilians in the Hamas-controlled area. No casualty figures in posts checked

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 211-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; fire put out, one crew member missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, 13 nm north of Khasab, Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued warning 211-26 at about 4:53 AM ET Nov. 18 after a time-late report of an incident 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Local authorities report a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile within the Strait of Hormuz; a fire broke out on board and has since been extinguished. Search and rescue efforts are under way for a missing crew member. UKMTO did not name the vessel or the attacker, and it is not clear whether this is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel attack reported on Nov. 17 (also one crew member missing), which is logged separately.
Middle East.status: Time-late report; vessel damage and environmental impact unknown; UKMTO advises vessels to transit with caution. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iran's army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone and missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait
Middle East.location: Ali Al Salem Air Base, Kuwait

This is the first formal Iranian military claim of responsibility linked to the drone attacks Kuwait's armed forces reported engaging since about 4:39 PM ET Nov. 17. Relays of the statement quote the army warning that any response to aggression will be decisive and without geographical limits.

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Kuwait's armed forces say air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks over Kuwait, hours after the US strike on Qeshm; attacker not officially named
Middle East.location: Kuwait (hosts major US bases incl. Camp Arifjan and Ali Al Salem)
Middle East.summary: Kuwait's state news agency KUNA reported about 4:46 PM ET Nov. 17 that the General Staff of the Kuwaiti Armed Forces announced its air defenses were actively engaging drone threats and urged the public to stay calm and follow safety instructions; the army said any explosions heard are interceptions. TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Attacker not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 5:02 to 5:40 AM ET: India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said TARA GAS, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and the whole 25-member crew was safe. Arab News and other outlets citing UKMTO say a tanker leaving the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile, setting its engine room on fire. Drop Site News, citing UKMTO, puts the strike at 05:58 UTC and says no casualties were reported and all crew are accounted for.
Middle East.status: Official warning issued (UKMTO); vessel name, flag and attacker not identified in posts checked; extent of damage being assessed; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16: aggregators repeat UKMTO's description of an engine-room fire and that all crew are accounted for; vessel still unnamed in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Rare overnight Israeli strike in Lebanon's eastern Beqaa Valley near the Syrian border
Middle East.location: Beqaa Valley near the Lebanon–Syria border
Middle East.summary: Lebanese media report an overnight Israeli Air Force strike near the Lebanon-Syria border in the eastern Beqaa Valley, the first in that area in several months. Times of Israel reporter Emanuel Fabian, citing Israeli security sources, says it was meant to stop a weapons shipment bound for Hezbollah. The IDF has not commented.
Middle East.status: Early reports; IDF has not commented; no casualty or damage figures found in posts checked; Nov. 16: JNS reports Israeli forces struck a Hezbollah-bound weapons shipment crossing from Syria; the Alma Center, citing Lebanese reports, places the strike at about 4:30 a.m. in the Al-Shaara–Janta area of the Nabi Chit barrens and says no casualties were officially reported; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Emanuel Fabian (Times of Israel) on X

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Yemeni government forces withdraw from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Reuters says Houthis in control
Middle East.location: Dhubab and Bab el-Mandeb area, Taiz/Lahj, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters reported Sunday that forces fighting for Yemen's internationally recognized government withdrew from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. Yemen's armed forces told Al Arabiya the redeployment reflects reprioritized objectives and aims to break the siege of Taiz. Al Jazeera says the Houthi advance threatens one of the government's last strongholds and brings fighting closer to the shipping route.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by government forces' statements and Reuters; no attacks on shipping linked to the withdrawal found in posts checked; extent of Houthi control along the coast unclear; Nov. 16: Anadolu Arabic reports the army foiled a Houthi attack in Taiz, cites two rights groups documenting 319 civilians killed or injured since September, and notes Houthi accusations of Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Saada with no Riyadh comment; Houthi-aligned YNP reports Saudi strikes on Sabr district south of Taiz city for the first time in weeks after a Houthi advance there (partisan source); Nov. 16 evening: Al Jazeera English says the Houthis have claimed control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait; Houthi claim, extent of control not independently confirmed; About 12:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Reuters reports Houthi forces are threatening Aden after capturing territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast, raising concerns for the Saudi-backed government and for shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 206-26: tanker approached by possible mothership and armed skiff 430 nm east of Socotra
Middle East.location: Indian Ocean, 430 nm east of Socotra, Yemen
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says the master of a tanker reported being approached at 0330 UTC on Nov. 16 by a possible mothership and a skiff about 430 nautical miles east of Socotra. Four armed people and a ladder were seen on the skiff. Ships are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO warning issued; suspicious approach, no boarding reported; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sirik and Kong, Hormozgan province, and in Shahriyar near Tehran; cause unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran
Middle East.summary: Several accounts reported explosions heard in Sirik in Iran's southern Hormozgan province on Sunday afternoon, citing Al Mihwar News and Iranian media. Other accounts said an explosion in Kong, also near the Strait of Hormuz, was linked to the targeting of an Iranian surface-to-air missile launcher. Separate reports describe an explosion in Shahriyar, west of Tehran.
Middle East.status: Early reports; claims that US forces struck air-defense launchers are speculation, and no official US or Iranian statement on a strike, damage or casualties was found; Nov. 15 evening: HormuzLetter and AI313_ say, citing only 'initial reports', that the US struck Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik; still no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Iranian official confirmation found, so the attribution remains unverified; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC Navy says two tankers hit naval mines on the 'unauthorized' southern Hormuz route Sunday and claims one supertanker sank
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: The IRGC Navy says two oil tankers that had switched off their tracking systems struck naval mines on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours, caught fire after large explosions, and that one, carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, sank. It released footage it says shows the explosions. The vessels have not been named, and it is unclear whether either is the tanker in UKMTO warning 205-26.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only, relayed by Tehran Times, The Cradle, FirstSquawk and ME Observer; not independently confirmed in posts checked; earlier IRGC tanker-mine claims in this log also remain unverified; Nov. 15 night: the IRGC Navy now claims two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire, saying six tankers have caught fire or sunk since Saturday (Iran International citing Iranian state media; Press TV). No confirmation from UKMTO, CENTCOM or ship operators found; ship names not given, so the claim remains unverified; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Tectonic, citing IRIB, says Iranian naval forces claimed three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, that the IRGC Navy again said six tankers have caught fire or are sinking since Sunday, and that a claimed sinking video shows fire on the water with no clearly visible vessel; ship names still not given and the claims remain unverified; Nov. 17 early: Persian-language outlets relay an IRGC Navy statement claiming a fourth oil tanker in 24 hours exploded after hitting a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; vessel not named; IRGC claim only, no UKMTO, CENTCOM or shipowner confirmation found; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi missile attack near Aden kills at least five civilians, AFP reports
Middle East.location: Lahj governorate, near Aden, Yemen
Middle East.summary: AFP, citing four sources, reports that a Houthi missile attack near Aden on Sunday, Nov. 15 killed five people and wounded eight (via LBCI). A Rai al-Youm report citing AFP and Anadolu puts the toll at at least eight civilians killed and 12 wounded in Lahj.
Middle East.status: Early reports via wire services; tolls differ between reports (5 dead/8 hurt vs. at least 8 dead/12 hurt); carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Rai al-Youm on X (cites AFP, Anadolu)

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 205-26: tanker attacked in the Gulf while heading toward the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.location: Southern Arabian Gulf, near the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says it is aware of a report from Indian shipping authorities of an attack on a tanker transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait of Hormuz. The crew are accounted for and safe. Damage and environmental impact were unknown at the time of the report, and vessels are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO advisory (reported 11:52 UTC, 6:52 AM ET) relayed by Iran International, Rudaw and others; attacker, vessel name and damage not identified; UKMTO text says the report came from Indian shipping authorities, the tanker was transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait, and the crew are accounted for and safe; damage and environmental impact unknown; Nov. 16: OSINT accounts say a crude tanker seen on Sentinel imagery being towed to port is believed to be the VLCC AL DHANNAH, the vessel in warning 205-26, with all crew safe; identification is OSINT assessment, not official; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. Low-credibility posts claiming a new Iranian attack on US bases in Bahrain or an IRGC statement of '550 Americans killed and wounded' have no primary source and are not logged; satellite-imagery claims that the radar was destroyed on Nov. 14 are unverified; As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Iranian drone and missile attacks on US bases in Bahrain seen only from low-credibility accounts, not logged. Kuwait's military separately reports engaging hostile drones (see Kuwait item); As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Bahrain attacks still only from low-credibility accounts, not logged; 7:15 PM ET UPDATE — renewed alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an 'alert of potential threat' at about 6:06 PM ET Nov. 17 (2:06 AM local Wednesday), urging people to stay calm and go to the nearest safe location; Al Arabiya's correspondent reported sirens, and blasts were reported. The ministry announced an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET. Bahrain News Agency reports the Arab League condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Bahrain; earlier the GCC secretary-general condemned repeated Iranian attacks. FaytuksNetwork's OSINT timeline puts this second Bahrain attack of the day at about 6:10 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on this wave, and no confirmed damage or casualties, as of about 7:10 PM ET; no formal IRGC claim for this wave found. Claims of a direct hit on Isa Air Base or US casualties (MintPress, DD_Geopolitics, MarioNawfal and others) are unverified and not logged; 8:15 PM ET UPDATE — third alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued another 'alert of potential threat' at about 7:48 PM ET Nov. 17 (3:48 AM local Wednesday), again urging people to go to the nearest safe location; Iran International notes it is the third such alert in less than 24 hours. About a minute later the Bahrain Defence Force General Command said Iran is continuing its 'systematic hostile approach' through attacks targeting the Kingdom. No all-clear from the Interior Ministry found as of about 8:05 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found; Iranian outlets such as Defa Press claim drones hit a US base in Bahrain, which is unverified. Ignored: Arabic and Persian relay claims of a 'direct hit' and large fires at Isa Air Base (no primary); 9:15 PM ET UPDATE: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17, ending the third alert of the night. The Bahrain News Agency (8:07 PM ET) carried the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses countered Iranian attacks; Anadolu reports Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks without specifying casualties or damage. Reuters: 'Bahrain issues all-clear after threat alert amid US-Iran exchanges of fire.' No new alert found as of about 9:05 PM ET; still no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found. A Civil Defence fire in a Souq Waqif building (moi_bahrain, no injuries, cause under investigation) is not linked to the attacks and is not logged; As of about 9:55 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no new CENTCOM statement on the evening waves (CENTCOM's earlier statement called the IRGC radar-hit claim false, with all drones intercepted and no damage or injuries); no confirmed damage or casualties and no formal IRGC claim found; About 10:38 PM ET Nov. 17: KUNA carries the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses fended off several Iranian aerial attacks and that Iran continues its 'systematic approach' of attacks on Bahrain (same BDF statement as earlier this evening). No new Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no confirmed damage or casualties and no new CENTCOM statement found as of about 11:10 PM ET; As of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; viral claims of a new wave and impacts at Sheikh Isa (BedouinReport, IranArabicMedia) have no official primary and are not logged; no new CENTCOM statement and no confirmed damage/casualties; About 12:12 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain News Agency reports the Muslim Council of Elders strongly condemns the renewed Iranian attack on Bahrain. No new Interior Ministry alert, CENTCOM statement, or confirmed damage or casualties found as of about 1:00 AM ET; Iranian-media claims of new explosions at US bases in Bahrain are not confirmed and not logged; As of about 2:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert (no moi_bahrain posts since about 12:30 AM ET in the search checked), no CENTCOM statement, and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert found; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Kuwait and Bahrain (see the Kuwait item). No CENTCOM statement and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 4:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert found since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 5:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert found since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry joined the condemnations of the Iranian attacks on Bahrain. No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert found since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear, and no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves or confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 7:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry or Bahrain Defence Force alert found since the 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17 all-clear (their accounts posted only routine items after 6:00 AM ET), and no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves or confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 8:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry or Bahrain Defence Force alert found since the 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17 all-clear; Bahrain's government issued a statement condemning the renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait (linked on the Kuwait item). No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves or confirmed damage or casualties found; About 9:28 AM ET Nov. 18: KUNA reports Bahrain's Foreign Ministry condemned the renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait. No new alerts, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked; About 12:27 PM ET Nov. 18: KUNA says Kuwait condemns continued Iranian attacks on Bahrain and the targeting of a UAE oil tanker and supports all measures Bahrain and the UAE may take. About 12:34 PM ET: CENTCOM says no US personnel were injured in any attempted Iranian attacks this week; As of about 3:05 PM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert found since the earlier all-clears; the US Embassy in Bahrain issued a heightened-vigilance alert (see the threats item on US Mission security alerts)

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iran launches drone attack on Kurdish opposition (PJAK) positions in Iraq's Kurdistan Region, the group says
Middle East.location: Sulaimani (Sulaymaniyah) province, Kurdistan Region, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Rudaw reports that Iran on Nov. 17 launched a suicide drone at positions of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group, in the Kurdistan Region, according to the group's spokesperson; it came a day after two missiles targeted another opposition group in the Region. The New Region says the suspected drone attack hit PJAK in Sulaimani province with no casualties reported. Iran has not commented in posts checked.
Middle East.status: Reported about 2:24–2:29 PM ET Nov. 17 by Kurdish outlets citing PJAK; no casualties reported; no Iraqi federal or KRG statement found; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC claims it shot down another drone south of Qeshm Island (Nov. 17), after earlier MQ-1 Predator claims
Middle East.location: Qeshm Island, Strait of Hormuz, Iran
Middle East.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Saturday it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Diario de Centro América reports. IEW Latest News relays CBS News reporting that this is the second straight day Iran has made such a claim.
Middle East.status: Iranian claim relayed by media; no US military confirmation found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: Al Mayadeen reports the IRGC now claims it took control of a ninth US MQM-170 drone over Qeshm; IRGC claim only, no US confirmation found; Nov. 17, about 5:42 to 5:50 AM ET: Al Jazeera and Roya News relay a new IRGC statement that its air defenses shot down a drone south of Qeshm Island. IRGC claim only; drone type and ownership not confirmed and no US comment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:34 AM ET: ISNA carries an IRGC statement saying its aerospace air defenses intercepted and destroyed a US MQ-1 drone south of Qeshm Island, which it calls the 18th MQ-1 destroyed. IRGC claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 11:40 AM–12:00 PM ET: ISNA and Tasnim publish IRGC video they say shows the 18th MQ-1 being shot down south of Qeshm; separately, Iran's regular army claims (via Mehr) its air defenses downed a US 'LUCAS' drone over the Strait of Hormuz. Both are Iranian military claims; no US confirmation found in posts checked; About 5:45 AM ET Nov. 18: Iran's regular army (Artesh) public relations office says its air defense units in the southeast shot down a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz (via Fars News and Press TV, which calls it 'another' MQ-9). Iranian military claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; About 8:34 AM ET Nov. 18: Press TV again posts 'Iran shoots down another US MQ-9 Reaper drone over Strait of Hormuz'; it is not clear from the post whether this is a new incident or a re-run of the 5:45 AM ET Iranian army claim. Iranian state-media claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Jaramana car bomb near Damascus — Syrian Internal Security and state news agency SANA confirm a man and a young girl killed

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Peter Obi condemns a reported attack on Kwankwaso's NDC convoy in Bichi, Kano State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Opposition presidential candidate Peter Obi says he is saddened by reports of an attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area. He calls for an immediate investigation and arrests. Kwankwaso had been commissioning NDC offices across Kano State on Sunday.
Africa.status: Early reports; party-side statement only; no police statement, casualty count or damage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya opens probe into violent protests at the Dadaab refugee complex
Africa.location: Hagadera camp, Dadaab, Garissa County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Anadolu reports that Kenyan authorities have opened an investigation after protesters opposing a planned market in Hagadera camp damaged government offices, stole equipment and broke into nearby businesses during clashes.
Africa.status: Single wire report citing authorities; casualty figures not reported; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. It cites Caasimada Online as saying forces loyal to a former South West state leader took Golweyn.
Africa.status: Single-source early report citing Caasimada Online; no official statement or claim of responsibility found; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: JNIM reportedly overruns a national police detachment at Balga, near Fada N'Gourma, eastern Burkina Faso
Africa.location: Balga, about 25 km from Fada N’Gourma, Est region, Burkina Faso
Africa.summary: A Sahel-focused account reports that a JNIM attack on the morning of Nov. 15 targeted the National Police detachment at Balga, sacking and burning it, and that many officers were killed and several are missing. It adds that the attackers took all weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no official Burkinabe statement or casualty figure found; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill a Zamfara governor's aide in a dawn attack in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits attacked worshippers at dawn prayer in Kaura Namoda on Sunday, Nov. 15, killing Nasiru Sani Kaura and abducting several others, according to the security platform Bakatsine (via Africa_lix). Nigerians_New reports he was an aide to Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal.
Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; About 2:31 PM ET Nov. 18: Borkena reports the Oromo Liberation Army acknowledged a role in the deadly Arsi Zone attack while contesting the civilian casualty figures

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Johannesburg Mayfair substation outage: City Power restores power to some essential services, including Garden City Hospital and the SABC
