threats.title: CONTINUATION: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. Still threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 17, about 5:48 AM ET: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the 'dirty bomb' allegations, attributed to the New York Times and spread by CNN, completely baseless and says enemies are trying to legitimize new aggression (Al Mayadeen). Still no DHS, FBI or NTAS bulletin found as of about 5:57 AM ET; only relays and explainers; Nov. 17, about 6:18 to 6:51 AM ET: Asked whether Iran poses an imminent threat to Washington, Trump said that if it does, 'they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' (Fox News); Al Arabiya English reports he said US authorities take any possible threat 'very seriously', and Faytuks Network, citing CBS, says Trump said the US is looking into the reported threat. Al Jazeera and Iran International report Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei denied the report as baseless; Iran International notes CNN said officials were divided on Tehran's capability and intent. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 7:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 8:07 AM ET: Al Arabiya English again reports Trump warning Iran it would 'pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' if it poses a threat to Washington. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 8:10 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 8:16–8:46 AM ET: New York Post and NewsNation report Trump, during his Asia trip, said the US takes a potential Iranian dirty-bomb threat 'very seriously because they happen to be crazy' and warned Tehran would 'pay a price.' Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 9:03–9:49 AM ET: Euronews and Iran International carry Trump's remarks in Manila that the threat is taken very seriously and Iran would pay an unprecedented price. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 10:08 AM ET; viral claims of a DHS Secretary war warning have no primary and are not logged; Nov. 17, about 10:40–11:04 AM ET: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf calls the claim that Iran planned to target senior Trump administration officials with a chemical weapon 'disinformation and fabrication' and incitement to war, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calls the reports 'RUBBISH' and Iraq War-style propaganda. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 11:10 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 11:31–11:45 AM ET: asked about the CNN report, President Trump said the US is taking seriously the possibility of an Iranian dirty-bomb plot in Washington (Reuters, BBC, Al Arabiya). Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 12:05 PM ET; Iran's parliament speaker and foreign minister continue to deny the report; Nov. 17, about 12:05–12:31 PM ET: CNN reports Trump said Iran would pay a major price if it detonated a dirty bomb in Washington; The Washington Times reports US officials held meetings on ways to counteract a potential Iranian plot against the homeland, while officials said there is no sign of an immediate threat. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 1:36 PM ET: Al Arabiya English reports Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi dismissed reports that Tehran is plotting a chemical-weapons attack in Washington, DC, and building missile bases beneath dams, calling them propaganda. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:31 PM ET: Axios reports President Trump warned Iran against orchestrating a 'dirty bomb' attack in Washington, D.C. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:19 PM ET: Iran's mission to the UN calls CNN's 'dirty bomb' report a 'fabricated narrative' and part of a disinformation campaign, and 'categorically rejects these baseless allegations'. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:24 PM ET: Iran International, citing IRGC-affiliated Tasnim, reports Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi called CNN's claim that Iran planned a chemical weapons attack in Washington a 'shameful lie'. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 5:05 PM ET; About 6:51 PM ET Nov. 17: CBS Evening News reports President Trump said, on arriving in the Philippines, that the US is 'looking in to' reports that Iran was developing plans for a potential dirty bomb targeting his administration. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 7:10 PM ET; As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new official statements beyond those already logged; still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; About 8:30–9:00 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed the CNN report, telling reporters he was not concerned about an imminent threat to Washington, D.C., that 'we have threat streams every day, the majority of them are not credible,' and calling media intelligence sources 'liars'. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; About 9:30–9:40 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran International quotes Secretary of State Rubio: 'I don't think there's any imminent threat,' expressing confidence in US intelligence agencies' ability to identify potential attacks; ABC World News Tonight reports President Trump says the US takes the dirty-bomb plot reports 'very seriously.' Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; About 5:43 AM ET Nov. 18: in Manila, Secretary of State Rubio called those leaking the intelligence behind the CNN report 'showboats and liars' and 'probably criminals,' and said he did not believe there was any imminent threat (via Iran International). Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; About 8:10 AM ET Nov. 18: C-SPAN says the House Homeland Security Committee's Worldwide Threats hearing airs live at 10 AM ET (DHS Secretary Mullin's testimony is being watched for comment on the reported Iran plot); About 9:55–9:57 AM ET Nov. 18: as the House Homeland Security Committee's Worldwide Threats hearing began (Reuters live video), DHS Secretary Mullin said the threat from Iran-backed terrorists is elevated (CGTN America; wire headlines relayed by financial-news accounts add that he will say Iran has targeted US cyber infrastructure, including transportation, energy, healthcare, water and financial services, since February; primary wire post not found on X). Separately, Zeteo (about 9:11 AM ET) reports unnamed sources calling the DC dirty-bomb plot story 'total horseshit'; Secretary Rubio earlier said there was no imminent threat. Threat reporting, not an attack; About 11:11–11:28 AM ET Nov. 18, at the House Homeland Security Committee's Worldwide Threats hearing, DNI Jay Clayton, asked about the reported Iranian dirty-bomb threat, said 'we do face a heightened threat from Iranians lethal plotting against our citizens at home and abroad,' citing a man indicted in New York for an Iranian-sponsored plot who kept plotting while in custody (Townhall clip; C-SPAN). Iran International (about 12:00 PM ET), citing Bloomberg, reports DHS Secretary Mullin's written testimony says Iranian cyber activity has increasingly targeted US transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services since February. No DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found. Threat reporting, not an attack; About 12:47 PM ET Nov. 18: Al Jazeera (breaking) quotes DHS Secretary Mullin as saying Iran does not pose an imminent threat of a dirty-bomb attack. CBS News (about 12:48 PM ET) reports DNI Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee Iranian threats inside and outside the US have 'substantially increased'; asked about Iranian sleeper cells, Mullin said DHS is working with intelligence and Justice Department officials to identify threats ('Is it a concern? Of course'). Threat reporting, not an attack; no NTAS change found; About 1:22 PM ET Nov. 18: Iran International reports FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia's written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee says the FBI continues to monitor Iranian plans for violent operations inside the US, citing disrupted plots against American officials and activists, and that the FBI has made 18 Iran-related counterintelligence and espionage arrests since President Trump returned to office. Threat reporting, not an attack; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

threats.title: CONTINUATION: Police and protesters clash in Manila as ASEAN summit opens; hundreds arrested in Manila and Muntinlupa

Arab Times reports two injured, and the journalists' union NUJP says police tried to arrest two student journalists.
threats.status: Police statements via Rappler and Philippine Star; multiple outlets; injury count from a single outlet; Malacañang has called for calm; Nov. 17, about 8:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya English says nearly 300 people have been arrested as demonstrations grip Manila during the ASEAN summit, which Trump is attending; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)
America.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme reported malicious JavaScript being served through the Optimizely web experimentation platform to the websites of about 178 organizations, including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax and Ledger. He and security firm Coinspect say the payload included a crypto address swapper, a card skimmer, cookie theft and iOS exploit code; Helme says about $7,000 in crypto had been diverted. Optimizely says it identified and contained a security incident affecting some Web Experimentation customers, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the injected code and contacted customers. BleepingComputer reports the attack.
America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known; Nov. 17: Optimizely's notice says an 'unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation' (Infosecurity Magazine). Reuters (via the New York Post, about 9:30 AM ET) cites researcher Scott Helme and says it could not independently establish whether every affected site was successfully exploited; AFP (about 12:45 PM ET) says nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted. Report URI names the iOS exploit kits as Coruna and DarkSword and advises updating to iOS 18.7.3+ or 26.3+; Mediaite, citing Reuters, says Salesforce disabled the scripts, Equifax stopped using the platform and found no compromise, and IKEA is investigating. Report URI says all infected files were clean by 23:11 UTC Nov. 16 (6:11 PM ET). STABILIZED: contained; moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: UPDATE: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; About 6:40 AM ET Nov. 18: ABC News says Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is due on Capitol Hill on Wednesday for a hearing on worldwide threats and is likely to face questions about the technology disruptions of the past week; About 11:42 AM ET Nov. 18: at the House Worldwide Threats hearing, DNI Jay Clayton said that, based on what is known today, the recent outages are separate service outages tied to maintenance and technical changes and 'not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack,' while the intelligence community keeps monitoring (House Homeland Security Committee GOP clip); About 1:38 PM ET Nov. 18: CBS News says top US national security officials told Congress they have found no evidence that the string of outages affecting airlines, banks, Microsoft services and national security communications systems were connected or caused by malicious cyberattacks. About 1:52 PM ET: CBS News, citing a person familiar with the investigation, reports the contractor that owns the network running the air traffic control system took several hours to pinpoint the source of the outage behind Friday's ground stop, delaying its lifting

The suspect barricaded himself in an apartment on the 1500 block of 15th Street NW and shot himself; MPD later said the barricade had concluded and the scene was safe, and the Washington Post says police report the suspect was pronounced dead. Interim police chief Jeffery Carroll described a conflict between the suspect and the building's homeowners association, and FOX 5 DC cites Councilmember Brooke Pinto saying the suspect allegedly targeted and killed the building's owner, with whom he was in litigation. At about 11:45 PM ET, Economist correspondent Oliver Carroll said Russian missile strikes have stopped traffic on the two main river bridges linking Kyiv's east and west and that there are some problems with water and electricity. No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 3:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post reports Russian missiles struck Kyiv's North and South bridges late Nov. 16, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting essential services, with three injured in Cherkasy region. Ukrainska Pravda says Mayor Klitschko released video of the damaged Northern Bridge. No official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 4:05 AM ET: Reuters reports Russian strikes hit two bridges in Kyiv, causing water and power cuts, citing the mayor. The Kyiv Independent published video and says the strike marks a return to targeted attacks on the capital's transit routes. Posts from Kyiv say the Left Bank is heavily congested because of traffic restrictions on the bridges while specialists assess the damage. No official structural assessment found in posts checked (an AMK Mapping post saying some Northern Bridge cables snapped is no longer available on X and was removed); Nov. 17, about 4:18 AM ET: NEXTA reports Kyiv residents are crossing the Northern Bridge on foot to reach the right bank after the overnight attack. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:44 AM ET: bne IntelliNews reports Kyiv has shut two Dnipro bridges after the Russian strikes. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:22 to 6:26 AM ET: Zelensky says Russia fired four ballistic missiles at Kyiv's Southern Bridge and three at the Northern Bridge, and that backup crossings are needed (NEXTA, Ukrainska Pravda). Footage of the Southern Bridge aftermath has been published despite city requests not to share it. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:00 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Kyiv metro service was restored between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. No structural assessment of the bridges found yet; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike hits port and industrial facilities in Mykolaiv, southern Ukraine
Russia.summary: A local official says Russian forces struck port facilities and industrial infrastructure in Mykolaiv overnight Nov. 17, as part of the wider missile and drone attack across Ukraine. Al Araby TV carries the same report citing Ukrainian authorities.
Russia.status: Early official report; damage and casualty figures not given in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine: two killed in Kyiv, two killed in Zaporizhzhia; substations reported hit in Rivne
Russia.location: Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Pavlohrad and other cities, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT mapping account AMK Mapping says Russia launched about 30 Iskander-M ballistic and about 10 Iskander-K cruise missiles overnight and that more than 300 Geran-2 drones were sent toward western Ukraine. It reports drones targeting electrical substations in Rivne, smoke over Zhytomyr, strong explosions and fires in Vinnytsia, and repeated attacks on Pavlohrad, where Ukrainian authorities report an enterprise was hit.
Russia.status: Developing; launch counts and damage come from OSINT tracking, with no Ukrainian Air Force tally or official damage assessment found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda report two people killed and one injured in Kyiv after a Russian attack, with non-residential buildings hit; Ukrainska Pravda reports Russian strikes on industrial sites in Zaporizhzhia killed two and injured 18. AMK Mapping reports Poland scrambled fighter jets to its eastern regions during the drone attack on western Ukraine (no Polish military post found in posts checked). The Energy Ministry reports outages in eight regions (see power grid item). Still no Ukrainian Air Force tally of launched or downed missiles and drones found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:00 to 5:54 AM ET: RBC-Ukraine reports Russia is massively striking western Ukraine, hitting Mukachevo, Ternopil and Chernivtsi; Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia (Mukachevo and Uzhhorod areas) in three waves around 10 a.m. Hungarian time, near the Hungarian border, with damage being assessed. Ukrainska Pravda reports a Russian strike on Dnipro hit a confectionery factory and homes, injuring 10; a school and apartment buildings in the Sobornyi district were also damaged. Ukrainian Air Force overnight tally still not found; Nov. 17, about 6:31 to 6:53 AM ET: Ukraine's Air Force says air defenses downed 205 of 306 Shahed-type drones, plus three Banderol/Dan-T mini cruise missiles and three Kh-59/69 cruise missiles, with no Iskander ballistic or cruise missiles shot down; hits were recorded at 44 locations (relayed by NOEL Reports and Ukrainska Pravda); Nov. 17, about 7:48 AM ET: Faytuks Network, citing Reuters, says Hungary suspended rail services to Ukraine for Tuesday and Wednesday as Russian drones struck western Ukraine, and a drone crashed about 300 meters from Mukachevo railway station, forcing crew to evacuate; Nov. 17, about 8:20–8:32 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports two killed and 38 injured in a Russian attack on industrial facilities in Zaporizhzhia; ZMiST reports a 51-year-old taxi driver killed and her passenger injured in a Russian attack on Vinnytsia; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, as the search ends
Russia.summary: NEXTA, citing Ukraine's Interior Ministry, says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha and that the search operation is complete. Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; About 2:00–2:40 AM ET Nov. 18: AFP reports Ukraine released images of the strike; Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says its special operation with the defence forces destroyed one of the bridge's arches and a road span, and Zelensky called the strike 'unprecedented'. New video of the destroyed road section is circulating; About 3:30 AM ET Nov. 18: footage filmed from a train crossing the bridge shows the missing road arch and adjacent span; trains appear to be running on the rail section, indicating rail traffic has resumed (OSINT reading of video). No confirmed new strikes; About 4:48 AM ET Nov. 18: Russia says rail traffic across the bridge is running on schedule despite the damage; its Transport Ministry is adding passenger trains and says the Kerch ferry crossing could be activated for cargo and passengers if necessary (via NOELreports). No confirmed new strikes; About 6:33 AM ET Nov. 18: the Kyiv Independent shares new video (from the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+) apparently filmed from a train crossing the bridge. It shows a large section of the motorway fully collapsed with the arch missing and debris in the water, and suggests the railway across the rest of the bridge is still working; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight
Russia.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Sunday that its forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield, home to the 929th State Flight Test Center and a Su-34 base, and a drone launch site at Tsymbulova in Oryol region overnight. Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry says Russian strikes left some consumers in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions without power and forced emergency outages there (via Flash). Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian attack on Zhytomyr region reportedly hits energy infrastructure and homes
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports Russian Geran-4 jet-powered drones attacked a locomotive depot in Dnipro overnight, with a fire visible after the attack. No casualty figures or official confirmation were available.
Russia.status: Single OSINT source; no Ukrainian Railways or regional official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts

It reports critical infrastructure in the Kirovohrad region was attacked, with two people injured, and that a business in Dnipro caught fire. Ukrainska Pravda and Ukrinform carry the same figures.
Russia.status: Daily casualty figures via Kyiv Independent, citing regional authorities; Air Force figures via NOEL Reports; damage assessments continuing; Nov. 16: Kyiv Independent says Russian attacks killed 6 and injured 45 across Ukraine over the past day as Kyiv endured almost nonstop air raid alerts; citing the Air Force, it says Russia launched 158 long-range attack drones overnight, including 77 jet-powered drones; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone hits a commuter train at Sumy railway station; no casualties reported
Russia.summary: The head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, Oleh Hryhorov, says a Russian drone deliberately struck a commuter train at the Sumy railway station on Tuesday morning. He says there were no passengers on board, the crew was in a shelter and there were no casualties. Ukrainska Pravda and RBC-Ukraine also report the attack on the train.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) statement; no casualties; damage to rolling stock; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drones kill two in Ladyzhyn, Vinnytsia region; energy facilities and a civilian enterprise hit; three days of mourning
Russia.summary: Ukrainska Pravda reports that Russian forces attacked a civilian enterprise in Vinnytsia region, killing two people. The type of enterprise and the extent of the damage were not given in the post.
Russia.status: Reported by Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda; energy damage extent not given; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drones target military aircraft repair plant in Russia's Novgorod region; explosions reported near Staraya Russa
Russia.location: Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, Russia; Crimea
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, citing Telegram monitoring channels, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea. No damage assessment or official Russian or Ukrainian statement was found. RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.
Russia.status: Early reports; Ukrainian outlets citing media and monitoring channels; damage not officially confirmed on X; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Centrenergo warns of 'extremely serious' consequences after Russian strike on Trypillia Thermal Power Plant
Russia.summary: Russian forces struck the Trypillia Thermal Power Plant, the Kyiv Independent reports. Centrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned generating company, said the impact appears significant, but the extent of the damage is not yet clear and needs further inspection.
Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Responsibility is not established in the posts found.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (IAEA, via Kyiv Independent); carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

IAEA: ZNPP employee killed in drone attack today

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Electrical substation in Kursk, Russia, reportedly struck by drones; fire at the facility
Russia.summary: NOEL Reports says an electrical substation supplying about 400,000 residents in Kursk was reportedly struck and caught fire; Kyiv Post also lists an attack on a Kursk substation among overnight Ukrainian strikes.
Russia.status: Reported by OSINT and Kyiv Post; no Russian official statement on damage or outages found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthis say the Saudi-led coalition carried out 87 airstrikes and missile attacks across Yemen in 24 hours
Middle East.location: Yemen (Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Taiz, Amran, Lahij, Saada, Al-Bayda, Marib, Ibb)
Middle East.summary: A Houthi statement carried by CGTN says Saudi warplanes and missiles carried out 87 strikes in the past 24 hours on Sanaa and eight governorates, causing civilian deaths and injuries, and 5,351 strikes in total since the latest escalation began. No casualty figures were given.
Middle East.status: Houthi claim (CGTN Europe and CGTN Africa, about 11:54 AM–12:02 PM ET Nov. 18); not independently confirmed; no coalition comment found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters' chief Saudi correspondent reports Saudi Arabia is preparing for its war against the Houthis to stretch well into next year
Middle East.location: Saudi Arabia / Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters' chief Saudi correspondent Timour Azhari posted that Saudi Arabia is preparing for its war against Yemen's Houthis to last well into next year, citing two Western officials briefed by Saudis. He reports Saudi officials have briefed the campaign could run up to six months, and that Riyadh has postponed major global events it was set to host to autumn/winter 2027.
Middle East.status: Single-journalist report citing two unnamed Western officials, posted about 8:46 AM ET Nov. 18; no official Saudi statement found. Escalation signal, not a new attack; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: India's shipping minister says the Liberia-flagged tanker NAVIG8 MESSI was hit by a projectile in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz; all crew safe
Middle East.location: Persian Gulf, approaches to the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: India's Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker MT NAVIG8 MESSI, carrying three Indian seafarers, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf on Nov. 18 while approaching the Strait of Hormuz. He says all three Indians and the entire crew are safe and accounted for with no serious injuries; one Indian officer was taken to hospital for first aid. Maritime-risk analyst Martin Kelly says NAVIG8 MESSI was struck this morning after a recent strike on its sister ship NAVIG8 MACALLISTER, and Osint613 says Kelly linked it to the tanker ADNOC reported struck. The attacker has not been officially named.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by India's shipping minister about 7:24 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker not named; how this relates to the ADNOC vessel and UKMTO 211-26 reports (which mention injured or missing crew) is not confirmed by ADNOC or UKMTO; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli military announces an operation in three blocks of central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and closes Salah al-Din Road, despite the ceasefire
Middle East.location: Central Gaza Strip (north of Bureij and Nuseirat camps), Palestinian Territories
Middle East.summary: Israel's coordinator of government activities in the territories (COGAT) said the Israeli military began an operation in three blocks of central Gaza and would close Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south road, to traffic there, Al Jazeera reports. The Israeli military said its forces began concentrated activity in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and called Hamas infrastructure threatening its troops a breach of the agreement. Anadolu calls it a new offensive despite the ceasefire, and Roya News says tanks were approaching Salah al-Din Road. A source at Al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera one person was killed and others injured in an Israeli strike on al-Maghraqa, north of Nuseirat.
Middle East.status: Announced about 6:00–6:55 AM ET Nov. 18; operation under way; casualty figures early and from one hospital source; no Hamas or mediator response found yet; About 7:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Al Jazeera, citing Israeli media, says the army has begun its first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire agreement. No updated casualty figures or Hamas or mediator response found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 211-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; fire put out, one crew member missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, 13 nm north of Khasab, Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued warning 211-26 at about 4:53 AM ET Nov. 18 after a time-late report of an incident 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Local authorities report a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile within the Strait of Hormuz; a fire broke out on board and has since been extinguished. Search and rescue efforts are under way for a missing crew member. UKMTO did not name the vessel or the attacker, and it is not clear whether this is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel attack reported on Nov. 17 (also one crew member missing), which is logged separately.
Middle East.status: Time-late report; vessel damage and environmental impact unknown; UKMTO advises vessels to transit with caution. Vessel name and attacker not stated as of about 6:00 AM ET; About 6:42 AM ET Nov. 18: the maritime-tracking account live_ais_com says the time-late UKMTO report followed ADNOC's press statement, suggesting the struck tanker is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel (logged separately). This link is the account's assessment; neither UKMTO nor ADNOC has said publicly that they are the same incident, and the vessel name and attacker are still not stated; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Saudi Civil Defense issues early-warning alerts in Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait; danger declared passed about 15 minutes later
Middle East.location: Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, southern Saudi Arabia
Middle East.summary: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued National Early Warning Platform alerts of a potential danger for Jazan Province, Najran Province and Khamis Mushait Governorate between about 4:04 and 4:06 AM ET Nov. 18. It declared the danger passed in all three between about 4:19 and 4:21 AM ET, and Reuters reported the all-clear. The alerts did not say what the threat was; they came amid continuing Houthi missile and drone fire at Saudi Arabia.
Middle East.status: All-clear issued; no impacts, damage or casualties reported as of about 5:00 AM ET; cause of the alerts not stated; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council issues a law designating the Houthis a terrorist organization
Middle East.location: Yemen
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English reports that Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council chairman Rashad al-Alimi issued a law designating the Iran-backed Houthi movement a terrorist organization. Under the law, anyone working for the Houthis or supporting them in word, deed, money or moral support is classified as a terrorist.
Middle East.status: Reported about 4:40 AM ET Nov. 18; no Houthi response found yet; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iran's army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone and missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait
Middle East.location: Ali Al Salem Air Base, Kuwait
Middle East.summary: Iran's regular army (Artesh) public relations office announced that in the early hours of Wednesday, Nov. 18 (Iran time), its combat and suicide drones targeted US Patriot air defense systems and US drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, according to Iran's state Press TV, Al Jazeera's breaking-news channel and Iran International. This is the first formal Iranian military claim of responsibility linked to the drone attacks Kuwait's armed forces reported engaging since about 4:39 PM ET Nov. 17. Relays of the statement quote the army warning that any response to aggression will be decisive and without geographical limits.
Middle East.status: Iranian military claim, published about 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17. No US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation of a hit, damage or casualties found as of about 11:10 PM ET; Kuwait has not named the attacker. Claim of targeting, not a confirmed hit; About 11:20–11:50 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's official IRNA English service carries the army statement claiming its drones struck Patriot air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Base; Al Jazeera English and Drop Site News report the claim, noting Iran's army is separate from the IRGC and that there was no immediate word on damage or casualties. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18. Remains an Iranian military claim; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Iranian and Arabic-language outlets (Press TV, IRNA, Al Jazeera Arabic, Al-Masirah) continue to repeat the army statement, and Press TV now headlines it as drones 'strike' US air defense systems at Ali Al Salem. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement on the attack found (KUNA's latest posts are routine). Remains an Iranian military claim; As of about 2:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry now officially blames Iran for repeated attacks on its territory, including drones earlier in the day (see the Kuwait item), but neither Kuwait nor the US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) has confirmed or denied that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit; no damage or casualty reports found. Press TV and Arabic/Persian outlets continue to repeat the army statement. Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; claims of US casualties rest on IRGC-affiliated channels and flight-tracking inferences only. Iran's army chief Amir Hatami said Wednesday the enemy is preparing its forces and any mistake would draw a stronger, more crushing response (Press TV, Iran International). Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 4:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found. The C-17 medevac-callsign flight from Ramstein and Iranian-sourced casualty claims remain unconfirmed by any US official. Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 5:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found. Iranian-sourced claims of US casualties and the C-17 medevac-callsign flight remain unconfirmed by any US official; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Arabic and Persian outlets keep re-running the Iranian army statement; still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; As of about 7:00 AM ET Nov. 18: outlets and relays continue to repeat the Iranian army claim; still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; About 7:45 AM ET Nov. 18: ABC News, citing Iranian state media, reports Iran's army chief warned Tehran 'will respond more forcefully and severely, without geographical limitations,' if the US military takes action again. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; About 12:34 PM ET Nov. 18: CENTCOM says online claims that US personnel were recently injured by Iranian attacks and needed medical evacuation are 'FALSE': no US personnel have been injured in any attempted Iranian attacks this week, all American service members are safe and accounted for, and IRGC-aligned accounts regularly spread false narratives (also posted by CENTCOM Arabic). CENTCOM did not say whether anything at Ali Al Salem was hit; no Kuwaiti damage report found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Kuwait's armed forces say air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks over Kuwait, hours after the US strike on Qeshm; attacker not officially named
Middle East.location: Kuwait (hosts major US bases incl. Camp Arifjan and Ali Al Salem)
Middle East.summary: Kuwait's state news agency KUNA reported about 4:46 PM ET Nov. 17 that the General Staff of the Kuwaiti Armed Forces announced its air defenses were actively engaging drone threats and urged the public to stay calm and follow safety instructions; the army said any explosions heard are interceptions. TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) cites Arabic sources reporting several explosions in Kuwait and says air-raid sirens sounded at US bases there — a claim. It comes hours after the US self-defense strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island (see Qeshm item).
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Kuwaiti military confirms an ongoing drone attack and interceptions; origin of the drones NOT officially confirmed (many accounts say Iranian drones, and some relays say the army named Iran, but the KUNA statement checked does not); no IRGC claim of responsibility, CENTCOM statement, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked. Unverified/not logged: claims of 5 IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site, claims of new attacks on US bases in Bahrain; Nov. 17, about 4:39 PM ET: the Kuwaiti Army General Staff's own account posted the statement that air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks and that any explosions heard are interceptions (no origin named). About 5:30–5:56 PM ET: Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) claims, citing local and Arab sources, renewed explosions in Kuwait and a video of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait; journalist Wladimir van Wilgenburg notes the Iraqi channel Naya claimed a US base in Kuwait was targeted with drones — all claims, unconfirmed. As of about 6:00 PM ET: still no formal IRGC statement claiming the attack found, no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties, and Kuwait has not named the attacker. Viral 'direct hit on US base' videos and lists of bases hit come from low-credibility accounts and are not logged; As of about 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: still no Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage/casualties, no new Kuwait Army or KUNA posts since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET statements, and no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Arabic relay accounts say the IRGC announced it targeted US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain in response to the Qeshm strike, but no Tasnim, Fars or Sepah News primary was found, so this is not treated as a formal IRGC claim. FaytuksNetwork relays a BNews claim that drones targeted Al-Jahra and Ali Al Salem (unverified). Ignored: 'six US bases hit', 'US troops in Kuwaiti hospitals' and 'Operation Nasr 2' claims (no primary); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET posts; the Arabic posts circulating around 7:40–7:50 PM ET re-quote that statement. Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties, and there is no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Iranian outlets (Defa Press, a Tasnim-branded account) report explosions in Kuwait and a drone attack on US positions citing 'Arab' or 'Iraqi' sources — media claims, not a formal IRGC statement. Ignored: 'missile swarm struck a major US installation' and lists of US bases hit (no primary); As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement since 4:39–4:46 PM ET; Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on Kuwait and no formal IRGC claim. Iranian outlets (Defa Press) repeat claims of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait citing 'Arab media' — unverified, not logged; As of about 9:55 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement on the drones since 4:39–4:46 PM ET; Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait and no formal IRGC claim found. Arabic claims of suicide drones hitting Ali Al Salem/Camp Arifjan remain unverified and are not logged; About 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's regular army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone/missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait in the early hours of Wednesday Iran time (see separate HIGH item). Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement since 4:39–4:46 PM ET and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found as of about 11:10 PM ET; About 11:33 PM ET Nov. 17: AFP reports Gulf nations on alert after the US strike on Qeshm, with Kuwait saying it is countering 'hostile drone attacks' and Bahrain saying its air defenses intercepted attacks from Iran. No new Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage or casualties, and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement naming the attacker or reporting damage or casualties, and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found; About 1:20–1:50 AM ET Nov. 18: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry, via the state news agency KUNA, condemned 'in the strongest terms' the repeated Iranian attacks on Kuwaiti territory, 'the latest of which involved drones earlier in the day,' saying they flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, international law, the UN Charter and UN Security Council Resolution 2817. Iran International reports the ministry said Kuwait reserves the right to take necessary measures, including self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. This is the first official Kuwaiti statement attributing the drone attacks to Iran found in posts checked. Still no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties; About 2:40–3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: the UAE (via state news agency WAM) strongly condemned the 'hostile attack' on Kuwait, and Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Kuwait and Bahrain as violations of both countries' sovereignty and international law, warning that continued attacks risk escalation and undermine diplomatic efforts. Al Jazeera English also reports Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called Iran's drone attack a 'direct threat to its security and stability'. Still no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking OSINT posts about a US Air Force C-17 medical-evacuation flight leaving Ramstein for the Middle East are being cited online as evidence of US casualties; no US official confirmation of casualties found, and this is not treated as confirmed; About 3:35 AM ET Nov. 18: UAE state news agency WAM headlines the UAE's condemnation as a 'hostile Iranian attack on Kuwait', naming Iran. As of about 4:00 AM ET: still no new Kuwaiti General Staff statement and no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking posts about the US Air Force C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) flying from Ramstein toward the Middle East keep circulating, along with claims attributed to a source close to Iran's parliament speaker that US troops were killed or wounded; no US official confirmation of any casualties found, and neither is treated as confirmed; About 4:52 AM ET Nov. 18: Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry, via the Saudi Press Agency, condemns 'in the strongest terms' the Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain and the attack on a UAE oil tanker, and calls on Iran to stop its attacks and allow diplomatic efforts to proceed. As of about 5:00 AM ET: still no new Kuwaiti General Staff statement and no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking posts about the US Air Force C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) flying from Ramstein toward the Middle East and claims attributed to a source close to Iran's parliament speaker that US troops were killed or wounded keep circulating; the Pentagon has not confirmed any casualties, and neither is treated as confirmed; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement on the attack since the earlier ones (the General Staff and KUNA accounts posted only routine items after 5:00 AM ET), and no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Claims of US casualties attributed to a source close to Iran's parliament speaker and flight-tracking posts about the C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) from Ramstein keep circulating; no US official has confirmed any casualties; As of about 7:00 AM ET Nov. 18: the Wall Street Journal, CBS News and AFP report Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain early Wednesday (Gulf time) and that both countries say they intercepted the incoming weapons; these reports describe the same overnight attacks, not a new wave. Still no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement on damage or casualties (the KUNA accounts posted only routine items after 6:00 AM ET), and no CENTCOM statement found. Claims of US casualties tied to the C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) medevac flight from Ramstein are still only relays and an unnamed Iranian source; no US official has confirmed any casualties; As of about 8:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain's state news agency says Bahrain condemned the renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait (about 7:41 AM ET). Kuwait's General Staff and KUNA posted only routine items in the past hour (a defense minister tour of military sites; condemnation calls); still no Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties and no CENTCOM statement found. Claims of US casualties (C-17 callsign BNDGE01) remain unconfirmed by any US official; As of about 9:00 AM ET Nov. 18: KUNA reports Saudi Arabia condemned Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain and the attack on an Emirati oil tanker (about 7:31 AM ET; Al Jazeera English carried the Saudi Foreign Ministry condemnation about 8:40 AM ET), and the Arab Parliament denounced the 'Iranian aggressions' on Kuwait (about 8:29 AM ET). Kuwait's General Staff posted only a defense minister tour of military sites; still no Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties and no CENTCOM statement found in posts checked. Claims of US casualties (C-17 callsign BNDGE01) remain unconfirmed by any US official; About 12:34 PM ET Nov. 18: CENTCOM says no US personnel were injured in any attempted Iranian attacks this week and calls US casualty/medevac claims false (see the Ali Al Salem item); carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found
