Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: ADNOC Logistics & Services says one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 17; 11 crew injured and one missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: ADNOC Logistics & Services, a unit of the UAE's state oil company, says one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of Nov. 17, 2026, according to The National, WAM, Khaleej Times, Arab News and Al Arabiya English. The company says 11 crew members were injured and are receiving medical care, one crew member is unaccounted for with search and rescue under way, and all other crew were evacuated from the vessel. The company statement as reported does not name the vessel or the attacker; it is not confirmed whether this is one of the tankers Iran's IRGC/navy claimed hit naval mines on Nov. 17.
Middle East.status: Company confirmation carried by UAE state news agency WAM and established outlets, about 1:30–2:00 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker and vessel not identified; one crew member missing; watch for UKMTO notice, vessel name, UAE government statement and any claim of responsibility; About 7:41 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain's state news agency says Bahrain condemned the attack on a vessel belonging to the UAE's ADNOC in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, India's shipping minister says the tanker NAVIG8 MESSI was hit by a projectile on Nov. 18 (logged separately); maritime analysts link that ship to an ADNOC press note, but ADNOC has not named the vessel in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile fired toward the Riyadh region
Middle East.location: Riyadh region, Saudi Arabia
Middle East.summary: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the coalition intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed Houthis toward the Riyadh region, Iran International reports, and the Saudi Press Agency carried the coalition statement. It comes hours after Iran's army claimed a drone attack on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and amid the ongoing Saudi-Houthi exchanges already in this log.
Middle East.status: Coalition statement late Nov. 17 ET (SPA about 12:03 AM ET Nov. 18). No reports of damage or casualties found; no Houthi claim found as of about 12:05 AM ET; About 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Anadolu Agency reports coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki confirms the Houthis launched the cruise missile and coalition forces destroyed it. Still no reports of damage or casualties and no Houthi claim found; About 4:06 AM ET Nov. 18: the Saudi Press Agency's regional account again carried a coalition statement that a Houthi cruise missile fired toward the Riyadh region was intercepted and destroyed; it is not clear from the post whether this is a second missile or a repeat of the earlier statement. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO 208-26: LPG tanker TARA GAS struck a second time off Khasab; crew abandoned ship, one Indian seafarer missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman

Analyst Noam Raydan, citing Vanguard, identifies the vessel (IMO 9290270) as disabled with an engine-room fire and says at least 17 ship attacks have been reported in November. Attacker still not identified in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:40 to 4:05 AM ET: OSINT accounts post images of a large smoke column still rising Tuesday morning from the tanker struck about 13 km north of Khasab (unverified). Hindustan Times reports India's minister says all 24 Indian seafarers are safe. Iranian outlets relay an IRGC Navy claim of an explosion on a fourth tanker in 24 hours; no UKMTO warning beyond 208-26 found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:17 to 4:46 AM ET: UKMTO issued update 001 to warning 208-26. This conflicts with India's earlier statement that all crew were safe (that statement preceded the second strike). Attacker not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 5:02 to 5:40 AM ET: India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said TARA GAS, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and the whole 25-member crew was safe. In an update he says the tanker was attacked again, forcing the entire crew to abandon ship; 24 crew are safely accounted for and one Indian seafarer is missing, and India is coordinating with the ship manager and regional rescue authorities. No US Navy involvement and no new UKMTO notice found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:03 AM ET: India's embassy in Muscat says 24 of the 25 crew of the Panama-flagged VLGC TARA GAS (24 of them Indian) have been evacuated ashore at Khasab and search-and-rescue operations continue for one missing Indian crew member, with Omani support; Nov. 17, about 8:55 AM ET: India strongly condemns the attack on MT TARA GAS; 21 Indian nationals were evacuated, two injured crew are hospitalised and one remains missing, with India's MEA coordinating with Omani authorities on search and rescue (as reported by News18); Nov. 17, about 10:46 AM ET: summarizing Indian officials, OSINTdefender says India confirmed the second attack on TARA GAS; Shipping Minister Sonowal says the crew abandoned the vessel, 24 of 25 are accounted for and one Indian seafarer is still missing. India's Ministry of External Affairs says two injured Indian crew are in hospital and the rest were evacuated ashore at Khasab, Oman. Attacker still not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 3:24–3:57 PM ET: The National reports India's Foreign Ministry confirmed 21 crew were safely evacuated, two hospitalized and one unaccounted for; Drop Site, citing Maritime Executive, says the abandoned carrier is at risk of exploding (Indian officials say a missile hit it, Maritime Executive says an IRGC drone, Iranian media say a mine); Sky News shows footage of the abandoned tanker engulfed in flames off Khasab; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. Middle East.summary: Rudaw reports that Iran on Nov. 17 launched a suicide drone at positions of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group, in the Kurdistan Region, according to the group's spokesperson; it came a day after two missiles targeted another opposition group in the Region. Middle East.location: Qeshm Island, Strait of Hormuz, Iran
Middle East.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Saturday it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Diario de Centro América reports. IEW Latest News relays CBS News reporting that this is the second straight day Iran has made such a claim.
Middle East.status: Iranian claim relayed by media; no US military confirmation found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: Al Mayadeen reports the IRGC now claims it took control of a ninth US MQM-170 drone over Qeshm; IRGC claim only, no US confirmation found; Nov. 17, about 5:42 to 5:50 AM ET: Al Jazeera and Roya News relay a new IRGC statement that its air defenses shot down a drone south of Qeshm Island. Middle East.location: Jaramana, Rif Dimashq (Damascus countryside), Syria
Middle East.summary: An explosive device planted inside a car detonated in Jaramana, a mainly Druze and Christian suburb southeast of Damascus, on the evening of Nov. 14. Middle East.summary: Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia warned commercial vessels 'not to be fooled' into taking 'fake American routes' in the Strait of Hormuz, citing the threat of 'sea mines, fire and explosion,' Al Jazeera English reports.
Middle East.status: Official Iranian warning reported by Al Jazeera; no new incident tied to it found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Loud explosion heard in Ahvaz, Iran; Khuzestan official says it was a controlled destruction of munitions
Middle East.location: Ahvaz, Khuzestan province, Iran
Middle East.summary: Residents and OSINT accounts reported a very loud explosion in Ahvaz at about 3:40 AM ET. Iranian outlets quote Khuzestan's deputy governor for security affairs as saying the sound came from a controlled operation to destroy munitions.
Middle East.status: Official Iranian explanation only; no independent confirmation of the cause and no casualty reports found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Raaz News on X: deputy governor explanation

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani reportedly in Baghdad to contain Iraq–Kataib Hezbollah tensions
Middle East.location: Baghdad, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reports that IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani led an Iranian delegation that arrived in Baghdad on Monday and met Iraqi officials and leaders of armed factions. The sources say the visit aims to ease tensions between the Iraqi government and Kataib Hezbollah, which Baghdad has given a deadline to leave Jurf al-Sakhar.
Middle East.status: Single outlet citing unnamed sources; no Iranian or Iraqi official confirmation found in posts checked; linked to the Jurf al-Sakhar standoff item; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:47 AM ET: Amwaj.media reports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has given Kataib Hezbollah only days to hand over Jurf al-Sakhar, its stronghold south of Baghdad; footage shared on X shows Iraqi military reinforcements near Jurf al-Sakhar. Qaani visit still single-source; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Al Arabiya English on X: details

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sanaa, Yemen: three near the al-Hafa camp and a fourth at Jabal Nuqm
Middle East.location: Sanaa, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya and Al Hadath, citing sources in Sanaa, report three explosions near the al-Hafa military camp and a fourth at Jabal Nuqm on Tuesday afternoon local time; residents quoted by Ain Yemen describe violent blasts shaking the capital. The cause is not known: no claim, no strike announcement and no Houthi statement found in posts checked. Earlier on Nov. 17 Houthi-run media reported Saudi airstrikes on northern Sanaa (see separate item)
Middle East.status: Early reports citing unnamed sources and residents, about 5:45 to 5:56 AM ET; cause and casualties unknown; Nov. 17, about 6:18 AM ET: Al Arabiya English, citing governorate sources, adds that explosions were heard at several Houthi barracks in Bani Jarmuz (Bani al-Harith district) following airstrikes on fortifications, tunnels and weapons depots. No coalition, US or Israeli statement and no Houthi casualty report found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Qatar says it will meet Iranian officials Tuesday as part of ongoing US–Iran mediation
Middle East.location: Doha, Qatar
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English reports Qatar says it will hold a meeting with Iranian officials on Tuesday, Nov. 17, as part of ongoing mediation efforts. This comes amid the Bahrain drone attack, the Hormuz tanker strikes and the DC threat reporting
Middle East.status: Diplomatic signal; single outlet relay of a Qatari statement, about 5:27 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 7:03 AM ET: Independent Persian, citing Tasnim, reports Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Muscat to discuss regional developments; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: US sanctions a Quds Force–Hezbollah gold and cash smuggling network in Lebanon and Turkey
Middle East.location: Lebanon / Turkey (US Treasury and State Department action)
Middle East.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned members of a gold and cash smuggling network it says is run by Iran's IRGC Quds Force and Hezbollah in Lebanon and Turkey to move Iranian funds to Hezbollah (Iran International). The State Department also announced sanctions on a Hezbollah front organization and an Iran-backed financial network (Al Arabiya). Treasury Secretary Bessent said Washington will keep targeting Iran's financing of its regional proxies.
Middle East.status: Announced Nov. 18 (posts about 1:22–1:48 PM ET); a sanctions action, not an attack

Middle East.title: NEW: Unconfirmed reports of air defense activity over Omidiyeh in Iran's Khuzestan province
Middle East.location: Omidiyeh, Khuzestan province, Iran
Middle East.summary: OSINT accounts report Iranian air defenses were active over Omidiyeh after an unidentified aircraft was spotted (Osint613, about 1:44 PM ET; osinthexagone, about 1:03 PM ET). No Iranian official or state-media statement and no US or Israeli statement found; cause unknown.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed as of about 2:00 PM ET Nov. 18; OSINT reports only

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight raid on Janju village on Kenya's Garissa–Isiolo border reportedly kills several people, including a mother and her baby
Africa.summary: Local outlets report an overnight raid on a settlement at Janju village along the Garissa–Isiolo county border. Brina TV puts the overnight death toll at four, including a mother and her child, and says livestock was stolen; Somali Breaking News says the toll has reached eight, including a 14-day-old baby, and blames Borana (Oromo) raiders. The area has seen recent inter-community clashes.
Africa.status: Death toll differs between reports (four vs. eight); separate claims of 11 killed are unverified; no Kenyan police or government statement found as of about 5:00 AM ET Nov. 18; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: posts widely shared in Kenya put the toll at eight, including a 14-day-old baby, its mother and a 10-year-old; still no Kenyan police or government statement found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least nine in an attack on Zuwakal (Zuwagal) village, Mangu, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zuwakal village, Jipal District, Mangu LGA, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Security-focused outlet Zagazola Makama reports that suspected armed herders killed at least eight residents, including men, women and children, burned houses and stole 18 cattle in an attack on Zuwakal village about 11:45 p.m. on Nov. 15. Troops of Operation Enduring Peace responded and recovered eight bodies; the attackers fled toward Nasarawa State.
Africa.status: Single security-source report published Nov. 17; no police or army statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:27 PM ET: the Mwaghavul Development Association says gunmen killed at least nine people in Zuwagal (Zuwakal), Mangu, days after a curfew was lifted; houses and food also destroyed in nearby Bong. Still no police or army statement found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Zagazola Makama on X: eight killed, houses burnt and 18 cattle rustled in an attack on a Mangu community, Plateau

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Troops thwart a suspected Boko Haram attack on Nigerian Senate chief whip Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa, Borno State
Africa.summary: Vanguard reports that Senate Chief Whip Monguno and others escaped a suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. Details on casualties and the location of the attack were not in the post checked.
Africa.status: Single-outlet report (Vanguard) about 10:30 AM ET Nov. 17; no military or police statement found; Nov. 17, about 12:16 PM ET: Iwere News, citing local outlet Yerwa News Express, says Operation Hadin Kai troops thwarted the attempted attack on Senate Chief Whip Mohammed Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa LGA on Monday, when suspected Boko Haram fighters fired three mortar bombs toward the town while he was there with former governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan and APC leaders; no casualties reported. No official army statement seen on X; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Iwere News on X: Operation Hadin Kai soldiers thwart attempted Boko Haram attack on Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa
Vanguard News on X: Senate chief whip Monguno, others escape suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Plateau State, Nigeria — gunmen kill an Operation Rainbow security commander and another person after fresh attacks kill five in three communities
Africa.location: Bokkos, Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi areas, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Premium Times reports gunmen killed a Plateau State security commander and one other person; other reports say the Operation Rainbow commander was ambushed near Bokkos returning from a condolence visit. Punch separately reports at least five people killed in fresh attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas.
Africa.status: Developing; no police or state government casualty figure found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Market shooting in South Sudan reportedly kills 17 and wounds 23, Afropages says
Africa.location: South Sudan (market, location not specified in the post)
Africa.summary: Afropages reports that a shooting in a market in South Sudan killed 17 people and wounded 23. Mwanzo TV posted a headline saying 17 were killed in a South Sudan revenge attack. The exact location, date of the shooting and official confirmation were not given in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early, thinly sourced reports; location and official confirmation lacking; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kordofan Human Rights Observatory says a drone strike on Abu Qalb, West Kordofan, killed at least 15 civilians, including four children
Africa.summary: Radio Dabanga reports that at least 15 civilians, including four children, were killed in a drone strike on Abu Qalb in West Kordofan, according to the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory. The attacker was not identified in the post checked, and no official confirmation was seen.
Africa.status: Single rights-group report via Radio Dabanga; unconfirmed by official sources in this sweep; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Explosion and fire at an NNPC filling station in Ipaja, Lagos, spread to a neighboring school building
Africa.location: Command / Ajasa-Command area, Ipaja, Lagos State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: The Guardian Nigeria says an explosion at a filling station in the Ajasa-Command area of Ipaja triggered a fire, and that the cause and extent of damage are not yet known. WithinNigeria and other local accounts say the fire spread to a school building next to the station. One account says it happened during school hours and that everyone was reportedly safe; no casualties have been confirmed officially in posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports from several Nigerian outlets; cause and casualties unconfirmed; no official emergency agency statement seen; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Sun Nigeria and Instablog9ja say the fire spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School near Savannah Bus Stop in the Command/Ipaja area; firefighters contained the blaze and no casualties were reported in the posts checked. The earlier Guardian Nigeria post used in the prior entry no longer resolves; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Drone or air strike on a village in Abu Zabad, West Kordofan, Sudan, reported to kill 13 to 15 people, including children
Africa.location: Abu Qalb area, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, Sudan
Africa.summary: CGTN Europe quotes the Emergency Lawyers group as saying an airstrike on the Abu Qalb area of Abu Zabad locality killed 13 women and children, according to preliminary figures. News Central TV reports 15 people, including four children, were killed in a Sudanese military drone strike on a West Kordofan village. The Sudanese army had not commented in posts checked.
Africa.status: Reported by two outlets citing a rights group; tolls differ (13 vs 15); attribution to the army not confirmed by the military; Nov. 17, about 5:15 to 5:27 AM ET: The Sudan Doctors Network says a Sudanese army drone struck Abu Qulb in Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, killing at least 13 civilians and injuring others, and calls for an independent investigation (CGTN Europe). KUNA reports the UN Human Rights Office says more than 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan from January to the end of October 2026, more than 1,630 of them in drone strikes; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Middle East Just Now on X
KUNA on X: UN civilian death toll

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Bomb threat on Sandton Drive, Johannesburg: all-clear given and roads reopened
Africa.location: Sandton Drive near Alice Lane, Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa
Africa.summary: The Citizen reports law enforcement on the scene of a bomb threat in Sandton, and other accounts tell people to avoid Sandton Drive near Alice Lane. No device, evacuation scale or injuries were reported in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports; one established outlet; no police statement found in posts checked; Nov. 16: All-clear given about 15:46 local time per a community security update relaying the Gauteng JOC; eNCA reports the area around Sandton Drive and Alice Lane has reopened; News24 says the threat targeted an office building; no device or injuries reported; resolved, can drop from monitoring; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Two weekend mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 17 dead — nine in Jeffsville near Pretoria and eight in a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg
Africa.location: Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says nine people, six men and three women, were found shot dead inside a four-roomed shack in Jeffsville informal settlement. Police say the shooting is reported to have happened between 10 and 11 p.m. on Nov. 15 and that they were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Nov. 16. The motive has not been established and no arrests have been made; Yfm reports a manhunt is under way and SABC says the Gauteng police commissioner is at the scene.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; comes hours after the separate Sweetwaters (KZN) shooting that killed eight; Nov. 16: Channels TV says police put the toll from the Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters shootings at 17; Newzroom Afrika and Sowetan carry Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni saying one of the nine victims was a person of interest in a December 2025 mass shooting and linking the case to the Saulsville shooting; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: WPLG says at least 17 were killed in the two mass shootings about 330 miles apart and police have not established motives; Pretoria News says SAPS is probing a possible retaliation motive after confirming one victim was a person of interest in the Saulsville case (also EWN); eNCA reports Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi's condolences; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: Reuters, NBC News, Al Jazeera and BBC report at least 17 dead in two weekend mass shootings: nine in the shack near Pretoria and eight men found in a bullet-riddled vehicle near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal; police say motives not yet established and no arrests reported; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: SABC News on X (commissioner at scene)

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight people shot dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters outside Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.location: Mabane Section, Sweetwaters, Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says KwaZulu-Natal police are investigating the murder of eight people who were allegedly shot and killed inside a vehicle along the road at Mabane Section in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg. Daily News reports the eight men were killed on Sunday evening and that a murder investigation is under way. No motive or arrests have been announced.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Peter Obi condemns a reported attack on Kwankwaso's NDC convoy in Bichi, Kano State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Opposition presidential candidate Peter Obi says he is saddened by reports of an attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area. He calls for an immediate investigation and arrests. Kwankwaso had been commissioning NDC offices across Kano State on Sunday.
Africa.status: Early reports; party-side statement only; no police statement, casualty count or damage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya opens probe into violent protests at the Dadaab refugee complex
Africa.location: Hagadera camp, Dadaab, Garissa County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Anadolu reports that Kenyan authorities have opened an investigation after protesters opposing a planned market in Hagadera camp damaged government offices, stole equipment and broke into nearby businesses during clashes.
Africa.status: Single wire report citing authorities; casualty figures not reported; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. It cites Caasimada Online as saying forces loyal to a former South West state leader took Golweyn.
Africa.status: Single-source early report citing Caasimada Online; no official statement or claim of responsibility found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: JNIM reportedly overruns a national police detachment at Balga, near Fada N'Gourma, eastern Burkina Faso
Africa.location: Balga, about 25 km from Fada N’Gourma, Est region, Burkina Faso
Africa.summary: A Sahel-focused account reports that a JNIM attack on the morning of Nov. 15 targeted the National Police detachment at Balga, sacking and burning it, and that many officers were killed and several are missing. It adds that the attackers took all weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no official Burkinabe statement or casualty figure found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill a Zamfara governor's aide in a dawn attack in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits attacked worshippers at dawn prayer in Kaura Namoda on Sunday, Nov. 15, killing Nasiru Sani Kaura and abducting several others, according to the security platform Bakatsine (via Africa_lix). Nigerians_New reports he was an aide to Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal.
Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Post on X citing Eye Radio

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 1:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Reuters Africa on X: attacks hinder Ebola response

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source
Africa.summary: A post circulating an Eritrean Ministry of Information editorial quotes it saying Eritreans and their army are ready to answer "Prosperity's invasion" in the language it has chosen. threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. Still threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 17, about 5:48 AM ET: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the 'dirty bomb' allegations, attributed to the New York Times and spread by CNN, completely baseless and says enemies are trying to legitimize new aggression (Al Mayadeen). Apple's official system status page lists an ongoing 'iCloud Account & Sign In' issue ('This service may be slow or unavailable') that began at 8:45 AM PT (11:45 AM ET); as of about 1:00 PM ET no other Apple service, including Apple Pay, Wallet and the App Store, showed an event. Google's Workspace Status Dashboard shows no incident on Nov. 17, and no @MSFT365Status post about a new incident was found. Reuters reports President Trump shrugged off the spate of US outages, saying 'things like that happen'.
America.status: Apple confirms only the iCloud sign-in issue; other services rest on user reports and Downdetector spikes; cause unknown; no evidence of a cyberattack (posts tying this to the FAA, NSA and bank outages as a coordinated attack are unsupported and not logged); consumer services, not critical infrastructure. Re-check Apple status, MSFT365Status, Google dashboard and Downdetector; Nov. 17, about 1:11 PM ET: Al Arabiya English reports Downdetector user reports of problems with iCloud, Apple Pay, the Apple Store, App Store and Apple Business Manager. Apple's system status page checked at 2:03 PM ET lists 'iCloud Account & Sign In' as an ongoing issue since 08:45 PST, 'AppleCare on Device' purchases temporarily unavailable since 08:15 PST, and Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork as possibly slow or unavailable since 10:40 PST (1:40 PM ET); Apple Pay, App Store and Apple Music show no issue. Google's Workspace status feed shows no Nov. 17 incident. No evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 2:50 PM ET: an Apple spokesperson says many of its systems are back up after an internal update caused some outages this morning and it is working to restore the remaining systems. Apple's status page checked at 3:01 PM ET: iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, Apple Business, Apple School Manager, Schoolwork and AppleCare on Device still ongoing; App Store and Volume Purchase Program issues ongoing since 11:27 PST; iCloud Mail resolved. Apple attributes the disruption to an internal update; no evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 3:10 PM ET: NBC News reports Apple said it was having tech issues affecting several consumer services. Apple's status page checked at 3:58 PM ET: App Store and Volume Purchase Program issues resolved (ended 12:00 PST), AppleCare on Device resolved (12:39 PST); iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork still listed as ongoing. Apple attributes the disruption to an internal update; no evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 4:15 PM ET: Fox News reports Apple is ruling out a cyberattack, saying an internal update triggered the disruptions and most services are restored. Apple's status page checked at about 5:03 PM ET: iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, iCloud Mail and Schoolwork now resolved; Apple Business and Apple School Manager still ongoing, and a new intermittent Volume Purchase Program issue listed (from 1:11 PM PST). Largely stabilized; About 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: CBS News reports Apple has restored services after an internal update caused the outages. Resolved; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: NSA's classified internal communications network (NSA Net) is down, CNN reports; sources say no evidence of a cyberattack
America.location: National Security Agency, Fort Meade, Maryland, United States
America.summary: CNN, citing six people familiar with the matter, reports that NSA Net, the highly classified network the National Security Agency uses for internal communications, is down. Sources told CNN there is no evidence of a cyberattack so far, and accounts summarizing the report say the agency staggered employee arrivals while it works out the scope of the outage. CNN says it has asked the NSA for comment. The outage follows the week's FAA, United, banking and Microsoft disruptions already in this log, none of which has been tied to a cyberattack.
America.status: Reported by CNN about 10:38 AM ET Nov. 17; cause unknown; no NSA statement found in posts checked as of about 11:10 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 11:30 AM–12:00 PM ET: Reuters reports a US official saying the recent run of tech problems is not tied to cyberattacks, and The Epoch Times says its own source confirms the NSA Net outage. No NSA statement on cause or restoration found as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:03–12:05 PM ET: Fox News (relayed by Walter Bloomberg) reports the outage is intermittent, critical communications remain intact and it appears technical; The Wall Street Journal (relayed) reports US officials say NSANet is temporarily offline because of a software update, not a cyberattack, and that DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the US is not under cyberattack. Still no NSA statement on cause or restoration found as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 1:14 PM ET: CBS News, citing multiple US officials, reports the NSA's internal classified network went offline Tuesday, prompting the agency to stagger arrival times for some personnel at Fort Meade. About 1:57 PM ET: Al Jazeera, citing CNN and a US official, reports the outage will not prevent urgent intelligence from reaching President Trump in Asia. Still no NSA statement and no evidence of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17, about 2:44–2:49 PM ET: Senate Majority Leader Thune says on the tech outages that 'a lot of bad actors' would love to damage the US; Al Jazeera reports the top House Democrat said it is not clear whether the outages are tied to infrastructure or malicious activity and that Congress needs a briefing. Still no NSA statement on cause or restoration; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:47 PM ET: Reuters reports a US official says the recent tech problems are not tied to cyberattacks; Director of National Intelligence Clayton tells Fox Business he is not seeing the outages as a cyberattack incident and that many institutions are patching or upgrading systems. Still no NSA statement on cause or restoration; Nov. 17, about 4:00–5:00 PM ET: Reuters reports the NSA says its classified national security communications network was hit by an outage; The Hill reports the agency describes the cause as 'routine maintenance'. Reuters: as the string of tech outages raises alarm, President Trump says everything is 'fine'. No evidence of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17, about 4:56 PM ET: the White House posts DNI Jay Clayton saying 'This is not a cyberattack and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation-state' about the string of outages. Still no NSA statement on restoration found; About 9:10 PM ET Nov. 17: Reuters reports the week's technology outages 'extended to the US National Security Agency' as the Trump administration downplayed concerns about a broader problem. No NSA statement on full restoration found; About 11:10 PM ET Nov. 17: Firstpost quotes the NSA statement: the agency 'experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance' and, while some internal systems were affected, 'mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational.' No NSA statement on full restoration found as of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18; ABC News reports Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said Tuesday that the technical issues affecting the NSA and other areas are not the result of a cyberattack or state-sponsored activity. No NSA statement on full restoration found as of about 4:00 AM ET Nov. 18; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)
America.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme reported malicious JavaScript being served through the Optimizely web experimentation platform to the websites of about 178 organizations, including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax and Ledger. He and security firm Coinspect say the payload included a crypto address swapper, a card skimmer, cookie theft and iOS exploit code; Helme says about $7,000 in crypto had been diverted. Optimizely says it identified and contained a security incident affecting some Web Experimentation customers, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the injected code and contacted customers. BleepingComputer reports the attack.
America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known; Nov. 17: Optimizely's notice says an 'unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation' (Infosecurity Magazine). Reuters (via the New York Post, about 9:30 AM ET) cites researcher Scott Helme and says it could not independently establish whether every affected site was successfully exploited; AFP (about 12:45 PM ET) says nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted. Report URI names the iOS exploit kits as Coruna and DarkSword and advises updating to iOS 18.7.3+ or 26.3+; Mediaite, citing Reuters, says Salesforce disabled the scripts, Equifax stopped using the platform and found no compromise, and IKEA is investigating. Report URI says all infected files were clean by 23:11 UTC Nov. 16 (6:11 PM ET). STABILIZED: contained; moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Peoria, Illinois — FBI arrests and a grand jury indicts a man over the emailed bomb threat to the BioUrja ethanol plant; evacuation order lifted earlier
America.location: Peoria and East Peoria, Illinois, US
America.summary: Peoria police ordered a mandatory evacuation within about one mile of the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant (the former ADM plant) after a bomb threat on Friday, the Peoria Journal Star reports. WCIA reports officials said there is a bomb, with Homeland Security monitoring, the Coast Guard holding river traffic, bridges shut and downtown businesses closed. Lookner, relaying Peoria Police, says bomb technicians rendered a suspicious package safe around 9:12 PM CT and that it had been determined to be a threat; the search was not complete and the evacuation order was still in effect.
America.status: Official all-clear relayed: CBS News reports the evacuation order was lifted Saturday and residents allowed home; KMOX reports the Coast Guard reopened the river and that Saturday's searches were negative after one bomb was found Friday; suspect and motive not stated. Situation has stabilized; can move to routine coverage; WPXI and other Hearst stations report police lifted the evacuation after a bomb was found near the ethanol plant; Nov. 16: CBS Chicago says Peoria police report a person is in custody in connection with the bomb threat and explosive device found at the ethanol plant; Nov. 16: NewsNation and WCCB say Peoria Mayor Rita Ali said a suspect is in custody in connection with the bomb found at the BioUrja ethanol plant; EODWX5 says Peoria police retracted their statement that a person of interest was taken into custody and that the FBI continues to lead the investigation. Custody status is conflicting in posts checked; Nov. 16, about 11:00 PM ET: Mario Nawfal, citing NBC Chicago, reports federal authorities say a 10-month trainee at the plant named Kozak was arrested for allegedly leaving the device and sending the bomb threat. This clears up the earlier conflicting custody reports, but it comes through a relay of NBC Chicago, not an official post. Evacuation remains lifted; stabilized; Nov. 17, about 1:29–1:30 PM ET: KPLR 11 reports an Illinois man has been indicted over the Peoria ethanol-plant bomb threat; a watch-floor account citing CBS News and NBC Chicago names him as Andrew M. Kozak, charged with one count of threats regarding explosives and one count of interstate communications. Stabilized; About 6:14 PM ET Nov. 17: FBI Director Kash Patel says the FBI arrested one person who allegedly sent the Nov. 13 email claiming explosive devices had been placed at the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant, and that a grand jury indicted him today on charges including making threatening interstate communications and threatening to damage or destroy property with an explosive device; no one was injured and the investigation is ongoing. OSINTdefender names him as BioUrja employee Andrew Kozak, arrested at the facility when he reported for work, and notes the indictment does not allege he placed the device found at the plant; About 10:20 PM ET Nov. 17: NBC News reports the Illinois man, a trainee at the Peoria ethanol plant, is charged by a federal grand jury with two felonies related to the bomb found at the facility; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. The vessel and the cause were not identified in the post checked; it follows recent drone strikes on commercial ships near Romania and the sinking of the BETUL 8 off Bulgaria.
Europe.status: Single Reuters report citing maritime security sources; cause unknown; watch for Bulgarian maritime administration statement; Nov. 17, about 8:39–8:45 AM ET: Reuters and gCaptain report the LPG tanker has sunk off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, the second ship to go down off Bulgaria in two days after BETUL 8. The cause is not established; one OSINT account claims a drone strike, which is unverified. Crew status not confirmed by an official source in posts checked; Nov. 17–18: the tanker is identified as the Liberian-flagged LPG carrier GAS HUSKY. Euractiv journalist Georgi Gotev reports it sank after a reported drone attack about a day after another merchant ship was hit nearby, and all 19 crew were rescued. A Ukrainian commentator's summary says Bulgaria's Defense Ministry sent two Su-25 aircraft and a Cougar helicopter for the rescue and that the captain told a maritime outlet the tanker was allegedly attacked by four drones. Who launched the drones is not established; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Gas explosion at the Maredsous Christmas market in Belgium injures five
Europe.summary: The Bulletin (Brussels) reports five people were injured in a gas explosion at the Maredsous Christmas market. No indication of a deliberate act in the report
Europe.status: Single outlet; about 5:03 AM ET; cause reported as gas; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Russian strike on central Odesa kills one person and injures others; residential building hit
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Dzerkalo Tyzhnia (ZN.ua) reports Russian forces attacked the center of Odesa, killing a woman and injuring others. Kyiv Post, citing local media, reports Russian forces struck central Odesa; relays quoting the head of Odesa's city military administration, Serhiy Lysak, say a residential building in the city center was hit. Later on Nov. 18 the death toll rose to three, with seven injured, according to the Kyiv Independent and the head of Odesa's city military administration.
Russia.status: Early reports about 3:30–4:00 AM ET Nov. 18; full casualty figures and official details pending; About 4:39 AM ET Nov. 18: citing Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper, NOELreports says one person was killed and seven injured; windows in residential buildings, cafés and shops were damaged, one car caught fire and several others were damaged; About 5:27–5:47 AM ET Nov. 18: the death toll rose to three, with seven injured. Ukrinform says Russian forces struck Odesa again; Al Jazeera cites the head of Odesa's city military administration saying three were killed in a Russian strike on a residential building in the city center, and the Kyiv Independent reports three killed and seven injured; About 7:06–8:03 AM ET Nov. 18: President Zelensky says Shahed drones struck a residential area in the very center of Odesa, with repeated (double-tap) strikes after first responders and police had arrived, and people were killed. Odesa Oblast Governor Oleh Kiper says Russia struck the city center three times during the morning (Kyiv Independent). Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna says three people were killed and 13 injured in Odesa; About 9:39 AM ET Nov. 18: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry says Russia's drone attacks on Odesa city centre killed at least four people and injured at least ten (preliminary), damaging residential buildings, a café, cars and a three-storey administrative building, with repeated strikes after rescuers and police arrived; About 12:33 PM ET Nov. 18: Reporters Without Borders says Khrystyna Lysenko, a producer at local TV channel Pershiy Miskiy, was killed in the Russian strike on Odesa on Nov. 18

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 141 drones overnight; 126 downed, impacts recorded at seven locations
Russia.summary: Suspilne, citing Ukraine's Air Force, reports Russia attacked Ukraine overnight Nov. 17–18 with 141 drones, of which 126 were shot down or suppressed, with impacts at seven locations and several drones still in the air. NOELreports adds that 59 of 73 jet-powered Shahed-type drones were downed and Gerbera decoys were also used.
Russia.status: Air Force figures as of about 3:15–3:25 AM ET Nov. 18; damage and casualties at impact sites not yet detailed (see Odesa item); carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a market in Zlatopil, Kharkiv region, injures 11, including an 11-year-old boy
Russia.summary: Kharkiv's regional governor says 11 people were injured in a Russian strike on a market in the city of Zlatopil, Al Jazeera's Arabic breaking-news account reports. A Ukrainian regional news channel citing the regional military administration says an 11-year-old boy is among the injured and trading pavilions are on fire, with emergency services and medics at the scene.
Russia.status: Regional governor's figures relayed by Al Jazeera (Arabic) and a regional news channel, about 2:15–2:30 AM ET Nov. 18; watch for updated casualty figures; About 5:27 AM ET Nov. 18: Ukrainian Interior Ministry adviser Anton Gerashchenko puts the number injured in the Zlatopil market strike at 12, including an 11-year-old boy; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Two Russian oil refineries in Krasnodar Krai reportedly targeted in overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports that two oil refineries in Russia's southern Krasnodar Krai were reportedly targeted in an overnight drone attack Nov. 17–18, with Ukrainian monitoring channels reporting strikes on both facilities. Pro-Ukrainian and local-source accounts name the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries and describe a night-long attack, but this is not confirmed by Russian officials in posts checked.
Russia.status: Early reports as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18; no Russian regional or Defense Ministry statement on damage or casualties found; About 11:50 PM ET Nov. 17–12:55 AM ET Nov. 18: Russian outlet Vedomosti reports four people were injured in the drone attack on the Kuban (Krasnodar Krai); the Russian-language news account AteoBreaking reports drones attacked the refineries at Ilsky and Afipsky and that fires broke out at both facilities. Relays quoting the regional operational headquarters place the injuries in the Seversky district. No Russian Defense Ministry statement on the refineries found; extent of damage not reported; About 3:20–3:40 AM ET Nov. 18: Kyiv Post reports the Krasnodar region's operational headquarters confirmed fires at both the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries after the drone attacks; a fire was still burning at Ilsky. No Russian Defense Ministry statement on the refineries found; extent of damage not reported; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian military An-12 transport plane crashes near Yagunovo in Siberia's Kemerovo region; Russia's Defence Ministry says all 19 aboard were killed, technical fault suspected
Russia.summary: Kemerovo regional governor Ilya Seredyuk reported an "aviation incident" near the village of Yagunovo on Tuesday without further details, Novaya Gazeta Europe reports. Russian media report a military An-12 transport crashed and that everyone aboard was killed; reported death tolls range from 13 to 17. Mario Nawfal relays CCTV footage that appears to show the aircraft burning in flight, with a suspected engine fire.
Russia.status: Governor confirms an aviation incident; death toll from Russian media only (13 to 17 reported); cause not officially established; Nov. 17, about 2:10–2:34 PM ET: Russia's Defence Ministry, as reported by Russian media and relayed by Roya News English and Aviation News, says all 19 people aboard were killed, the plane came down in an unpopulated area and a technical malfunction is the preliminary cause; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone attack sets fires at the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refining and petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, Russia
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports a fire at a major oil-refining and petrochemical complex in Russia's Republic of Bashkortostan overnight on Nov. 17, amid reports of a drone attack on the region. Ukraine's Anton Gerashchenko and OSINT accounts post footage of fires at Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat, and Sentdefender says Ukrainian forces heavily targeted the plant, more than 700 miles from the front line. This came alongside the large Ukrainian drone and missile attack on the Kerch Bridge.
Russia.status: Developing; fires reported from about 10:15 PM ET Nov. 16; no official Russian or Ukrainian statement on damage found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:57 AM ET: Kyiv Post reports Ukrainian drones targeted the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex, sparking a major fire, as Moscow claimed it intercepted 1,441 drones overnight; no Russian official damage figure found; Nov. 17, about 6:55 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Ukraine's Defense Forces hit one of Russia's largest petrochemical complexes in Bashkortostan. No Russian official damage assessment found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro in a massive overnight attack across Ukraine
Russia.location: Kyiv, Ukraine (also Kharkiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Cherkasy)
Russia.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said preliminary reports indicate impacts on the North and South bridges in the capital during a massive Russian ballistic missile attack late Monday, Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report. BBC's John Simpson says the attacks began about 11:36 PM local time and he counted 10 or 11 explosions, with both bridges apparently hit, after President Zelensky warned of big strikes. Drop Site News notes the Southern Bridge also carries a metro line, that explosions were reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Cherkasy, and that no casualties had been reported. Secondary accounts citing Kyiv Independent say strikes knocked out water and heat (and some power) in parts of the city.
Russia.status: Mayor's preliminary statement relayed by Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post; corroborated by a BBC correspondent; extent of bridge damage, utility outages and casualties not yet officially detailed; Nov. 16 night: Reuters reports Klitschko said Russian forces struck the two Dnipro bridges along with some other critical infrastructure as Moscow sent drones and missiles across Ukraine; outlets relaying the mayor say water, heating and power were cut in parts of the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says five Iskander-M missiles hit the bridges (three on the Northern, two on the Southern), with a fire on the Northern Bridge (unofficial). No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 16, about 10:40 PM ET (5:40 AM Kyiv time): Al Jazeera's correspondent reports a series of explosions in Kyiv with air-raid sirens on, and Ukrainian channels relayed by Faytuks report a new Russian missile attack on bridge(s) in the city. At about 11:45 PM ET, Economist correspondent Oliver Carroll said Russian missile strikes have stopped traffic on the two main river bridges linking Kyiv's east and west and that there are some problems with water and electricity. No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 3:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post reports Russian missiles struck Kyiv's North and South bridges late Nov. 16, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting essential services, with three injured in Cherkasy region. Ukrainska Pravda says Mayor Klitschko released video of the damaged Northern Bridge. No official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 4:05 AM ET: Reuters reports Russian strikes hit two bridges in Kyiv, causing water and power cuts, citing the mayor. The Kyiv Independent published video and says the strike marks a return to targeted attacks on the capital's transit routes. Posts from Kyiv say the Left Bank is heavily congested because of traffic restrictions on the bridges while specialists assess the damage. No official structural assessment found in posts checked (an AMK Mapping post saying some Northern Bridge cables snapped is no longer available on X and was removed); Nov. 17, about 4:18 AM ET: NEXTA reports Kyiv residents are crossing the Northern Bridge on foot to reach the right bank after the overnight attack. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:44 AM ET: bne IntelliNews reports Kyiv has shut two Dnipro bridges after the Russian strikes. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:22 to 6:26 AM ET: Zelensky says Russia fired four ballistic missiles at Kyiv's Southern Bridge and three at the Northern Bridge, and that backup crossings are needed (NEXTA, Ukrainska Pravda). Footage of the Southern Bridge aftermath has been published despite city requests not to share it. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:00 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Kyiv metro service was restored between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. No structural assessment of the bridges found yet; carried forward from 12:15 PM ET, no newer change found
