Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Yemeni government forces withdraw from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Reuters says Houthis in control
Middle East.location: Dhubab and Bab el-Mandeb area, Taiz/Lahj, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters reported Sunday that forces fighting for Yemen's internationally recognized government withdrew from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. Yemen's armed forces told Al Arabiya the redeployment reflects reprioritized objectives and aims to break the siege of Taiz. Al Jazeera says the Houthi advance threatens one of the government's last strongholds and brings fighting closer to the shipping route.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by government forces' statements and Reuters; no attacks on shipping linked to the withdrawal found in posts checked; extent of Houthi control along the coast unclear; Nov. 16: Anadolu Arabic reports the army foiled a Houthi attack in Taiz, cites two rights groups documenting 319 civilians killed or injured since September, and notes Houthi accusations of Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Saada with no Riyadh comment; Houthi-aligned YNP reports Saudi strikes on Sabr district south of Taiz city for the first time in weeks after a Houthi advance there (partisan source); Nov. 16 evening: Al Jazeera English says the Houthis have claimed control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait; Houthi claim, extent of control not independently confirmed; About 12:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Reuters reports Houthi forces are threatening Aden after capturing territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast, raising concerns for the Saudi-backed government and for shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 206-26: tanker approached by possible mothership and armed skiff 430 nm east of Socotra
Middle East.location: Indian Ocean, 430 nm east of Socotra, Yemen
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says the master of a tanker reported being approached at 0330 UTC on Nov. 16 by a possible mothership and a skiff about 430 nautical miles east of Socotra. Four armed people and a ladder were seen on the skiff. Ships are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO warning issued; suspicious approach, no boarding reported; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sirik and Kong, Hormozgan province, and in Shahriyar near Tehran; cause unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran
Middle East.summary: Several accounts reported explosions heard in Sirik in Iran's southern Hormozgan province on Sunday afternoon, citing Al Mihwar News and Iranian media. Other accounts said an explosion in Kong, also near the Strait of Hormuz, was linked to the targeting of an Iranian surface-to-air missile launcher. Separate reports describe an explosion in Shahriyar, west of Tehran.
Middle East.status: Early reports; claims that US forces struck air-defense launchers are speculation, and no official US or Iranian statement on a strike, damage or casualties was found; Nov. 15 evening: HormuzLetter and AI313_ say, citing only 'initial reports', that the US struck Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik; still no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Iranian official confirmation found, so the attribution remains unverified; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC Navy says two tankers hit naval mines on the 'unauthorized' southern Hormuz route Sunday and claims one supertanker sank
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: The IRGC Navy says two oil tankers that had switched off their tracking systems struck naval mines on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours, caught fire after large explosions, and that one, carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, sank. It released footage it says shows the explosions. The vessels have not been named, and it is unclear whether either is the tanker in UKMTO warning 205-26.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only, relayed by Tehran Times, The Cradle, FirstSquawk and ME Observer; not independently confirmed in posts checked; earlier IRGC tanker-mine claims in this log also remain unverified; Nov. 15 night: the IRGC Navy now claims two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire, saying six tankers have caught fire or sunk since Saturday (Iran International citing Iranian state media; Press TV). No confirmation from UKMTO, CENTCOM or ship operators found; ship names not given, so the claim remains unverified; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Tectonic, citing IRIB, says Iranian naval forces claimed three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, that the IRGC Navy again said six tankers have caught fire or are sinking since Sunday, and that a claimed sinking video shows fire on the water with no clearly visible vessel; ship names still not given and the claims remain unverified; Nov. 17 early: Persian-language outlets relay an IRGC Navy statement claiming a fourth oil tanker in 24 hours exploded after hitting a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; vessel not named; IRGC claim only, no UKMTO, CENTCOM or shipowner confirmation found; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi missile attack near Aden kills at least five civilians, AFP reports
Middle East.location: Lahj governorate, near Aden, Yemen
Middle East.summary: AFP, citing four sources, reports that a Houthi missile attack near Aden on Sunday, Nov. 15 killed five people and wounded eight (via LBCI). A Rai al-Youm report citing AFP and Anadolu puts the toll at at least eight civilians killed and 12 wounded in Lahj.
Middle East.status: Early reports via wire services; tolls differ between reports (5 dead/8 hurt vs. at least 8 dead/12 hurt); carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 205-26: tanker attacked in the Gulf while heading toward the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.location: Southern Arabian Gulf, near the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says it is aware of a report from Indian shipping authorities of an attack on a tanker transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait of Hormuz. The crew are accounted for and safe. Damage and environmental impact were unknown at the time of the report, and vessels are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO advisory (reported 11:52 UTC, 6:52 AM ET) relayed by Iran International, Rudaw and others; attacker, vessel name and damage not identified; UKMTO text says the report came from Indian shipping authorities, the tanker was transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait, and the crew are accounted for and safe; damage and environmental impact unknown; Nov. 16: OSINT accounts say a crude tanker seen on Sentinel imagery being towed to port is believed to be the VLCC AL DHANNAH, the vessel in warning 205-26, with all crew safe; identification is OSINT assessment, not official; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. Low-credibility posts claiming a new Iranian attack on US bases in Bahrain or an IRGC statement of '550 Americans killed and wounded' have no primary source and are not logged; satellite-imagery claims that the radar was destroyed on Nov. 14 are unverified; As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Iranian drone and missile attacks on US bases in Bahrain seen only from low-credibility accounts, not logged. Kuwait's military separately reports engaging hostile drones (see Kuwait item); As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Bahrain attacks still only from low-credibility accounts, not logged; 7:15 PM ET UPDATE — renewed alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an 'alert of potential threat' at about 6:06 PM ET Nov. 17 (2:06 AM local Wednesday), urging people to stay calm and go to the nearest safe location; Al Arabiya's correspondent reported sirens, and blasts were reported. The ministry announced an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET. Bahrain News Agency reports the Arab League condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Bahrain; earlier the GCC secretary-general condemned repeated Iranian attacks. FaytuksNetwork's OSINT timeline puts this second Bahrain attack of the day at about 6:10 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on this wave, and no confirmed damage or casualties, as of about 7:10 PM ET; no formal IRGC claim for this wave found. Claims of a direct hit on Isa Air Base or US casualties (MintPress, DD_Geopolitics, MarioNawfal and others) are unverified and not logged; 8:15 PM ET UPDATE — third alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued another 'alert of potential threat' at about 7:48 PM ET Nov. 17 (3:48 AM local Wednesday), again urging people to go to the nearest safe location; Iran International notes it is the third such alert in less than 24 hours. About a minute later the Bahrain Defence Force General Command said Iran is continuing its 'systematic hostile approach' through attacks targeting the Kingdom. No all-clear from the Interior Ministry found as of about 8:05 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found; Iranian outlets such as Defa Press claim drones hit a US base in Bahrain, which is unverified. Ignored: Arabic and Persian relay claims of a 'direct hit' and large fires at Isa Air Base (no primary); 9:15 PM ET UPDATE: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17, ending the third alert of the night. The Bahrain News Agency (8:07 PM ET) carried the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses countered Iranian attacks; Anadolu reports Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks without specifying casualties or damage. Reuters: 'Bahrain issues all-clear after threat alert amid US-Iran exchanges of fire.' No new alert found as of about 9:05 PM ET; still no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found. A Civil Defence fire in a Souq Waqif building (moi_bahrain, no injuries, cause under investigation) is not linked to the attacks and is not logged; As of about 9:55 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no new CENTCOM statement on the evening waves (CENTCOM's earlier statement called the IRGC radar-hit claim false, with all drones intercepted and no damage or injuries); no confirmed damage or casualties and no formal IRGC claim found; About 10:38 PM ET Nov. 17: KUNA carries the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses fended off several Iranian aerial attacks and that Iran continues its 'systematic approach' of attacks on Bahrain (same BDF statement as earlier this evening). No new Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no confirmed damage or casualties and no new CENTCOM statement found as of about 11:10 PM ET; As of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; viral claims of a new wave and impacts at Sheikh Isa (BedouinReport, IranArabicMedia) have no official primary and are not logged; no new CENTCOM statement and no confirmed damage/casualties; About 12:12 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain News Agency reports the Muslim Council of Elders strongly condemns the renewed Iranian attack on Bahrain. No new Interior Ministry alert, CENTCOM statement, or confirmed damage or casualties found as of about 1:00 AM ET; Iranian-media claims of new explosions at US bases in Bahrain are not confirmed and not logged; As of about 2:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert (no moi_bahrain posts since about 12:30 AM ET in the search checked), no CENTCOM statement, and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert found; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Kuwait and Bahrain (see the Kuwait item). No CENTCOM statement and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 4:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert found since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 5:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Interior Ministry alert found since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry joined the condemnations of the Iranian attacks on Bahrain. No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves and no confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert found since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear, and no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves or confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 7:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry or Bahrain Defence Force alert found since the 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17 all-clear (their accounts posted only routine items after 6:00 AM ET), and no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves or confirmed damage or casualties found; As of about 8:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry or Bahrain Defence Force alert found since the 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17 all-clear; Bahrain's government issued a statement condemning the renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait (linked on the Kuwait item). No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves or confirmed damage or casualties found; About 9:28 AM ET Nov. 18: KUNA reports Bahrain's Foreign Ministry condemned the renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait. No new alerts, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.

Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; About 6:40 AM ET Nov. 18: ABC News says Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is due on Capitol Hill on Wednesday for a hearing on worldwide threats and is likely to face questions about the technology disruptions of the past week; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

K.G. (katha1502) says the Thuringia state criminal office and prosecutors are investigating, that the clinic received an extortion message, and that the hospital has 256 beds. Official statements from the district or MDR were not checked directly in this sweep.
Europe.status: Multiple secondary reports of an official local story; primary hospital or Landkreis post not fetched; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Germany's BundID citizen-login service faces a wave of automated login attempts; password login temporarily restricted
Europe.summary: Die Zeit reports that hackers used a wave of automated login attempts to try to access numerous BundID accounts and that security measures blocked the attack. Other German accounts say the government restricted username-and-password login to BundID on Monday morning after many failed attempts, with some account holders receiving lockout notices. The scale of any successful access was not stated in posts checked.
Europe.status: Corroborated by Die Zeit; described as a blocked or contained credential-stuffing style attack, not a confirmed data breach; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Lithuania's customs agency partially restores online services after a Nov. 10 cyberattack
Europe.summary: A widely shared report says Lithuanian Customs has partially restored online services after a cyberattack detected Nov. 10 forced it to shut its BAP user-management portal. The shutdown disrupted access to several EU customs platforms used for import declarations and goods-status checks, and the report says personal information of hundreds of individuals and businesses may have been exposed.
Europe.status: Single circulating English-language account of the restoration; official customs statement not checked directly; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Cargo ship BETUL 8 sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast; all 12 crew rescued, cause not established
Europe.location: Black Sea, about 40 nautical miles southeast of Cape Kaliakra, Bulgaria
Europe.summary: The Somali-flagged cargo ship BETUL 8 sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone after a distress call on Monday morning, with all 12 crew rescued. DD Geopolitics says the ship was carrying about 3,000 tons of Ukrainian wheat from Tulcea, Romania, to Egypt and that four ships from NATO's Black Sea mine countermeasures group were sent to the scene. One smaller account says an explosion caused the sinking; no official cause has been confirmed in posts checked.
Europe.status: Sinking and crew rescue reported by several outlets; cause (including any explosion or mine) unconfirmed; follows recent drone strikes on ships near Romania's coast; Nov. 17: Ships & Ports reports the Somali-flagged BETUL 8, carrying nearly 3,000 tonnes of wheat, capsized after what crew members described as an attack by two sea drones; all 12 crew were rescued by Bulgarian, Romanian and Turkish units. Potentially exposed data include email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses and payment card details. The company says there is no evidence so far that data was copied or misused, transaction processing is unaffected, and it is notifying potentially affected customers.
Europe.status: Company statement relayed by a single state broadcaster; investigation ongoing; no independent corroboration found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.location: East Lothian, Scotland (Edinburgh–Newcastle rail corridor), UK

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Propane cylinder explosion and fire at the Maredsous Abbey Christmas market in Belgium injure five, two critically
Europe.location: Maredsous Abbey, Anhée, Namur province, Belgium

Five people were injured, two critically, and one was flown by helicopter to a hospital in Liège. The market was closed after the blast.
Europe.status: Media reports describe the explosion as accidental; posts speculating about an attack are not supported by reports found; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.location: Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Pavlohrad and other cities, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT mapping account AMK Mapping says Russia launched about 30 Iskander-M ballistic and about 10 Iskander-K cruise missiles overnight and that more than 300 Geran-2 drones were sent toward western Ukraine. It reports drones targeting electrical substations in Rivne, smoke over Zhytomyr, strong explosions and fires in Vinnytsia, and repeated attacks on Pavlohrad, where Ukrainian authorities report an enterprise was hit.
Russia.status: Developing; launch counts and damage come from OSINT tracking, with no Ukrainian Air Force tally or official damage assessment found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda report two people killed and one injured in Kyiv after a Russian attack, with non-residential buildings hit; Ukrainska Pravda reports Russian strikes on industrial sites in Zaporizhzhia killed two and injured 18. AMK Mapping reports Poland scrambled fighter jets to its eastern regions during the drone attack on western Ukraine (no Polish military post found in posts checked). The Energy Ministry reports outages in eight regions (see power grid item). Still no Ukrainian Air Force tally of launched or downed missiles and drones found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:00 to 5:54 AM ET: RBC-Ukraine reports Russia is massively striking western Ukraine, hitting Mukachevo, Ternopil and Chernivtsi; Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia (Mukachevo and Uzhhorod areas) in three waves around 10 a.m. Hungarian time, near the Hungarian border, with damage being assessed. Ukrainska Pravda reports a Russian strike on Dnipro hit a confectionery factory and homes, injuring 10; a school and apartment buildings in the Sobornyi district were also damaged. Ukrainian Air Force overnight tally still not found; Nov. 17, about 6:31 to 6:53 AM ET: Ukraine's Air Force says air defenses downed 205 of 306 Shahed-type drones, plus three Banderol/Dan-T mini cruise missiles and three Kh-59/69 cruise missiles, with no Iskander ballistic or cruise missiles shot down; hits were recorded at 44 locations (relayed by NOEL Reports and Ukrainska Pravda); Nov. 17, about 7:48 AM ET: Faytuks Network, citing Reuters, says Hungary suspended rail services to Ukraine for Tuesday and Wednesday as Russian drones struck western Ukraine, and a drone crashed about 300 meters from Mukachevo railway station, forcing crew to evacuate; Nov. 17, about 8:20–8:32 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports two killed and 38 injured in a Russian attack on industrial facilities in Zaporizhzhia; ZMiST reports a 51-year-old taxi driver killed and her passenger injured in a Russian attack on Vinnytsia; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, as the search ends
Russia.summary: NEXTA, citing Ukraine's Interior Ministry, says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha and that the search operation is complete. Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; About 2:00–2:40 AM ET Nov. 18: AFP reports Ukraine released images of the strike; Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says its special operation with the defence forces destroyed one of the bridge's arches and a road span, and Zelensky called the strike 'unprecedented'. New video of the destroyed road section is circulating; About 3:30 AM ET Nov. 18: footage filmed from a train crossing the bridge shows the missing road arch and adjacent span; trains appear to be running on the rail section, indicating rail traffic has resumed (OSINT reading of video). No confirmed new strikes; About 4:48 AM ET Nov. 18: Russia says rail traffic across the bridge is running on schedule despite the damage; its Transport Ministry is adding passenger trains and says the Kerch ferry crossing could be activated for cargo and passengers if necessary (via NOELreports). No confirmed new strikes; About 6:33 AM ET Nov. 18: the Kyiv Independent shares new video (from the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+) apparently filmed from a train crossing the bridge. It shows a large section of the motorway fully collapsed with the arch missing and debris in the water, and suggests the railway across the rest of the bridge is still working; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight
Russia.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Sunday that its forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield, home to the 929th State Flight Test Center and a Su-34 base, and a drone launch site at Tsymbulova in Oryol region overnight. Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry says Russian strikes left some consumers in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions without power and forced emergency outages there (via Flash). Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian attack on Zhytomyr region reportedly hits energy infrastructure and homes
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports Russian Geran-4 jet-powered drones attacked a locomotive depot in Dnipro overnight, with a fire visible after the attack. No casualty figures or official confirmation were available.
Russia.status: Single OSINT source; no Ukrainian Railways or regional official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts; no Ukrainian Air Force tally, regional administration statement or damage reports found yet; AMK Mapping reports a large fire in Chornomorsk after the attack and says NASA FIRMS data shows a large fire at the impact area; it says a likely target was a freight-logistics company or the Chornomorsk Automobile Plant; still no official Ukrainian damage or casualty report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays a Russian Defense Ministry claim that the targets were a ferry terminal, the Chornomorsk port administration and a nearby electrical substation; this is a Russian military claim, not independently confirmed, and no official Ukrainian damage report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays Ukrainian energy company DTEK confirming a substation in Chornomorsk was hit by multiple drones, leaving about 41,000 homes without power; Gerashchenko and Flash report six people injured in Chornomorsk and damage to energy infrastructure, an administrative building, a gas pipeline and nearby homes; the same overnight wave injured six in Zaporizhzhia (12 strikes, per Flash) and three in a drone hit on a Kropyvnytskyi residential building; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. The Russian Defense Ministry says it downed 533 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and seas between 8 PM Nov 14 and 8 AM Nov 15 Moscow time, and SOTA and Charter 97 report Rosaviatsia restrictions at about 12 airports including Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Samara, Sochi and Volgograd. An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran drone strikes reported on the Kremenchuk oil refinery, Poltava region, Ukraine
Russia.summary: A pro-Russian channel posts photos and video it says show a fire at the Kremenchuk oil refinery after Russian Geran drone strikes on Nov. 14, with geolocation coordinates. No casualty or damage details are given.
Russia.status: Single pro-Russian source; no Ukrainian official or Poltava regional confirmation found on X; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian double-tap drone strike in Hlukhiv, Sumy region, wounds a grandmother, her grandson and a police officer
Russia.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential area in Hlukhiv on the morning of Nov. 14, wounding a woman; a second drone hit while police were evacuating her and her 9-year-old grandson. NOEL Reports names officers Mykola Savchenko and Ihor Voloshko and says Voloshko was wounded; Ukraine's United24 says the officer and the boy were both injured and all survived.
Russia.status: Reported by Ukrainian government fundraising account United24 and multiple Ukrainian outlets with bodycam footage; final casualty details not confirmed by Sumy regional officials on X; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone strike on a house in Proletarsky, Belgorod region, kills three, Russian regional officials say
Russia.location: Proletarsky, Rakitnoye district, Belgorod region, Russia
Russia.summary: SOTA, citing the Belgorod regional operational headquarters, reports a drone hit a private house in the settlement of Proletarsky, killing a married couple and their 24-year-old daughter and injuring another man. It also reports injuries from drone attacks in Shebekino and the village of Rzhevka.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Russian regional authorities, relayed); not independently verified; no Ukrainian comment found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone strike sets warehouses on fire in Vyshhorod, just north of Kyiv

Russia.status: Early reports; casualties and official Ukrainian regional statement not found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, injure more than 50, including eight children; a rescuer clearing rubble is killed
Russia.summary: A Russian strike on Friday damaged two five-storey apartment buildings in Zaporizhzhia, causing fires, and rescuers freed people trapped in their apartments. Ukraine's State Emergency Service says 30 people were injured, including six children. Kyiv Post reports Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed two people on Friday, including a 17-year-old boy.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones strike the Volgograd oil refinery, setting fires; governor says four killed and two injured
Russia.summary: Multiple posts with video, including Liveuamap, report a drone attack on the Lukoil-operated Volgograd oil refinery on the evening of Nov. 12, with fires on the plant's grounds; one post says the extent of damage remains unconfirmed. A separate post relays Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as saying more than 50 drones headed for Moscow were destroyed in about 90 minutes. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car explodes while driving in southern Moscow, seriously injuring the driver; Russian media say the car belonged to commentator Sergey Zavorotny
Russia.location: Kirovogradskaya Street, Chertanovo district, Moscow, Russia
Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. It comes a day after a car bomb killed a Russian Air Force colonel in St. Petersburg.
Russia.status: Early reports; cause under investigation; one Russian outlet cited a preliminary suspicion of a gas-system malfunction; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; The Washington Post now describes it as a car bombing that seriously injured a former adviser to ex-Ukrainian PM Mykola Azarov who became a pro-Kremlin commentator in Russia; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; Nov. 16: CGTN Français says Russia announced the arrest of a Russian woman it accuses of involvement in the Moscow car bombing on behalf of Ukrainian special services (Russian official claim; not independently verified); carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russian media cited by these accounts identify him as the chief navigator of the 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army, but he has not been named. Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says its journalists heard multiple explosions in Kyiv around 1 a.m. local time on Thursday (Nov. 12; about 6 p.m. ET Wednesday), shortly after Ukraine's Air Force warned that missiles were targeting the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says at least 11 missiles were used, including about five Iskander-Ms, and lists an Epicentr shopping center in northern Kyiv and the eastern industrial zone among the targets, with further strikes in the Bila Tserkva and Irpin areas. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery

NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.
Russia.status: Regional authorities report; toll rose from one to three killed during the morning; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Hromadske Radio later reported the toll rose to three, with businesses and a private home also damaged and four men hospitalized, two in serious condition. CGTN Europe, citing Ukraine's health service, reports three killed and five injured across Dnipropetrovsk region during the day.

Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; Nov. 16 afternoon: journalist Christopher Miller says Mayor Boris Filatov reports about half of Dnipro, a city of about one million, is without power after Russian attacks on the energy system, calling it the sixth blackout in two weeks, with two people killed, 10 high-rise buildings damaged and the Bunge-owned Oleina plant hit a third time; UNIAN says the city was left completely without power after a series of attacks, with outages also in parts of the region; MAKS 26 quotes DTEK as saying Dnipro lost electricity entirely and that crews were first restoring power to water, heat and social facilities; Nov. 17, about 3:00 to 4:05 AM ET: Ukraine's deputy energy minister says Russian overnight strikes on energy infrastructure caused power outages in eight regions (CGTN Europe, First Squawk). The Energy Ministry calls the situation in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions extremely difficult, with some consumers without power in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi regions and emergency outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Poltava and Kharkiv regions; Ukrenergo says crews worked overnight on repairs; Nov. 17, about 5:20 AM ET: Reuters reports nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries say the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is increasing this winter and urge Russia to stop attacking the country's power infrastructure; Nov. 17, about 8:15 AM ET: Reuters reports that 38 nuclear regulators warn Russia's attacks on Ukraine's power grid risk a major nuclear accident; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found
