Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight
Russia.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Sunday that its forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield, home to the 929th State Flight Test Center and a Su-34 base, and a drone launch site at Tsymbulova in Oryol region overnight. Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry says Russian strikes left some consumers in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions without power and forced emergency outages there (via Flash). Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian attack on Zhytomyr region reportedly hits energy infrastructure and homes
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts; no Ukrainian Air Force tally, regional administration statement or damage reports found yet; AMK Mapping reports a large fire in Chornomorsk after the attack and says NASA FIRMS data shows a large fire at the impact area; it says a likely target was a freight-logistics company or the Chornomorsk Automobile Plant; still no official Ukrainian damage or casualty report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays a Russian Defense Ministry claim that the targets were a ferry terminal, the Chornomorsk port administration and a nearby electrical substation; this is a Russian military claim, not independently confirmed, and no official Ukrainian damage report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays Ukrainian energy company DTEK confirming a substation in Chornomorsk was hit by multiple drones, leaving about 41,000 homes without power; Gerashchenko and Flash report six people injured in Chornomorsk and damage to energy infrastructure, an administrative building, a gas pipeline and nearby homes; the same overnight wave injured six in Zaporizhzhia (12 strikes, per Flash) and three in a drone hit on a Kropyvnytskyi residential building; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drones target military aircraft repair plant in Russia's Novgorod region; explosions reported near Staraya Russa
Russia.location: Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, Russia; Crimea
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, citing Telegram monitoring channels, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea. No damage assessment or official Russian or Ukrainian statement was found. RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.
Russia.status: Early reports; Ukrainian outlets citing media and monitoring channels; damage not officially confirmed on X; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Centrenergo warns of 'extremely serious' consequences after Russian strike on Trypillia Thermal Power Plant
Russia.summary: Russian forces struck the Trypillia Thermal Power Plant, the Kyiv Independent reports. Centrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned generating company, said the impact appears significant, but the extent of the damage is not yet clear and needs further inspection.
Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Electrical substation in Kursk, Russia, reportedly struck by drones; fire at the facility
Russia.summary: NOEL Reports says an electrical substation supplying about 400,000 residents in Kursk was reportedly struck and caught fire; Kyiv Post also lists an attack on a Kursk substation among overnight Ukrainian strikes.
Russia.status: Reported by OSINT and Kyiv Post; no Russian official statement on damage or outages found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: Reuters' chief Saudi correspondent reports Saudi Arabia is preparing for its war against the Houthis to stretch well into next year
Middle East.location: Saudi Arabia / Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters' chief Saudi correspondent Timour Azhari posted that Saudi Arabia is preparing for its war against Yemen's Houthis to last well into next year, citing two Western officials briefed by Saudis. He reports Saudi officials have briefed the campaign could run up to six months, and that Riyadh has postponed major global events it was set to host to autumn/winter 2027.
Middle East.status: Single-journalist report citing two unnamed Western officials, posted about 8:46 AM ET Nov. 18; no official Saudi statement found. Escalation signal, not a new attack

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: India's shipping minister says the Liberia-flagged tanker NAVIG8 MESSI was hit by a projectile in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz; all crew safe
Middle East.location: Persian Gulf, approaches to the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: India's Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker MT NAVIG8 MESSI, carrying three Indian seafarers, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf on Nov. 18 while approaching the Strait of Hormuz. He says all three Indians and the entire crew are safe and accounted for with no serious injuries; one Indian officer was taken to hospital for first aid. Maritime-risk analyst Martin Kelly says NAVIG8 MESSI was struck this morning after a recent strike on its sister ship NAVIG8 MACALLISTER, and Osint613 says Kelly linked it to the tanker ADNOC reported struck. The attacker has not been officially named.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by India's shipping minister about 7:24 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker not named; how this relates to the ADNOC vessel and UKMTO 211-26 reports (which mention injured or missing crew) is not confirmed by ADNOC or UKMTO; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli military announces an operation in three blocks of central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and closes Salah al-Din Road, despite the ceasefire
Middle East.location: Central Gaza Strip (north of Bureij and Nuseirat camps), Palestinian Territories
Middle East.summary: Israel's coordinator of government activities in the territories (COGAT) said the Israeli military began an operation in three blocks of central Gaza and would close Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south road, to traffic there, Al Jazeera reports. The Israeli military said its forces began concentrated activity in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and called Hamas infrastructure threatening its troops a breach of the agreement. Anadolu calls it a new offensive despite the ceasefire, and Roya News says tanks were approaching Salah al-Din Road. A source at Al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera one person was killed and others injured in an Israeli strike on al-Maghraqa, north of Nuseirat.
Middle East.status: Announced about 6:00–6:55 AM ET Nov. 18; operation under way; casualty figures early and from one hospital source; no Hamas or mediator response found yet; About 7:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Al Jazeera, citing Israeli media, says the army has begun its first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire agreement. No updated casualty figures or Hamas or mediator response found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 211-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; fire put out, one crew member missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, 13 nm north of Khasab, Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued warning 211-26 at about 4:53 AM ET Nov. 18 after a time-late report of an incident 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Local authorities report a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile within the Strait of Hormuz; a fire broke out on board and has since been extinguished. Search and rescue efforts are under way for a missing crew member. UKMTO did not name the vessel or the attacker, and it is not clear whether this is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel attack reported on Nov. 17 (also one crew member missing), which is logged separately.
Middle East.status: Time-late report; vessel damage and environmental impact unknown; UKMTO advises vessels to transit with caution. Vessel name and attacker not stated as of about 6:00 AM ET; About 6:42 AM ET Nov. 18: the maritime-tracking account live_ais_com says the time-late UKMTO report followed ADNOC's press statement, suggesting the struck tanker is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel (logged separately). This link is the account's assessment; neither UKMTO nor ADNOC has said publicly that they are the same incident, and the vessel name and attacker are still not stated; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Saudi Civil Defense issues early-warning alerts in Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait; danger declared passed about 15 minutes later
Middle East.location: Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, southern Saudi Arabia
Middle East.summary: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued National Early Warning Platform alerts of a potential danger for Jazan Province, Najran Province and Khamis Mushait Governorate between about 4:04 and 4:06 AM ET Nov. 18. It declared the danger passed in all three between about 4:19 and 4:21 AM ET, and Reuters reported the all-clear. The alerts did not say what the threat was; they came amid continuing Houthi missile and drone fire at Saudi Arabia.
Middle East.status: All-clear issued; no impacts, damage or casualties reported as of about 5:00 AM ET; cause of the alerts not stated; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council issues a law designating the Houthis a terrorist organization
Middle East.location: Yemen
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English reports that Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council chairman Rashad al-Alimi issued a law designating the Iran-backed Houthi movement a terrorist organization. Under the law, anyone working for the Houthis or supporting them in word, deed, money or moral support is classified as a terrorist.
Middle East.status: Reported about 4:40 AM ET Nov. 18; no Houthi response found yet; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iran's army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone and missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait
Middle East.location: Ali Al Salem Air Base, Kuwait
Middle East.summary: Iran's regular army (Artesh) public relations office announced that in the early hours of Wednesday, Nov. 18 (Iran time), its combat and suicide drones targeted US Patriot air defense systems and US drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, according to Iran's state Press TV, Al Jazeera's breaking-news channel and Iran International. This is the first formal Iranian military claim of responsibility linked to the drone attacks Kuwait's armed forces reported engaging since about 4:39 PM ET Nov. 17. Relays of the statement quote the army warning that any response to aggression will be decisive and without geographical limits.
Middle East.status: Iranian military claim, published about 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17. No US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation of a hit, damage or casualties found as of about 11:10 PM ET; Kuwait has not named the attacker. Claim of targeting, not a confirmed hit; About 11:20–11:50 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's official IRNA English service carries the army statement claiming its drones struck Patriot air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Base; Al Jazeera English and Drop Site News report the claim, noting Iran's army is separate from the IRGC and that there was no immediate word on damage or casualties. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18. Remains an Iranian military claim; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Iranian and Arabic-language outlets (Press TV, IRNA, Al Jazeera Arabic, Al-Masirah) continue to repeat the army statement, and Press TV now headlines it as drones 'strike' US air defense systems at Ali Al Salem. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement on the attack found (KUNA's latest posts are routine). Remains an Iranian military claim; As of about 2:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry now officially blames Iran for repeated attacks on its territory, including drones earlier in the day (see the Kuwait item), but neither Kuwait nor the US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) has confirmed or denied that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit; no damage or casualty reports found. Press TV and Arabic/Persian outlets continue to repeat the army statement. Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; claims of US casualties rest on IRGC-affiliated channels and flight-tracking inferences only. Iran's army chief Amir Hatami said Wednesday the enemy is preparing its forces and any mistake would draw a stronger, more crushing response (Press TV, Iran International). Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 4:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found. The C-17 medevac-callsign flight from Ramstein and Iranian-sourced casualty claims remain unconfirmed by any US official. Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 5:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found. Iranian-sourced claims of US casualties and the C-17 medevac-callsign flight remain unconfirmed by any US official; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Arabic and Persian outlets keep re-running the Iranian army statement; still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; As of about 7:00 AM ET Nov. 18: outlets and relays continue to repeat the Iranian army claim; still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; About 7:45 AM ET Nov. 18: ABC News, citing Iranian state media, reports Iran's army chief warned Tehran 'will respond more forcefully and severely, without geographical limitations,' if the US military takes action again. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Kuwait's armed forces say air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks over Kuwait, hours after the US strike on Qeshm; attacker not officially named
Middle East.location: Kuwait (hosts major US bases incl. Camp Arifjan and Ali Al Salem)
Middle East.summary: Kuwait's state news agency KUNA reported about 4:46 PM ET Nov. 17 that the General Staff of the Kuwaiti Armed Forces announced its air defenses were actively engaging drone threats and urged the public to stay calm and follow safety instructions; the army said any explosions heard are interceptions. TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) cites Arabic sources reporting several explosions in Kuwait and says air-raid sirens sounded at US bases there — a claim. It comes hours after the US self-defense strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island (see Qeshm item).
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Kuwaiti military confirms an ongoing drone attack and interceptions; origin of the drones NOT officially confirmed (many accounts say Iranian drones, and some relays say the army named Iran, but the KUNA statement checked does not); no IRGC claim of responsibility, CENTCOM statement, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked. Unverified/not logged: claims of 5 IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site, claims of new attacks on US bases in Bahrain; Nov. 17, about 4:39 PM ET: the Kuwaiti Army General Staff's own account posted the statement that air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks and that any explosions heard are interceptions (no origin named). About 5:30–5:56 PM ET: Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) claims, citing local and Arab sources, renewed explosions in Kuwait and a video of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait; journalist Wladimir van Wilgenburg notes the Iraqi channel Naya claimed a US base in Kuwait was targeted with drones — all claims, unconfirmed. As of about 6:00 PM ET: still no formal IRGC statement claiming the attack found, no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties, and Kuwait has not named the attacker. Viral 'direct hit on US base' videos and lists of bases hit come from low-credibility accounts and are not logged; As of about 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: still no Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage/casualties, no new Kuwait Army or KUNA posts since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET statements, and no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Arabic relay accounts say the IRGC announced it targeted US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain in response to the Qeshm strike, but no Tasnim, Fars or Sepah News primary was found, so this is not treated as a formal IRGC claim. FaytuksNetwork relays a BNews claim that drones targeted Al-Jahra and Ali Al Salem (unverified). Ignored: 'six US bases hit', 'US troops in Kuwaiti hospitals' and 'Operation Nasr 2' claims (no primary); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET posts; the Arabic posts circulating around 7:40–7:50 PM ET re-quote that statement. Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties, and there is no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Iranian outlets (Defa Press, a Tasnim-branded account) report explosions in Kuwait and a drone attack on US positions citing 'Arab' or 'Iraqi' sources — media claims, not a formal IRGC statement. Ignored: 'missile swarm struck a major US installation' and lists of US bases hit (no primary); As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement since 4:39–4:46 PM ET; Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on Kuwait and no formal IRGC claim. Iranian outlets (Defa Press) repeat claims of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait citing 'Arab media' — unverified, not logged; As of about 9:55 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement on the drones since 4:39–4:46 PM ET; Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait and no formal IRGC claim found. Arabic claims of suicide drones hitting Ali Al Salem/Camp Arifjan remain unverified and are not logged; About 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's regular army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone/missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait in the early hours of Wednesday Iran time (see separate HIGH item). Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement since 4:39–4:46 PM ET and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found as of about 11:10 PM ET; About 11:33 PM ET Nov. 17: AFP reports Gulf nations on alert after the US strike on Qeshm, with Kuwait saying it is countering 'hostile drone attacks' and Bahrain saying its air defenses intercepted attacks from Iran. No new Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage or casualties, and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement naming the attacker or reporting damage or casualties, and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found; About 1:20–1:50 AM ET Nov. 18: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry, via the state news agency KUNA, condemned 'in the strongest terms' the repeated Iranian attacks on Kuwaiti territory, 'the latest of which involved drones earlier in the day,' saying they flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, international law, the UN Charter and UN Security Council Resolution 2817. Iran International reports the ministry said Kuwait reserves the right to take necessary measures, including self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. This is the first official Kuwaiti statement attributing the drone attacks to Iran found in posts checked. Still no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties; About 2:40–3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: the UAE (via state news agency WAM) strongly condemned the 'hostile attack' on Kuwait, and Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Kuwait and Bahrain as violations of both countries' sovereignty and international law, warning that continued attacks risk escalation and undermine diplomatic efforts. Al Jazeera English also reports Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called Iran's drone attack a 'direct threat to its security and stability'. Still no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking OSINT posts about a US Air Force C-17 medical-evacuation flight leaving Ramstein for the Middle East are being cited online as evidence of US casualties; no US official confirmation of casualties found, and this is not treated as confirmed; About 3:35 AM ET Nov. 18: UAE state news agency WAM headlines the UAE's condemnation as a 'hostile Iranian attack on Kuwait', naming Iran. As of about 4:00 AM ET: still no new Kuwaiti General Staff statement and no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking posts about the US Air Force C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) flying from Ramstein toward the Middle East keep circulating, along with claims attributed to a source close to Iran's parliament speaker that US troops were killed or wounded; no US official confirmation of any casualties found, and neither is treated as confirmed; About 4:52 AM ET Nov. 18: Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry, via the Saudi Press Agency, condemns 'in the strongest terms' the Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain and the attack on a UAE oil tanker, and calls on Iran to stop its attacks and allow diplomatic efforts to proceed. As of about 5:00 AM ET: still no new Kuwaiti General Staff statement and no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking posts about the US Air Force C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) flying from Ramstein toward the Middle East and claims attributed to a source close to Iran's parliament speaker that US troops were killed or wounded keep circulating; the Pentagon has not confirmed any casualties, and neither is treated as confirmed; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement on the attack since the earlier ones (the General Staff and KUNA accounts posted only routine items after 5:00 AM ET), and no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Claims of US casualties attributed to a source close to Iran's parliament speaker and flight-tracking posts about the C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) from Ramstein keep circulating; no US official has confirmed any casualties; As of about 7:00 AM ET Nov. 18: the Wall Street Journal, CBS News and AFP report Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain early Wednesday (Gulf time) and that both countries say they intercepted the incoming weapons; these reports describe the same overnight attacks, not a new wave. Still no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement on damage or casualties (the KUNA accounts posted only routine items after 6:00 AM ET), and no CENTCOM statement found. Claims of US casualties tied to the C-17 (callsign BNDGE01) medevac flight from Ramstein are still only relays and an unnamed Iranian source; no US official has confirmed any casualties; As of about 8:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain's state news agency says Bahrain condemned the renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait (about 7:41 AM ET). Kuwait's General Staff and KUNA posted only routine items in the past hour (a defense minister tour of military sites; condemnation calls); still no Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties and no CENTCOM statement found. Claims of US casualties (C-17 callsign BNDGE01) remain unconfirmed by any US official; As of about 9:00 AM ET Nov. 18: KUNA reports Saudi Arabia condemned Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain and the attack on an Emirati oil tanker (about 7:31 AM ET; Al Jazeera English carried the Saudi Foreign Ministry condemnation about 8:40 AM ET), and the Arab Parliament denounced the 'Iranian aggressions' on Kuwait (about 8:29 AM ET). Kuwait's General Staff posted only a defense minister tour of military sites; still no Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties and no CENTCOM statement found in posts checked. Claims of US casualties (C-17 callsign BNDGE01) remain unconfirmed by any US official

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: ADNOC Logistics & Services says one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 17; 11 crew injured and one missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: ADNOC Logistics & Services, a unit of the UAE's state oil company, says one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of Nov. 17, 2026, according to The National, WAM, Khaleej Times, Arab News and Al Arabiya English. The company says 11 crew members were injured and are receiving medical care, one crew member is unaccounted for with search and rescue under way, and all other crew were evacuated from the vessel. The company statement as reported does not name the vessel or the attacker; it is not confirmed whether this is one of the tankers Iran's IRGC/navy claimed hit naval mines on Nov. 17.
Middle East.status: Company confirmation carried by UAE state news agency WAM and established outlets, about 1:30–2:00 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker and vessel not identified; one crew member missing; watch for UKMTO notice, vessel name, UAE government statement and any claim of responsibility; About 7:41 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain's state news agency says Bahrain condemned the attack on a vessel belonging to the UAE's ADNOC in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, India's shipping minister says the tanker NAVIG8 MESSI was hit by a projectile on Nov. 18 (logged separately); maritime analysts link that ship to an ADNOC press note, but ADNOC has not named the vessel in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile fired toward the Riyadh region
Middle East.location: Riyadh region, Saudi Arabia
Middle East.summary: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the coalition intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed Houthis toward the Riyadh region, Iran International reports, and the Saudi Press Agency carried the coalition statement. It comes hours after Iran's army claimed a drone attack on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and amid the ongoing Saudi-Houthi exchanges already in this log.
Middle East.status: Coalition statement late Nov. 17 ET (SPA about 12:03 AM ET Nov. 18). No reports of damage or casualties found; no Houthi claim found as of about 12:05 AM ET; About 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Anadolu Agency reports coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki confirms the Houthis launched the cruise missile and coalition forces destroyed it. Still no reports of damage or casualties and no Houthi claim found; About 4:06 AM ET Nov. 18: the Saudi Press Agency's regional account again carried a coalition statement that a Houthi cruise missile fired toward the Riyadh region was intercepted and destroyed; it is not clear from the post whether this is a second missile or a repeat of the earlier statement. It came at the same time as Civil Defense early-warning alerts in southern Saudi Arabia (separate item). No damage or casualties reported; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthis say they launched drones toward Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, Reuters reports
Middle East.location: Saudi Arabia (East-West pipeline)
Middle East.summary: Yemen's Houthis say they launched drones toward Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, Reuters reports. It is the latest in a series of Houthi claims against Saudi energy infrastructure this month.

No Saudi or coalition statement on interceptions or damage found as of about 3:05 PM ET; About 3:57 AM ET Nov. 18: the terrorism-tracking service TRAC reports the Houthis claim five drone attacks on East-West pipeline Pumping Stations No. 8 and No. 9 in Riyadh Province (Houthi claim). Middle East.location: Khor Omeira and Ras al-Ara, Lahj province, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Around 20 airstrikes targeted Houthi positions, gatherings and reinforcements in Khor Omeira and Ras al-Ara, west of Lahj, sources told Al Arabiya English, which says more than 60 Houthis were killed. Iran International relays the report.

Middle East.location: Sulaymaniyah province, Kurdistan Region of Iraq
Middle East.summary: Two drones targeted sites belonging to Iranian Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq's Sulaymaniyah province, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing two security sources (relayed by Iran International and Al Jazeera Arabic). Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: US military official confirms US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defense after IRGC attacks on US forces; Iranian official says residential areas and infrastructure were not damaged
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: A US military official says US fighter aircraft used precision munitions earlier on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defense in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets (first reported by Axios' Barak Ravid, then Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera and, per Iran International, Reuters). Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO 208-26: LPG tanker TARA GAS struck a second time off Khasab; crew abandoned ship, one Indian seafarer missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16 evening: NDTV reports the Khasab tanker attack citing UKMTO; vessel still not identified and no responsibility claim found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:40 AM ET: India's shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and that all 25 crew are safe (PTI relays). Analyst Noam Raydan, citing Vanguard, identifies the vessel (IMO 9290270) as disabled with an engine-room fire and says at least 17 ship attacks have been reported in November. Attacker still not identified in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:40 to 4:05 AM ET: OSINT accounts post images of a large smoke column still rising Tuesday morning from the tanker struck about 13 km north of Khasab (unverified). Hindustan Times reports India's minister says all 24 Indian seafarers are safe. Iran International and JNS, summarizing the update, say the tanker first hit about 7 nm north of Khasab was struck a second time, causing another fire on board, and that the crew's status is unknown/unaccounted for after the second strike, citing a maritime security agency. This conflicts with India's earlier statement that all crew were safe (that statement preceded the second strike). Attacker not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 5:02 to 5:40 AM ET: India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said TARA GAS, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and the whole 25-member crew was safe. In an update he says the tanker was attacked again, forcing the entire crew to abandon ship; 24 crew are safely accounted for and one Indian seafarer is missing, and India is coordinating with the ship manager and regional rescue authorities. No US Navy involvement and no new UKMTO notice found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:03 AM ET: India's embassy in Muscat says 24 of the 25 crew of the Panama-flagged VLGC TARA GAS (24 of them Indian) have been evacuated ashore at Khasab and search-and-rescue operations continue for one missing Indian crew member, with Omani support; Nov. 17, about 8:55 AM ET: India strongly condemns the attack on MT TARA GAS; 21 Indian nationals were evacuated, two injured crew are hospitalised and one remains missing, with India's MEA coordinating with Omani authorities on search and rescue (as reported by News18); Nov. 17, about 10:46 AM ET: summarizing Indian officials, OSINTdefender says India confirmed the second attack on TARA GAS; Shipping Minister Sonowal says the crew abandoned the vessel, 24 of 25 are accounted for and one Indian seafarer is still missing. India's Ministry of External Affairs says two injured Indian crew are in hospital and the rest were evacuated ashore at Khasab, Oman. Attacker still not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 3:24–3:57 PM ET: The National reports India's Foreign Ministry confirmed 21 crew were safely evacuated, two hospitalized and one unaccounted for; Drop Site, citing Maritime Executive, says the abandoned carrier is at risk of exploding (Indian officials say a missile hit it, Maritime Executive says an IRGC drone, Iranian media say a mine); Sky News shows footage of the abandoned tanker engulfed in flames off Khasab; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. Low-credibility posts claiming a new Iranian attack on US bases in Bahrain or an IRGC statement of '550 Americans killed and wounded' have no primary source and are not logged; satellite-imagery claims that the radar was destroyed on Nov. 14 are unverified; As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Iranian drone and missile attacks on US bases in Bahrain seen only from low-credibility accounts, not logged. Kuwait's military separately reports engaging hostile drones (see Kuwait item); As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Bahrain attacks still only from low-credibility accounts, not logged; 7:15 PM ET UPDATE — renewed alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an 'alert of potential threat' at about 6:06 PM ET Nov. 17 (2:06 AM local Wednesday), urging people to stay calm and go to the nearest safe location; Al Arabiya's correspondent reported sirens, and blasts were reported. The ministry announced an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET. Bahrain News Agency reports the Arab League condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Bahrain; earlier the GCC secretary-general condemned repeated Iranian attacks. FaytuksNetwork's OSINT timeline puts this second Bahrain attack of the day at about 6:10 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on this wave, and no confirmed damage or casualties, as of about 7:10 PM ET; no formal IRGC claim for this wave found. Claims of a direct hit on Isa Air Base or US casualties (MintPress, DD_Geopolitics, MarioNawfal and others) are unverified and not logged; 8:15 PM ET UPDATE — third alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued another 'alert of potential threat' at about 7:48 PM ET Nov. 17 (3:48 AM local Wednesday), again urging people to go to the nearest safe location; Iran International notes it is the third such alert in less than 24 hours. About a minute later the Bahrain Defence Force General Command said Iran is continuing its 'systematic hostile approach' through attacks targeting the Kingdom. Brina TV puts the overnight death toll at four, including a mother and her child, and says livestock was stolen; Somali Breaking News says the toll has reached eight, including a 14-day-old baby, and blames Borana (Oromo) raiders. The area has seen recent inter-community clashes.
Africa.status: Death toll differs between reports (four vs. eight); separate claims of 11 killed are unverified; no Kenyan police or government statement found as of about 5:00 AM ET Nov. 18; As of about 6:00 AM ET Nov. 18: posts widely shared in Kenya put the toll at eight, including a 14-day-old baby, its mother and a 10-year-old; still no Kenyan police or government statement found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least nine in an attack on Zuwakal (Zuwagal) village, Mangu, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zuwakal village, Jipal District, Mangu LGA, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Security-focused outlet Zagazola Makama reports that suspected armed herders killed at least eight residents, including men, women and children, burned houses and stole 18 cattle in an attack on Zuwakal village about 11:45 p.m. on Nov. 15. Troops of Operation Enduring Peace responded and recovered eight bodies; the attackers fled toward Nasarawa State.
Africa.status: Single security-source report published Nov. 17; no police or army statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:27 PM ET: the Mwaghavul Development Association says gunmen killed at least nine people in Zuwagal (Zuwakal), Mangu, days after a curfew was lifted; houses and food also destroyed in nearby Bong. Still no police or army statement found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Troops thwart a suspected Boko Haram attack on Nigerian Senate chief whip Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa, Borno State
Africa.summary: Vanguard reports that Senate Chief Whip Monguno and others escaped a suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. Details on casualties and the location of the attack were not in the post checked.
Africa.status: Single-outlet report (Vanguard) about 10:30 AM ET Nov. 17; no military or police statement found; Nov. 17, about 12:16 PM ET: Iwere News, citing local outlet Yerwa News Express, says Operation Hadin Kai troops thwarted the attempted attack on Senate Chief Whip Mohammed Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa LGA on Monday, when suspected Boko Haram fighters fired three mortar bombs toward the town while he was there with former governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan and APC leaders; no casualties reported. No official army statement seen on X; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Plateau State, Nigeria — gunmen kill an Operation Rainbow security commander and another person after fresh attacks kill five in three communities
Africa.location: Bokkos, Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi areas, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Premium Times reports gunmen killed a Plateau State security commander and one other person; other reports say the Operation Rainbow commander was ambushed near Bokkos returning from a condolence visit. Punch separately reports at least five people killed in fresh attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas.
Africa.status: Developing; no police or state government casualty figure found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Market shooting in South Sudan reportedly kills 17 and wounds 23, Afropages says
Africa.location: South Sudan (market, location not specified in the post)
Africa.summary: Afropages reports that a shooting in a market in South Sudan killed 17 people and wounded 23. Mwanzo TV posted a headline saying 17 were killed in a South Sudan revenge attack. The exact location, date of the shooting and official confirmation were not given in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early, thinly sourced reports; location and official confirmation lacking; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kordofan Human Rights Observatory says a drone strike on Abu Qalb, West Kordofan, killed at least 15 civilians, including four children
Africa.summary: Radio Dabanga reports that at least 15 civilians, including four children, were killed in a drone strike on Abu Qalb in West Kordofan, according to the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory. The attacker was not identified in the post checked, and no official confirmation was seen.
Africa.status: Single rights-group report via Radio Dabanga; unconfirmed by official sources in this sweep; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Explosion and fire at an NNPC filling station in Ipaja, Lagos, spread to a neighboring school building
Africa.location: Command / Ajasa-Command area, Ipaja, Lagos State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: The Guardian Nigeria says an explosion at a filling station in the Ajasa-Command area of Ipaja triggered a fire, and that the cause and extent of damage are not yet known. WithinNigeria and other local accounts say the fire spread to a school building next to the station. One account says it happened during school hours and that everyone was reportedly safe; no casualties have been confirmed officially in posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports from several Nigerian outlets; cause and casualties unconfirmed; no official emergency agency statement seen; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Sun Nigeria and Instablog9ja say the fire spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School near Savannah Bus Stop in the Command/Ipaja area; firefighters contained the blaze and no casualties were reported in the posts checked. The earlier Guardian Nigeria post used in the prior entry no longer resolves; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Drone or air strike on a village in Abu Zabad, West Kordofan, Sudan, reported to kill 13 to 15 people, including children
Africa.location: Abu Qalb area, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, Sudan
Africa.summary: CGTN Europe quotes the Emergency Lawyers group as saying an airstrike on the Abu Qalb area of Abu Zabad locality killed 13 women and children, according to preliminary figures. News Central TV reports 15 people, including four children, were killed in a Sudanese military drone strike on a West Kordofan village. The Sudanese army had not commented in posts checked.
Africa.status: Reported by two outlets citing a rights group; tolls differ (13 vs 15); attribution to the army not confirmed by the military; Nov. 17, about 5:15 to 5:27 AM ET: The Sudan Doctors Network says a Sudanese army drone struck Abu Qulb in Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, killing at least 13 civilians and injuring others, and calls for an independent investigation (CGTN Europe). KUNA reports the UN Human Rights Office says more than 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan from January to the end of October 2026, more than 1,630 of them in drone strikes; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found
