KUNA on X: UN civilian death toll

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Bomb threat on Sandton Drive, Johannesburg: all-clear given and roads reopened
Africa.location: Sandton Drive near Alice Lane, Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa
Africa.summary: The Citizen reports law enforcement on the scene of a bomb threat in Sandton, and other accounts tell people to avoid Sandton Drive near Alice Lane. No device, evacuation scale or injuries were reported in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports; one established outlet; no police statement found in posts checked; Nov. 16: All-clear given about 15:46 local time per a community security update relaying the Gauteng JOC; eNCA reports the area around Sandton Drive and Alice Lane has reopened; News24 says the threat targeted an office building; no device or injuries reported; resolved, can drop from monitoring; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Two weekend mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 17 dead — nine in Jeffsville near Pretoria and eight in a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg
Africa.location: Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says nine people, six men and three women, were found shot dead inside a four-roomed shack in Jeffsville informal settlement. Police say the shooting is reported to have happened between 10 and 11 p.m. on Nov. 15 and that they were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Nov. 16. The motive has not been established and no arrests have been made; Yfm reports a manhunt is under way and SABC says the Gauteng police commissioner is at the scene.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; comes hours after the separate Sweetwaters (KZN) shooting that killed eight; Nov. 16: Channels TV says police put the toll from the Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters shootings at 17; Newzroom Afrika and Sowetan carry Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni saying one of the nine victims was a person of interest in a December 2025 mass shooting and linking the case to the Saulsville shooting; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: WPLG says at least 17 were killed in the two mass shootings about 330 miles apart and police have not established motives; Pretoria News says SAPS is probing a possible retaliation motive after confirming one victim was a person of interest in the Saulsville case (also EWN); eNCA reports Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi's condolences; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: Reuters, NBC News, Al Jazeera and BBC report at least 17 dead in two weekend mass shootings: nine in the shack near Pretoria and eight men found in a bullet-riddled vehicle near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal; police say motives not yet established and no arrests reported; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: SABC News on X (commissioner at scene)

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight people shot dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters outside Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.location: Mabane Section, Sweetwaters, Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says KwaZulu-Natal police are investigating the murder of eight people who were allegedly shot and killed inside a vehicle along the road at Mabane Section in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg. Daily News reports the eight men were killed on Sunday evening and that a murder investigation is under way. No motive or arrests have been announced.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Peter Obi condemns a reported attack on Kwankwaso's NDC convoy in Bichi, Kano State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Opposition presidential candidate Peter Obi says he is saddened by reports of an attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area. He calls for an immediate investigation and arrests. Kwankwaso had been commissioning NDC offices across Kano State on Sunday.
Africa.status: Early reports; party-side statement only; no police statement, casualty count or damage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya opens probe into violent protests at the Dadaab refugee complex
Africa.location: Hagadera camp, Dadaab, Garissa County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Anadolu reports that Kenyan authorities have opened an investigation after protesters opposing a planned market in Hagadera camp damaged government offices, stole equipment and broke into nearby businesses during clashes.
Africa.status: Single wire report citing authorities; casualty figures not reported; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. It cites Caasimada Online as saying forces loyal to a former South West state leader took Golweyn.
Africa.status: Single-source early report citing Caasimada Online; no official statement or claim of responsibility found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: JNIM reportedly overruns a national police detachment at Balga, near Fada N'Gourma, eastern Burkina Faso
Africa.location: Balga, about 25 km from Fada N’Gourma, Est region, Burkina Faso
Africa.summary: A Sahel-focused account reports that a JNIM attack on the morning of Nov. 15 targeted the National Police detachment at Balga, sacking and burning it, and that many officers were killed and several are missing. It adds that the attackers took all weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no official Burkinabe statement or casualty figure found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill a Zamfara governor's aide in a dawn attack in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits attacked worshippers at dawn prayer in Kaura Namoda on Sunday, Nov. 15, killing Nasiru Sani Kaura and abducting several others, according to the security platform Bakatsine (via Africa_lix). Nigerians_New reports he was an aide to Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal.
Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Post on X citing Eye Radio

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Reuters Africa on X: attacks hinder Ebola response

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source
Africa.summary: A post circulating an Eritrean Ministry of Information editorial quotes it saying Eritreans and their army are ready to answer "Prosperity's invasion" in the language it has chosen. A widely shared post claims Eritrea's government announced that Ethiopia has invaded, but another account says the ministry accused Ethiopia of "preparing aggression." No independent confirmation of cross-border fighting was found.
Africa.status: Early reports; contested framing; no Ethiopian government response or independent confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Post on X: ministry editorial quote (low-follower account)

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Post on X relaying News Central TV

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Deadly clash during anti-illegal-mining operation at Manso Keniago, Ghana; Citi FM reports four dead and 15 injured
Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A confrontation broke out on Wednesday (Nov. 11) between personnel of Ghana's National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents and suspected illegal miners as the task force removed seized excavators at Manso Keniago. NAIMOS, as reported by TV3/3News, says two of its personnel were shot and injured by an armed mob. threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon

Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.

Campaigns it cites include attacks on South Korean financial institutions (data on about 67,000 people exfiltrated) and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise (more than 2,250 downstream tenants). The developer pulled the GitHub repository on Oct. 8, 2026, but forks, archived copies and a commercial ARTEX PRO still circulate, and more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles were found in early November. BleepingComputer and The Record covered the advisory; today's X coverage comes from viral relays of the Nov. 13 FLASH.

America.title: CONTINUATION: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)
America.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme reported malicious JavaScript being served through the Optimizely web experimentation platform to the websites of about 178 organizations, including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax and Ledger. He and security firm Coinspect say the payload included a crypto address swapper, a card skimmer, cookie theft and iOS exploit code; Helme says about $7,000 in crypto had been diverted. Optimizely says it identified and contained a security incident affecting some Web Experimentation customers, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the injected code and contacted customers. BleepingComputer reports the attack.
America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known; Nov. 17: Optimizely's notice says an 'unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation' (Infosecurity Magazine). Reuters (via the New York Post, about 9:30 AM ET) cites researcher Scott Helme and says it could not independently establish whether every affected site was successfully exploited; AFP (about 12:45 PM ET) says nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted. Report URI names the iOS exploit kits as Coruna and DarkSword and advises updating to iOS 18.7.3+ or 26.3+; Mediaite, citing Reuters, says Salesforce disabled the scripts, Equifax stopped using the platform and found no compromise, and IKEA is investigating. Report URI says all infected files were clean by 23:11 UTC Nov. 16 (6:11 PM ET). STABILIZED: contained; moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; About 6:40 AM ET Nov. 18: ABC News says Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is due on Capitol Hill on Wednesday for a hearing on worldwide threats and is likely to face questions about the technology disruptions of the past week; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 16, about 10:40 PM ET (5:40 AM Kyiv time): Al Jazeera's correspondent reports a series of explosions in Kyiv with air-raid sirens on, and Ukrainian channels relayed by Faytuks report a new Russian missile attack on bridge(s) in the city. At about 11:45 PM ET, Economist correspondent Oliver Carroll said Russian missile strikes have stopped traffic on the two main river bridges linking Kyiv's east and west and that there are some problems with water and electricity. No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 3:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post reports Russian missiles struck Kyiv's North and South bridges late Nov. 16, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting essential services, with three injured in Cherkasy region. Ukrainska Pravda says Mayor Klitschko released video of the damaged Northern Bridge. No official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 4:05 AM ET: Reuters reports Russian strikes hit two bridges in Kyiv, causing water and power cuts, citing the mayor. The Kyiv Independent published video and says the strike marks a return to targeted attacks on the capital's transit routes. Posts from Kyiv say the Left Bank is heavily congested because of traffic restrictions on the bridges while specialists assess the damage. No official structural assessment found in posts checked (an AMK Mapping post saying some Northern Bridge cables snapped is no longer available on X and was removed); Nov. 17, about 4:18 AM ET: NEXTA reports Kyiv residents are crossing the Northern Bridge on foot to reach the right bank after the overnight attack. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:44 AM ET: bne IntelliNews reports Kyiv has shut two Dnipro bridges after the Russian strikes. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:22 to 6:26 AM ET: Zelensky says Russia fired four ballistic missiles at Kyiv's Southern Bridge and three at the Northern Bridge, and that backup crossings are needed (NEXTA, Ukrainska Pravda). Footage of the Southern Bridge aftermath has been published despite city requests not to share it. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:00 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Kyiv metro service was restored between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. No structural assessment of the bridges found yet; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike hits port and industrial facilities in Mykolaiv, southern Ukraine
Russia.summary: A local official says Russian forces struck port facilities and industrial infrastructure in Mykolaiv overnight Nov. 17, as part of the wider missile and drone attack across Ukraine. Al Araby TV carries the same report citing Ukrainian authorities.
Russia.status: Early official report; damage and casualty figures not given in posts checked; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine: two killed in Kyiv, two killed in Zaporizhzhia; substations reported hit in Rivne
Russia.location: Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Pavlohrad and other cities, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT mapping account AMK Mapping says Russia launched about 30 Iskander-M ballistic and about 10 Iskander-K cruise missiles overnight and that more than 300 Geran-2 drones were sent toward western Ukraine. It reports drones targeting electrical substations in Rivne, smoke over Zhytomyr, strong explosions and fires in Vinnytsia, and repeated attacks on Pavlohrad, where Ukrainian authorities report an enterprise was hit.
Russia.status: Developing; launch counts and damage come from OSINT tracking, with no Ukrainian Air Force tally or official damage assessment found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda report two people killed and one injured in Kyiv after a Russian attack, with non-residential buildings hit; Ukrainska Pravda reports Russian strikes on industrial sites in Zaporizhzhia killed two and injured 18. AMK Mapping reports Poland scrambled fighter jets to its eastern regions during the drone attack on western Ukraine (no Polish military post found in posts checked). The Energy Ministry reports outages in eight regions (see power grid item). Still no Ukrainian Air Force tally of launched or downed missiles and drones found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:00 to 5:54 AM ET: RBC-Ukraine reports Russia is massively striking western Ukraine, hitting Mukachevo, Ternopil and Chernivtsi; Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia (Mukachevo and Uzhhorod areas) in three waves around 10 a.m. Hungarian time, near the Hungarian border, with damage being assessed. Ukrainska Pravda reports a Russian strike on Dnipro hit a confectionery factory and homes, injuring 10; a school and apartment buildings in the Sobornyi district were also damaged. Ukrainian Air Force overnight tally still not found; Nov. 17, about 6:31 to 6:53 AM ET: Ukraine's Air Force says air defenses downed 205 of 306 Shahed-type drones, plus three Banderol/Dan-T mini cruise missiles and three Kh-59/69 cruise missiles, with no Iskander ballistic or cruise missiles shot down; hits were recorded at 44 locations (relayed by NOEL Reports and Ukrainska Pravda); Nov. 17, about 7:48 AM ET: Faytuks Network, citing Reuters, says Hungary suspended rail services to Ukraine for Tuesday and Wednesday as Russian drones struck western Ukraine, and a drone crashed about 300 meters from Mukachevo railway station, forcing crew to evacuate; Nov. 17, about 8:20–8:32 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports two killed and 38 injured in a Russian attack on industrial facilities in Zaporizhzhia; ZMiST reports a 51-year-old taxi driver killed and her passenger injured in a Russian attack on Vinnytsia; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, as the search ends
Russia.summary: NEXTA, citing Ukraine's Interior Ministry, says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha and that the search operation is complete. Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; About 2:00–2:40 AM ET Nov. 18: AFP reports Ukraine released images of the strike; Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says its special operation with the defence forces destroyed one of the bridge's arches and a road span, and Zelensky called the strike 'unprecedented'. New video of the destroyed road section is circulating; About 3:30 AM ET Nov. 18: footage filmed from a train crossing the bridge shows the missing road arch and adjacent span; trains appear to be running on the rail section, indicating rail traffic has resumed (OSINT reading of video). No confirmed new strikes; About 4:48 AM ET Nov. 18: Russia says rail traffic across the bridge is running on schedule despite the damage; its Transport Ministry is adding passenger trains and says the Kerch ferry crossing could be activated for cargo and passengers if necessary (via NOELreports). No confirmed new strikes; About 6:33 AM ET Nov. 18: the Kyiv Independent shares new video (from the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+) apparently filmed from a train crossing the bridge. It shows a large section of the motorway fully collapsed with the arch missing and debris in the water, and suggests the railway across the rest of the bridge is still working; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight
Russia.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Sunday that its forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield, home to the 929th State Flight Test Center and a Su-34 base, and a drone launch site at Tsymbulova in Oryol region overnight. Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Energy Ministry says Russian strikes left some consumers in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions without power and forced emergency outages there (via Flash). Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian attack on Zhytomyr region reportedly hits energy infrastructure and homes
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports Russian Geran-4 jet-powered drones attacked a locomotive depot in Dnipro overnight, with a fire visible after the attack. No casualty figures or official confirmation were available.
Russia.status: Single OSINT source; no Ukrainian Railways or regional official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.

FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says air defenses neutralized 135 of 162 Russian drones, 70 of them jet-powered, and that Russia also launched an Iskander-M ballistic missile. It says hits were recorded in 19 locations and debris fell in nine more. It reports critical infrastructure in the Kirovohrad region was attacked, with two people injured, and that a business in Dnipro caught fire. Ukrainska Pravda and Ukrinform carry the same figures.
Russia.status: Daily casualty figures via Kyiv Independent, citing regional authorities; Air Force figures via NOEL Reports; damage assessments continuing; Nov. 16: Kyiv Independent says Russian attacks killed 6 and injured 45 across Ukraine over the past day as Kyiv endured almost nonstop air raid alerts; citing the Air Force, it says Russia launched 158 long-range attack drones overnight, including 77 jet-powered drones; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone hits a commuter train at Sumy railway station; no casualties reported
Russia.summary: The head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, Oleh Hryhorov, says a Russian drone deliberately struck a commuter train at the Sumy railway station on Tuesday morning. He says there were no passengers on board, the crew was in a shelter and there were no casualties. Ukrainska Pravda and RBC-Ukraine also report the attack on the train.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) statement; no casualties; damage to rolling stock; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.status: Reported by Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda; energy damage extent not given; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drones target military aircraft repair plant in Russia's Novgorod region; explosions reported near Staraya Russa
Russia.location: Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, Russia; Crimea
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, citing Telegram monitoring channels, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea. RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Centrenergo warns of 'extremely serious' consequences after Russian strike on Trypillia Thermal Power Plant
Russia.summary: Russian forces struck the Trypillia Thermal Power Plant, the Kyiv Independent reports. Centrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned generating company, said the impact appears significant, but the extent of the damage is not yet clear and needs further inspection.
Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Responsibility is not established in the posts found.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (IAEA, via Kyiv Independent); carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Electrical substation in Kursk, Russia, reportedly struck by drones; fire at the facility
Russia.summary: NOEL Reports says an electrical substation supplying about 400,000 residents in Kursk was reportedly struck and caught fire; Kyiv Post also lists an attack on a Kursk substation among overnight Ukrainian strikes.
Russia.status: Reported by OSINT and Kyiv Post; no Russian official statement on damage or outages found in posts checked; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: India's shipping minister says the Liberia-flagged tanker NAVIG8 MESSI was hit by a projectile in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz; all crew safe
Middle East.location: Persian Gulf, approaches to the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: India's Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker MT NAVIG8 MESSI, carrying three Indian seafarers, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf on Nov. 18 while approaching the Strait of Hormuz. He says all three Indians and the entire crew are safe and accounted for with no serious injuries; one Indian officer was taken to hospital for first aid. Maritime-risk analyst Martin Kelly says NAVIG8 MESSI was struck this morning after a recent strike on its sister ship NAVIG8 MACALLISTER, and Osint613 says Kelly linked it to the tanker ADNOC reported struck. The attacker has not been officially named.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by India's shipping minister about 7:24 AM ET Nov. 18; attacker not named; how this relates to the ADNOC vessel and UKMTO 211-26 reports (which mention injured or missing crew) is not confirmed by ADNOC or UKMTO

links.label: Indian shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on X

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Israeli military announces an operation in three blocks of central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and closes Salah al-Din Road, despite the ceasefire
Middle East.location: Central Gaza Strip (north of Bureij and Nuseirat camps), Palestinian Territories
Middle East.summary: Israel's coordinator of government activities in the territories (COGAT) said the Israeli military began an operation in three blocks of central Gaza and would close Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south road, to traffic there, Al Jazeera reports. The Israeli military said its forces began concentrated activity in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line and called Hamas infrastructure threatening its troops a breach of the agreement. Anadolu calls it a new offensive despite the ceasefire, and Roya News says tanks were approaching Salah al-Din Road. A source at Al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera one person was killed and others injured in an Israeli strike on al-Maghraqa, north of Nuseirat.
Middle East.status: Announced about 6:00–6:55 AM ET Nov. 18; operation under way; casualty figures early and from one hospital source; no Hamas or mediator response found yet; About 7:35 AM ET Nov. 18: Al Jazeera, citing Israeli media, says the army has begun its first large-scale military operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire agreement. No updated casualty figures or Hamas or mediator response found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 211-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; fire put out, one crew member missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, 13 nm north of Khasab, Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued warning 211-26 at about 4:53 AM ET Nov. 18 after a time-late report of an incident 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Local authorities report a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile within the Strait of Hormuz; a fire broke out on board and has since been extinguished. Search and rescue efforts are under way for a missing crew member. UKMTO did not name the vessel or the attacker, and it is not clear whether this is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel attack reported on Nov. 17 (also one crew member missing), which is logged separately.
Middle East.status: Time-late report; vessel damage and environmental impact unknown; UKMTO advises vessels to transit with caution. Vessel name and attacker not stated as of about 6:00 AM ET; About 6:42 AM ET Nov. 18: the maritime-tracking account live_ais_com says the time-late UKMTO report followed ADNOC's press statement, suggesting the struck tanker is the ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel (logged separately). This link is the account's assessment; neither UKMTO nor ADNOC has said publicly that they are the same incident, and the vessel name and attacker are still not stated; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found
