Russia.title: UPDATE: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; About 2:00–2:40 AM ET Nov. 18: AFP reports Ukraine released images of the strike; Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) says its special operation with the defence forces destroyed one of the bridge's arches and a road span, and Zelensky called the strike 'unprecedented'. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; Nov. 16 afternoon: journalist Christopher Miller says Mayor Boris Filatov reports about half of Dnipro, a city of about one million, is without power after Russian attacks on the energy system, calling it the sixth blackout in two weeks, with two people killed, 10 high-rise buildings damaged and the Bunge-owned Oleina plant hit a third time; UNIAN says the city was left completely without power after a series of attacks, with outages also in parts of the region; MAKS 26 quotes DTEK as saying Dnipro lost electricity entirely and that crews were first restoring power to water, heat and social facilities; Nov. 17, about 3:00 to 4:05 AM ET: Ukraine's deputy energy minister says Russian overnight strikes on energy infrastructure caused power outages in eight regions (CGTN Europe, First Squawk). The Energy Ministry calls the situation in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions extremely difficult, with some consumers without power in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi regions and emergency outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Poltava and Kharkiv regions; Ukrenergo says crews worked overnight on repairs; Nov. 17, about 5:20 AM ET: Reuters reports nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries say the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is increasing this winter and urge Russia to stop attacking the country's power infrastructure; Nov. 17, about 8:15 AM ET: Reuters reports that 38 nuclear regulators warn Russia's attacks on Ukraine's power grid risk a major nuclear accident; carried forward from 2:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iran's army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone and missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait
Middle East.location: Ali Al Salem Air Base, Kuwait
Middle East.summary: Iran's regular army (Artesh) public relations office announced that in the early hours of Wednesday, Nov. 18 (Iran time), its combat and suicide drones targeted US Patriot air defense systems and US drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, according to Iran's state Press TV, Al Jazeera's breaking-news channel and Iran International. This is the first formal Iranian military claim of responsibility linked to the drone attacks Kuwait's armed forces reported engaging since about 4:39 PM ET Nov. 17. Relays of the statement quote the army warning that any response to aggression will be decisive and without geographical limits.
Middle East.status: Iranian military claim, published about 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17. No US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation of a hit, damage or casualties found as of about 11:10 PM ET; Kuwait has not named the attacker. Claim of targeting, not a confirmed hit; About 11:20–11:50 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's official IRNA English service carries the army statement claiming its drones struck Patriot air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Base; Al Jazeera English and Drop Site News report the claim, noting Iran's army is separate from the IRGC and that there was no immediate word on damage or casualties. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18. Remains an Iranian military claim; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Iranian and Arabic-language outlets (Press TV, IRNA, Al Jazeera Arabic, Al-Masirah) continue to repeat the army statement, and Press TV now headlines it as drones 'strike' US air defense systems at Ali Al Salem. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement on the attack found (KUNA's latest posts are routine). Remains an Iranian military claim; As of about 2:00 AM ET Nov. 18: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry now officially blames Iran for repeated attacks on its territory, including drones earlier in the day (see the Kuwait item), but neither Kuwait nor the US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) has confirmed or denied that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit; no damage or casualty reports found. Press TV and Arabic/Persian outlets continue to repeat the army statement. Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets; As of about 3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial that anything at Ali Al Salem was hit, and no official damage or casualty report found; claims of US casualties rest on IRGC-affiliated channels and flight-tracking inferences only. Iran's army chief Amir Hatami said Wednesday the enemy is preparing its forces and any mistake would draw a stronger, more crushing response (Press TV, Iran International). Remains an Iranian military claim on the specific targets

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Kuwait's armed forces say air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks over Kuwait, hours after the US strike on Qeshm; attacker not officially named
Middle East.location: Kuwait (hosts major US bases incl. Camp Arifjan and Ali Al Salem)
Middle East.summary: Kuwait's state news agency KUNA reported about 4:46 PM ET Nov. 17 that the General Staff of the Kuwaiti Armed Forces announced its air defenses were actively engaging drone threats and urged the public to stay calm and follow safety instructions; the army said any explosions heard are interceptions. TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) cites Arabic sources reporting several explosions in Kuwait and says air-raid sirens sounded at US bases there — a claim. It comes hours after the US self-defense strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island (see Qeshm item).
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Kuwaiti military confirms an ongoing drone attack and interceptions; origin of the drones NOT officially confirmed (many accounts say Iranian drones, and some relays say the army named Iran, but the KUNA statement checked does not); no IRGC claim of responsibility, CENTCOM statement, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked. Unverified/not logged: claims of 5 IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site, claims of new attacks on US bases in Bahrain; Nov. 17, about 4:39 PM ET: the Kuwaiti Army General Staff's own account posted the statement that air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks and that any explosions heard are interceptions (no origin named). About 5:30–5:56 PM ET: Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) claims, citing local and Arab sources, renewed explosions in Kuwait and a video of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait; journalist Wladimir van Wilgenburg notes the Iraqi channel Naya claimed a US base in Kuwait was targeted with drones — all claims, unconfirmed. As of about 6:00 PM ET: still no formal IRGC statement claiming the attack found, no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties, and Kuwait has not named the attacker. Viral 'direct hit on US base' videos and lists of bases hit come from low-credibility accounts and are not logged; As of about 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: still no Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage/casualties, no new Kuwait Army or KUNA posts since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET statements, and no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Arabic relay accounts say the IRGC announced it targeted US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain in response to the Qeshm strike, but no Tasnim, Fars or Sepah News primary was found, so this is not treated as a formal IRGC claim. FaytuksNetwork relays a BNews claim that drones targeted Al-Jahra and Ali Al Salem (unverified). Ignored: 'six US bases hit', 'US troops in Kuwaiti hospitals' and 'Operation Nasr 2' claims (no primary); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET posts; the Arabic posts circulating around 7:40–7:50 PM ET re-quote that statement. Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties, and there is no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Iranian outlets (Defa Press, a Tasnim-branded account) report explosions in Kuwait and a drone attack on US positions citing 'Arab' or 'Iraqi' sources — media claims, not a formal IRGC statement. Ignored: 'missile swarm struck a major US installation' and lists of US bases hit (no primary); As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement since 4:39–4:46 PM ET; Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on Kuwait and no formal IRGC claim. Iranian outlets (Defa Press) repeat claims of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait citing 'Arab media' — unverified, not logged; As of about 9:55 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Kuwait Army (KuwaitArmyGHQ) or KUNA statement on the drones since 4:39–4:46 PM ET; Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait and no formal IRGC claim found. Arabic claims of suicide drones hitting Ali Al Salem/Camp Arifjan remain unverified and are not logged; About 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's regular army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone/missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait in the early hours of Wednesday Iran time (see separate HIGH item). Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties; no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement since 4:39–4:46 PM ET and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found as of about 11:10 PM ET; About 11:33 PM ET Nov. 17: AFP reports Gulf nations on alert after the US strike on Qeshm, with Kuwait saying it is countering 'hostile drone attacks' and Bahrain saying its air defenses intercepted attacks from Iran. No new Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage or casualties, and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Kuwaiti General Staff or KUNA statement naming the attacker or reporting damage or casualties, and no CENTCOM statement on Kuwait found; About 1:20–1:50 AM ET Nov. 18: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry, via the state news agency KUNA, condemned 'in the strongest terms' the repeated Iranian attacks on Kuwaiti territory, 'the latest of which involved drones earlier in the day,' saying they flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, international law, the UN Charter and UN Security Council Resolution 2817. Iran International reports the ministry said Kuwait reserves the right to take necessary measures, including self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. This is the first official Kuwaiti statement attributing the drone attacks to Iran found in posts checked. Still no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties; About 2:40–3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: the UAE (via state news agency WAM) strongly condemned the 'hostile attack' on Kuwait, and Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Kuwait and Bahrain as violations of both countries' sovereignty and international law, warning that continued attacks risk escalation and undermine diplomatic efforts. Al Jazeera English also reports Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called Iran's drone attack a 'direct threat to its security and stability'. Still no Kuwaiti or CENTCOM statement on damage or casualties found. Flight-tracking OSINT posts about a US Air Force C-17 medical-evacuation flight leaving Ramstein for the Middle East are being cited online as evidence of US casualties; no US official confirmation of casualties found, and this is not treated as confirmed

The statement, which calls the Houthis a terrorist militia, gave no details on damage or casualties. It follows the Saudi strikes on Sanaa, Omran and Hodeidah already in this log.

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Protest in Abdanan, Ilam province, Iran, after a bus crash that killed 13; security forces reportedly fire into the air and use tear gas
Middle East.location: Abdanan, Ilam province, Iran (protests also reported in Abadan)
Middle East.summary: IRGC-affiliated Fars says a protest began Tuesday, Nov. 17, in Abdanan's Vali-Asr square over a bus crash that killed 13 people, growing from 200–300 to about 1,000 people, and says some tried to damage public property before police intervened. Eyewitnesses told Iran International that security forces on motorcycles fired into the air and used tear gas to disperse protesters. Videos shared by OSINT accounts show protesters tearing down an IRGC/Basij banner and chanting anti-regime and pro-Pahlavi slogans, and separate footage shows crowds protesting in Abadan in the southwest.
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 10:08 AM ET; casualty and arrest figures not reported; Nov. 17, about 10:20–10:39 AM ET: Iran International says videos show hundreds chanting pro-monarchy slogans ('Pahlavi will return'); it relays Fars as saying the crowd moved into surrounding streets, some slogans became 'political', police were deployed and the protest was continuing. No casualty or arrest figures reported; Nov. 17, about 12:50 PM ET: Iran International says protesters are again on the streets of Abdanan chanting anti-regime and pro-monarchy slogans. No casualty or arrest figures reported; Nov. 17, about 3:50 PM ET: Iran International, citing rights groups Hana and Kurdpa, reports at least six people arrested, including a 15-year-old; Kurdpa reports riot police deployed, severe internet disruptions, tear gas and pellet guns used against protesters; carried forward from 2:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: US military official confirms US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defense after IRGC attacks on US forces; Iranian official says residential areas and infrastructure were not damaged
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: A US military official says US fighter aircraft used precision munitions earlier on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defense in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets (first reported by Axios' Barak Ravid, then Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera and, per Iran International, Reuters). Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. From about 9:09 AM ET Al Arabiya and Al Hadath cite unnamed Iranian media saying a US strike hit the Nariman air defense site; Al Arabiya English carries the same at about 9:39 AM ET. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. This is the first named Iranian official confirmation of a US strike, so the item is upgraded to HIGH. As of about 11:10 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; viral 'US official: the United States is attacking Qeshm' posts have no traceable primary and are not logged. Casualty claims (6 IRGC killed) remain unverified; the Osint613 post on a further round of explosions (10:10 AM ET) has since been deleted and its link removed; Nov. 17, about 11:37–11:54 AM ET: ISNA, Iran International Arabic, Al Arabiya and Annahar carry the same Iranian account. Nafisi says the situation on the island is under control and relief services are on high alert; Al Arabiya, citing Iranian media, says the target was the Nariman air-defense site and Fars residents reported several consecutive blasts northwest of Qeshm city with rising smoke, with no damage or casualty details. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. No IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; OSINT reports of missile launches inside Iran are listed separately as unconfirmed; Nov. 17, about 12:10–12:55 PM ET: international outlets (TRT World, Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera Arabic, Iran International Persian) carry the Iranian deputy governor's account; Iran International Persian says five to six explosions were heard in Qeshm city with smoke in the island's northwest, and IRGC-affiliated media say air-defense positions were targeted, with no independent damage report. Al-Monitor reports a top Iranian official warned that civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases would be considered 'dual use'. About 12:59–1:02 PM ET: OSINT accounts report another explosion on Qeshm; BeamTracker says it is most likely an anti-ship cruise missile launch from the island rather than an airstrike, and MintPress says it would be a third round of US strikes if confirmed; neither is confirmed. As of about 1:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X (a post claiming AFP as its source was not matched to any AFP post and is not logged). No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm confirmed; Nov. 17, about 1:54 PM ET: TRT Persian repeats Iran's statement that the US attack on Qeshm caused no damage to infrastructure. Persian-language accounts claim further explosions and casualties on Qeshm, but these are unverified and not logged. As of about 2:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X. No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; Nov. 17, about 2:25–2:50 PM ET: a US military official confirmed the strike. Axios' Barak Ravid quotes the official: 'Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense,' in response to 'IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets.' Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera, Iran International (citing Reuters) and Ynet report the same official account. Independent Persian says Tasnim, citing provincial officials, confirmed the blasts heard on Qeshm were US strikes, described as a response to the IRGC drone attack on Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base. No formal CENTCOM press release seen on X as of about 3:05 PM ET; damage and casualties not officially reported (claims that six IRGC personnel were killed are unverified and not logged); no IRGC retaliation against US forces confirmed so far. Now a confirmed US strike on Iranian territory; Nov. 17, about 2:30–2:35 PM ET: more Pentagon reporters (Libbey Dean, Al Jazeera's Fadi Mansour) carry the same US military official statement: US fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense. As of about 4:00 PM ET there is still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (six IRGC killed, 'martyrs' on Qeshm) remain unverified and not logged; no confirmed IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states (an IRGC spokesman threat against Bahrain's rulers seen only via relays, not logged); As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement found on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (e.g. five IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site) unverified and not logged. About 4:46 PM ET Kuwait's military said its air defenses were engaging hostile drone attacks (attacker not officially named) — see the Kuwait item; As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release or Pentagon/White House statement on the strike found on X (CENTCOM account search since 4:00 PM ET returned nothing); no confirmed further US strikes; Iranian casualty claims still unconfirmed. Kuwait drone attack (possible retaliation) remains unattributed by Kuwait — see Kuwait item; About 6:42 PM ET Nov. 17: euronews reports that Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island. As of about 7:10 PM ET: still no formal CENTCOM press release found; no further US strikes confirmed by US officials. Iran's retaliation remains unclaimed by any primary IRGC source (see the Kuwait and Bahrain items); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release (no CENTCOM posts since 7:05 PM ET), and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; relays describing 'fresh airstrikes' refer to the same strike; About 9:40 PM ET Nov. 17: ABC World News Tonight says that with Iranian attacks on commercial ships intensifying in the Strait of Hormuz, 'the U.S. has launched new airstrikes on Iran'; the post does not name targets beyond the Qeshm strike already reported. Still no formal CENTCOM press release on the Qeshm strike (CENTCOM/Pentagon account search since 4:00 PM ET found nothing new), and no separate additional US strike confirmed by US officials; About 10:42 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran International relays an NBC News report, citing two US officials and a person familiar with the matter, that the US and Iran have continued exchanging military strikes almost daily, with the Pentagon leaving many US operations publicly unacknowledged. ABC's 'new airstrikes on Iran' report (9:40 PM ET) still does not name a separate target, and no separate new US strike beyond Qeshm has been confirmed by a US official or major outlet as of about 11:10 PM ET; still no formal CENTCOM press release; As of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18: no new US strike on Iran confirmed by a US official or major outlet since the Qeshm strike; the ABC 'new airstrikes' report still has no separate named target; still no formal CENTCOM press release; As of about 1:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no formal CENTCOM release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials; 'US strikes Iranian missile site' headlines circulating overnight (Bloomberg/AFP relays) refer to this same Qeshm strike; As of about 2:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no formal CENTCOM release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials; As of about 3:00 AM ET Nov. 18: still no formal CENTCOM release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC and Iran's Army Navy say a supertanker and an LNG carrier caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC says two vessels it calls 'violators', a supertanker reportedly carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and a liquefied gas carrier, caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, Nov. 17 (Al Jazeera English, Al Araby TV, IRNA Arabic). Iran's Army Navy separately said an oil tanker that entered a restricted area east of the strait struck a mine and burst into flames, a statement Reuters reported citing state media; Iran International posted video of a burning tanker.
Middle East.status: Iranian claims only; vessel names, flags, crews and casualties not identified; no UKMTO, CENTCOM or shipowner confirmation of these mine strikes found in posts checked as of about 7:05 AM ET. Iranian state media frames the ships as unauthorized transits.; Nov. 17, about 8:53 AM ET: Fars quotes Iran's army navy as saying a third 'violating' tanker struck a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz today and caught fire. No vessel name, UKMTO notice or independent confirmation found in posts checked (Iranian claim); Nov. 17, about 10:16–10:50 AM ET: Iran's navy/IRGC, via Fars, now claims a fourth 'violating' tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours. No vessel name, UKMTO warning (latest seen 210-26) or independent confirmation found in posts checked (Iranian claim); Nov. 17, about 2:37–2:57 PM ET: IRNA and Sepah News carry a new IRGC Navy statement that a 'third violating vessel' on an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz exploded about an hour earlier after hitting a naval mine; Press TV says the tanker remains ablaze near Ghannam Island. Iranian claim only; no vessel name, UKMTO warning or independent confirmation found as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: Iran International reports Iran's Navy and the IRGC now say two more tankers struck mines and caught fire on Tuesday, bringing Iran's tally that day to four; the IRGC says the third hit a mine near Ghanam Island at 9:45 PM local time, and the Navy says a fourth was severely damaged east of the strait. Vessels and crews not named; Iranian claims only, no UKMTO confirmation found as of about 4:00 PM ET; carried forward from 2:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, West Bank

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO 208-26: LPG tanker TARA GAS struck a second time off Khasab; crew abandoned ship, one Indian seafarer missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16 evening: NDTV reports the Khasab tanker attack citing UKMTO; vessel still not identified and no responsibility claim found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:40 AM ET: India's shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and that all 25 crew are safe (PTI relays). Analyst Noam Raydan, citing Vanguard, identifies the vessel (IMO 9290270) as disabled with an engine-room fire and says at least 17 ship attacks have been reported in November. Attacker still not identified in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:40 to 4:05 AM ET: OSINT accounts post images of a large smoke column still rising Tuesday morning from the tanker struck about 13 km north of Khasab (unverified). Hindustan Times reports India's minister says all 24 Indian seafarers are safe. Iranian outlets relay an IRGC Navy claim of an explosion on a fourth tanker in 24 hours; no UKMTO warning beyond 208-26 found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:17 to 4:46 AM ET: UKMTO issued update 001 to warning 208-26. Iran International and JNS, summarizing the update, say the tanker first hit about 7 nm north of Khasab was struck a second time, causing another fire on board, and that the crew's status is unknown/unaccounted for after the second strike, citing a maritime security agency. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. threats.title: CONTINUATION: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. Still threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 17, about 5:48 AM ET: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the 'dirty bomb' allegations, attributed to the New York Times and spread by CNN, completely baseless and says enemies are trying to legitimize new aggression (Al Mayadeen). Still no DHS, FBI or NTAS bulletin found as of about 5:57 AM ET; only relays and explainers; Nov. 17, about 6:18 to 6:51 AM ET: Asked whether Iran poses an imminent threat to Washington, Trump said that if it does, 'they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' (Fox News); Al Arabiya English reports he said US authorities take any possible threat 'very seriously', and Faytuks Network, citing CBS, says Trump said the US is looking into the reported threat. Al Jazeera and Iran International report Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei denied the report as baseless; Iran International notes CNN said officials were divided on Tehran's capability and intent. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 7:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 8:07 AM ET: Al Arabiya English again reports Trump warning Iran it would 'pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' if it poses a threat to Washington. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 8:10 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 8:16–8:46 AM ET: New York Post and NewsNation report Trump, during his Asia trip, said the US takes a potential Iranian dirty-bomb threat 'very seriously because they happen to be crazy' and warned Tehran would 'pay a price.' Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 9:03–9:49 AM ET: Euronews and Iran International carry Trump's remarks in Manila that the threat is taken very seriously and Iran would pay an unprecedented price. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 10:08 AM ET; viral claims of a DHS Secretary war warning have no primary and are not logged; Nov. 17, about 10:40–11:04 AM ET: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf calls the claim that Iran planned to target senior Trump administration officials with a chemical weapon 'disinformation and fabrication' and incitement to war, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calls the reports 'RUBBISH' and Iraq War-style propaganda. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 11:10 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 11:31–11:45 AM ET: asked about the CNN report, President Trump said the US is taking seriously the possibility of an Iranian dirty-bomb plot in Washington (Reuters, BBC, Al Arabiya). Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 12:05 PM ET; Iran's parliament speaker and foreign minister continue to deny the report; Nov. 17, about 12:05–12:31 PM ET: CNN reports Trump said Iran would pay a major price if it detonated a dirty bomb in Washington; The Washington Times reports US officials held meetings on ways to counteract a potential Iranian plot against the homeland, while officials said there is no sign of an immediate threat. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 1:36 PM ET: Al Arabiya English reports Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi dismissed reports that Tehran is plotting a chemical-weapons attack in Washington, DC, and building missile bases beneath dams, calling them propaganda. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:31 PM ET: Axios reports President Trump warned Iran against orchestrating a 'dirty bomb' attack in Washington, D.C. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:19 PM ET: Iran's mission to the UN calls CNN's 'dirty bomb' report a 'fabricated narrative' and part of a disinformation campaign, and 'categorically rejects these baseless allegations'. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:24 PM ET: Iran International, citing IRGC-affiliated Tasnim, reports Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi called CNN's claim that Iran planned a chemical weapons attack in Washington a 'shameful lie'. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 5:05 PM ET; About 6:51 PM ET Nov. 17: CBS Evening News reports President Trump said, on arriving in the Philippines, that the US is 'looking in to' reports that Iran was developing plans for a potential dirty bomb targeting his administration. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found as of about 7:10 PM ET; As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new official statements beyond those already logged; still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; About 8:30–9:00 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed the CNN report, telling reporters he was not concerned about an imminent threat to Washington, D.C., that 'we have threat streams every day, the majority of them are not credible,' and calling media intelligence sources 'liars'. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; About 9:30–9:40 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran International quotes Secretary of State Rubio: 'I don't think there's any imminent threat,' expressing confidence in US intelligence agencies' ability to identify potential attacks; ABC World News Tonight reports President Trump says the US takes the dirty-bomb plot reports 'very seriously.' Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found; carried forward from 2:15 AM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FBI FLASH warns cybercriminals and state-aligned hackers are using ARTEX, an AI-driven autonomous hacking framework, to automate attacks on organizations worldwide
America.summary: FBI FLASH-20261113-001, dated Nov. 13, 2026, warns that cybercriminals and state-aligned actors are using ARTEX, an open-source, LLM-driven agentic penetration-testing platform, against financial, government, technology, defense, energy, healthcare, telecom and other sectors since at least August 2026, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours. Campaigns it cites include attacks on South Korean financial institutions (data on about 67,000 people exfiltrated) and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise (more than 2,250 downstream tenants). The developer pulled the GitHub repository on Oct. 8, 2026, but forks, archived copies and a commercial ARTEX PRO still circulate, and more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles were found in early November. BleepingComputer and The Record covered the advisory; today's X coverage comes from viral relays of the Nov. 13 FLASH.
America.status: Official statement issued (FBI FLASH, Nov. 13, 2026, ic3.gov); renewed media and viral coverage Nov. 17; no new FBI or CISA post on ARTEX found on X in this sweep; Nov. 17, about 3:24 PM ET: the FBI says the ARTEX cyber advisory was released Friday, Nov. 13, is not a new announcement, and no additional warning has been issued since; the guidance remains current. Stabilized; carried forward from 1:15 AM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Apple confirms an iCloud sign-in issue as users report problems with Apple Pay, the App Store, Gmail, Outlook/Microsoft 365 and Marriott; no evidence of a cyberattack
America.location: United States and global (consumer online services)
America.summary: Starting late Tuesday morning, Nov. 17, Downdetector logged user reports of problems with Apple Support from 11:45 AM ET and Apple Pay from 11:48 AM ET, and Breaking911 reported at 12:30 PM ET that users were also reporting outages at Gmail, Marriott, Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft 365. Apple's official system status page lists an ongoing 'iCloud Account & Sign In' issue ('This service may be slow or unavailable') that began at 8:45 AM PT (11:45 AM ET); as of about 1:00 PM ET no other Apple service, including Apple Pay, Wallet and the App Store, showed an event. Google's Workspace Status Dashboard shows no incident on Nov. 17, and no @MSFT365Status post about a new incident was found. Reuters reports President Trump shrugged off the spate of US outages, saying 'things like that happen'.
America.status: Apple confirms only the iCloud sign-in issue; other services rest on user reports and Downdetector spikes; cause unknown; no evidence of a cyberattack (posts tying this to the FAA, NSA and bank outages as a coordinated attack are unsupported and not logged); consumer services, not critical infrastructure. Re-check Apple status, MSFT365Status, Google dashboard and Downdetector; Nov. 17, about 1:11 PM ET: Al Arabiya English reports Downdetector user reports of problems with iCloud, Apple Pay, the Apple Store, App Store and Apple Business Manager. Apple's system status page checked at 2:03 PM ET lists 'iCloud Account & Sign In' as an ongoing issue since 08:45 PST, 'AppleCare on Device' purchases temporarily unavailable since 08:15 PST, and Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork as possibly slow or unavailable since 10:40 PST (1:40 PM ET); Apple Pay, App Store and Apple Music show no issue. Google's Workspace status feed shows no Nov. 17 incident. No evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 2:50 PM ET: an Apple spokesperson says many of its systems are back up after an internal update caused some outages this morning and it is working to restore the remaining systems. Apple's status page checked at 3:01 PM ET: iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, Apple Business, Apple School Manager, Schoolwork and AppleCare on Device still ongoing; App Store and Volume Purchase Program issues ongoing since 11:27 PST; iCloud Mail resolved. Apple attributes the disruption to an internal update; no evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 3:10 PM ET: NBC News reports Apple said it was having tech issues affecting several consumer services. Apple's status page checked at 3:58 PM ET: App Store and Volume Purchase Program issues resolved (ended 12:00 PST), AppleCare on Device resolved (12:39 PST); iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork still listed as ongoing. Apple attributes the disruption to an internal update; no evidence of a cyberattack; Nov. 17, about 4:15 PM ET: Fox News reports Apple is ruling out a cyberattack, saying an internal update triggered the disruptions and most services are restored. Apple's status page checked at about 5:03 PM ET: iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Web Apps, iCloud Mail and Schoolwork now resolved; Apple Business and Apple School Manager still ongoing, and a new intermittent Volume Purchase Program issue listed (from 1:11 PM PST). Largely stabilized; About 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: CBS News reports Apple has restored services after an internal update caused the outages. America.title: CONTINUATION: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)
America.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme reported malicious JavaScript being served through the Optimizely web experimentation platform to the websites of about 178 organizations, including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax and Ledger. He and security firm Coinspect say the payload included a crypto address swapper, a card skimmer, cookie theft and iOS exploit code; Helme says about $7,000 in crypto had been diverted. Optimizely says it identified and contained a security incident affecting some Web Experimentation customers, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the injected code and contacted customers. BleepingComputer reports the attack.
America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known; Nov. 17: Optimizely's notice says an 'unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation' (Infosecurity Magazine). Reuters (via the New York Post, about 9:30 AM ET) cites researcher Scott Helme and says it could not independently establish whether every affected site was successfully exploited; AFP (about 12:45 PM ET) says nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted. Report URI names the iOS exploit kits as Coruna and DarkSword and advises updating to iOS 18.7.3+ or 26.3+; Mediaite, citing Reuters, says Salesforce disabled the scripts, Equifax stopped using the platform and found no compromise, and IKEA is investigating. Report URI says all infected files were clean by 23:11 UTC Nov. 16 (6:11 PM ET). STABILIZED: contained; moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 1:15 AM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; carried forward from 1:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Drop Site News notes the Southern Bridge also carries a metro line, that explosions were reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Cherkasy, and that no casualties had been reported. Secondary accounts citing Kyiv Independent say strikes knocked out water and heat (and some power) in parts of the city.
