Middle East.title: UPDATE: US military official confirms US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defense after IRGC attacks on US forces; Iranian official says residential areas and infrastructure were not damaged
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: A US military official says US fighter aircraft used precision munitions earlier on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defense in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets (first reported by Axios' Barak Ravid, then Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera and, per Iran International, Reuters). Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. From about 9:09 AM ET Al Arabiya and Al Hadath cite unnamed Iranian media saying a US strike hit the Nariman air defense site; Al Arabiya English carries the same at about 9:39 AM ET. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. This is the first named Iranian official confirmation of a US strike, so the item is upgraded to HIGH. As of about 11:10 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; viral 'US official: the United States is attacking Qeshm' posts have no traceable primary and are not logged. Casualty claims (6 IRGC killed) remain unverified; the Osint613 post on a further round of explosions (10:10 AM ET) has since been deleted and its link removed; Nov. 17, about 11:37–11:54 AM ET: ISNA, Iran International Arabic, Al Arabiya and Annahar carry the same Iranian account. Nafisi says the situation on the island is under control and relief services are on high alert; Al Arabiya, citing Iranian media, says the target was the Nariman air-defense site and Fars residents reported several consecutive blasts northwest of Qeshm city with rising smoke, with no damage or casualty details. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. No IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; OSINT reports of missile launches inside Iran are listed separately as unconfirmed; Nov. 17, about 12:10–12:55 PM ET: international outlets (TRT World, Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera Arabic, Iran International Persian) carry the Iranian deputy governor's account; Iran International Persian says five to six explosions were heard in Qeshm city with smoke in the island's northwest, and IRGC-affiliated media say air-defense positions were targeted, with no independent damage report. Al-Monitor reports a top Iranian official warned that civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases would be considered 'dual use'. About 12:59–1:02 PM ET: OSINT accounts report another explosion on Qeshm; BeamTracker says it is most likely an anti-ship cruise missile launch from the island rather than an airstrike, and MintPress says it would be a third round of US strikes if confirmed; neither is confirmed. As of about 1:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X (a post claiming AFP as its source was not matched to any AFP post and is not logged). No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm confirmed; Nov. 17, about 1:54 PM ET: TRT Persian repeats Iran's statement that the US attack on Qeshm caused no damage to infrastructure. Persian-language accounts claim further explosions and casualties on Qeshm, but these are unverified and not logged. As of about 2:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X. No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; Nov. 17, about 2:25–2:50 PM ET: a US military official confirmed the strike. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. Low-credibility posts claiming a new Iranian attack on US bases in Bahrain or an IRGC statement of '550 Americans killed and wounded' have no primary source and are not logged; satellite-imagery claims that the radar was destroyed on Nov. 14 are unverified; As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Iranian drone and missile attacks on US bases in Bahrain seen only from low-credibility accounts, not logged. Kuwait's military separately reports engaging hostile drones (see Kuwait item); As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Bahrain attacks still only from low-credibility accounts, not logged; 7:15 PM ET UPDATE — renewed alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an 'alert of potential threat' at about 6:06 PM ET Nov. 17 (2:06 AM local Wednesday), urging people to stay calm and go to the nearest safe location; Al Arabiya's correspondent reported sirens, and blasts were reported. The ministry announced an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET. Bahrain News Agency reports the Arab League condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Bahrain; earlier the GCC secretary-general condemned repeated Iranian attacks. FaytuksNetwork's OSINT timeline puts this second Bahrain attack of the day at about 6:10 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on this wave, and no confirmed damage or casualties, as of about 7:10 PM ET; no formal IRGC claim for this wave found. Claims of a direct hit on Isa Air Base or US casualties (MintPress, DD_Geopolitics, MarioNawfal and others) are unverified and not logged; 8:15 PM ET UPDATE — third alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued another 'alert of potential threat' at about 7:48 PM ET Nov. 17 (3:48 AM local Wednesday), again urging people to go to the nearest safe location; Iran International notes it is the third such alert in less than 24 hours. About a minute later the Bahrain Defence Force General Command said Iran is continuing its 'systematic hostile approach' through attacks targeting the Kingdom. No all-clear from the Interior Ministry found as of about 8:05 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found; Iranian outlets such as Defa Press claim drones hit a US base in Bahrain, which is unverified. Ignored: Arabic and Persian relay claims of a 'direct hit' and large fires at Isa Air Base (no primary); 9:15 PM ET UPDATE: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17, ending the third alert of the night. The Bahrain News Agency (8:07 PM ET) carried the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses countered Iranian attacks; Anadolu reports Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks without specifying casualties or damage. Reuters: 'Bahrain issues all-clear after threat alert amid US-Iran exchanges of fire.' No new alert found as of about 9:05 PM ET; still no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found. A Civil Defence fire in a Souq Waqif building (moi_bahrain, no injuries, cause under investigation) is not linked to the attacks and is not logged; As of about 9:55 PM ET Nov. 17: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no new CENTCOM statement on the evening waves (CENTCOM's earlier statement called the IRGC radar-hit claim false, with all drones intercepted and no damage or injuries); no confirmed damage or casualties and no formal IRGC claim found; About 10:38 PM ET Nov. 17: KUNA carries the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses fended off several Iranian aerial attacks and that Iran continues its 'systematic approach' of attacks on Bahrain (same BDF statement as earlier this evening). No new Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; no confirmed damage or casualties and no new CENTCOM statement found as of about 11:10 PM ET; As of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18: no new Bahrain Interior Ministry alert since the 8:11 PM ET all-clear; viral claims of a new wave and impacts at Sheikh Isa (BedouinReport, IranArabicMedia) have no official primary and are not logged; no new CENTCOM statement and no confirmed damage/casualties; About 12:12 AM ET Nov. 18: Bahrain News Agency reports the Muslim Council of Elders strongly condemns the renewed Iranian attack on Bahrain. No new Interior Ministry alert, CENTCOM statement, or confirmed damage or casualties found as of about 1:00 AM ET; Iranian-media claims of new explosions at US bases in Bahrain are not confirmed and not logged

Earlier on Nov. 17 Houthi-run media reported Saudi airstrikes on northern Sanaa (see separate item)
Middle East.status: Early reports citing unnamed sources and residents, about 5:45 to 5:56 AM ET; cause and casualties unknown; Nov. 17, about 6:18 AM ET: Al Arabiya English, citing governorate sources, adds that explosions were heard at several Houthi barracks in Bani Jarmuz (Bani al-Harith district) following airstrikes on fortifications, tunnels and weapons depots. No coalition, US or Israeli statement and no Houthi casualty report found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Qatar says it will meet Iranian officials Tuesday as part of ongoing US–Iran mediation
Middle East.location: Doha, Qatar

Africa.status: Single security-source report published Nov. 17; no police or army statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:27 PM ET: the Mwaghavul Development Association says gunmen killed at least nine people in Zuwagal (Zuwakal), Mangu, days after a curfew was lifted; houses and food also destroyed in nearby Bong. Africa.summary: Vanguard reports that Senate Chief Whip Monguno and others escaped a suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. Details on casualties and the location of the attack were not in the post checked.

Africa.location: Bokkos, Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi areas, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Premium Times reports gunmen killed a Plateau State security commander and one other person; other reports say the Operation Rainbow commander was ambushed near Bokkos returning from a condolence visit. Africa.status: Developing; no police or state government casualty figure found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Market shooting in South Sudan reportedly kills 17 and wounds 23, Afropages says
Africa.location: South Sudan (market, location not specified in the post)
Africa.summary: Afropages reports that a shooting in a market in South Sudan killed 17 people and wounded 23. Mwanzo TV posted a headline saying 17 were killed in a South Sudan revenge attack. The exact location, date of the shooting and official confirmation were not given in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early, thinly sourced reports; location and official confirmation lacking; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kordofan Human Rights Observatory says a drone strike on Abu Qalb, West Kordofan, killed at least 15 civilians, including four children
Africa.summary: Radio Dabanga reports that at least 15 civilians, including four children, were killed in a drone strike on Abu Qalb in West Kordofan, according to the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory. The attacker was not identified in the post checked, and no official confirmation was seen.
Africa.status: Single rights-group report via Radio Dabanga; unconfirmed by official sources in this sweep; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Explosion and fire at an NNPC filling station in Ipaja, Lagos, spread to a neighboring school building
Africa.location: Command / Ajasa-Command area, Ipaja, Lagos State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: The Guardian Nigeria says an explosion at a filling station in the Ajasa-Command area of Ipaja triggered a fire, and that the cause and extent of damage are not yet known. WithinNigeria and other local accounts say the fire spread to a school building next to the station. One account says it happened during school hours and that everyone was reportedly safe; no casualties have been confirmed officially in posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports from several Nigerian outlets; cause and casualties unconfirmed; no official emergency agency statement seen; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Sun Nigeria and Instablog9ja say the fire spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School near Savannah Bus Stop in the Command/Ipaja area; firefighters contained the blaze and no casualties were reported in the posts checked. The earlier Guardian Nigeria post used in the prior entry no longer resolves; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Drone or air strike on a village in Abu Zabad, West Kordofan, Sudan, reported to kill 13 to 15 people, including children
Africa.location: Abu Qalb area, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, Sudan
Africa.summary: CGTN Europe quotes the Emergency Lawyers group as saying an airstrike on the Abu Qalb area of Abu Zabad locality killed 13 women and children, according to preliminary figures. News Central TV reports 15 people, including four children, were killed in a Sudanese military drone strike on a West Kordofan village. The Sudanese army had not commented in posts checked.
Africa.status: Reported by two outlets citing a rights group; tolls differ (13 vs 15); attribution to the army not confirmed by the military; Nov. 17, about 5:15 to 5:27 AM ET: The Sudan Doctors Network says a Sudanese army drone struck Abu Qulb in Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, killing at least 13 civilians and injuring others, and calls for an independent investigation (CGTN Europe). KUNA reports the UN Human Rights Office says more than 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan from January to the end of October 2026, more than 1,630 of them in drone strikes; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Bomb threat on Sandton Drive, Johannesburg: all-clear given and roads reopened
Africa.location: Sandton Drive near Alice Lane, Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa
Africa.summary: The Citizen reports law enforcement on the scene of a bomb threat in Sandton, and other accounts tell people to avoid Sandton Drive near Alice Lane. No device, evacuation scale or injuries were reported in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports; one established outlet; no police statement found in posts checked; Nov. 16: All-clear given about 15:46 local time per a community security update relaying the Gauteng JOC; eNCA reports the area around Sandton Drive and Alice Lane has reopened; News24 says the threat targeted an office building; no device or injuries reported; resolved, can drop from monitoring; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Two weekend mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 17 dead — nine in Jeffsville near Pretoria and eight in a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg
Africa.location: Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says nine people, six men and three women, were found shot dead inside a four-roomed shack in Jeffsville informal settlement. Police say the shooting is reported to have happened between 10 and 11 p.m. on Nov. 15 and that they were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Nov. 16. The motive has not been established and no arrests have been made; Yfm reports a manhunt is under way and SABC says the Gauteng police commissioner is at the scene.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; comes hours after the separate Sweetwaters (KZN) shooting that killed eight; Nov. 16: Channels TV says police put the toll from the Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters shootings at 17; Newzroom Afrika and Sowetan carry Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni saying one of the nine victims was a person of interest in a December 2025 mass shooting and linking the case to the Saulsville shooting; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: WPLG says at least 17 were killed in the two mass shootings about 330 miles apart and police have not established motives; Pretoria News says SAPS is probing a possible retaliation motive after confirming one victim was a person of interest in the Saulsville case (also EWN); eNCA reports Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi's condolences; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: Reuters, NBC News, Al Jazeera and BBC report at least 17 dead in two weekend mass shootings: nine in the shack near Pretoria and eight men found in a bullet-riddled vehicle near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal; police say motives not yet established and no arrests reported; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: SABC News on X (commissioner at scene)

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight people shot dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters outside Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.location: Mabane Section, Sweetwaters, Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says KwaZulu-Natal police are investigating the murder of eight people who were allegedly shot and killed inside a vehicle along the road at Mabane Section in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg. Daily News reports the eight men were killed on Sunday evening and that a murder investigation is under way. No motive or arrests have been announced.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Peter Obi condemns a reported attack on Kwankwaso's NDC convoy in Bichi, Kano State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Opposition presidential candidate Peter Obi says he is saddened by reports of an attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area. He calls for an immediate investigation and arrests. Kwankwaso had been commissioning NDC offices across Kano State on Sunday.
Africa.status: Early reports; party-side statement only; no police statement, casualty count or damage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya opens probe into violent protests at the Dadaab refugee complex
Africa.location: Hagadera camp, Dadaab, Garissa County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Anadolu reports that Kenyan authorities have opened an investigation after protesters opposing a planned market in Hagadera camp damaged government offices, stole equipment and broke into nearby businesses during clashes.
Africa.status: Single wire report citing authorities; casualty figures not reported; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. It cites Caasimada Online as saying forces loyal to a former South West state leader took Golweyn.
Africa.status: Single-source early report citing Caasimada Online; no official statement or claim of responsibility found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: JNIM reportedly overruns a national police detachment at Balga, near Fada N'Gourma, eastern Burkina Faso
Africa.location: Balga, about 25 km from Fada N’Gourma, Est region, Burkina Faso
Africa.summary: A Sahel-focused account reports that a JNIM attack on the morning of Nov. 15 targeted the National Police detachment at Balga, sacking and burning it, and that many officers were killed and several are missing. It adds that the attackers took all weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no official Burkinabe statement or casualty figure found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill a Zamfara governor's aide in a dawn attack in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits attacked worshippers at dawn prayer in Kaura Namoda on Sunday, Nov. 15, killing Nasiru Sani Kaura and abducting several others, according to the security platform Bakatsine (via Africa_lix). Nigerians_New reports he was an aide to Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal.
Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.

threats.title: CONTINUATION: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon

Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

BBC's John Simpson says the attacks began about 11:36 PM local time and he counted 10 or 11 explosions, with both bridges apparently hit, after President Zelensky warned of big strikes. Drop Site News notes the Southern Bridge also carries a metro line, that explosions were reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Cherkasy, and that no casualties had been reported. Secondary accounts citing Kyiv Independent say strikes knocked out water and heat (and some power) in parts of the city.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian drone attack on Ukraine — 117 drones launched, strikes at 24 locations; at least two killed, medical facility hit in Kyiv

Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iran's army claims its drones targeted US Patriot air defenses and drone and missile launchers at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait
Middle East.location: Ali Al Salem Air Base, Kuwait
Middle East.summary: Iran's regular army (Artesh) public relations office announced that in the early hours of Wednesday, Nov. 18 (Iran time), its combat and suicide drones targeted US Patriot air defense systems and US drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, according to Iran's state Press TV, Al Jazeera's breaking-news channel and Iran International. This is the first formal Iranian military claim of responsibility linked to the drone attacks Kuwait's armed forces reported engaging since about 4:39 PM ET Nov. 17. Relays of the statement quote the army warning that any response to aggression will be decisive and without geographical limits.
Middle East.status: Iranian military claim, published about 10:55–11:05 PM ET Nov. 17. No US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation of a hit, damage or casualties found as of about 11:10 PM ET; Kuwait has not named the attacker. Claim of targeting, not a confirmed hit; About 11:20–11:50 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran's official IRNA English service carries the army statement claiming its drones struck Patriot air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Base; Al Jazeera English and Drop Site News report the claim, noting Iran's army is separate from the IRGC and that there was no immediate word on damage or casualties. Still no US (CENTCOM/Pentagon) or Kuwaiti confirmation or denial of a hit, damage or casualties, and no new KuwaitArmyGHQ/KUNA statement found as of about 12:05 AM ET Nov. 18. Remains an Iranian military claim

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Kuwait's armed forces say air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks over Kuwait, hours after the US strike on Qeshm; attacker not officially named
Middle East.location: Kuwait (hosts major US bases incl. Camp Arifjan and Ali Al Salem)
Middle East.summary: Kuwait's state news agency KUNA reported about 4:46 PM ET Nov. 17 that the General Staff of the Kuwaiti Armed Forces announced its air defenses were actively engaging drone threats and urged the public to stay calm and follow safety instructions; the army said any explosions heard are interceptions. TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) cites Arabic sources reporting several explosions in Kuwait and says air-raid sirens sounded at US bases there — a claim. It comes hours after the US self-defense strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island (see Qeshm item).
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Kuwaiti military confirms an ongoing drone attack and interceptions; origin of the drones NOT officially confirmed (many accounts say Iranian drones, and some relays say the army named Iran, but the KUNA statement checked does not); no IRGC claim of responsibility, CENTCOM statement, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked. Unverified/not logged: claims of 5 IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site, claims of new attacks on US bases in Bahrain; Nov. 17, about 4:39 PM ET: the Kuwaiti Army General Staff's own account posted the statement that air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks and that any explosions heard are interceptions (no origin named). About 5:30–5:56 PM ET: Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) claims, citing local and Arab sources, renewed explosions in Kuwait and a video of a large fire at a US base in Kuwait; journalist Wladimir van Wilgenburg notes the Iraqi channel Naya claimed a US base in Kuwait was targeted with drones — all claims, unconfirmed. As of about 6:00 PM ET: still no formal IRGC statement claiming the attack found, no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties, and Kuwait has not named the attacker. Viral 'direct hit on US base' videos and lists of bases hit come from low-credibility accounts and are not logged; As of about 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: still no Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage/casualties, no new Kuwait Army or KUNA posts since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET statements, and no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement.
