Middle East.title: UPDATE: US military official confirms US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defense after IRGC attacks on US forces; Iranian official says residential areas and infrastructure were not damaged
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: A US military official says US fighter aircraft used precision munitions earlier on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defense in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets (first reported by Axios' Barak Ravid, then Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera and, per Iran International, Reuters). Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. From about 9:09 AM ET Al Arabiya and Al Hadath cite unnamed Iranian media saying a US strike hit the Nariman air defense site; Al Arabiya English carries the same at about 9:39 AM ET. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. This is the first named Iranian official confirmation of a US strike, so the item is upgraded to HIGH. As of about 11:10 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; viral 'US official: the United States is attacking Qeshm' posts have no traceable primary and are not logged. Casualty claims (6 IRGC killed) remain unverified; the Osint613 post on a further round of explosions (10:10 AM ET) has since been deleted and its link removed; Nov. 17, about 11:37–11:54 AM ET: ISNA, Iran International Arabic, Al Arabiya and Annahar carry the same Iranian account. Nafisi says the situation on the island is under control and relief services are on high alert; Al Arabiya, citing Iranian media, says the target was the Nariman air-defense site and Fars residents reported several consecutive blasts northwest of Qeshm city with rising smoke, with no damage or casualty details. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. No IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; OSINT reports of missile launches inside Iran are listed separately as unconfirmed; Nov. 17, about 12:10–12:55 PM ET: international outlets (TRT World, Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera Arabic, Iran International Persian) carry the Iranian deputy governor's account; Iran International Persian says five to six explosions were heard in Qeshm city with smoke in the island's northwest, and IRGC-affiliated media say air-defense positions were targeted, with no independent damage report. Al-Monitor reports a top Iranian official warned that civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases would be considered 'dual use'. About 12:59–1:02 PM ET: OSINT accounts report another explosion on Qeshm; BeamTracker says it is most likely an anti-ship cruise missile launch from the island rather than an airstrike, and MintPress says it would be a third round of US strikes if confirmed; neither is confirmed. As of about 1:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X (a post claiming AFP as its source was not matched to any AFP post and is not logged). No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm confirmed; Nov. 17, about 1:54 PM ET: TRT Persian repeats Iran's statement that the US attack on Qeshm caused no damage to infrastructure. Persian-language accounts claim further explosions and casualties on Qeshm, but these are unverified and not logged. As of about 2:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X. No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; Nov. 17, about 2:25–2:50 PM ET: a US military official confirmed the strike. Axios' Barak Ravid quotes the official: 'Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense,' in response to 'IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets.' Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera, Iran International (citing Reuters) and Ynet report the same official account. Independent Persian says Tasnim, citing provincial officials, confirmed the blasts heard on Qeshm were US strikes, described as a response to the IRGC drone attack on Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base. No formal CENTCOM press release seen on X as of about 3:05 PM ET; damage and casualties not officially reported (claims that six IRGC personnel were killed are unverified and not logged); no IRGC retaliation against US forces confirmed so far. Now a confirmed US strike on Iranian territory; Nov. 17, about 2:30–2:35 PM ET: more Pentagon reporters (Libbey Dean, Al Jazeera's Fadi Mansour) carry the same US military official statement: US fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense. As of about 4:00 PM ET there is still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (six IRGC killed, 'martyrs' on Qeshm) remain unverified and not logged; no confirmed IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states (an IRGC spokesman threat against Bahrain's rulers seen only via relays, not logged); As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement found on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (e.g. five IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site) unverified and not logged. Iran's retaliation remains unclaimed by any primary IRGC source (see the Kuwait and Bahrain items); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release (no CENTCOM posts since 7:05 PM ET), and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; relays describing 'fresh airstrikes' refer to the same strike; About 9:40 PM ET Nov. 17: ABC World News Tonight says that with Iranian attacks on commercial ships intensifying in the Strait of Hormuz, 'the U.S. has launched new airstrikes on Iran'; the post does not name targets beyond the Qeshm strike already reported. Middle East.summary: Citing Iran's state Press TV, accounts report the IRGC Aerospace Force says it used electronic warfare to seize another American MQM-170 drone over waters south of Qeshm Island and land it undamaged, which it says makes nine captured. This is an Iranian state claim.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Palestinian woman killed and 10 wounded by what Palestinian TV calls Israeli settler gunfire in Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho
Middle East.location: Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, West Bank
Middle East.summary: Reuters reports Palestinian official television said a Palestinian woman was killed and 10 others wounded by what it described as gunfire from Israeli settlers in Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho. Haaretz reports the Palestinian account alongside the IDF's report of the attack on Israelis in the same area earlier Monday.
Middle East.status: Palestinian official account reported by Reuters and Haaretz; no IDF statement on the shooting found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: the IDF says that on the outskirts of Jericho, attackers rammed an Israeli vehicle, then got out with weapons and attacked the occupants; rocks were thrown and the Israelis fired 'to remove the threat,' with Israeli and Palestinian casualties. Forces are pursuing suspects and setting up roadblocks. i24NEWS reports two Israelis injured in a suspected terror attack outside Jericho and a Palestinian woman shot dead. The accounts conflict: Palestinian sources describe settler gunfire, while the IDF describes a ramming attack; Nov. 17, about 1:40 AM ET: Reuters reports a Palestinian woman killed and 10 wounded in settler gunfire, citing official Palestinian TV; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: CENTCOM confirms the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group is operating in the Middle East, giving the US three carriers in the region
Middle East.location: US Central Command area of responsibility (Middle East)
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English and Kuwait's state news agency KUNA report that US Central Command confirmed the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt is operating in the Middle East as part of a scheduled deployment. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO 208-26: LPG tanker TARA GAS struck a second time off Khasab; crew abandoned ship, one Indian seafarer missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16 evening: NDTV reports the Khasab tanker attack citing UKMTO; vessel still not identified and no responsibility claim found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:40 AM ET: India's shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and that all 25 crew are safe (PTI relays). Analyst Noam Raydan, citing Vanguard, identifies the vessel (IMO 9290270) as disabled with an engine-room fire and says at least 17 ship attacks have been reported in November. Attacker still not identified in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:40 to 4:05 AM ET: OSINT accounts post images of a large smoke column still rising Tuesday morning from the tanker struck about 13 km north of Khasab (unverified). Hindustan Times reports India's minister says all 24 Indian seafarers are safe. Iranian outlets relay an IRGC Navy claim of an explosion on a fourth tanker in 24 hours; no UKMTO warning beyond 208-26 found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:17 to 4:46 AM ET: UKMTO issued update 001 to warning 208-26. Iran International and JNS, summarizing the update, say the tanker first hit about 7 nm north of Khasab was struck a second time, causing another fire on board, and that the crew's status is unknown/unaccounted for after the second strike, citing a maritime security agency. This conflicts with India's earlier statement that all crew were safe (that statement preceded the second strike). Attacker not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 5:02 to 5:40 AM ET: India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said TARA GAS, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and the whole 25-member crew was safe. In an update he says the tanker was attacked again, forcing the entire crew to abandon ship; 24 crew are safely accounted for and one Indian seafarer is missing, and India is coordinating with the ship manager and regional rescue authorities. No US Navy involvement and no new UKMTO notice found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:03 AM ET: India's embassy in Muscat says 24 of the 25 crew of the Panama-flagged VLGC TARA GAS (24 of them Indian) have been evacuated ashore at Khasab and search-and-rescue operations continue for one missing Indian crew member, with Omani support; Nov. 17, about 8:55 AM ET: India strongly condemns the attack on MT TARA GAS; 21 Indian nationals were evacuated, two injured crew are hospitalised and one remains missing, with India's MEA coordinating with Omani authorities on search and rescue (as reported by News18); Nov. 17, about 10:46 AM ET: summarizing Indian officials, OSINTdefender says India confirmed the second attack on TARA GAS; Shipping Minister Sonowal says the crew abandoned the vessel, 24 of 25 are accounted for and one Indian seafarer is still missing. India's Ministry of External Affairs says two injured Indian crew are in hospital and the rest were evacuated ashore at Khasab, Oman. Attacker still not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 3:24–3:57 PM ET: The National reports India's Foreign Ministry confirmed 21 crew were safely evacuated, two hospitalized and one unaccounted for; Drop Site, citing Maritime Executive, says the abandoned carrier is at risk of exploding (Indian officials say a missile hit it, Maritime Executive says an IRGC drone, Iranian media say a mine); Sky News shows footage of the abandoned tanker engulfed in flames off Khasab; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iraq orders forces into Kataib Hezbollah's Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold with a deadline after an oil-smuggling probe; the Iran-backed militia vows to keep its weapons
Middle East.location: Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), Babil province, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Rudaw reports Iraqi government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi said Iraqi forces are preparing to enter the militia-held town of Jurf al-Sakhar, with Baghdad setting a deadline for the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah. Al Jazeera English says forces were ordered in following oil-smuggling allegations, which the group denies, calling the crackdown an attempt to seize its weapons. Kataib Hezbollah posted that its weapons 'will remain in the hands of our Mujahideen' with photos of fighters setting up drones (Rudaw). Kurdistan24 and a Rudaw journalist report a tense Coordination Framework meeting, with Prime Minister al-Zaidi walking out over the dispute.
Middle East.status: Official Iraqi government statements reported by Rudaw and Al Jazeera; no clashes reported in posts checked; standoff developing; Nov. 16 night: The New Arab quotes Iraqi security expert Hashim al-Saadi saying Kataib Hezbollah and its allies are unlikely to give up Jurf al-Sakhar easily; no clashes or entry by government forces reported in posts checked; Nov. 16 night: Iran International, citing Al Arabiya sources, says an Iranian delegation arrived in Baghdad for talks to defuse the Iraqi government–Kataib Hezbollah standoff over Jurf al-Sakhar. Some Coordination Framework leaders have proposed replacing Kataib Hezbollah fighters with shrine-affiliated PMF units as a compromise. No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17 early: The New Arab says Kataib Hezbollah denies involvement in oil smuggling from Jurf al-Sakhar; Channel8, citing sources, says the group opposes bloodshed and that mediation is under way. No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:03 AM ET: Al Arabiya English, citing AFP, says a Kataib Hezbollah commander said the group will not leave its Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold despite Iraqi authorities' call to withdraw and let the army enter. No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 9:01 AM ET: Iraq's parliament speaker, addressing Kataib Hezbollah, says 'there is no armed party above the law.' No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 9:50 AM ET: an Iraqi official tells Al Jazeera that IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani has arrived in Iraq and met the prime minister and political leaders to push for a deal ending the Jurf al-Sakhar standoff; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi health officials say Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Omran province killed three, including a child
Middle East.location: Sanaa and Harf Sufian (Omran province), Yemen
Middle East.summary: The Tectonic, citing the AP, says a Houthi health ministry spokesman reported that a drone strike on a house in Sanaa's al-Sarar quarter killed a child and wounded seven, and that airstrikes on a private fuel station in Harf Sufian district killed two and wounded eight. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iranian media say air-defence systems were activated over Isfahan; local security official says no hostile aircraft was detected
Middle East.location: Isfahan, Iran
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English says air-defence systems were activated in Iran's central city of Isfahan, according to Mehr news agency, with no further details reported. Middle East.status: Single-agency report via Al Jazeera; cause of the activation unconfirmed; Nov. 16 evening: Al Jazeera and Reuters report an Isfahan security official said no hostile aircraft was detected in Iran's airspace after air-defence systems were activated. Viral claims of US-Israeli strikes on Isfahan are unsupported by any official or major-outlet report and are excluded. Stabilized; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, occupied West Bank
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English, citing local sources, says at least eight Palestinians were injured after an Israeli settler allegedly rammed a vehicle into them in the town of Tuqu, south of Bethlehem. Eye on Palestine reported the same account from southeast of Bethlehem.
Middle East.status: Early reports from Al Jazeera and local accounts; Israeli official comment not seen in posts checked; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 207-26 on Monday. Arab News and other outlets citing UKMTO say a tanker leaving the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile, setting its engine room on fire. Drop Site News, citing UKMTO, puts the strike at 05:58 UTC and says no casualties were reported and all crew are accounted for.

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Rare overnight Israeli strike in Lebanon's eastern Beqaa Valley near the Syrian border
Middle East.location: Beqaa Valley near the Lebanon–Syria border
Middle East.summary: Lebanese media report an overnight Israeli Air Force strike near the Lebanon-Syria border in the eastern Beqaa Valley, the first in that area in several months. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Yemeni government forces withdraw from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Reuters says Houthis in control
Middle East.location: Dhubab and Bab el-Mandeb area, Taiz/Lahj, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters reported Sunday that forces fighting for Yemen's internationally recognized government withdrew from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. Yemen's armed forces told Al Arabiya the redeployment reflects reprioritized objectives and aims to break the siege of Taiz. Al Jazeera says the Houthi advance threatens one of the government's last strongholds and brings fighting closer to the shipping route.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by government forces' statements and Reuters; no attacks on shipping linked to the withdrawal found in posts checked; extent of Houthi control along the coast unclear; Nov. 16: Anadolu Arabic reports the army foiled a Houthi attack in Taiz, cites two rights groups documenting 319 civilians killed or injured since September, and notes Houthi accusations of Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Saada with no Riyadh comment; Houthi-aligned YNP reports Saudi strikes on Sabr district south of Taiz city for the first time in weeks after a Houthi advance there (partisan source); Nov. 16 evening: Al Jazeera English says the Houthis have claimed control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait; Houthi claim, extent of control not independently confirmed; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Indian Ocean, 430 nm east of Socotra, Yemen

Middle East.status: UKMTO warning issued; suspicious approach, no boarding reported; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sirik and Kong, Hormozgan province, and in Shahriyar near Tehran; cause unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran
Middle East.summary: Several accounts reported explosions heard in Sirik in Iran's southern Hormozgan province on Sunday afternoon, citing Al Mihwar News and Iranian media. Other accounts said an explosion in Kong, also near the Strait of Hormuz, was linked to the targeting of an Iranian surface-to-air missile launcher. Separate reports describe an explosion in Shahriyar, west of Tehran.
Middle East.status: Early reports; claims that US forces struck air-defense launchers are speculation, and no official US or Iranian statement on a strike, damage or casualties was found; Nov. 15 evening: HormuzLetter and AI313_ say, citing only 'initial reports', that the US struck Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik; still no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Iranian official confirmation found, so the attribution remains unverified; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC Navy says two tankers hit naval mines on the 'unauthorized' southern Hormuz route Sunday and claims one supertanker sank
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: The IRGC Navy says two oil tankers that had switched off their tracking systems struck naval mines on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours, caught fire after large explosions, and that one, carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, sank. It released footage it says shows the explosions. The vessels have not been named, and it is unclear whether either is the tanker in UKMTO warning 205-26.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only, relayed by Tehran Times, The Cradle, FirstSquawk and ME Observer; not independently confirmed in posts checked; earlier IRGC tanker-mine claims in this log also remain unverified; Nov. 15 night: the IRGC Navy now claims two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire, saying six tankers have caught fire or sunk since Saturday (Iran International citing Iranian state media; Press TV). No confirmation from UKMTO, CENTCOM or ship operators found; ship names not given, so the claim remains unverified; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Tectonic, citing IRIB, says Iranian naval forces claimed three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, that the IRGC Navy again said six tankers have caught fire or are sinking since Sunday, and that a claimed sinking video shows fire on the water with no clearly visible vessel; ship names still not given and the claims remain unverified; Nov. 17 early: Persian-language outlets relay an IRGC Navy statement claiming a fourth oil tanker in 24 hours exploded after hitting a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; vessel not named; IRGC claim only, no UKMTO, CENTCOM or shipowner confirmation found; carried forward from 11:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. threats.title: CONTINUATION: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. Still threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 17, about 5:48 AM ET: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the 'dirty bomb' allegations, attributed to the New York Times and spread by CNN, completely baseless and says enemies are trying to legitimize new aggression (Al Mayadeen). Still no DHS, FBI or NTAS bulletin found as of about 5:57 AM ET; only relays and explainers; Nov. 17, about 6:18 to 6:51 AM ET: Asked whether Iran poses an imminent threat to Washington, Trump said that if it does, 'they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' (Fox News); Al Arabiya English reports he said US authorities take any possible threat 'very seriously', and Faytuks Network, citing CBS, says Trump said the US is looking into the reported threat. Al Jazeera and Iran International report Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei denied the report as baseless; Iran International notes CNN said officials were divided on Tehran's capability and intent. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 7:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 8:07 AM ET: Al Arabiya English again reports Trump warning Iran it would 'pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' if it poses a threat to Washington. America.title: CONTINUATION: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)
America.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme reported malicious JavaScript being served through the Optimizely web experimentation platform to the websites of about 178 organizations, including Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax and Ledger. He and security firm Coinspect say the payload included a crypto address swapper, a card skimmer, cookie theft and iOS exploit code; Helme says about $7,000 in crypto had been diverted. Optimizely says it identified and contained a security incident affecting some Web Experimentation customers, blocked the vulnerable path, removed the injected code and contacted customers. BleepingComputer reports the attack.
America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known; Nov. 17: Optimizely's notice says an 'unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation' (Infosecurity Magazine). Reuters (via the New York Post, about 9:30 AM ET) cites researcher Scott Helme and says it could not independently establish whether every affected site was successfully exploited; AFP (about 12:45 PM ET) says nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, were targeted. Report URI names the iOS exploit kits as Coruna and DarkSword and advises updating to iOS 18.7.3+ or 26.3+; Mediaite, citing Reuters, says Salesforce disabled the scripts, Equifax stopped using the platform and found no compromise, and IKEA is investigating. Report URI says all infected files were clean by 23:11 UTC Nov. 16 (6:11 PM ET). STABILIZED: contained; moving to routine coverage; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported; Nov. 17: Quartz reports the White House formed a multi-agency team to prevent a repeat of the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop; Nov. 17, about 11:21–11:34 AM ET: The Wall Street Journal (via LiveSquawk and Al Jazeera) reports the FAA has paused router installations after the nationwide ground stop; Al Jazeera's summary says the routers were behind the disruption; Nov. 17, about 1:56 PM ET: AP reports the FAA itself said installation of the routers linked to last week's nationwide ground stop has been paused, confirming the earlier WSJ report. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 2:56 PM ET: Al Jazeera reports the US Transportation Secretary says the root cause of Friday's air-traffic routing equipment failure has not yet been determined. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 3:35–3:42 PM ET: Transportation Secretary Duffy says intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack but the FBI has joined the investigation; the root cause of the router malfunction is still unclear. Stabilized; About 8:30 PM ET Nov. 17: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the government has 'zero evidence' linking the past week's outages (Microsoft, the FAA, major banks), and no indication that any were caused by hackers, criminals, foreign actors or a malign insider; About 9:19 PM ET Nov. 17: BBC reports Rubio said the US is not 'under systemic attack' after the series of tech outages. Stabilized; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Europe.summary: Moldova restricted its entire national airspace at 16:27 local time (about 9:27 AM ET) on Tuesday, Nov. 17, after a drone was detected heading toward Chisinau, the Moldovan Ministry of Defense said. President Maia Sandu said a Russian drone flew over the capital, alarming residents, and that Moldova will press for more sanctions on Moscow. OSINT accounts identified it as a Geran-2 (Shahed-type) drone that crossed into Moldova twice from Ukraine's Odesa region during large-scale Russian strikes on Ukraine.

Moldova's Ministry of Defense reported restricting the country's entire airspace after detecting a drone heading toward Chisinau (Militarnyi), and President Maia Sandu said a Russian drone flew over the capital and Moldova will press for more sanctions on Moscow (CGTN). Faytuks reports police logged three emergency calls between 5:09 and 5:35 p.m. local time about an unexploded drone near Pohorniceni (Orhei district) and loud explosions near Cheltuitori and Cuhureștii de Sus, and bomb disposal teams were sent; those details are not yet confirmed by officials in posts checked. Upgraded to MEDIUM; Nov. 17, about 12:24–12:40 PM ET: Aviation News, citing Moldova's Civil Aviation Authority, says the central sector reopened to civil flights at 17:03 local (about 10:03 AM ET) after the 16:27 closure, and a FlyOne flight held near the Romanian border for about 30 minutes. UNITED24 says President Sandu condemned the incursion. No casualties reported; Nov. 17, about 2:10 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent, citing Moldova's Defense Ministry, reports seven drones crossed into Moldovan airspace during the latest Russian attack and a Shahed-type drone was spotted over Chisinau; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

BBC's John Simpson says the attacks began about 11:36 PM local time and he counted 10 or 11 explosions, with both bridges apparently hit, after President Zelensky warned of big strikes. Drop Site News notes the Southern Bridge also carries a metro line, that explosions were reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Cherkasy, and that no casualties had been reported. Secondary accounts citing Kyiv Independent say strikes knocked out water and heat (and some power) in parts of the city.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Kuwait's armed forces say air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks over Kuwait, hours after the US strike on Qeshm; attacker not officially named

TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) cites Arabic sources reporting several explosions in Kuwait and says air-raid sirens sounded at US bases there — a claim. It comes hours after the US self-defense strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island (see Qeshm item).
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Kuwaiti military confirms an ongoing drone attack and interceptions; origin of the drones NOT officially confirmed (many accounts say Iranian drones, and some relays say the army named Iran, but the KUNA statement checked does not); no IRGC claim of responsibility, CENTCOM statement, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked. Viral 'direct hit on US base' videos and lists of bases hit come from low-credibility accounts and are not logged; As of about 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: still no Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage/casualties, no new Kuwait Army or KUNA posts since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET statements, and no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Middle East.summary: The Saudi-led coalition's spokesman, Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, said on Tuesday, Nov. 17, that coalition forces intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen's Houthis toward the Riyadh region. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Saudi airstrike on a sponge factory in Hodeidah, Yemen, kills at least seven, Houthi health ministry says (via AP)

The strike follows Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Omran reported earlier. There is no Saudi-led coalition statement so far.

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Protest in Abdanan, Ilam province, Iran, after a bus crash that killed 13; security forces reportedly fire into the air and use tear gas
Middle East.location: Abdanan, Ilam province, Iran (protests also reported in Abadan)
Middle East.summary: IRGC-affiliated Fars says a protest began Tuesday, Nov. 17, in Abdanan's Vali-Asr square over a bus crash that killed 13 people, growing from 200–300 to about 1,000 people, and says some tried to damage public property before police intervened. Eyewitnesses told Iran International that security forces on motorcycles fired into the air and used tear gas to disperse protesters. Videos shared by OSINT accounts show protesters tearing down an IRGC/Basij banner and chanting anti-regime and pro-Pahlavi slogans, and separate footage shows crowds protesting in Abadan in the southwest.
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 10:08 AM ET; casualty and arrest figures not reported; Nov. 17, about 10:20–10:39 AM ET: Iran International says videos show hundreds chanting pro-monarchy slogans ('Pahlavi will return'); it relays Fars as saying the crowd moved into surrounding streets, some slogans became 'political', police were deployed and the protest was continuing. No casualty or arrest figures reported; Nov. 17, about 12:50 PM ET: Iran International says protesters are again on the streets of Abdanan chanting anti-regime and pro-monarchy slogans. No casualty or arrest figures reported; Nov. 17, about 3:50 PM ET: Iran International, citing rights groups Hana and Kurdpa, reports at least six people arrested, including a 15-year-old; Kurdpa reports riot police deployed, severe internet disruptions, tear gas and pellet guns used against protesters; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: US military official confirms US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defense after IRGC attacks on US forces; Iranian official says residential areas and infrastructure were not damaged
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: A US military official says US fighter aircraft used precision munitions earlier on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defense in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets (first reported by Axios' Barak Ravid, then Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera and, per Iran International, Reuters). Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. From about 9:09 AM ET Al Arabiya and Al Hadath cite unnamed Iranian media saying a US strike hit the Nariman air defense site; Al Arabiya English carries the same at about 9:39 AM ET. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. This is the first named Iranian official confirmation of a US strike, so the item is upgraded to HIGH. As of about 11:10 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; viral 'US official: the United States is attacking Qeshm' posts have no traceable primary and are not logged. Casualty claims (6 IRGC killed) remain unverified; the Osint613 post on a further round of explosions (10:10 AM ET) has since been deleted and its link removed; Nov. 17, about 11:37–11:54 AM ET: ISNA, Iran International Arabic, Al Arabiya and Annahar carry the same Iranian account. Nafisi says the situation on the island is under control and relief services are on high alert; Al Arabiya, citing Iranian media, says the target was the Nariman air-defense site and Fars residents reported several consecutive blasts northwest of Qeshm city with rising smoke, with no damage or casualty details. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. No IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; OSINT reports of missile launches inside Iran are listed separately as unconfirmed; Nov. 17, about 12:10–12:55 PM ET: international outlets (TRT World, Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera Arabic, Iran International Persian) carry the Iranian deputy governor's account; Iran International Persian says five to six explosions were heard in Qeshm city with smoke in the island's northwest, and IRGC-affiliated media say air-defense positions were targeted, with no independent damage report. Al-Monitor reports a top Iranian official warned that civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases would be considered 'dual use'. About 12:59–1:02 PM ET: OSINT accounts report another explosion on Qeshm; BeamTracker says it is most likely an anti-ship cruise missile launch from the island rather than an airstrike, and MintPress says it would be a third round of US strikes if confirmed; neither is confirmed. As of about 1:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X (a post claiming AFP as its source was not matched to any AFP post and is not logged). No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm confirmed; Nov. 17, about 1:54 PM ET: TRT Persian repeats Iran's statement that the US attack on Qeshm caused no damage to infrastructure. Persian-language accounts claim further explosions and casualties on Qeshm, but these are unverified and not logged. As of about 2:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X. No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; Nov. 17, about 2:25–2:50 PM ET: a US military official confirmed the strike. Axios' Barak Ravid quotes the official: 'Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense,' in response to 'IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets.' Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera, Iran International (citing Reuters) and Ynet report the same official account. Independent Persian says Tasnim, citing provincial officials, confirmed the blasts heard on Qeshm were US strikes, described as a response to the IRGC drone attack on Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base. No formal CENTCOM press release seen on X as of about 3:05 PM ET; damage and casualties not officially reported (claims that six IRGC personnel were killed are unverified and not logged); no IRGC retaliation against US forces confirmed so far. Now a confirmed US strike on Iranian territory; Nov. 17, about 2:30–2:35 PM ET: more Pentagon reporters (Libbey Dean, Al Jazeera's Fadi Mansour) carry the same US military official statement: US fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense. As of about 4:00 PM ET there is still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (six IRGC killed, 'martyrs' on Qeshm) remain unverified and not logged; no confirmed IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states (an IRGC spokesman threat against Bahrain's rulers seen only via relays, not logged); As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement found on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (e.g. five IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site) unverified and not logged. About 4:46 PM ET Kuwait's military said its air defenses were engaging hostile drone attacks (attacker not officially named) — see the Kuwait item; As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release or Pentagon/White House statement on the strike found on X (CENTCOM account search since 4:00 PM ET returned nothing); no confirmed further US strikes; Iranian casualty claims still unconfirmed. Kuwait drone attack (possible retaliation) remains unattributed by Kuwait — see Kuwait item; About 6:42 PM ET Nov. 17: euronews reports that Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island. As of about 7:10 PM ET: still no formal CENTCOM press release found; no further US strikes confirmed by US officials. Iran's retaliation remains unclaimed by any primary IRGC source (see the Kuwait and Bahrain items); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release (no CENTCOM posts since 7:05 PM ET), and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; relays describing 'fresh airstrikes' refer to the same strike; About 9:40 PM ET Nov. 17: ABC World News Tonight says that with Iranian attacks on commercial ships intensifying in the Strait of Hormuz, 'the U.S. has launched new airstrikes on Iran'; the post does not name targets beyond the Qeshm strike already reported. Still no formal CENTCOM press release on the Qeshm strike (CENTCOM/Pentagon account search since 4:00 PM ET found nothing new), and no separate additional US strike confirmed by US officials; About 10:42 PM ET Nov. 17: Iran International relays an NBC News report, citing two US officials and a person familiar with the matter, that the US and Iran have continued exchanging military strikes almost daily, with the Pentagon leaving many US operations publicly unacknowledged. ABC's 'new airstrikes on Iran' report (9:40 PM ET) still does not name a separate target, and no separate new US strike beyond Qeshm has been confirmed by a US official or major outlet as of about 11:10 PM ET; still no formal CENTCOM press release
