Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source

A widely shared post claims Eritrea's government announced that Ethiopia has invaded, but another account says the ministry accused Ethiopia of "preparing aggression." No independent confirmation of cross-border fighting was found.
Africa.status: Early reports; contested framing; no Ethiopian government response or independent confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Deadly clash during anti-illegal-mining operation at Manso Keniago, Ghana; Citi FM reports four dead and 15 injured
Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A confrontation broke out on Wednesday (Nov. 11) between personnel of Ghana's National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents and suspected illegal miners as the task force removed seized excavators at Manso Keniago. NAIMOS, as reported by TV3/3News, says two of its personnel were shot and injured by an armed mob. Death tolls in reports range from two to four; Citi FM's latest report says four dead and 15 injured.
Africa.status: Casualty figures differ between outlets (two, three, then four dead); circumstances, including who fired the fatal shots, not established in posts checked; NAIMOS statement covers its two injured personnel; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Mandera ambush kills eight — Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, blames suspected al-Shabaab
Africa.location: Hagarsu, Arabia Road, Mandera County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, reports eight people — two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver — were killed Tuesday in northeast Kenya near the Somali border in an attack by suspected al-Shabaab militants. Kahawa Tungu and Nairobi News, citing police, place the ambush at Hagarsu along Arabia Road in Mandera County, targeting workers on the Arabia–Lafey road construction project. No group has claimed responsibility.
Africa.status: Confirmed by police (Reuters, Citizen TV, CGTN Africa); suspected al-Shabaab per officials; no claim of responsibility found; NTV Kenya says Mandera legislators are demanding security reinforcement along the Somali border after the attack; Voice of Horn reports Kenyan police now say they are treating the ambush as banditry rather than a terror attack, that the attackers crossed into Somalia with two stolen AK-47s, and that no arrests have been made (single outlet in posts checked); Prime Media Kenya reports the eight dead were five construction workers, two police reservists and a driver, and that attackers stole the officers' rifles and fled toward Somalia; Somalia's federal government, via state news agency SONNA, condemned the attack and offered condolences; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: AFP now says 39 migrants died in the Nov. 6 boat sinking off Senegal
Africa.summary: AFP reports 39 people died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal on Nov. 6, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years, as families mourn. Reuters earlier carried a government figure of at least 21 dead, and Al Jazeera English said the Interior Ministry called its toll provisional.
Africa.status: Toll raised to 39 per AFP (earlier official provisional figure at least 21); figures differ by source; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: UNHCR says nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year
Africa.summary: Reuters reports nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for neighbouring Niger this year, escaping attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to the UN refugee agency. It says the arrivals add to mounting humanitarian needs in Niger.
Africa.status: UN agency figure via Reuters; ongoing displacement; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudan: UNICEF says 15 power stations hit in October as drone strikes spread; rights group says RSF drone attack on displaced people in Blue Nile's Al-Kurmuk killed 16
Africa.summary: UN News reports UNICEF's James Elder said 15 power stations were hit in October alone as long-range drone strikes and drought threaten survival in Sudan. Arab News reports the UN says two thirds of children killed or injured in Sudan this year were victims of drone strikes. Wasl News reports an RSF drone attack killed nine civilians in a Blue Nile village on Tuesday; that toll is not independently confirmed.
Africa.status: UN agency statements; Blue Nile casualty report from a single regional outlet, unverified; ongoing conflict; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the toll from an RSF drone attack on displaced people in Bani Shako village, Al-Kurmuk (Blue Nile), has risen to 16; it is not confirmed whether this is the same attack Wasl News reported with nine dead; rights-group figure, not independently verified; Africa_lix quotes Kurmuk governor Abdel Ati al Faki: the toll from the drone strike on displaced civilians near Bani Shako is 16 dead and six wounded with several missing (first count was nine); he blames the RSF; Nov. 17, about 8:50 AM ET: Reuters reports the UN says drones account for nearly three-quarters of Sudan war deaths this year; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somali Guardian says al-Shabaab attacks are slowing Uganda's troop withdrawal from Somalia; casualty claims unconfirmed
Africa.location: Mogadishu to Barawe corridor, Lower Shabelle, Somalia
Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Claims circulating on X that 11 Ugandan soldiers were killed in IED blasts have not been confirmed by the Ugandan military or major outlets.
Africa.status: Early reports; single regional outlet; no UPDF statement found; casualty figures unverified; the Uganda People's Defence Forces, via the government's Uganda Media Centre, rejected online reports that its troops were attacked and killed in Somalia and called them al-Shabaab propaganda; casualty claims remain unsupported; carried forward from 9:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people
Africa.summary: Voice of Horn reports Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan says clashes around Ethiopia's Moyale area have displaced more than 50,000 people, many into northern Kenya, with shortages of food, shelter and bedding. It adds that Kenya's police chief said more officers will deploy along the border. The IFRC says it is funding a Kenya Red Cross response for arrivals in Moyale, Kenya.

Africa.summary: Assahifa English, citing residents and a community organisation, reports gunmen killed at least three people at a mining site in Plateau State on Nov. 11, following another deadly attack in the area earlier in the week.

Africa.summary: South Africa's public broadcaster SABC says transmission of some services is disrupted because of a power outage around Auckland Park that began on Nov. 8. South America.summary: ADN Radio Chile reports a shooting attack at a nightclub in central Santiago that left one person dead and several injured. The number of wounded, the motive and any arrests were not given in the posts checked.

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. Still threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 17, about 5:48 AM ET: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the 'dirty bomb' allegations, attributed to the New York Times and spread by CNN, completely baseless and says enemies are trying to legitimize new aggression (Al Mayadeen). Still no DHS, FBI or NTAS bulletin found as of about 5:57 AM ET; only relays and explainers; Nov. 17, about 6:18 to 6:51 AM ET: Asked whether Iran poses an imminent threat to Washington, Trump said that if it does, 'they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' (Fox News); Al Arabiya English reports he said US authorities take any possible threat 'very seriously', and Faytuks Network, citing CBS, says Trump said the US is looking into the reported threat. Al Jazeera and Iran International report Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei denied the report as baseless; Iran International notes CNN said officials were divided on Tehran's capability and intent. Still no DHS/FBI bulletin or NTAS change found in posts checked as of about 7:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 8:07 AM ET: Al Arabiya English again reports Trump warning Iran it would 'pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' if it poses a threat to Washington. America.title: UPDATE: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; UNITED24 says President Sandu condemned the incursion. Footage of the Southern Bridge aftermath has been published despite city requests not to share it. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:00 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Kyiv metro service was restored between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine: two killed in Kyiv, two killed in Zaporizhzhia; substations reported hit in Rivne
Russia.location: Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Pavlohrad and other cities, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT mapping account AMK Mapping says Russia launched about 30 Iskander-M ballistic and about 10 Iskander-K cruise missiles overnight and that more than 300 Geran-2 drones were sent toward western Ukraine. It reports drones targeting electrical substations in Rivne, smoke over Zhytomyr, strong explosions and fires in Vinnytsia, and repeated attacks on Pavlohrad, where Ukrainian authorities report an enterprise was hit.
Russia.status: Developing; launch counts and damage come from OSINT tracking, with no Ukrainian Air Force tally or official damage assessment found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda report two people killed and one injured in Kyiv after a Russian attack, with non-residential buildings hit; Ukrainska Pravda reports Russian strikes on industrial sites in Zaporizhzhia killed two and injured 18. AMK Mapping reports Poland scrambled fighter jets to its eastern regions during the drone attack on western Ukraine (no Polish military post found in posts checked). The Energy Ministry reports outages in eight regions (see power grid item). Still no Ukrainian Air Force tally of launched or downed missiles and drones found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:00 to 5:54 AM ET: RBC-Ukraine reports Russia is massively striking western Ukraine, hitting Mukachevo, Ternopil and Chernivtsi; Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia (Mukachevo and Uzhhorod areas) in three waves around 10 a.m. Hungarian time, near the Hungarian border, with damage being assessed. Ukrainska Pravda reports a Russian strike on Dnipro hit a confectionery factory and homes, injuring 10; a school and apartment buildings in the Sobornyi district were also damaged. Ukrainian Air Force overnight tally still not found; Nov. 17, about 6:31 to 6:53 AM ET: Ukraine's Air Force says air defenses downed 205 of 306 Shahed-type drones, plus three Banderol/Dan-T mini cruise missiles and three Kh-59/69 cruise missiles, with no Iskander ballistic or cruise missiles shot down; hits were recorded at 44 locations (relayed by NOEL Reports and Ukrainska Pravda); Nov. 17, about 7:48 AM ET: Faytuks Network, citing Reuters, says Hungary suspended rail services to Ukraine for Tuesday and Wednesday as Russian drones struck western Ukraine, and a drone crashed about 300 meters from Mukachevo railway station, forcing crew to evacuate; Nov. 17, about 8:20–8:32 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports two killed and 38 injured in a Russian attack on industrial facilities in Zaporizhzhia; ZMiST reports a 51-year-old taxi driver killed and her passenger injured in a Russian attack on Vinnytsia; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, as the search ends
Russia.summary: NEXTA, citing Ukraine's Interior Ministry, says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha and that the search operation is complete. Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found; Nov. 17, about 12:55 PM ET: Russia's Federal Agency for Railway Transport says rail traffic across the bridge has been fully restored and delayed Tavria trains have arrived in Kerch (via Kevin Rothrock). About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 5:18 PM ET: OSINTdefender reports Destinus says Ukraine used nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles in last night's attack, with at least seven striking the bridge (company claim). No confirmed new strikes as of about 6:00 PM ET; Nov. 17 evening: new footage published showing the moment the bridge's main road span collapsed after the Ukrainian cruise missile strike; no new strikes confirmed

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. TRT World, Iran International and Drop Site News relay the army statement and note it gives no further details and does not say who launched the drones. Iran's Fars News (IRGC-affiliated) cites Arabic sources reporting several explosions in Kuwait and says air-raid sirens sounded at US bases there — a claim. It comes hours after the US self-defense strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island (see Qeshm item).
Middle East.status: Developing as of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: Kuwaiti military confirms an ongoing drone attack and interceptions; origin of the drones NOT officially confirmed (many accounts say Iranian drones, and some relays say the army named Iran, but the KUNA statement checked does not); no IRGC claim of responsibility, CENTCOM statement, damage or casualty reports found in posts checked. Unverified/not logged: claims of 5 IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site, claims of new attacks on US bases in Bahrain; Nov. 17, about 4:39 PM ET: the Kuwaiti Army General Staff's own account posted the statement that air defenses are engaging hostile drone attacks and that any explosions heard are interceptions (no origin named). As of about 6:00 PM ET: still no formal IRGC statement claiming the attack found, no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Kuwaiti statement on damage or casualties, and Kuwait has not named the attacker. Viral 'direct hit on US base' videos and lists of bases hit come from low-credibility accounts and are not logged; As of about 7:10 PM ET Nov. 17: still no Kuwaiti statement naming the attacker or reporting damage/casualties, no new Kuwait Army or KUNA posts since the 4:39–4:46 PM ET statements, and no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Kuwait still has not named the attacker or reported damage or casualties, and there is no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement. Iranian outlets (Defa Press, a Tasnim-branded account) report explosions in Kuwait and a drone attack on US positions citing 'Arab' or 'Iraqi' sources — media claims, not a formal IRGC statement. Middle East.title: UPDATE: US military official confirms US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defense after IRGC attacks on US forces; Iranian official says residential areas and infrastructure were not damaged
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: A US military official says US fighter aircraft used precision munitions earlier on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defense in response to IRGC aggression targeting US personnel and assets (first reported by Axios' Barak Ravid, then Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera and, per Iran International, Reuters). Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. From about 9:09 AM ET Al Arabiya and Al Hadath cite unnamed Iranian media saying a US strike hit the Nariman air defense site; Al Arabiya English carries the same at about 9:39 AM ET. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. This is the first named Iranian official confirmation of a US strike, so the item is upgraded to HIGH. As of about 11:10 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; viral 'US official: the United States is attacking Qeshm' posts have no traceable primary and are not logged. Casualty claims (6 IRGC killed) remain unverified; the Osint613 post on a further round of explosions (10:10 AM ET) has since been deleted and its link removed; Nov. 17, about 11:37–11:54 AM ET: ISNA, Iran International Arabic, Al Arabiya and Annahar carry the same Iranian account. Nafisi says the situation on the island is under control and relief services are on high alert; Al Arabiya, citing Iranian media, says the target was the Nariman air-defense site and Fars residents reported several consecutive blasts northwest of Qeshm city with rising smoke, with no damage or casualty details. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. No IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; OSINT reports of missile launches inside Iran are listed separately as unconfirmed; Nov. 17, about 12:10–12:55 PM ET: international outlets (TRT World, Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera Arabic, Iran International Persian) carry the Iranian deputy governor's account; Iran International Persian says five to six explosions were heard in Qeshm city with smoke in the island's northwest, and IRGC-affiliated media say air-defense positions were targeted, with no independent damage report. Al-Monitor reports a top Iranian official warned that civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases would be considered 'dual use'. About 12:59–1:02 PM ET: OSINT accounts report another explosion on Qeshm; BeamTracker says it is most likely an anti-ship cruise missile launch from the island rather than an airstrike, and MintPress says it would be a third round of US strikes if confirmed; neither is confirmed. As of about 1:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X (a post claiming AFP as its source was not matched to any AFP post and is not logged). No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm confirmed; Nov. 17, about 1:54 PM ET: TRT Persian repeats Iran's statement that the US attack on Qeshm caused no damage to infrastructure. Persian-language accounts claim further explosions and casualties on Qeshm, but these are unverified and not logged. As of about 2:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X. No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; Nov. 17, about 2:25–2:50 PM ET: a US military official confirmed the strike. Axios' Barak Ravid quotes the official: 'Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense,' in response to 'IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets.' Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera, Iran International (citing Reuters) and Ynet report the same official account. Independent Persian says Tasnim, citing provincial officials, confirmed the blasts heard on Qeshm were US strikes, described as a response to the IRGC drone attack on Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base. No formal CENTCOM press release seen on X as of about 3:05 PM ET; damage and casualties not officially reported (claims that six IRGC personnel were killed are unverified and not logged); no IRGC retaliation against US forces confirmed so far. Now a confirmed US strike on Iranian territory; Nov. 17, about 2:30–2:35 PM ET: more Pentagon reporters (Libbey Dean, Al Jazeera's Fadi Mansour) carry the same US military official statement: US fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense. As of about 4:00 PM ET there is still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (six IRGC killed, 'martyrs' on Qeshm) remain unverified and not logged; no confirmed IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states (an IRGC spokesman threat against Bahrain's rulers seen only via relays, not logged); As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement found on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (e.g. five IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site) unverified and not logged. About 4:46 PM ET Kuwait's military said its air defenses were engaging hostile drone attacks (attacker not officially named) — see the Kuwait item; As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release or Pentagon/White House statement on the strike found on X (CENTCOM account search since 4:00 PM ET returned nothing); no confirmed further US strikes; Iranian casualty claims still unconfirmed. Kuwait drone attack (possible retaliation) remains unattributed by Kuwait — see Kuwait item; About 6:42 PM ET Nov. 17: euronews reports that Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island. As of about 7:10 PM ET: still no formal CENTCOM press release found; no further US strikes confirmed by US officials. Iran's retaliation remains unclaimed by any primary IRGC source (see the Kuwait and Bahrain items); As of about 8:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release (no CENTCOM posts since 7:05 PM ET), and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; As of about 9:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release on X and no further US strikes on Iran confirmed by US officials or major outlets; relays describing 'fresh airstrikes' refer to the same strike

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false. Late on Nov. 17 (about 6:06 PM ET) Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new threat alert, with sirens and blasts reported, before an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET; the Arab League condemned what it called renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain. At about 7:48 PM ET Bahrain issued a third threat alert in under 24 hours, and the Bahrain Defence Force said Iran was continuing its attacks on the Kingdom. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. Low-credibility posts claiming a new Iranian attack on US bases in Bahrain or an IRGC statement of '550 Americans killed and wounded' have no primary source and are not logged; satellite-imagery claims that the radar was destroyed on Nov. 14 are unverified; As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Iranian drone and missile attacks on US bases in Bahrain seen only from low-credibility accounts, not logged. Kuwait's military separately reports engaging hostile drones (see Kuwait item); As of about 6:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Bahrain attacks still only from low-credibility accounts, not logged; 7:15 PM ET UPDATE — renewed alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued an 'alert of potential threat' at about 6:06 PM ET Nov. 17 (2:06 AM local Wednesday), urging people to stay calm and go to the nearest safe location; Al Arabiya's correspondent reported sirens, and blasts were reported. The ministry announced an all-clear at about 7:04 PM ET. Bahrain News Agency reports the Arab League condemned 'renewed Iranian attacks' on Bahrain; earlier the GCC secretary-general condemned repeated Iranian attacks. FaytuksNetwork's OSINT timeline puts this second Bahrain attack of the day at about 6:10 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on this wave, and no confirmed damage or casualties, as of about 7:10 PM ET; no formal IRGC claim for this wave found. Claims of a direct hit on Isa Air Base or US casualties (MintPress, DD_Geopolitics, MarioNawfal and others) are unverified and not logged; 8:15 PM ET UPDATE — third alert: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued another 'alert of potential threat' at about 7:48 PM ET Nov. 17 (3:48 AM local Wednesday), again urging people to go to the nearest safe location; Iran International notes it is the third such alert in less than 24 hours. About a minute later the Bahrain Defence Force General Command said Iran is continuing its 'systematic hostile approach' through attacks targeting the Kingdom. No all-clear from the Interior Ministry found as of about 8:05 PM ET. No CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found; Iranian outlets such as Defa Press claim drones hit a US base in Bahrain, which is unverified. Ignored: Arabic and Persian relay claims of a 'direct hit' and large fires at Isa Air Base (no primary); 9:15 PM ET UPDATE: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear at about 8:11 PM ET Nov. 17, ending the third alert of the night. The Bahrain News Agency (8:07 PM ET) carried the Bahrain Defence Force General Command statement that its air defenses countered Iranian attacks; Anadolu reports Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks without specifying casualties or damage. Reuters: 'Bahrain issues all-clear after threat alert amid US-Iran exchanges of fire.' No new alert found as of about 9:05 PM ET; still no CENTCOM statement on the evening waves, no confirmed damage or casualties, and no formal IRGC (Tasnim/Fars/Sepah News) claim found. A Civil Defence fire in a Souq Waqif building (moi_bahrain, no injuries, cause under investigation) is not linked to the attacks and is not logged

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.

The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. America.summary: Starting late Tuesday morning, Nov. 17, Downdetector logged user reports of problems with Apple Support from 11:45 AM ET and Apple Pay from 11:48 AM ET, and Breaking911 reported at 12:30 PM ET that users were also reporting outages at Gmail, Marriott, Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft 365. Apple's official system status page lists an ongoing 'iCloud Account & Sign In' issue ('This service may be slow or unavailable') that began at 8:45 AM PT (11:45 AM ET); as of about 1:00 PM ET no other Apple service, including Apple Pay, Wallet and the App Store, showed an event. America.status: Apple confirms only the iCloud sign-in issue; other services rest on user reports and Downdetector spikes; cause unknown; no evidence of a cyberattack (posts tying this to the FAA, NSA and bank outages as a coordinated attack are unsupported and not logged); consumer services, not critical infrastructure.
