Russia.title: UPDATE: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 10:03 AM ET: Zelensky says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge overnight as the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks, in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span collapse; Nov. 17, about 10:08 AM ET: Euromaidan Press, citing Zelensky and the SBU, says Palianytsia missile-drones hit the road section while Neptune, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo missiles hit the railway; the SBU calls it its fourth strike on the bridge since 2022; rail traffic is on one track and no cars can cross. Still no independent Reuters/AP confirmation of the extent of the span damage; Nov. 17, about 11:13–11:27 AM ET: Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, at the Ramstein meeting, said of the Crimean Bridge operation 'we just begin'; NEXTA cites Finnish OSINT analyst Emil Kastehelmi saying the road bridge will need an entirely new span and steel arch, rail-bridge damage is unknown, and wreckage appears to block the only shipping channel. Still no Reuters/AP independent damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:33 PM ET: the Kyiv Independent reports part of the road section collapsed, halting vehicle traffic indefinitely, and that the rail section is still standing but damaged. About 12:53–12:58 PM ET: Russian monitoring channels, relayed by NEXTA and Ukrainian accounts, report about 10 Flamingo and Neptune missiles heading toward the bridge, with missile alerts issued in Crimea, Adygea, Voronezh Oblast and Krasnodar Krai; no impact or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this new wave found as of about 1:05 PM ET. About 12:58–1:32 PM ET: Osinttechnical and Russian-language accounts relay Russian monitoring channels reporting another wave of drones and Flamingo/Neptune cruise missiles headed for the bridge and a large-scale attack under way; no confirmed new impacts, damage or official Russian or Ukrainian statement on this wave found as of about 2:05 PM ET. About 1:15 PM ET: Ukraine's Defense Minister Khmara says the bridge was struck with domestic weapons in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. About 1:50 PM ET: Reuters publishes Ukrainian drone footage it says shows a bridge section collapsing into the water (Ukrainian-released video; Reuters has not given its own damage assessment); Nov. 17, about 2:23–2:37 PM ET: The Kyiv Independent reports Zelensky described a 'seven-phase operation' that brought an entire section down; AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water. A viral claim that Ukraine is launching Neptune and Flamingo missiles at the bridge again is not confirmed and not logged; no confirmed impacts from a new wave as of about 3:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:42 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares video filmed overnight from the Crimean coast showing at least half a dozen missiles striking the bridge and the arch and roadway collapsing into the water. No confirmed new strikes since as of about 4:00 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 4:37 PM ET: OSINTdefender shares footage published by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point showing three FP-5 'Flamingo' cruise missiles being launched in last night's strike operation on the bridge. No confirmed new strikes as of about 5:05 PM ET

Earlier, Hormozgan Province deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi told the state agency Mehr that the US military attacked points around Qeshm, saying there was no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure; IRGC-affiliated Fars and Tasnim had reported explosions, smoke and projectiles around the island. The strike follows the IRGC drone launches toward the US radar site at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, which CENTCOM says were intercepted. No formal CENTCOM release, Pentagon or White House statement has been seen on X, and casualty claims remain unverified.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships; Nov. 17, about 9:30–9:51 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Tasnim reports that several projectiles may have fallen around Qeshm Island, citing unconfirmed accounts, and says efforts are under way to determine the source. From about 9:09 AM ET Al Arabiya and Al Hadath cite unnamed Iranian media saying a US strike hit the Nariman air defense site; Al Arabiya English carries the same at about 9:39 AM ET. About 9:49 AM ET: Al Arabiya's Washington correspondent says there is no US confirmation so far. OSINT claims of a second wave and of at least six killed or injured remain unverified; about 10:10 AM ET Osint613 reports unconfirmed new powerful explosions on Qeshm, possibly near the Nariman site. As of about 10:11 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation; Nov. 17, about 10:43–11:02 AM ET: an Iranian official now attributes the Qeshm blasts to the United States. Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province's deputy governor for political, security and social affairs, says (via Mehr, relayed by Iran International, Al Arabiya, Asharq and Asharq Al-Awsat) that a US military attack hit points around Qeshm Island but caused no damage to residential, commercial or vital infrastructure and that the situation is under control. This is the first named Iranian official confirmation of a US strike, so the item is upgraded to HIGH. As of about 11:10 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; viral 'US official: the United States is attacking Qeshm' posts have no traceable primary and are not logged. Casualty claims (6 IRGC killed) remain unverified; the Osint613 post on a further round of explosions (10:10 AM ET) has since been deleted and its link removed; Nov. 17, about 11:37–11:54 AM ET: ISNA, Iran International Arabic, Al Arabiya and Annahar carry the same Iranian account. Nafisi says the situation on the island is under control and relief services are on high alert; Al Arabiya, citing Iranian media, says the target was the Nariman air-defense site and Fars residents reported several consecutive blasts northwest of Qeshm city with rising smoke, with no damage or casualty details. As of about 12:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation; a few accounts post 'a US official said the United States attacked Qeshm' without naming any outlet, and those are not logged. No IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; OSINT reports of missile launches inside Iran are listed separately as unconfirmed; Nov. 17, about 12:10–12:55 PM ET: international outlets (TRT World, Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera Arabic, Iran International Persian) carry the Iranian deputy governor's account; Iran International Persian says five to six explosions were heard in Qeshm city with smoke in the island's northwest, and IRGC-affiliated media say air-defense positions were targeted, with no independent damage report. Al-Monitor reports a top Iranian official warned that civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases would be considered 'dual use'. About 12:59–1:02 PM ET: OSINT accounts report another explosion on Qeshm; BeamTracker says it is most likely an anti-ship cruise missile launch from the island rather than an airstrike, and MintPress says it would be a third round of US strikes if confirmed; neither is confirmed. As of about 1:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X (a post claiming AFP as its source was not matched to any AFP post and is not logged). No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm confirmed; Nov. 17, about 1:54 PM ET: TRT Persian repeats Iran's statement that the US attack on Qeshm caused no damage to infrastructure. Persian-language accounts claim further explosions and casualties on Qeshm, but these are unverified and not logged. As of about 2:05 PM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon or White House statement and no Reuters/AP/AFP independent confirmation found on X. No IRGC retaliation hitting US forces or Gulf states tied to Qeshm has been confirmed; Nov. 17, about 2:25–2:50 PM ET: a US military official confirmed the strike. Axios' Barak Ravid quotes the official: 'Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense,' in response to 'IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets.' Al Arabiya English, Al Jazeera, Iran International (citing Reuters) and Ynet report the same official account. Independent Persian says Tasnim, citing provincial officials, confirmed the blasts heard on Qeshm were US strikes, described as a response to the IRGC drone attack on Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base. No formal CENTCOM press release seen on X as of about 3:05 PM ET; damage and casualties not officially reported (claims that six IRGC personnel were killed are unverified and not logged); no IRGC retaliation against US forces confirmed so far. Now a confirmed US strike on Iranian territory; Nov. 17, about 2:30–2:35 PM ET: more Pentagon reporters (Libbey Dean, Al Jazeera's Fadi Mansour) carry the same US military official statement: US fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense. As of about 4:00 PM ET there is still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (six IRGC killed, 'martyrs' on Qeshm) remain unverified and not logged; no confirmed IRGC retaliation against US forces or Gulf states (an IRGC spokesman threat against Bahrain's rulers seen only via relays, not logged); As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: still no formal CENTCOM press release, Pentagon or White House statement found on X; no confirmed further US strikes; casualty claims (e.g. five IRGC killed at a Qeshm air-defense site) unverified and not logged. About 4:46 PM ET Kuwait's military said its air defenses were engaging hostile drone attacks (attacker not officially named) — see the Kuwait item

Middle East.summary: Lebanese media report an overnight Israeli Air Force strike near the Lebanon-Syria border in the eastern Beqaa Valley, the first in that area in several months. Times of Israel reporter Emanuel Fabian, citing Israeli security sources, says it was meant to stop a weapons shipment bound for Hezbollah. The IDF has not commented.
Middle East.status: Early reports; IDF has not commented; no casualty or damage figures found in posts checked; Nov. 16: JNS reports Israeli forces struck a Hezbollah-bound weapons shipment crossing from Syria; the Alma Center, citing Lebanese reports, places the strike at about 4:30 a.m. in the Al-Shaara–Janta area of the Nabi Chit barrens and says no casualties were officially reported; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Emanuel Fabian (Times of Israel) on X

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Yemeni government forces withdraw from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Reuters says Houthis in control
Middle East.location: Dhubab and Bab el-Mandeb area, Taiz/Lahj, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters reported Sunday that forces fighting for Yemen's internationally recognized government withdrew from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. Yemen's armed forces told Al Arabiya the redeployment reflects reprioritized objectives and aims to break the siege of Taiz. Al Jazeera says the Houthi advance threatens one of the government's last strongholds and brings fighting closer to the shipping route.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by government forces' statements and Reuters; no attacks on shipping linked to the withdrawal found in posts checked; extent of Houthi control along the coast unclear; Nov. 16: Anadolu Arabic reports the army foiled a Houthi attack in Taiz, cites two rights groups documenting 319 civilians killed or injured since September, and notes Houthi accusations of Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Saada with no Riyadh comment; Houthi-aligned YNP reports Saudi strikes on Sabr district south of Taiz city for the first time in weeks after a Houthi advance there (partisan source); Nov. 16 evening: Al Jazeera English says the Houthis have claimed control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait; Houthi claim, extent of control not independently confirmed; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 206-26: tanker approached by possible mothership and armed skiff 430 nm east of Socotra
Middle East.location: Indian Ocean, 430 nm east of Socotra, Yemen
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says the master of a tanker reported being approached at 0330 UTC on Nov. 16 by a possible mothership and a skiff about 430 nautical miles east of Socotra. Four armed people and a ladder were seen on the skiff. Ships are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO warning issued; suspicious approach, no boarding reported; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sirik and Kong, Hormozgan province, and in Shahriyar near Tehran; cause unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran
Middle East.summary: Several accounts reported explosions heard in Sirik in Iran's southern Hormozgan province on Sunday afternoon, citing Al Mihwar News and Iranian media. Other accounts said an explosion in Kong, also near the Strait of Hormuz, was linked to the targeting of an Iranian surface-to-air missile launcher. Separate reports describe an explosion in Shahriyar, west of Tehran.
Middle East.status: Early reports; claims that US forces struck air-defense launchers are speculation, and no official US or Iranian statement on a strike, damage or casualties was found; Nov. 15 evening: HormuzLetter and AI313_ say, citing only 'initial reports', that the US struck Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik; still no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Iranian official confirmation found, so the attribution remains unverified; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC Navy says two tankers hit naval mines on the 'unauthorized' southern Hormuz route Sunday and claims one supertanker sank
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: The IRGC Navy says two oil tankers that had switched off their tracking systems struck naval mines on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours, caught fire after large explosions, and that one, carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, sank. It released footage it says shows the explosions. The vessels have not been named, and it is unclear whether either is the tanker in UKMTO warning 205-26.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only, relayed by Tehran Times, The Cradle, FirstSquawk and ME Observer; not independently confirmed in posts checked; earlier IRGC tanker-mine claims in this log also remain unverified; Nov. 15 night: the IRGC Navy now claims two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire, saying six tankers have caught fire or sunk since Saturday (Iran International citing Iranian state media; Press TV). No confirmation from UKMTO, CENTCOM or ship operators found; ship names not given, so the claim remains unverified; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Tectonic, citing IRIB, says Iranian naval forces claimed three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, that the IRGC Navy again said six tankers have caught fire or are sinking since Sunday, and that a claimed sinking video shows fire on the water with no clearly visible vessel; ship names still not given and the claims remain unverified; Nov. 17 early: Persian-language outlets relay an IRGC Navy statement claiming a fourth oil tanker in 24 hours exploded after hitting a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; vessel not named; IRGC claim only, no UKMTO, CENTCOM or shipowner confirmation found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi missile attack near Aden kills at least five civilians, AFP reports
Middle East.location: Lahj governorate, near Aden, Yemen
Middle East.summary: AFP, citing four sources, reports that a Houthi missile attack near Aden on Sunday, Nov. 15 killed five people and wounded eight (via LBCI). A Rai al-Youm report citing AFP and Anadolu puts the toll at at least eight civilians killed and 12 wounded in Lahj.
Middle East.status: Early reports via wire services; tolls differ between reports (5 dead/8 hurt vs. at least 8 dead/12 hurt); carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 205-26: tanker attacked in the Gulf while heading toward the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.location: Southern Arabian Gulf, near the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says it is aware of a report from Indian shipping authorities of an attack on a tanker transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait of Hormuz. The crew are accounted for and safe. Damage and environmental impact were unknown at the time of the report, and vessels are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO advisory (reported 11:52 UTC, 6:52 AM ET) relayed by Iran International, Rudaw and others; attacker, vessel name and damage not identified; UKMTO text says the report came from Indian shipping authorities, the tanker was transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait, and the crew are accounted for and safe; damage and environmental impact unknown; Nov. 16: OSINT accounts say a crude tanker seen on Sentinel imagery being towed to port is believed to be the VLCC AL DHANNAH, the vessel in warning 205-26, with all crew safe; identification is OSINT assessment, not official; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item); Nov. 17, about 8:40 AM ET: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain; about 8:58 AM ET Iran International reports the UAE Foreign Ministry also condemned the renewed drone attack. No further waves against Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed in posts checked as of about 9:05 AM ET (the reported Qeshm strike remains unconfirmed); Nov. 17, about 11:04–11:48 AM ET: diplomatic follow-up only. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry says Secretary of State Rubio condemned the attacks and reaffirmed Washington's commitment to Bahrain's security in a call with FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani; Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned Iran's continued attacks as a serious escalation; Iran's WANA agency says the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain over its actions against Iran. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 12:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 12:33–1:00 PM ET: NBC News calls it Iran's third attack in recent days on US military targets in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on its Arab neighbors after a roughly two-month lull; CBS News notes authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted; Al Arabiya repeats CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties or equipment damage. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain confirmed as of about 1:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:00 PM ET: the US government's Persian-language account (USABehFarsi) calls the IRGC claim false, saying several one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted and shot down with no damage to US equipment and no US personnel injured, and that CENTCOM and partner forces remain on the highest alert. No new drone waves on Bahrain and no US military response tied to Bahrain found as of about 2:05 PM ET; Nov. 17, about 2:53 PM ET: Ynet reports a US military official confirmed US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island after the attack in Bahrain (see the Qeshm item). No new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed as of about 3:05 PM ET; As of about 4:00 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed. Low-credibility posts claiming a new Iranian attack on US bases in Bahrain or an IRGC statement of '550 Americans killed and wounded' have no primary source and are not logged; satellite-imagery claims that the radar was destroyed on Nov. 14 are unverified; As of about 5:05 PM ET Nov. 17: no new drone waves toward Bahrain confirmed by Bahrain or CENTCOM; claims of new Iranian drone and missile attacks on US bases in Bahrain seen only from low-credibility accounts, not logged. Kuwait's military separately reports engaging hostile drones (see Kuwait item)

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC claims it shot down another drone south of Qeshm Island (Nov. 17), after earlier MQ-1 Predator claims
Middle East.location: Qeshm Island, Strait of Hormuz, Iran
Middle East.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Saturday it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Diario de Centro América reports. IEW Latest News relays CBS News reporting that this is the second straight day Iran has made such a claim.
Middle East.status: Iranian claim relayed by media; no US military confirmation found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: Al Mayadeen reports the IRGC now claims it took control of a ninth US MQM-170 drone over Qeshm; IRGC claim only, no US confirmation found; Nov. 17, about 5:42 to 5:50 AM ET: Al Jazeera and Roya News relay a new IRGC statement that its air defenses shot down a drone south of Qeshm Island. IRGC claim only; drone type and ownership not confirmed and no US comment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:34 AM ET: ISNA carries an IRGC statement saying its aerospace air defenses intercepted and destroyed a US MQ-1 drone south of Qeshm Island, which it calls the 18th MQ-1 destroyed. IRGC claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 11:40 AM–12:00 PM ET: ISNA and Tasnim publish IRGC video they say shows the 18th MQ-1 being shot down south of Qeshm; separately, Iran's regular army claims (via Mehr) its air defenses downed a US 'LUCAS' drone over the Strait of Hormuz. Both are Iranian military claims; no US confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli airstrike in Khan Younis kills senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis, Hamas sources tell Reuters
Middle East.location: Khan Younis, Gaza Strip
Middle East.summary: The Israeli military says it struck a senior Hamas commander in Khan Younis on Saturday evening. Hamas sources told Reuters that Samir Abu Younis, described as head of the Rafah Brigade of Hamas's Qassam Brigades, was killed. Other casualties were not stated.
Middle East.status: Israeli military statement and Hamas sources via Reuters (relayed by Al Arabiya English); further casualties and wider escalation not reported; FirstSquawk relays a Hamas source telling Reuters that Abu Younis was killed, and reports Israel vows to keep targeting Hamas leaders in Gaza; Hamas's armed wing has now confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, commander of its Rafah Brigade, was killed in the strike, Times of Israel military correspondent Emanuel Fabian reports; the IDF said it struck a senior commander in the Khan Younis area; All India Radio News and CityNews Toronto report the Israeli military said Abu Younis was involved in rebuilding Hamas's capabilities and planning attacks, and that Hamas confirmed his death in a statement; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Jaramana car bomb near Damascus — Syrian Internal Security and state news agency SANA confirm a man and a young girl killed
Middle East.location: Jaramana, Rif Dimashq (Damascus countryside), Syria
Middle East.summary: An explosive device planted inside a car detonated in Jaramana, a mainly Druze and Christian suburb southeast of Damascus, on the evening of Nov. 14. Syria's Internal Security Forces and state news agency SANA say a man and a young girl were killed and another person injured; EFE reports two dead and two injured. Al Arabiya's correspondent says the blast was near a bus garage serving routes to Suwayda, and OSINT account Qalaat Al Mudiq says it resembles an IED attack in Jaramana three months ago.
Middle East.status: Official statement issued (Syrian Internal Security Forces, relayed by Al Jazeera and Al Arabiya; SANA quoted by Seth Frantzman); two killed, injury counts vary from one to three; no claim of responsibility found on X; ABC News reports state TV and the Interior Ministry said the car bomb killed two people and wounded at least one; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Large explosion reported at dawn in Zawtar al-Sharqiya, southern Lebanon, amid Israeli artillery shelling of nearby areas
Middle East.location: Zawtar al-Sharqiya, Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon
Middle East.summary: A Lebanon Debate correspondent reports a large explosion in the town of Zawtar al-Sharqiya at dawn on Saturday. NBN reports Israeli artillery shelling targeting Khiam, Khraibeh, the area between Mayfadoun and Zawtar al-Sharqiya, and the outskirts of Barashit and Mansouri. Asharq Al-Awsat says repeated detonations in Zawtar and shelling in the south are raising questions about Israeli objectives.
Middle East.status: Early reports; cause of the dawn explosion and any casualties not stated; no IDF or Lebanese army statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthis claim drone attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and East-West pipeline Pumping Station No. 3; Arab states condemn continued attacks on Saudi Arabia
Middle East.location: Riyadh and East-West pipeline, Saudi Arabia
Middle East.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group carried out drone attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Pumping Station No. 3 on the East-West oil pipeline east of Riyadh, Iran International reports. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation and the claims could not be independently verified. Saudi Gazette reports Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain and the Arab League condemned the continued Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia.
Middle East.status: Houthi claim only; no Saudi confirmation of damage or disruption at the airport or pumping station found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: Xinhua says the Houthis claim to have launched missiles at targets in Riyadh including its international airport; Middle East Observer relays unconfirmed reports that air traffic at Riyadh airport was halted, with an unverified image. No Saudi official confirmation found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Jask and Bandar Abbas, Hormozgan province, Iran
Middle East.summary: Iranian state media IRNA reported explosions heard in the port city of Jask near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday evening, with further reports from Bandar Abbas. Iran International cites the Hormozgan governor's office as saying sounds were heard but no explosions or strikes had been recorded as of 10:25 p.m. local time. Anadolu reports no impacts in the city or elsewhere in the province.
Middle East.status: Under investigation; official provincial statement says no impacts; cause unknown; claims of US drone activity and air-defense fire are unverified; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Saudi Arabia (East-West pipeline; Yanbu)

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: India says tanker MT Dominica Prosperity was hit by a projectile off Mina Saqr, UAE; UKMTO issues separate time-late warning of a tanker attack with casualties in the Arabian Gulf
Middle East.location: Off Mina Saqr (Ras Al Khaimah), UAE / southern Arabian Gulf
Middle East.summary: India's shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Liberia-flagged crude tanker MT Dominica Prosperity, with 19 Indian seafarers aboard, was targeted in a projectile attack on Nov. 11 while drifting off Mina Saqr, and the entire 22-member crew was evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard. Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera reports two Israeli attacks on an industrial metalworking facility in Gaza City killed three Palestinians and started a fire at a nearby displacement camp. It says at least seven Palestinians, including a child, were killed in several attacks on Tuesday.
Middle East.status: Single established outlet found on X this window; no Israeli military statement found; figures not independently verified; Reuters, citing medics, confirms an airstrike on a Sabra metal foundry killed three and four more were killed elsewhere in Gaza City and Khan Younis; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Heavy rain floods more than 70,000 tents in Gaza, killing four Palestinians including three children
Middle East.location: Gaza Strip
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera reports heavy rain flooded more than 70,000 tents in Gaza, killing four Palestinians, including three children. US Senator Brian Schatz urged Israel to allow building materials, rescue equipment and winter supplies in.
Middle East.status: Reported by Al Jazeera; no UN or local authority post checked directly; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UAE retailer Landmark Group investigates unauthorised access to its Shukran loyalty programme
Middle East.location: United Arab Emirates (Dubai-based Landmark Group)
Middle East.summary: Landmark Group says it is investigating a cyber incident involving unauthorised access to its Shukran loyalty programme, The National reports. Customer information involved includes names, contact details and dates of birth.
Middle East.status: Company statement reported by The National; number of affected customers not given; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli settlers set fire to a vehicle scrapyard in al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus; more than 100 vehicles destroyed
Middle East.location: al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus, occupied West Bank
Middle East.summary: Arab News reports that Israeli settlers set fire to a vehicle scrapyard in the Palestinian village of al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya on Wednesday (Nov. 11), destroying more than 100 vehicles. Anadolu Arabic reports Hamas described the burning of more than 100 Palestinian vehicles and other property as a terrorist attack.
Middle East.status: Early reports; no casualties reported in posts checked; no Israeli police or military statement found on X in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israel indicts 19-year-old East Jerusalem man accused of planning a bomb and shooting attack on the Temple Mount
Middle East.location: Jerusalem
Middle East.summary: i24NEWS reports an indictment has been filed against a 19-year-old from East Jerusalem accused of planning a terror attack on the Temple Mount; other accounts describe it as a planned two-stage bombing and shooting attack.
Middle East.status: Indictment filed; plot was disrupted before any attack. Details come from a single outlet in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iran's parliament speaker Qalibaf says dams, ports or power plants near US or Israeli bases would be treated as dual-use
Middle East.location: Iran
Middle East.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that any dam, port or power plant near a US or Israeli base would now be treated as dual-use, responding to experts quoted by The New York Times who described dams near Iran's missile sites as dual-use, Osint613 reports.
Middle East.status: Rhetorical threat; no action reported; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iran's army warns ships not to use 'fake American routes' through the Strait of Hormuz, citing sea mines
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia warned commercial vessels 'not to be fooled' into taking 'fake American routes' in the Strait of Hormuz, citing the threat of 'sea mines, fire and explosion,' Al Jazeera English reports.
Middle East.status: Official Iranian warning reported by Al Jazeera; no new incident tied to it found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Loud explosion heard in Ahvaz, Iran; Khuzestan official says it was a controlled destruction of munitions
Middle East.location: Ahvaz, Khuzestan province, Iran
Middle East.summary: Residents and OSINT accounts reported a very loud explosion in Ahvaz at about 3:40 AM ET. Iranian outlets quote Khuzestan's deputy governor for security affairs as saying the sound came from a controlled operation to destroy munitions.
Middle East.status: Official Iranian explanation only; no independent confirmation of the cause and no casualty reports found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani reportedly in Baghdad to contain Iraq–Kataib Hezbollah tensions
Middle East.location: Baghdad, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reports that IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani led an Iranian delegation that arrived in Baghdad on Monday and met Iraqi officials and leaders of armed factions. The sources say the visit aims to ease tensions between the Iraqi government and Kataib Hezbollah, which Baghdad has given a deadline to leave Jurf al-Sakhar.
Middle East.status: Single outlet citing unnamed sources; no Iranian or Iraqi official confirmation found in posts checked; linked to the Jurf al-Sakhar standoff item; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:47 AM ET: Amwaj.media reports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has given Kataib Hezbollah only days to hand over Jurf al-Sakhar, its stronghold south of Baghdad; footage shared on X shows Iraqi military reinforcements near Jurf al-Sakhar. Qaani visit still single-source; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sanaa, Yemen: three near the al-Hafa camp and a fourth at Jabal Nuqm
Middle East.location: Sanaa, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya and Al Hadath, citing sources in Sanaa, report three explosions near the al-Hafa military camp and a fourth at Jabal Nuqm on Tuesday afternoon local time; residents quoted by Ain Yemen describe violent blasts shaking the capital. The cause is not known: no claim, no strike announcement and no Houthi statement found in posts checked. Earlier on Nov. 17 Houthi-run media reported Saudi airstrikes on northern Sanaa (see separate item)
Middle East.status: Early reports citing unnamed sources and residents, about 5:45 to 5:56 AM ET; cause and casualties unknown; Nov. 17, about 6:18 AM ET: Al Arabiya English, citing governorate sources, adds that explosions were heard at several Houthi barracks in Bani Jarmuz (Bani al-Harith district) following airstrikes on fortifications, tunnels and weapons depots. No coalition, US or Israeli statement and no Houthi casualty report found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Qatar says it will meet Iranian officials Tuesday as part of ongoing US–Iran mediation
Middle East.location: Doha, Qatar
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English reports Qatar says it will hold a meeting with Iranian officials on Tuesday, Nov. 17, as part of ongoing mediation efforts. This comes amid the Bahrain drone attack, the Hormuz tanker strikes and the DC threat reporting
Middle East.status: Diplomatic signal; single outlet relay of a Qatari statement, about 5:27 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 7:03 AM ET: Independent Persian, citing Tasnim, reports Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Muscat to discuss regional developments; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: UPDATE: Gunmen kill at least nine in an attack on Zuwakal (Zuwagal) village, Mangu, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zuwakal village, Jipal District, Mangu LGA, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Security-focused outlet Zagazola Makama reports that suspected armed herders killed at least eight residents, including men, women and children, burned houses and stole 18 cattle in an attack on Zuwakal village about 11:45 p.m. on Nov. 15. Troops of Operation Enduring Peace responded and recovered eight bodies; the attackers fled toward Nasarawa State.
Africa.status: Single security-source report published Nov. 17; no police or army statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:27 PM ET: the Mwaghavul Development Association says gunmen killed at least nine people in Zuwagal (Zuwakal), Mangu, days after a curfew was lifted; houses and food also destroyed in nearby Bong. Still no police or army statement found

links.label: Zagazola Makama on X: eight killed, houses burnt and 18 cattle rustled in an attack on a Mangu community, Plateau

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Troops thwart a suspected Boko Haram attack on Nigerian Senate chief whip Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa, Borno State
Africa.summary: Vanguard reports that Senate Chief Whip Monguno and others escaped a suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. Details on casualties and the location of the attack were not in the post checked.
Africa.status: Single-outlet report (Vanguard) about 10:30 AM ET Nov. 17; no military or police statement found; Nov. 17, about 12:16 PM ET: Iwere News, citing local outlet Yerwa News Express, says Operation Hadin Kai troops thwarted the attempted attack on Senate Chief Whip Mohammed Monguno's campaign entourage in Kukawa LGA on Monday, when suspected Boko Haram fighters fired three mortar bombs toward the town while he was there with former governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan and APC leaders; no casualties reported. No official army statement seen on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Plateau State, Nigeria — gunmen kill an Operation Rainbow security commander and another person after fresh attacks kill five in three communities
Africa.location: Bokkos, Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi areas, Plateau State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Premium Times reports gunmen killed a Plateau State security commander and one other person; other reports say the Operation Rainbow commander was ambushed near Bokkos returning from a condolence visit. Punch separately reports at least five people killed in fresh attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas.
Africa.status: Developing; no police or state government casualty figure found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Market shooting in South Sudan reportedly kills 17 and wounds 23, Afropages says
Africa.location: South Sudan (market, location not specified in the post)
Africa.summary: Afropages reports that a shooting in a market in South Sudan killed 17 people and wounded 23. Mwanzo TV posted a headline saying 17 were killed in a South Sudan revenge attack. The exact location, date of the shooting and official confirmation were not given in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early, thinly sourced reports; location and official confirmation lacking; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kordofan Human Rights Observatory says a drone strike on Abu Qalb, West Kordofan, killed at least 15 civilians, including four children
Africa.summary: Radio Dabanga reports that at least 15 civilians, including four children, were killed in a drone strike on Abu Qalb in West Kordofan, according to the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory. The attacker was not identified in the post checked, and no official confirmation was seen.
Africa.status: Single rights-group report via Radio Dabanga; unconfirmed by official sources in this sweep; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Explosion and fire at an NNPC filling station in Ipaja, Lagos, spread to a neighboring school building
Africa.location: Command / Ajasa-Command area, Ipaja, Lagos State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: The Guardian Nigeria says an explosion at a filling station in the Ajasa-Command area of Ipaja triggered a fire, and that the cause and extent of damage are not yet known. WithinNigeria and other local accounts say the fire spread to a school building next to the station. One account says it happened during school hours and that everyone was reportedly safe; no casualties have been confirmed officially in posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports from several Nigerian outlets; cause and casualties unconfirmed; no official emergency agency statement seen; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Sun Nigeria and Instablog9ja say the fire spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School near Savannah Bus Stop in the Command/Ipaja area; firefighters contained the blaze and no casualties were reported in the posts checked. The earlier Guardian Nigeria post used in the prior entry no longer resolves; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Drone or air strike on a village in Abu Zabad, West Kordofan, Sudan, reported to kill 13 to 15 people, including children
Africa.location: Abu Qalb area, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, Sudan
Africa.summary: CGTN Europe quotes the Emergency Lawyers group as saying an airstrike on the Abu Qalb area of Abu Zabad locality killed 13 women and children, according to preliminary figures. News Central TV reports 15 people, including four children, were killed in a Sudanese military drone strike on a West Kordofan village. The Sudanese army had not commented in posts checked.
Africa.status: Reported by two outlets citing a rights group; tolls differ (13 vs 15); attribution to the army not confirmed by the military; Nov. 17, about 5:15 to 5:27 AM ET: The Sudan Doctors Network says a Sudanese army drone struck Abu Qulb in Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan, killing at least 13 civilians and injuring others, and calls for an independent investigation (CGTN Europe). KUNA reports the UN Human Rights Office says more than 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan from January to the end of October 2026, more than 1,630 of them in drone strikes; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

KUNA on X: UN civilian death toll

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Bomb threat on Sandton Drive, Johannesburg: all-clear given and roads reopened
Africa.location: Sandton Drive near Alice Lane, Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa
Africa.summary: The Citizen reports law enforcement on the scene of a bomb threat in Sandton, and other accounts tell people to avoid Sandton Drive near Alice Lane. No device, evacuation scale or injuries were reported in the posts checked.
Africa.status: Early reports; one established outlet; no police statement found in posts checked; Nov. 16: All-clear given about 15:46 local time per a community security update relaying the Gauteng JOC; eNCA reports the area around Sandton Drive and Alice Lane has reopened; News24 says the threat targeted an office building; no device or injuries reported; resolved, can drop from monitoring; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Two weekend mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 17 dead — nine in Jeffsville near Pretoria and eight in a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg
Africa.location: Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says nine people, six men and three women, were found shot dead inside a four-roomed shack in Jeffsville informal settlement. Police say the shooting is reported to have happened between 10 and 11 p.m. on Nov. 15 and that they were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Nov. 16. The motive has not been established and no arrests have been made; Yfm reports a manhunt is under way and SABC says the Gauteng police commissioner is at the scene.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; comes hours after the separate Sweetwaters (KZN) shooting that killed eight; Nov. 16: Channels TV says police put the toll from the Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters shootings at 17; Newzroom Afrika and Sowetan carry Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni saying one of the nine victims was a person of interest in a December 2025 mass shooting and linking the case to the Saulsville shooting; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: WPLG says at least 17 were killed in the two mass shootings about 330 miles apart and police have not established motives; Pretoria News says SAPS is probing a possible retaliation motive after confirming one victim was a person of interest in the Saulsville case (also EWN); eNCA reports Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi's condolences; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: Reuters, NBC News, Al Jazeera and BBC report at least 17 dead in two weekend mass shootings: nine in the shack near Pretoria and eight men found in a bullet-riddled vehicle near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal; police say motives not yet established and no arrests reported; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: SABC News on X (commissioner at scene)

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight people shot dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters outside Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.location: Mabane Section, Sweetwaters, Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says KwaZulu-Natal police are investigating the murder of eight people who were allegedly shot and killed inside a vehicle along the road at Mabane Section in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg. Daily News reports the eight men were killed on Sunday evening and that a murder investigation is under way. No motive or arrests have been announced.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Peter Obi condemns a reported attack on Kwankwaso's NDC convoy in Bichi, Kano State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Opposition presidential candidate Peter Obi says he is saddened by reports of an attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area. He calls for an immediate investigation and arrests. Kwankwaso had been commissioning NDC offices across Kano State on Sunday.
Africa.status: Early reports; party-side statement only; no police statement, casualty count or damage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya opens probe into violent protests at the Dadaab refugee complex
Africa.location: Hagadera camp, Dadaab, Garissa County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Anadolu reports that Kenyan authorities have opened an investigation after protesters opposing a planned market in Hagadera camp damaged government offices, stole equipment and broke into nearby businesses during clashes.
Africa.status: Single wire report citing authorities; casualty figures not reported; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. It cites Caasimada Online as saying forces loyal to a former South West state leader took Golweyn.
Africa.status: Single-source early report citing Caasimada Online; no official statement or claim of responsibility found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: JNIM reportedly overruns a national police detachment at Balga, near Fada N'Gourma, eastern Burkina Faso
Africa.location: Balga, about 25 km from Fada N’Gourma, Est region, Burkina Faso
Africa.summary: A Sahel-focused account reports that a JNIM attack on the morning of Nov. 15 targeted the National Police detachment at Balga, sacking and burning it, and that many officers were killed and several are missing. It adds that the attackers took all weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no official Burkinabe statement or casualty figure found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill a Zamfara governor's aide in a dawn attack in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits attacked worshippers at dawn prayer in Kaura Namoda on Sunday, Nov. 15, killing Nasiru Sani Kaura and abducting several others, according to the security platform Bakatsine (via Africa_lix). Nigerians_New reports he was an aide to Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal.
Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Post on X citing Eye Radio

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing.
