Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Reuters Africa on X: attacks hinder Ebola response

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source
Africa.summary: A post circulating an Eritrean Ministry of Information editorial quotes it saying Eritreans and their army are ready to answer "Prosperity's invasion" in the language it has chosen. A widely shared post claims Eritrea's government announced that Ethiopia has invaded, but another account says the ministry accused Ethiopia of "preparing aggression." No independent confirmation of cross-border fighting was found.
Africa.status: Early reports; contested framing; no Ethiopian government response or independent confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Deadly clash during anti-illegal-mining operation at Manso Keniago, Ghana; Citi FM reports four dead and 15 injured
Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A confrontation broke out on Wednesday (Nov. 11) between personnel of Ghana's National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents and suspected illegal miners as the task force removed seized excavators at Manso Keniago. NAIMOS, as reported by TV3/3News, says two of its personnel were shot and injured by an armed mob. Death tolls in reports range from two to four; Citi FM's latest report says four dead and 15 injured.
Africa.status: Casualty figures differ between outlets (two, three, then four dead); circumstances, including who fired the fatal shots, not established in posts checked; NAIMOS statement covers its two injured personnel; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Mandera ambush kills eight — Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, blames suspected al-Shabaab
Africa.location: Hagarsu, Arabia Road, Mandera County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, reports eight people — two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver — were killed Tuesday in northeast Kenya near the Somali border in an attack by suspected al-Shabaab militants. Kahawa Tungu and Nairobi News, citing police, place the ambush at Hagarsu along Arabia Road in Mandera County, targeting workers on the Arabia–Lafey road construction project. No group has claimed responsibility.
Africa.status: Confirmed by police (Reuters, Citizen TV, CGTN Africa); suspected al-Shabaab per officials; no claim of responsibility found; NTV Kenya says Mandera legislators are demanding security reinforcement along the Somali border after the attack; Voice of Horn reports Kenyan police now say they are treating the ambush as banditry rather than a terror attack, that the attackers crossed into Somalia with two stolen AK-47s, and that no arrests have been made (single outlet in posts checked); Prime Media Kenya reports the eight dead were five construction workers, two police reservists and a driver, and that attackers stole the officers' rifles and fled toward Somalia; Somalia's federal government, via state news agency SONNA, condemned the attack and offered condolences; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: AFP now says 39 migrants died in the Nov. 6 boat sinking off Senegal
Africa.summary: AFP reports 39 people died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal on Nov. 6, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years, as families mourn. Reuters earlier carried a government figure of at least 21 dead, and Al Jazeera English said the Interior Ministry called its toll provisional.
Africa.status: Toll raised to 39 per AFP (earlier official provisional figure at least 21); figures differ by source; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: UNHCR says nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year
Africa.summary: Reuters reports nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for neighbouring Niger this year, escaping attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to the UN refugee agency. It says the arrivals add to mounting humanitarian needs in Niger.
Africa.status: UN agency figure via Reuters; ongoing displacement; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudan: UNICEF says 15 power stations hit in October as drone strikes spread; rights group says RSF drone attack on displaced people in Blue Nile's Al-Kurmuk killed 16
Africa.summary: UN News reports UNICEF's James Elder said 15 power stations were hit in October alone as long-range drone strikes and drought threaten survival in Sudan. Arab News reports the UN says two thirds of children killed or injured in Sudan this year were victims of drone strikes. Wasl News reports an RSF drone attack killed nine civilians in a Blue Nile village on Tuesday; that toll is not independently confirmed.
Africa.status: UN agency statements; Blue Nile casualty report from a single regional outlet, unverified; ongoing conflict; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the toll from an RSF drone attack on displaced people in Bani Shako village, Al-Kurmuk (Blue Nile), has risen to 16; it is not confirmed whether this is the same attack Wasl News reported with nine dead; rights-group figure, not independently verified; Africa_lix quotes Kurmuk governor Abdel Ati al Faki: the toll from the drone strike on displaced civilians near Bani Shako is 16 dead and six wounded with several missing (first count was nine); he blames the RSF; Nov. 17, about 8:50 AM ET: Reuters reports the UN says drones account for nearly three-quarters of Sudan war deaths this year; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somali Guardian says al-Shabaab attacks are slowing Uganda's troop withdrawal from Somalia; casualty claims unconfirmed
Africa.location: Mogadishu to Barawe corridor, Lower Shabelle, Somalia
Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Claims circulating on X that 11 Ugandan soldiers were killed in IED blasts have not been confirmed by the Ugandan military or major outlets.
Africa.status: Early reports; single regional outlet; no UPDF statement found; casualty figures unverified; the Uganda People's Defence Forces, via the government's Uganda Media Centre, rejected online reports that its troops were attacked and killed in Somalia and called them al-Shabaab propaganda; casualty claims remain unsupported; carried forward from 9:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people
Africa.summary: Voice of Horn reports Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan says clashes around Ethiopia's Moyale area have displaced more than 50,000 people, many into northern Kenya, with shortages of food, shelter and bedding. It adds that Kenya's police chief said more officers will deploy along the border. The IFRC says it is funding a Kenya Red Cross response for arrivals in Moyale, Kenya.

Africa.summary: The Guardian Nigeria reports unknown gunmen killed Ibrahim Dio, the chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN) in Takum Local Council Area of Taraba State.

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least three at a mining site in Plateau State, Nigeria, days after another deadly attack in the area
Africa.summary: Assahifa English, citing residents and a community organisation, reports gunmen killed at least three people at a mining site in Plateau State on Nov. 11, following another deadly attack in the area earlier in the week.

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Johannesburg Mayfair substation outage: City Power restores power to some essential services, including Garden City Hospital and the SABC
Africa.summary: South Africa's public broadcaster SABC says transmission of some services is disrupted because of a power outage around Auckland Park that began on Nov. 8. South America.summary: The Belo Horizonte city government (PBH) confirmed a cyberattack on the system that issues municipal tax-payment slips, CNN Brasil reports. O Tempo says the system was normalized on Monday and the city extended tax due dates.

South America.title: CONTINUATION: Shooting at a nightclub in central Santiago, Chile, leaves one dead and several injured
South America.summary: ADN Radio Chile reports a shooting attack at a nightclub in central Santiago that left one person dead and several injured. The number of wounded, the motive and any arrests were not given in the posts checked.

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. America.title: UPDATE: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; Nov. 17, about 8:30 AM ET: The Washington Post reports Transportation Secretary Duffy says the FAA needs billions more for system upgrades, but experts and former officials say Friday's ground stop was not tied to a lack of funding. No sign of a cyberattack reported

No official structural assessment found in posts checked (an AMK Mapping post saying some Northern Bridge cables snapped is no longer available on X and was removed); Nov. 17, about 4:18 AM ET: NEXTA reports Kyiv residents are crossing the Northern Bridge on foot to reach the right bank after the overnight attack. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:00 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Kyiv metro service was restored between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. No structural assessment of the bridges found yet; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found; Nov. 17, about 8:19–8:43 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports Russia vowing to rebuild the bridge 'even better,' with experts saying repairs may take a while; Russia's Transport Ministry and Aksyonov say trains are running again on one track while crews repair the second (first passenger train left Taman at 1:04 PM Moscow time); Drop Site News says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a road span and arch fell into the Kerch Strait, its third attack on the bridge in about 24 hours; the SBU released strike footage. Road traffic remains halted. Still no Reuters/AP independent confirmation of the collapse in posts checked

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed

An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car explodes while driving in southern Moscow, seriously injuring the driver; Russian media say the car belonged to commentator Sergey Zavorotny
Russia.location: Kirovogradskaya Street, Chertanovo district, Moscow, Russia
Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. It comes a day after a car bomb killed a Russian Air Force colonel in St. Petersburg.
Russia.status: Early reports; cause under investigation; one Russian outlet cited a preliminary suspicion of a gas-system malfunction; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; The Washington Post now describes it as a car bombing that seriously injured a former adviser to ex-Ukrainian PM Mykola Azarov who became a pro-Kremlin commentator in Russia; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; Nov. 16: CGTN Français says Russia announced the arrest of a Russian woman it accuses of involvement in the Moscow car bombing on behalf of Ukrainian special services (Russian official claim; not independently verified); carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.

Russia.title: UPDATE: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions

NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; Nov. 16 afternoon: journalist Christopher Miller says Mayor Boris Filatov reports about half of Dnipro, a city of about one million, is without power after Russian attacks on the energy system, calling it the sixth blackout in two weeks, with two people killed, 10 high-rise buildings damaged and the Bunge-owned Oleina plant hit a third time; UNIAN says the city was left completely without power after a series of attacks, with outages also in parts of the region; MAKS 26 quotes DTEK as saying Dnipro lost electricity entirely and that crews were first restoring power to water, heat and social facilities; Nov. 17, about 3:00 to 4:05 AM ET: Ukraine's deputy energy minister says Russian overnight strikes on energy infrastructure caused power outages in eight regions (CGTN Europe, First Squawk). Middle East.title: UPDATE: Explosions on Iran's Qeshm Island confirmed by Iranian state media; reported US strike on a Nariman air defense site and claimed IRGC fire at warships still unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Nariman area, Qeshm Island, Hormozgan Province, Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
Middle East.summary: Iranian state media (the IRGC-affiliated Fars news agency) confirm that residents of Qeshm Island heard explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke on Tuesday morning, Nov. 17, but Fars says the cause is unknown. OSINT accounts have reported since about 7:52 AM ET that a US strike hit an Iranian surface-to-air missile site in the Nariman area, and regional media claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at the warships involved. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is no confirmation from CENTCOM, the Pentagon, the White House, Iranian officials, Reuters, AP or AFP of a US strike or of IRGC fire at US warships.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; developing; Nov. 17, about 8:20 AM ET: IRGC-affiliated Fars says residents heard one or more explosions northwest of Qeshm city and saw smoke, cause unclear; by about 8:50–8:57 AM ET Al Jazeera English, Al Arabiya and Iran International relay Fars, still with no cause given. About 8:40 AM ET: regional media (Sabereen News, via Walter Bloomberg) claim the IRGC fired missiles and drones at warships involved in the attack — targets, damage and casualties unconfirmed. About 8:45 AM ET: Iran's army says it shot down a US LUCAS drone over the Strait of Hormuz. About 8:43–8:53 AM ET: OSINT accounts report five missile launches from Omidiyeh, Khuzestan, with no target identified; one OSINT account says Iranian state media denied them. As of about 9:05 AM ET there is still NO CENTCOM, Pentagon, White House, Iranian official, Reuters, AP or AFP confirmation that the US struck Qeshm. Remains MEDIUM; upgrade to HIGH (NEW HIGH) only on official or major-outlet confirmation, or confirmed IRGC fire on US warships

IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon

Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

BBC's John Simpson says the attacks began about 11:36 PM local time and he counted 10 or 11 explosions, with both bridges apparently hit, after President Zelensky warned of big strikes. Drop Site News notes the Southern Bridge also carries a metro line, that explosions were reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Cherkasy, and that no casualties had been reported. Secondary accounts citing Kyiv Independent say strikes knocked out water and heat (and some power) in parts of the city.
Russia.status: Mayor's preliminary statement relayed by Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post; corroborated by a BBC correspondent; extent of bridge damage, utility outages and casualties not yet officially detailed; Nov. 16 night: Reuters reports Klitschko said Russian forces struck the two Dnipro bridges along with some other critical infrastructure as Moscow sent drones and missiles across Ukraine; outlets relaying the mayor say water, heating and power were cut in parts of the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says five Iskander-M missiles hit the bridges (three on the Northern, two on the Southern), with a fire on the Northern Bridge (unofficial). No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 16, about 10:40 PM ET (5:40 AM Kyiv time): Al Jazeera's correspondent reports a series of explosions in Kyiv with air-raid sirens on, and Ukrainian channels relayed by Faytuks report a new Russian missile attack on bridge(s) in the city. At about 11:45 PM ET, Economist correspondent Oliver Carroll said Russian missile strikes have stopped traffic on the two main river bridges linking Kyiv's east and west and that there are some problems with water and electricity. No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 3:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post reports Russian missiles struck Kyiv's North and South bridges late Nov. 16, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting essential services, with three injured in Cherkasy region. Ukrainska Pravda says Mayor Klitschko released video of the damaged Northern Bridge. No official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:50 to 4:05 AM ET: Reuters reports Russian strikes hit two bridges in Kyiv, causing water and power cuts, citing the mayor. The Kyiv Independent published video and says the strike marks a return to targeted attacks on the capital's transit routes. Posts from Kyiv say the Left Bank is heavily congested because of traffic restrictions on the bridges while specialists assess the damage. No official structural assessment found in posts checked (an AMK Mapping post saying some Northern Bridge cables snapped is no longer available on X and was removed); Nov. 17, about 4:18 AM ET: NEXTA reports Kyiv residents are crossing the Northern Bridge on foot to reach the right bank after the overnight attack. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:44 AM ET: bne IntelliNews reports Kyiv has shut two Dnipro bridges after the Russian strikes. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:22 to 6:26 AM ET: Zelensky says Russia fired four ballistic missiles at Kyiv's Southern Bridge and three at the Northern Bridge, and that backup crossings are needed (NEXTA, Ukrainska Pravda). Footage of the Southern Bridge aftermath has been published despite city requests not to share it. Still no official structural assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:00 AM ET: Ukrainska Pravda reports Kyiv metro service was restored between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. No structural assessment of the bridges found yet

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike hits port and industrial facilities in Mykolaiv, southern Ukraine
Russia.summary: A local official says Russian forces struck port facilities and industrial infrastructure in Mykolaiv overnight Nov. 17, as part of the wider missile and drone attack across Ukraine. Al Araby TV carries the same report citing Ukrainian authorities.
Russia.status: Early official report; damage and casualty figures not given in posts checked; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Large Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine: two killed in Kyiv, two killed in Zaporizhzhia; substations reported hit in Rivne
Russia.location: Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Pavlohrad and other cities, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT mapping account AMK Mapping says Russia launched about 30 Iskander-M ballistic and about 10 Iskander-K cruise missiles overnight and that more than 300 Geran-2 drones were sent toward western Ukraine. It reports drones targeting electrical substations in Rivne, smoke over Zhytomyr, strong explosions and fires in Vinnytsia, and repeated attacks on Pavlohrad, where Ukrainian authorities report an enterprise was hit.
Russia.status: Developing; launch counts and damage come from OSINT tracking, with no Ukrainian Air Force tally or official damage assessment found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda report two people killed and one injured in Kyiv after a Russian attack, with non-residential buildings hit; Ukrainska Pravda reports Russian strikes on industrial sites in Zaporizhzhia killed two and injured 18. AMK Mapping reports Poland scrambled fighter jets to its eastern regions during the drone attack on western Ukraine (no Polish military post found in posts checked). The Energy Ministry reports outages in eight regions (see power grid item). Still no Ukrainian Air Force tally of launched or downed missiles and drones found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:00 to 5:54 AM ET: RBC-Ukraine reports Russia is massively striking western Ukraine, hitting Mukachevo, Ternopil and Chernivtsi; Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia (Mukachevo and Uzhhorod areas) in three waves around 10 a.m. Hungarian time, near the Hungarian border, with damage being assessed. Ukrainska Pravda reports a Russian strike on Dnipro hit a confectionery factory and homes, injuring 10; a school and apartment buildings in the Sobornyi district were also damaged. Ukrainian Air Force overnight tally still not found; Nov. 17, about 6:31 to 6:53 AM ET: Ukraine's Air Force says air defenses downed 205 of 306 Shahed-type drones, plus three Banderol/Dan-T mini cruise missiles and three Kh-59/69 cruise missiles, with no Iskander ballistic or cruise missiles shot down; hits were recorded at 44 locations (relayed by NOEL Reports and Ukrainska Pravda); Nov. 17, about 7:48 AM ET: Faytuks Network, citing Reuters, says Hungary suspended rail services to Ukraine for Tuesday and Wednesday as Russian drones struck western Ukraine, and a drone crashed about 300 meters from Mukachevo railway station, forcing crew to evacuate

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, as the search ends
Russia.summary: NEXTA, citing Ukraine's Interior Ministry, says 72 people were killed in the Nov. 2 Russian strike on Komyshuvakha and that the search operation is complete. Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 7:21 to 7:57 AM ET: Ukraine says it carried out a seven-stage operation, first targeting air defenses and electronic-warfare systems, then striking the bridge repeatedly with missiles and drones (Faytuks Network). Defense maker Destinus says its RUTA missiles hit the bridge on two consecutive days, with the first night damaging the upper load-bearing structure and seven missiles today causing one span to collapse (company claim, via NOEL Reports). Fox News reports Moscow claims its defenses shot down more than 1,400 drones overnight in what appears to be Ukraine's largest drone assault of the war. Still no Reuters/AP confirmation of the span collapse found
