Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region

Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts; no Ukrainian Air Force tally, regional administration statement or damage reports found yet; AMK Mapping reports a large fire in Chornomorsk after the attack and says NASA FIRMS data shows a large fire at the impact area; it says a likely target was a freight-logistics company or the Chornomorsk Automobile Plant; still no official Ukrainian damage or casualty report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays a Russian Defense Ministry claim that the targets were a ferry terminal, the Chornomorsk port administration and a nearby electrical substation; this is a Russian military claim, not independently confirmed, and no official Ukrainian damage report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays Ukrainian energy company DTEK confirming a substation in Chornomorsk was hit by multiple drones, leaving about 41,000 homes without power; Gerashchenko and Flash report six people injured in Chornomorsk and damage to energy infrastructure, an administrative building, a gas pipeline and nearby homes; the same overnight wave injured six in Zaporizhzhia (12 strikes, per Flash) and three in a drone hit on a Kropyvnytskyi residential building; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. The Russian Defense Ministry says it downed 533 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and seas between 8 PM Nov 14 and 8 AM Nov 15 Moscow time, and SOTA and Charter 97 report Rosaviatsia restrictions at about 12 airports including Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Samara, Sochi and Volgograd. An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone strike on a house in Proletarsky, Belgorod region, kills three, Russian regional officials say

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, injure more than 50, including eight children; a rescuer clearing rubble is killed

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO 208-26: LPG tanker TARA GAS struck a second time off Khasab; crew abandoned ship, one Indian seafarer missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16 evening: NDTV reports the Khasab tanker attack citing UKMTO; vessel still not identified and no responsibility claim found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:40 AM ET: India's shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and that all 25 crew are safe (PTI relays). Analyst Noam Raydan, citing Vanguard, identifies the vessel (IMO 9290270) as disabled with an engine-room fire and says at least 17 ship attacks have been reported in November. Attacker still not identified in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:40 to 4:05 AM ET: OSINT accounts post images of a large smoke column still rising Tuesday morning from the tanker struck about 13 km north of Khasab (unverified). Hindustan Times reports India's minister says all 24 Indian seafarers are safe. Iranian outlets relay an IRGC Navy claim of an explosion on a fourth tanker in 24 hours; no UKMTO warning beyond 208-26 found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:17 to 4:46 AM ET: UKMTO issued update 001 to warning 208-26. Iran International and JNS, summarizing the update, say the tanker first hit about 7 nm north of Khasab was struck a second time, causing another fire on board, and that the crew's status is unknown/unaccounted for after the second strike, citing a maritime security agency. This conflicts with India's earlier statement that all crew were safe (that statement preceded the second strike). Attacker not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 5:02 to 5:40 AM ET: India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said TARA GAS, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and the whole 25-member crew was safe. In an update he says the tanker was attacked again, forcing the entire crew to abandon ship; 24 crew are safely accounted for and one Indian seafarer is missing, and India is coordinating with the ship manager and regional rescue authorities. No US Navy involvement and no new UKMTO notice found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:03 AM ET: India's embassy in Muscat says 24 of the 25 crew of the Panama-flagged VLGC TARA GAS (24 of them Indian) have been evacuated ashore at Khasab and search-and-rescue operations continue for one missing Indian crew member, with Omani support; carried forward from 7:15 AM ET, no newer change found

No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17 early: The New Arab says Kataib Hezbollah denies involvement in oil smuggling from Jurf al-Sakhar; Channel8, citing sources, says the group opposes bloodshed and that mediation is under way. No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 8:03 AM ET: Al Arabiya English, citing AFP, says a Kataib Hezbollah commander said the group will not leave its Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold despite Iraqi authorities' call to withdraw and let the army enter. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties; Nov. 17, about 7:03 to 7:31 AM ET: Al Jazeera English and Iran International relay CENTCOM's statement that the IRGC drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment or personnel. Iran International reports the IRGC spokesman warned Bahrain its future in the region could be in question over 'cooperation in the aggression against Iran.' No further drone waves against Bahrain and no announced US response to the Bahrain attack found as of about 8:10 AM ET (a separate, unconfirmed report of a US strike on Qeshm Island is logged as its own item)

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:10 to 3:05 AM ET: ABC News reports Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night, citing Russian-installed authorities. The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Russia's Transport Ministry says train and car traffic across the bridge is suspended after the repeat attack, with no casualties, and the Russian cabinet says a government commission on the aftermath will meet shortly. AFP reports Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second night in a row, citing officials. Kyiv Post reports a key road arch reportedly collapsed into the sea. These are the first Russian official acknowledgments of structural damage found; Russian officials have not described the extent, and no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself was found in posts checked. Rail-span damage and Kerch Strait shipping disruption still come from OSINT and Ukrainian channels; Nov. 17, about 4:15 to 5:05 AM ET: Ukraine's General Staff officially says Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge overnight, that an arch and a span of the bridge are down and that road traffic to occupied Crimea is halted. President Zelensky thanked the SBU and the military for an 'unprecedented operation' in response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure; Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report he called it the seventh phase of a weeks-long operation and said both the road and railway sections were hit. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Izvestia there is no doubt the bridge will be restored and will be 'even better than before' (TASS, Sputnik), an implicit acknowledgment of major damage; Russian officials have still not described the extent. Al Jazeera reports the Ukrainian attack killed at least two people in Crimea. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse itself found in posts checked; rail-span status and Kerch Strait shipping still come from Ukrainian and OSINT sources; Nov. 17, about 4:55 to 5:47 AM ET: Kyiv Independent reports a section of the bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian Flamingo missile strike, the final part of a seven-phase operation carried out over several weeks; Ukraine's Defence Ministry posted Zelensky's statement that everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing into Crimea. NOEL Reports, citing SBU footage, says part of the railway section burned after a direct hit and that SBU Alpha units collapsed the road section with Palianytsia missile-drones; Ukrainska Pravda quotes the SBU saying the road section is 'dead' and no car will cross it. bne IntelliNews reports Russia has convened a government commission to repair the bridge. Unverified posts claim passenger rail traffic has resumed and a passenger-only ferry is running; no Russian official confirmation of rail status, and still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse, found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 5:57 to 6:59 AM ET: AFP reports a section of the bridge appeared to be lying in rubble in the water after Ukraine's overnight missile attack, and CBS News reports Ukraine struck the bridge for the second night in a row. Militarnyi says 11 types of Ukrainian-made missiles and drones were used after weeks of preparation by the SBU and General Staff; OSINTtechnical relays a claim by European manufacturer Destinus that seven of its RUTA cruise missiles hit the bridge (company claim). Novaya Gazeta Europe and Vot Tak report rail traffic across the bridge has resumed, citing the carrier Grand Service Express and Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov, with the Moscow–Kerch 'Tavria' train departing from Taman; road traffic remains halted. Peskov says Russia opposes temporary ceasefires and that the strikes will not change the agenda of the planned Putin–Trump–Xi talks in Shenzhen. Still no Reuters or AP confirmation of the span collapse found in posts checked

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. The Russian Defense Ministry says it downed 533 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and seas between 8 PM Nov 14 and 8 AM Nov 15 Moscow time, and SOTA and Charter 97 report Rosaviatsia restrictions at about 12 airports including Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Samara, Sochi and Volgograd. An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight — one woman killed in a Solomianskyi high-rise; State Emergency Service says two rescuers killed in Kyiv region
Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says its journalists heard multiple explosions in Kyiv around 1 a.m. local time on Thursday (Nov. 12; about 6 p.m. ET Wednesday), shortly after Ukraine's Air Force warned that missiles were targeting the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says at least 11 missiles were used, including about five Iskander-Ms, and lists an Epicentr shopping center in northern Kyiv and the eastern industrial zone among the targets, with further strikes in the Bila Tserkva and Irpin areas. Journalist Oliver Carroll also reported ballistic strikes on Kyiv.
Russia.status: Official statements issued (Kyiv City Military Administration; State Emergency Service as relayed by CGTN Europe): one killed and five injured in Kyiv city, two rescuers killed in Kyiv region; Russian MoD target claims unverified; Ukrinform, citing Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, says one person was killed and seven injured in the strike on the residential building, with fire on the third to sixth floors; Euromaidan Press says the woman killed was 44; ZMiST reports the overnight attack caused damage across eight Ukrainian regions, mainly energy and transport infrastructure, including a power generation facility in Zaporizhzhia and high-voltage substations in Odesa and Rivne regions; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery
Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)
Russia.summary: Russian local channels and multiple OSINT and media accounts report a prolonged Ukrainian drone attack on Omsk on Nov. 11, with the Gazprom Neft refinery named as the target and air defense activity lasting more than two hours. NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a crowded market in Chornomorsk, Odesa region, kills three and injures 11
Russia.summary: A Russian strike hit a market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing three people and injuring 11, according to regional authorities cited by NOELreports and Ukrainian outlets. Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.
Russia.status: Regional authorities report; toll rose from one to three killed during the morning; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: New Voice of Ukraine on X

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro kills three and injures four
Russia.summary: Suspilne, citing regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha, reports a Russian strike hit a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro, killing two people, injuring at least four and starting a fire. Hromadske Radio later reported the toll rose to three, with businesses and a private home also damaged and four men hospitalized, two in serious condition. CGTN Europe, citing Ukraine's health service, reports three killed and five injured across Dnipropetrovsk region during the day.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) figures relayed by Ukrainian outlets; emergency services at the scene; facility not named; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Hromadske Radio: toll rises to three

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian missile and drone strikes target Odesa Oblast bridges and 330 kV substations, plus substations in Kharkiv and Chernihiv, OSINT mapper reports
Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports a large combined Russian attack on Odesa Oblast overnight using cruise missiles, glide bombs and drones, targeting the Mayaky and Zatoka road bridges that link southern Odesa Oblast to the rest of Ukraine, as well as 330 kV substations in Artsyz and the "Podilska" substation. It says at least four cruise missiles were shot down and two flew briefly through Moldovan airspace. The same account reports fires in Kharkiv and Chernihiv after strikes on 110 kV substations.
Russia.status: Early reports; single OSINT mapping source; damage and outages not yet confirmed by Ukrainian officials or utilities on X; Kharkiv and Chernihiv substation strikes echoed by other OSINT accounts (one says one person injured in Kharkiv); still no Ukrainian official or utility statement found on X; First Squawk relays the Odesa governor saying energy targets were hit overnight; bne IntelliNews reports Russian strikes cut power to 135,000 in Odesa region; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; Nov. 16 afternoon: journalist Christopher Miller says Mayor Boris Filatov reports about half of Dnipro, a city of about one million, is without power after Russian attacks on the energy system, calling it the sixth blackout in two weeks, with two people killed, 10 high-rise buildings damaged and the Bunge-owned Oleina plant hit a third time; UNIAN says the city was left completely without power after a series of attacks, with outages also in parts of the region; MAKS 26 quotes DTEK as saying Dnipro lost electricity entirely and that crews were first restoring power to water, heat and social facilities; Nov. 17, about 3:00 to 4:05 AM ET: Ukraine's deputy energy minister says Russian overnight strikes on energy infrastructure caused power outages in eight regions (CGTN Europe, First Squawk). The Energy Ministry calls the situation in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions extremely difficult, with some consumers without power in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi regions and emergency outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Poltava and Kharkiv regions; Ukrenergo says crews worked overnight on repairs; Nov. 17, about 5:20 AM ET: Reuters reports nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries say the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is increasing this winter and urge Russia to stop attacking the country's power infrastructure; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kryvyi Rih — AMK Mapping says two 330 kV substations hit by at least 16 Geran-2 drones; Reuters confirms partial blackout
Russia.summary: A massed Russian drone attack on energy infrastructure left parts of Kryvyi Rih without power, according to city official Oleksandr Vilkul. Apartment buildings, schools and kindergartens were damaged. Water and sewage services are being stabilized with generators, but heating will be harder to restore. AMK Mapping says at least 16 Geran-2 drones were used and that the "Pivdenna" and "Hirnycha" 330 kV substations on the city's southern outskirts were hit.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (city official Oleksandr Vilkul); Reuters reports the outage; substation details from OSINT mapping account, not officially confirmed; casualty figures not reported; Reuters headline reconfirmed this window; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Leningrad governor confirms fire in Ust-Luga port area and emergency substation shutdown during drone attack; says 146 drones intercepted overnight
Russia.summary: Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko said a fire broke out in the Ust-Luga port area during an overnight Ukrainian drone attack and that a substation in the port zone went into emergency shutdown. He said 146 drones were intercepted over the region as of 7:30 a.m. local time and that there was no information on casualties. Earlier OSINT footage showed the oil terminal burning.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Leningrad governor, relayed by OSINT/news accounts); no casualty information; extent of terminal damage unknown; tanker damage claims unconfirmed; NASA FIRMS satellite data shows multiple fires at and just off the port (OSINTdefender); Estonian public broadcaster ERR shows the fire visible from Estonia; Reuters carries the governor's account of the fire; Hromadske cites the governor on a substation shutdown and three injured workers; Meduza says two people were killed in the Smolensk region when officials say drone debris hit an apartment building; NOELreports says the Ust-Luga port terminal was still burning on Wednesday morning after the overnight attack; NOELreports cites OSINT channel Absreliable reporting fires at three 30,000-cubic-meter tanks and damage to processing equipment and a berth at Novatek; Russian sources cited by Osint613, OSINTdefender and NOELreports say two Ka-52 attack helicopters and an Mi-8 went down while responding to the drone attack, reportedly partly to friendly air defense, with one to three crews killed (Russian-source claims, unconfirmed by officials); Ukraine's SBU says the overnight operation struck port and oil infrastructure at Ust-Luga, damaging several petroleum storage tanks, and also hit the Buyan-M-class missile ship Naro-Fominsk; damage to the ship not established; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Ukrainian strikes have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%; fuel purchase limits spread to St. Petersburg and Leningrad region
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent and Novaya Gazeta Europe, citing Reuters and two industry sources, report renewed Ukrainian attacks since late October have cut Russian refining capacity by about 30%, disrupting nine of Russia's 35 major refineries over the past week, including plants in Ryazan and Yaroslavl, per Meduza. SOTA, citing Bumaga, reports Rosneft stations in St. Petersburg have capped purchases since Nov. 8, and Novaya Gazeta Europe reports fuel limits returning in Leningrad region.
Russia.status: Refining capacity cut reported by Reuters (via established outlets); regional rationing reported; no official nationwide measure; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: Meduza reports a span of a railway bridge collapsed in the Arkhangelsk region and several passenger trains were delayed. NEXTA reports several freight cars derailed after a section of the bridge over the Viled River collapsed between Cheryomukha and Viled and rail traffic on the section was suspended. Posts on X claim sabotage, but no official cause has been established.
Russia.status: Traffic halted on the section; at least eight passenger trains delayed per reports; cause under investigation; sabotage claims unverified; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kyiv Independent says Russian attacks killed 10 and injured 40 across Ukraine over the past day; ballistic and Zircon missiles plus 123 drones launched overnight
Russia.location: Kirovohrad, Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says air defenses neutralized 135 of 162 Russian drones, 70 of them jet-powered, and that Russia also launched an Iskander-M ballistic missile. It says hits were recorded in 19 locations and debris fell in nine more. It reports critical infrastructure in the Kirovohrad region was attacked, with two people injured, and that a business in Dnipro caught fire. Ukrainska Pravda and Ukrinform carry the same figures.
Russia.status: Daily casualty figures via Kyiv Independent, citing regional authorities; Air Force figures via NOEL Reports; damage assessments continuing; Nov. 16: Kyiv Independent says Russian attacks killed 6 and injured 45 across Ukraine over the past day as Kyiv endured almost nonstop air raid alerts; citing the Air Force, it says Russia launched 158 long-range attack drones overnight, including 77 jet-powered drones; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone hits a commuter train at Sumy railway station; no casualties reported
Russia.summary: The head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, Oleh Hryhorov, says a Russian drone deliberately struck a commuter train at the Sumy railway station on Tuesday morning. He says there were no passengers on board, the crew was in a shelter and there were no casualties. Ukrainska Pravda and RBC-Ukraine also report the attack on the train.

Russia.summary: Ukrainska Pravda reports that Russian forces attacked a civilian enterprise in Vinnytsia region, killing two people. The type of enterprise and the extent of the damage were not given in the post.
Russia.status: Reported by Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda; energy damage extent not given; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drones target military aircraft repair plant in Russia's Novgorod region; explosions reported near Staraya Russa
Russia.location: Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, Russia; Crimea
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, citing Telegram monitoring channels, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea. No damage assessment or official Russian or Ukrainian statement was found. RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.
Russia.status: Early reports; Ukrainian outlets citing media and monitoring channels; damage not officially confirmed on X; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Centrenergo warns of 'extremely serious' consequences after Russian strike on Trypillia Thermal Power Plant
Russia.summary: Russian forces struck the Trypillia Thermal Power Plant, the Kyiv Independent reports. Centrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned generating company, said the impact appears significant, but the extent of the damage is not yet clear and needs further inspection.
Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Responsibility is not established in the posts found.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (IAEA, via Kyiv Independent); carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Electrical substation in Kursk, Russia, reportedly struck by drones; fire at the facility
Russia.summary: NOEL Reports says an electrical substation supplying about 400,000 residents in Kursk was reportedly struck and caught fire; Kyiv Post also lists an attack on a Kursk substation among overnight Ukrainian strikes.
Russia.status: Reported by OSINT and Kyiv Post; no Russian official statement on damage or outages found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: IRGC and Iran's Army Navy say a supertanker and an LNG carrier caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC says two vessels it calls 'violators', a supertanker reportedly carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and a liquefied gas carrier, caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, Nov. 17 (Al Jazeera English, Al Araby TV, IRNA Arabic). Iran's Army Navy separately said an oil tanker that entered a restricted area east of the strait struck a mine and burst into flames, a statement Reuters reported citing state media; Iran International posted video of a burning tanker.
Middle East.status: Iranian claims only; vessel names, flags, crews and casualties not identified; no UKMTO, CENTCOM or shipowner confirmation of these mine strikes found in posts checked as of about 7:05 AM ET. Iranian state media frames the ships as unauthorized transits.

Middle East.location: Arabian Gulf, west of the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued warning 209-26 on Nov. 17 for a time-late, verified report: a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile on Nov. 13 while transiting eastbound through the Arabian Gulf before entering the Strait of Hormuz. All crew are safe and accounted for; damage and environmental impact are unknown.

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi-run Saba says seven Saudi airstrikes hit northern Sanaa before dawn Tuesday; no coalition statement
Middle East.location: Sanaa, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Yemeni accounts citing local residents report a series of heavy airstrikes on Houthi-held sites in Sanaa around 6:10 AM local time on Nov. 17 (about 10:10 PM ET Nov. 16), with explosions heard across the city and warplanes flying low. Houthi-aligned commentator Hussain al-Bukhaiti says there were three Saudi airstrikes on the capital. A situation-map account says the reports cite unnamed Arab sources with no official confirmation.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; no Saudi-led coalition or Houthi official statement, targets or casualty figures found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:40 AM ET: Houthi-run Saba news agency, relayed by Al Mayadeen, says seven Saudi airstrikes destroyed a textile and shoe factory belonging to an orphans' development foundation in al-Nahda, northern Sanaa, and separately reports four Saudi strikes in al-Misrakh district, Taiz. No Saudi-led coalition statement or casualty figures found; target descriptions are Houthi claims; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC claims it captured a ninth US MQM-170 drone intact south of Qeshm Island
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, south of Qeshm Island, Iran
Middle East.summary: Citing Iran's state Press TV, accounts report the IRGC Aerospace Force says it used electronic warfare to seize another American MQM-170 drone over waters south of Qeshm Island and land it undamaged, which it says makes nine captured. This is an Iranian state claim.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Palestinian woman killed and 10 wounded by what Palestinian TV calls Israeli settler gunfire in Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho
Middle East.location: Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, West Bank
Middle East.summary: Reuters reports Palestinian official television said a Palestinian woman was killed and 10 others wounded by what it described as gunfire from Israeli settlers in Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho. Haaretz reports the Palestinian account alongside the IDF's report of the attack on Israelis in the same area earlier Monday.
Middle East.status: Palestinian official account reported by Reuters and Haaretz; no IDF statement on the shooting found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: the IDF says that on the outskirts of Jericho, attackers rammed an Israeli vehicle, then got out with weapons and attacked the occupants; rocks were thrown and the Israelis fired 'to remove the threat,' with Israeli and Palestinian casualties. Forces are pursuing suspects and setting up roadblocks. i24NEWS reports two Israelis injured in a suspected terror attack outside Jericho and a Palestinian woman shot dead. The accounts conflict: Palestinian sources describe settler gunfire, while the IDF describes a ramming attack; Nov. 17, about 1:40 AM ET: Reuters reports a Palestinian woman killed and 10 wounded in settler gunfire, citing official Palestinian TV; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: CENTCOM confirms the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group is operating in the Middle East, giving the US three carriers in the region
Middle East.location: US Central Command area of responsibility (Middle East)
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English and Kuwait's state news agency KUNA report that US Central Command confirmed the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt is operating in the Middle East as part of a scheduled deployment. Xinhua and Antiwar.com say this brings the number of US carrier strike groups in the region to three, though the Roosevelt is expected to replace the USS George Washington at an unannounced time.
Middle East.status: Officially announced deployment (CENTCOM, as reported by Al Jazeera and KUNA); escalation signal amid Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Hormuz shipping; no new US strikes on Iran reported; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: KUNA on X (Kuwait state news agency)

Middle East.title: UPDATE: UKMTO 208-26: LPG tanker TARA GAS struck a second time off Khasab; crew abandoned ship, one Indian seafarer missing
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16 evening: NDTV reports the Khasab tanker attack citing UKMTO; vessel still not identified and no responsibility claim found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:40 AM ET: India's shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS, carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and that all 25 crew are safe (PTI relays). Analyst Noam Raydan, citing Vanguard, identifies the vessel (IMO 9290270) as disabled with an engine-room fire and says at least 17 ship attacks have been reported in November. Attacker still not identified in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 3:40 to 4:05 AM ET: OSINT accounts post images of a large smoke column still rising Tuesday morning from the tanker struck about 13 km north of Khasab (unverified). Hindustan Times reports India's minister says all 24 Indian seafarers are safe. Iranian outlets relay an IRGC Navy claim of an explosion on a fourth tanker in 24 hours; no UKMTO warning beyond 208-26 found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 4:17 to 4:46 AM ET: UKMTO issued update 001 to warning 208-26. Iran International and JNS, summarizing the update, say the tanker first hit about 7 nm north of Khasab was struck a second time, causing another fire on board, and that the crew's status is unknown/unaccounted for after the second strike, citing a maritime security agency. This conflicts with India's earlier statement that all crew were safe (that statement preceded the second strike). Attacker not identified by UKMTO; Nov. 17, about 5:02 to 5:40 AM ET: India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said TARA GAS, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers, was targeted in a missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov. 16 and the whole 25-member crew was safe. In an update he says the tanker was attacked again, forcing the entire crew to abandon ship; 24 crew are safely accounted for and one Indian seafarer is missing, and India is coordinating with the ship manager and regional rescue authorities. No US Navy involvement and no new UKMTO notice found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 6:03 AM ET: India's embassy in Muscat says 24 of the 25 crew of the Panama-flagged VLGC TARA GAS (24 of them Indian) have been evacuated ashore at Khasab and search-and-rescue operations continue for one missing Indian crew member, with Omani support

Middle East.location: Jericho area, Jordan Valley, West Bank
Middle East.summary: The IDF said it was investigating a suspected terror attack in the Jericho area and dispatched troops and set up roadblocks, Israel Red Alert reports. Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iraq orders forces into Kataib Hezbollah's Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold with a deadline after an oil-smuggling probe; the Iran-backed militia vows to keep its weapons
Middle East.location: Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), Babil province, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Rudaw reports Iraqi government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi said Iraqi forces are preparing to enter the militia-held town of Jurf al-Sakhar, with Baghdad setting a deadline for the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iranian drone attack targeting US radar in Bahrain: CENTCOM confirms IRGC one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and intercepted with no US damage or injuries, calls IRGC hit claim false
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base; earlier attacks near the Riffa helicopter base)
Middle East.summary: Iran's IRGC launched one-way attack drones toward Bahrain early Tuesday, Nov. 17, saying it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in retaliation for US drone incursions; it is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter alerts and later an all-clear, and the Bahrain Defence Force says its air defenses intercepted the attacks; Reuters headlined 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'. CENTCOM says the drones were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel and calls the IRGC's claim of a hit false.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post; Nov. 17, about 3:24 to 5:05 AM ET: The Bahrain Defence Force General Command says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a number of Iranian aerial attacks on Tuesday, Nov. 17, before they reached their targets. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. As of about 5:05 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack (no CENTCOM post found since about 1:30 AM ET), and no damage or casualties reported by Bahrain; the IRGC hit claim remains unverified; Nov. 17, about 5:30 to 5:37 AM ET: Reuters headlines its story 'Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones'; Defence24 notes this is the third such Iranian claim in five days. Bahrain still says the attack was intercepted, with no damage or casualties reported. As of about 5:57 AM ET there is still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on the Nov. 17 attack found in posts checked, and no confirmation of any hit on the radar or on US personnel; Nov. 17, about 6:43 AM ET: CENTCOM says the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US military radar system at a base in Bahrain is FALSE, and that multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC toward Bahrain on Tuesday were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or injury to American personnel (Al Arabiya English and Iran International relay the statement). Iranian state media (IRNA) posted footage it says shows the attack. Upgraded to HIGH this entry as an IRGC drone attack aimed at US forces, now confirmed by CENTCOM as an attempted attack that was intercepted; no hit, damage or casualties
