KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source
Africa.summary: A post circulating an Eritrean Ministry of Information editorial quotes it saying Eritreans and their army are ready to answer "Prosperity's invasion" in the language it has chosen. A widely shared post claims Eritrea's government announced that Ethiopia has invaded, but another account says the ministry accused Ethiopia of "preparing aggression." No independent confirmation of cross-border fighting was found.
Africa.status: Early reports; contested framing; no Ethiopian government response or independent confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Deadly clash during anti-illegal-mining operation at Manso Keniago, Ghana; Citi FM reports four dead and 15 injured
Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A confrontation broke out on Wednesday (Nov. 11) between personnel of Ghana's National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents and suspected illegal miners as the task force removed seized excavators at Manso Keniago. NAIMOS, as reported by TV3/3News, says two of its personnel were shot and injured by an armed mob. Death tolls in reports range from two to four; Citi FM's latest report says four dead and 15 injured.
Africa.status: Casualty figures differ between outlets (two, three, then four dead); circumstances, including who fired the fatal shots, not established in posts checked; NAIMOS statement covers its two injured personnel; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Mandera ambush kills eight — Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, blames suspected al-Shabaab
Africa.location: Hagarsu, Arabia Road, Mandera County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, reports eight people — two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver — were killed Tuesday in northeast Kenya near the Somali border in an attack by suspected al-Shabaab militants. Kahawa Tungu and Nairobi News, citing police, place the ambush at Hagarsu along Arabia Road in Mandera County, targeting workers on the Arabia–Lafey road construction project. No group has claimed responsibility.
Africa.status: Confirmed by police (Reuters, Citizen TV, CGTN Africa); suspected al-Shabaab per officials; no claim of responsibility found; NTV Kenya says Mandera legislators are demanding security reinforcement along the Somali border after the attack; Voice of Horn reports Kenyan police now say they are treating the ambush as banditry rather than a terror attack, that the attackers crossed into Somalia with two stolen AK-47s, and that no arrests have been made (single outlet in posts checked); Prime Media Kenya reports the eight dead were five construction workers, two police reservists and a driver, and that attackers stole the officers' rifles and fled toward Somalia; Somalia's federal government, via state news agency SONNA, condemned the attack and offered condolences; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: AFP now says 39 migrants died in the Nov. 6 boat sinking off Senegal
Africa.summary: AFP reports 39 people died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal on Nov. 6, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years, as families mourn. Reuters earlier carried a government figure of at least 21 dead, and Al Jazeera English said the Interior Ministry called its toll provisional.
Africa.status: Toll raised to 39 per AFP (earlier official provisional figure at least 21); figures differ by source; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: UNHCR says nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year
Africa.summary: Reuters reports nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for neighbouring Niger this year, escaping attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to the UN refugee agency. It says the arrivals add to mounting humanitarian needs in Niger.
Africa.status: UN agency figure via Reuters; ongoing displacement; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudan: UNICEF says 15 power stations hit in October as drone strikes spread; rights group says RSF drone attack on displaced people in Blue Nile's Al-Kurmuk killed 16
Africa.summary: UN News reports UNICEF's James Elder said 15 power stations were hit in October alone as long-range drone strikes and drought threaten survival in Sudan. Arab News reports the UN says two thirds of children killed or injured in Sudan this year were victims of drone strikes. Wasl News reports an RSF drone attack killed nine civilians in a Blue Nile village on Tuesday; that toll is not independently confirmed.
Africa.status: UN agency statements; Blue Nile casualty report from a single regional outlet, unverified; ongoing conflict; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the toll from an RSF drone attack on displaced people in Bani Shako village, Al-Kurmuk (Blue Nile), has risen to 16; it is not confirmed whether this is the same attack Wasl News reported with nine dead; rights-group figure, not independently verified; Africa_lix quotes Kurmuk governor Abdel Ati al Faki: the toll from the drone strike on displaced civilians near Bani Shako is 16 dead and six wounded with several missing (first count was nine); he blames the RSF; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somali Guardian says al-Shabaab attacks are slowing Uganda's troop withdrawal from Somalia; casualty claims unconfirmed
Africa.location: Mogadishu to Barawe corridor, Lower Shabelle, Somalia
Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Claims circulating on X that 11 Ugandan soldiers were killed in IED blasts have not been confirmed by the Ugandan military or major outlets.
Africa.status: Early reports; single regional outlet; no UPDF statement found; casualty figures unverified; the Uganda People's Defence Forces, via the government's Uganda Media Centre, rejected online reports that its troops were attacked and killed in Somalia and called them al-Shabaab propaganda; casualty claims remain unsupported; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people
Africa.summary: Voice of Horn reports Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan says clashes around Ethiopia's Moyale area have displaced more than 50,000 people, many into northern Kenya, with shortages of food, shelter and bedding. It adds that Kenya's police chief said more officers will deploy along the border. The IFRC says it is funding a Kenya Red Cross response for arrivals in Moyale, Kenya.
Africa.status: Humanitarian figures from Kenya Red Cross; final total not independently established; Citizen TV reports stray bullets from the fighting across the border have killed two people in Moyale, Kenya, and injured 22, and quotes Marsabit Governor Mohamud Ali as saying more than 10,000 Kenyans have been displaced; Nation Africa also reports about 10,000 Kenyans driven from border homes; Nov. 16: New Vision, citing AFP, says fresh territorial clashes broke out Monday with Somali and Oromia regional forces using heavy weaponry; Addis Standard reports six killed in a suspected clan militia attack near the Ethiopia-Kenya border; journalist Bashir Hashi Yusuf reports fighting on several fronts in Moyale town and says a federal delegation is there seeking a resolution; casualty totals unconfirmed; carried forward from 5:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: Assahifa English, citing residents and a community organisation, reports gunmen killed at least three people at a mining site in Plateau State on Nov. 11, following another deadly attack in the area earlier in the week.

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Johannesburg Mayfair substation outage: City Power restores power to some essential services, including Garden City Hospital and the SABC
Africa.summary: South Africa's public broadcaster SABC says transmission of some services is disrupted because of a power outage around Auckland Park that began on Nov. 8. South America.summary: Ecuador's interior minister, John Reimberg, has warned of an alleged plan to attack President Daniel Noboa, which a local outlet says he linked to a criminal leader known as 'Loco Ovidio' and the ELN. Colombian broadcaster La FM interviewed Reimberg about the alleged plot.

South America.location: Desepaz, eastern Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia

South America.title: CONTINUATION: Remedios de Escalada (Lanús) gas explosion — five remain critical with severe burns, new gas leaks found and search of rubble continues for a missing MetroGAS worker

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). Still threat reporting, not an attack; officials say there is no credible imminent threat; Nov. 17, about midnight to 2:00 AM ET: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found; i24NEWS and other outlets repeat the CNN report alongside the White House line that there is no credible threat to the homeland. Viral posts claiming an FBI dirty-bomb arrest near the White House have no primary source and are excluded. Still threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 17, about 5:48 AM ET: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the 'dirty bomb' allegations, attributed to the New York Times and spread by CNN, completely baseless and says enemies are trying to legitimize new aggression (Al Mayadeen). DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Europe.summary: Die Zeit reports that hackers used a wave of automated login attempts to try to access numerous BundID accounts and that security measures blocked the attack. The scale of any successful access was not stated in posts checked.
Europe.status: Corroborated by Die Zeit; described as a blocked or contained credential-stuffing style attack, not a confirmed data breach; carried forward from 4:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.status: Single circulating English-language account of the restoration; official customs statement not checked directly; carried forward from 4:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.location: Black Sea, about 40 nautical miles southeast of Cape Kaliakra, Bulgaria

DD Geopolitics says the ship was carrying about 3,000 tons of Ukrainian wheat from Tulcea, Romania, to Egypt and that four ships from NATO's Black Sea mine countermeasures group were sent to the scene. Russia.title: UPDATE: Crimean (Kerch) Bridge road span and arch down after second Ukrainian strike; Ukraine's General Staff and Zelensky confirm, Kremlin vows to restore it

Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and Anadolu relay the IRGC claim that it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; Nov. 17, about 3:00 AM ET: Reuters reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it remains unclear why a router installed by L3Harris Technologies at a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour Nov. 13 ground stop; the New York Post reports Duffy vowing to modernize the system. Stabilized; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Ukrainian strikes collapse a road span and arch of the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge; Russia's Investigative Committee confirms structural damage and opens a terrorism case
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). The Kyiv Independent reports an entire section collapsed after a reported Flamingo missile strike, with one arch and the roadway between two supports gone. Ukrainska Pravda says one arch fell into the sea and all traffic has stopped. Militarnyi cites Fire Point's Denys Shtilierman saying Flamingo cruise missiles destroyed a road section, and United24 says footage also shows damage to the railway arch. Still no official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 2:30 to 4:05 AM ET: Russia's Investigative Committee says Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge with drones on Nov. 16 and 17, causing damage to the structure, and has opened a terrorism case (Novaya Gazeta Europe). Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight

Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region

Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian attack on Zhytomyr region reportedly hits energy infrastructure and homes
Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports Russian Geran-4 jet-powered drones attacked a locomotive depot in Dnipro overnight, with a fire visible after the attack. No casualty figures or official confirmation were available.
Russia.status: Single OSINT source; no Ukrainian Railways or regional official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts; no Ukrainian Air Force tally, regional administration statement or damage reports found yet; AMK Mapping reports a large fire in Chornomorsk after the attack and says NASA FIRMS data shows a large fire at the impact area; it says a likely target was a freight-logistics company or the Chornomorsk Automobile Plant; still no official Ukrainian damage or casualty report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays a Russian Defense Ministry claim that the targets were a ferry terminal, the Chornomorsk port administration and a nearby electrical substation; this is a Russian military claim, not independently confirmed, and no official Ukrainian damage report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays Ukrainian energy company DTEK confirming a substation in Chornomorsk was hit by multiple drones, leaving about 41,000 homes without power; Gerashchenko and Flash report six people injured in Chornomorsk and damage to energy infrastructure, an administrative building, a gas pipeline and nearby homes; the same overnight wave injured six in Zaporizhzhia (12 strikes, per Flash) and three in a drone hit on a Kropyvnytskyi residential building; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. The Russian Defense Ministry says it downed 533 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and seas between 8 PM Nov 14 and 8 AM Nov 15 Moscow time, and SOTA and Charter 97 report Rosaviatsia restrictions at about 12 airports including Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Samara, Sochi and Volgograd. An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian double-tap drone strike in Hlukhiv, Sumy region, wounds a grandmother, her grandson and a police officer

NOEL Reports names officers Mykola Savchenko and Ihor Voloshko and says Voloshko was wounded; Ukraine's United24 says the officer and the boy were both injured and all survived.
Russia.status: Reported by Ukrainian government fundraising account United24 and multiple Ukrainian outlets with bodycam footage; final casualty details not confirmed by Sumy regional officials on X; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone strike on a house in Proletarsky, Belgorod region, kills three, Russian regional officials say
Russia.location: Proletarsky, Rakitnoye district, Belgorod region, Russia
Russia.summary: SOTA, citing the Belgorod regional operational headquarters, reports a drone hit a private house in the settlement of Proletarsky, killing a married couple and their 24-year-old daughter and injuring another man. It also reports injuries from drone attacks in Shebekino and the village of Rzhevka.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Russian regional authorities, relayed); not independently verified; no Ukrainian comment found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone strike sets warehouses on fire in Vyshhorod, just north of Kyiv

Russia.status: Early reports; casualties and official Ukrainian regional statement not found in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, injure more than 50, including eight children; a rescuer clearing rubble is killed
Russia.summary: A Russian strike on Friday damaged two five-storey apartment buildings in Zaporizhzhia, causing fires, and rescuers freed people trapped in their apartments. Ukraine's State Emergency Service says 30 people were injured, including six children. Kyiv Post reports Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed two people on Friday, including a 17-year-old boy.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Ukrainian drone attacks hit Rostov region and the Samara oil pumping station; Rostov-on-Don declares an emergency regime
Russia.location: Rostov-on-Don and Aksay district (Rostov region); Samara region, Russia
Russia.summary: NEXTA reports more than 120 drones attacked Russia's Rostov region on the night of Nov. 13, sparking a fire at a 1,500-square-metre warehouse in Aksay district and setting an industrial facility and three cars on fire in Rostov-on-Don. Sota reports Rostov-on-Don's mayor declared an emergency regime on streets where homes were damaged, saying nine apartment buildings were damaged and 114 houses were left without heat. The Insider reports the Samara regional governor confirmed a drone attack on an industrial enterprise, which monitoring channels identify as the Transneft-operated Samara oil pumping station (LPDS).

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones strike the Volgograd oil refinery, setting fires; governor says four killed and two injured
Russia.summary: Multiple posts with video, including Liveuamap, report a drone attack on the Lukoil-operated Volgograd oil refinery on the evening of Nov. 12, with fires on the plant's grounds; one post says the extent of damage remains unconfirmed. A separate post relays Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as saying more than 50 drones headed for Moscow were destroyed in about 90 minutes. Russian-source claims of 750 or more drones launched overall have not been verified.
Russia.status: Early reports with video from multiple accounts; no Volgograd regional or Lukoil statement found in posts checked; damage and casualties unconfirmed; a post citing ASTRA says reader photos show fires inside the refinery complex and that regional governor Andrei Bocharov confirmed fires at an unnamed enterprise in Volgograd's southern industrial zone, attributing them to falling drone debris; Kyiv Independent reports the mass drone attack on Moscow grounded flights at the region's airports, with Mayor Sobyanin claiming over a hundred drones shot down; claims that the refinery halted operations remain unconfirmed; a further post with video says the refinery was still burning after a lengthy drone attack, with several fires visible; Volgograd Governor Andrei Bocharov says four people, described as workers in the city's southern industrial zone, were killed and two injured in the overnight drone attack (TV Rain; Al Arabiya citing Reuters); Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 1,198 drones downed overnight over Russian regions and Crimea, per TV Rain; independent outlets report queues at Volgograd gas stations; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car explodes while driving in southern Moscow, seriously injuring the driver; Russian media say the car belonged to commentator Sergey Zavorotny
Russia.location: Kirovogradskaya Street, Chertanovo district, Moscow, Russia
Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. It comes a day after a car bomb killed a Russian Air Force colonel in St. Petersburg.
Russia.status: Early reports; cause under investigation; one Russian outlet cited a preliminary suspicion of a gas-system malfunction; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; The Washington Post now describes it as a car bombing that seriously injured a former adviser to ex-Ukrainian PM Mykola Azarov who became a pro-Kremlin commentator in Russia; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; Nov. 16: CGTN Français says Russia announced the arrest of a Russian woman it accuses of involvement in the Moscow car bombing on behalf of Ukrainian special services (Russian official claim; not independently verified); carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russia launched 117 drones overnight, including 63 jet-powered drones; 80 were intercepted or suppressed, but strikes were recorded at 24 locations and at least two people were killed. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russian media cited by these accounts identify him as the chief navigator of the 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army, but he has not been named. It is the second similar under-car bombing of an officer in the same area since late August.

Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says its journalists heard multiple explosions in Kyiv around 1 a.m. local time on Thursday (Nov. 12; about 6 p.m. ET Wednesday), shortly after Ukraine's Air Force warned that missiles were targeting the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says at least 11 missiles were used, including about five Iskander-Ms, and lists an Epicentr shopping center in northern Kyiv and the eastern industrial zone among the targets, with further strikes in the Bila Tserkva and Irpin areas. Journalist Oliver Carroll also reported ballistic strikes on Kyiv.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery
Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)
Russia.summary: Russian local channels and multiple OSINT and media accounts report a prolonged Ukrainian drone attack on Omsk on Nov. 11, with the Gazprom Neft refinery named as the target and air defense activity lasting more than two hours. Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 3:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a crowded market in Chornomorsk, Odesa region, kills three and injures 11
Russia.summary: A Russian strike hit a market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing three people and injuring 11, according to regional authorities cited by NOELreports and Ukrainian outlets. Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.

Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine

Russia.title: UPDATE: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kryvyi Rih — AMK Mapping says two 330 kV substations hit by at least 16 Geran-2 drones; Reuters confirms partial blackout
Russia.summary: A massed Russian drone attack on energy infrastructure left parts of Kryvyi Rih without power, according to city official Oleksandr Vilkul. The IRGC said six drones hit the radar of a US air-defense site at the Riffa helicopter base as the 'second phase' of its response and again declared the Strait of Hormuz closed. AMK Mapping describes a combined cruise missile and drone attack, and Al Hadath (Kuwait) reports Bahrain said air defenses intercepted an Iranian drone.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. No independent confirmation of damage found; Nov. 15 evening: FOX Baltimore reports Bahrain said it intercepted six Iranian drones aimed at a US air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa air base; Frontline Flash says no injuries or damage were reported; Nov. 16 evening: the State Department says Secretary Rubio, in a call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the US commitment to the security of Bahrain and Gulf partners (readout relayed by ANI, CGTN America and Iran International); Nov. 17, about 1:56 AM ET (9:54 AM local): Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a new potential-threat alert telling residents to go to the nearest safe location, and Al Arabiya's correspondent reported air-raid sirens. Shortly after, the IRGC (via Tasnim, relayed by Faytuks Network and ME Observer) said it targeted a US military radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base with combat drones in retaliation for US drone incursions into Iranian airspace. OSINT accounts and residents report explosions heard; no CENTCOM or Bahraini statement on interceptions, damage or casualties found as of about 2:10 AM ET. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET; Nov. 17, about 3:10 to 4:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued two threat alerts (about 1:56 and 2:14 AM ET) before the all-clear at about 2:48 AM ET. TRT World and The Jerusalem Post report Bahrain says it intercepted the Iranian air attacks; Anadolu relays the IRGC claim that the attack retaliated for US drone incursions. Still no CENTCOM or Pentagon statement on this attack, and no US damage or casualties, found in posts checked as of about 4:05 AM ET (CENTCOM has posted nothing since 1:30 AM ET in posts checked); viral posts saying CENTCOM confirmed no damage could not be traced to a CENTCOM post

America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

The IRGC said six drones hit the radar of a US air-defense site at the Riffa helicopter base as the 'second phase' of its response and again declared the Strait of Hormuz closed. AMK Mapping describes a combined cruise missile and drone attack, and Al Hadath (Kuwait) reports Bahrain said air defenses intercepted an Iranian drone.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. IRGC damage claims are unverified; Nov. 17, about 2:48 to 3:05 AM ET: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced an all-clear (MOI). Al Arabiya English reports Bahraini authorities said the threat had passed after air defenses intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, and Al Jazeera English cites Bahraini state television saying the IRGC drone attack was thwarted. The IRGC's claim of a hit on a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base remains a claim only: no CENTCOM statement, US damage or casualties found in posts checked as of about 3:05 AM ET

America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro in a massive overnight attack across Ukraine
Russia.location: Kyiv, Ukraine (also Kharkiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Cherkasy)
Russia.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said preliminary reports indicate impacts on the North and South bridges in the capital during a massive Russian ballistic missile attack late Monday, Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post report. BBC's John Simpson says the attacks began about 11:36 PM local time and he counted 10 or 11 explosions, with both bridges apparently hit, after President Zelensky warned of big strikes. Drop Site News notes the Southern Bridge also carries a metro line, that explosions were reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Cherkasy, and that no casualties had been reported. Secondary accounts citing Kyiv Independent say strikes knocked out water and heat (and some power) in parts of the city.
Russia.status: Mayor's preliminary statement relayed by Kyiv Independent and Kyiv Post; corroborated by a BBC correspondent; extent of bridge damage, utility outages and casualties not yet officially detailed; Nov. 16 night: Reuters reports Klitschko said Russian forces struck the two Dnipro bridges along with some other critical infrastructure as Moscow sent drones and missiles across Ukraine; outlets relaying the mayor say water, heating and power were cut in parts of the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says five Iskander-M missiles hit the bridges (three on the Northern, two on the Southern), with a fire on the Northern Bridge (unofficial). No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; Nov. 16, about 10:40 PM ET (5:40 AM Kyiv time): Al Jazeera's correspondent reports a series of explosions in Kyiv with air-raid sirens on, and Ukrainian channels relayed by Faytuks report a new Russian missile attack on bridge(s) in the city. At about 11:45 PM ET, Economist correspondent Oliver Carroll said Russian missile strikes have stopped traffic on the two main river bridges linking Kyiv's east and west and that there are some problems with water and electricity. No casualty figures or official damage assessment found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found
