Russia.title: UPDATE: Ukrainian strikes collapse a road span and arch of the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge overnight, imagery shows; Aksyonov confirms second attack and closure
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge for the second time in about 24 hours overnight Nov. 16–17. Daylight imagery published by Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender and NEXTA shows the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the water, and a prominent Russian milblogger acknowledges significant damage. Russian-installed Crimea head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the attack, suspended traffic and said two people were killed in a drone attack on Crimea. The bridge is Russia's only direct road and rail link to occupied Crimea, and debris may block shipping between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed; Nov. 16 late evening: Drop Site News says Aksyonov reported a second strike early Tuesday local time, halted traffic and urged people to avoid the area; videos purport to show two impacts on the arches. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called Monday's damage minor, while Russian TV footage showed a direct hit on the main road arch, reportedly tilted 4.9 degrees (not officially confirmed). Fox News and a BBC-cited summary say Russia reports 2,049 drones downed in 24 hours (about 600 toward Moscow) and fires at industrial facilities and refineries; Nov. 16, about 11:15 PM ET: Faytuks quotes the Russian military channel Two Majors as saying a massive overnight strike overloaded and broke through air defenses near the Crimean Bridge, reportedly with Western missiles, and that the attack continued through the night. This is a Russian milblogger claim; no official Russian damage statement found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 12:15 to 2:00 AM ET: daylight photos and video show the road arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road span collapsed into the Kerch Strait (Militarnyi, Faytuks, OSINTdefender, NEXTA); Russian milblogger Boris Rozhin (Colonelcassad) is quoted saying a span and arch of the roadway section collapsed and 'the damage is significant'. Aksyonov confirmed the second attack, closed the bridge and said two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea (Al Arabiya). Ukrainian forces released video they say shows an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile before impact. United24 and OSINT accounts say rail and Kerch Strait shipping traffic are also halted and debris blocks the channel; the rail span shows damage. No official Russian damage assessment found in posts checked

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian drone attack on Ukraine — 117 drones launched, strikes at 24 locations; at least two killed, medical facility hit in Kyiv
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russia launched 117 drones overnight, including 63 jet-powered drones; 80 were intercepted or suppressed, but strikes were recorded at 24 locations and at least two people were killed. A Ukrainian outlet reports a 17-year-old was killed in Zaporizhzhia and that a night strike on a medical facility in Kyiv injured one person, with seven people freed and 30 evacuated.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Ukrainian government communications center); casualty details from a single media account; First Squawk reports Ukraine's deputy energy minister says the overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure caused power outages in 12 regions; Ukraine's Foreign Ministry says the overnight Russian strikes killed two people and injured at least 14 across Ukraine, including a strike that destroyed a private house in Odesa (two killed, five injured) and an attack on an apartment building in Rivne (six injured); TVP World reports Ukrainian authorities count at least nine killed and 61 wounded in the overnight attacks across multiple regions, including three wounded and 30 evacuated in Kyiv; this is higher than the Foreign Ministry's earlier count of two killed and 14 injured, and the regions covered may differ; Ukrinform reports a Russian attack on an energy facility in Odesa region left nearly 50,000 consumers without power; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Finland says its forces detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland; reports name the missile corvette Naro-Fominsk
Russia.summary: Reuters reports that Finland's military said it detected "a strike" on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea a day earlier but that the security situation in the area remained stable. Estonian media reported that the small navy ship later returned to St. Petersburg. Posts citing Yle sources and Estonia's defence minister name the Buyan-M corvette Naro-Fominsk; Ukrainian drone involvement is reported but not confirmed in posts checked.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Finnish Defence Forces, via Reuters); casualties and cause not confirmed; vessel identification from media reports; Visegrád 24 says Estonia confirms the Russian corvette was struck by three Ukrainian drones near the Finnish coast and was towed back to port; single-source relay, no Estonian official post found on X; UKikaski and visionergeo say Estonian Defence Forces now confirm Ukrainian drones struck and disabled the Baltic Fleet missile ship Naro-Fominsk (595) in the Gulf of Finland on Nov. 11, with dead and wounded among the crew per an Estonian division deputy commander; relayed by OSINT accounts, no Estonian official post or Russian confirmation found on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russian media cited by these accounts identify him as the chief navigator of the 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army, but he has not been named. It is the second similar under-car bombing of an officer in the same area since late August.
Russia.status: Corroborated by multiple outlets (Novaya Gazeta Europe, The Straits Times; Russia's Investigative Committee cited by journalist Christopher Miller); colonel's name not officially confirmed; suspect reports come from Russian media only; no claim of responsibility; The Kyiv Independent and Xinhua cite St. Petersburg's Investigative Committee saying a serviceman was killed when his car exploded in the Pushkinsky district (Shushary) and a murder case has been opened; CGTN Europe reports a Russian serviceman was killed when his SUV was destroyed by an explosion in the Pushkinsky District, with a nearby bus also damaged; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight — one woman killed in a Solomianskyi high-rise; State Emergency Service says two rescuers killed in Kyiv region
Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says its journalists heard multiple explosions in Kyiv around 1 a.m. local time on Thursday (Nov. 12; about 6 p.m. ET Wednesday), shortly after Ukraine's Air Force warned that missiles were targeting the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says at least 11 missiles were used, including about five Iskander-Ms, and lists an Epicentr shopping center in northern Kyiv and the eastern industrial zone among the targets, with further strikes in the Bila Tserkva and Irpin areas. Journalist Oliver Carroll also reported ballistic strikes on Kyiv.
Russia.status: Official statements issued (Kyiv City Military Administration; State Emergency Service as relayed by CGTN Europe): one killed and five injured in Kyiv city, two rescuers killed in Kyiv region; Russian MoD target claims unverified; Ukrinform, citing Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, says one person was killed and seven injured in the strike on the residential building, with fire on the third to sixth floors; Euromaidan Press says the woman killed was 44; ZMiST reports the overnight attack caused damage across eight Ukrainian regions, mainly energy and transport infrastructure, including a power generation facility in Zaporizhzhia and high-voltage substations in Odesa and Rivne regions; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery
Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)
Russia.summary: Russian local channels and multiple OSINT and media accounts report a prolonged Ukrainian drone attack on Omsk on Nov. 11, with the Gazprom Neft refinery named as the target and air defense activity lasting more than two hours. NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a crowded market in Chornomorsk, Odesa region, kills three and injures 11
Russia.summary: A Russian strike hit a market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing three people and injuring 11, according to regional authorities cited by NOELreports and Ukrainian outlets. Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.
Russia.status: Regional authorities report; toll rose from one to three killed during the morning; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: New Voice of Ukraine on X

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro kills three and injures four
Russia.summary: Suspilne, citing regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha, reports a Russian strike hit a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro, killing two people, injuring at least four and starting a fire. Hromadske Radio later reported the toll rose to three, with businesses and a private home also damaged and four men hospitalized, two in serious condition. CGTN Europe, citing Ukraine's health service, reports three killed and five injured across Dnipropetrovsk region during the day.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) figures relayed by Ukrainian outlets; emergency services at the scene; facility not named; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Hromadske Radio: toll rises to three

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian missile and drone strikes target Odesa Oblast bridges and 330 kV substations, plus substations in Kharkiv and Chernihiv, OSINT mapper reports
Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports a large combined Russian attack on Odesa Oblast overnight using cruise missiles, glide bombs and drones, targeting the Mayaky and Zatoka road bridges that link southern Odesa Oblast to the rest of Ukraine, as well as 330 kV substations in Artsyz and the "Podilska" substation. It says at least four cruise missiles were shot down and two flew briefly through Moldovan airspace. The same account reports fires in Kharkiv and Chernihiv after strikes on 110 kV substations.
Russia.status: Early reports; single OSINT mapping source; damage and outages not yet confirmed by Ukrainian officials or utilities on X; Kharkiv and Chernihiv substation strikes echoed by other OSINT accounts (one says one person injured in Kharkiv); still no Ukrainian official or utility statement found on X; First Squawk relays the Odesa governor saying energy targets were hit overnight; bne IntelliNews reports Russian strikes cut power to 135,000 in Odesa region; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: First Squawk: governor says Odesa energy targets hit
bne IntelliNews: power cut to 135,000 in Odesa region

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; Nov. 16 afternoon: journalist Christopher Miller says Mayor Boris Filatov reports about half of Dnipro, a city of about one million, is without power after Russian attacks on the energy system, calling it the sixth blackout in two weeks, with two people killed, 10 high-rise buildings damaged and the Bunge-owned Oleina plant hit a third time; UNIAN says the city was left completely without power after a series of attacks, with outages also in parts of the region; MAKS 26 quotes DTEK as saying Dnipro lost electricity entirely and that crews were first restoring power to water, heat and social facilities; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kryvyi Rih — AMK Mapping says two 330 kV substations hit by at least 16 Geran-2 drones; Reuters confirms partial blackout
Russia.summary: A massed Russian drone attack on energy infrastructure left parts of Kryvyi Rih without power, according to city official Oleksandr Vilkul. Apartment buildings, schools and kindergartens were damaged. Water and sewage services are being stabilized with generators, but heating will be harder to restore. AMK Mapping says at least 16 Geran-2 drones were used and that the "Pivdenna" and "Hirnycha" 330 kV substations on the city's southern outskirts were hit.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (city official Oleksandr Vilkul); Reuters reports the outage; substation details from OSINT mapping account, not officially confirmed; casualty figures not reported; Reuters headline reconfirmed this window; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Leningrad governor confirms fire in Ust-Luga port area and emergency substation shutdown during drone attack; says 146 drones intercepted overnight
Russia.summary: Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko said a fire broke out in the Ust-Luga port area during an overnight Ukrainian drone attack and that a substation in the port zone went into emergency shutdown. He said 146 drones were intercepted over the region as of 7:30 a.m. local time and that there was no information on casualties. Earlier OSINT footage showed the oil terminal burning.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Leningrad governor, relayed by OSINT/news accounts); no casualty information; extent of terminal damage unknown; tanker damage claims unconfirmed; NASA FIRMS satellite data shows multiple fires at and just off the port (OSINTdefender); Estonian public broadcaster ERR shows the fire visible from Estonia; Reuters carries the governor's account of the fire; Hromadske cites the governor on a substation shutdown and three injured workers; Meduza says two people were killed in the Smolensk region when officials say drone debris hit an apartment building; NOELreports says the Ust-Luga port terminal was still burning on Wednesday morning after the overnight attack; NOELreports cites OSINT channel Absreliable reporting fires at three 30,000-cubic-meter tanks and damage to processing equipment and a berth at Novatek; Russian sources cited by Osint613, OSINTdefender and NOELreports say two Ka-52 attack helicopters and an Mi-8 went down while responding to the drone attack, reportedly partly to friendly air defense, with one to three crews killed (Russian-source claims, unconfirmed by officials); Ukraine's SBU says the overnight operation struck port and oil infrastructure at Ust-Luga, damaging several petroleum storage tanks, and also hit the Buyan-M-class missile ship Naro-Fominsk; damage to the ship not established; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Ukrainian strikes have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%; fuel purchase limits spread to St. Petersburg and Leningrad region
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent and Novaya Gazeta Europe, citing Reuters and two industry sources, report renewed Ukrainian attacks since late October have cut Russian refining capacity by about 30%, disrupting nine of Russia's 35 major refineries over the past week, including plants in Ryazan and Yaroslavl, per Meduza. SOTA, citing Bumaga, reports Rosneft stations in St. Petersburg have capped purchases since Nov. 8, and Novaya Gazeta Europe reports fuel limits returning in Leningrad region.
Russia.status: Refining capacity cut reported by Reuters (via established outlets); regional rationing reported; no official nationwide measure; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Railway bridge span collapses over the Viled River in Russia's Arkhangelsk region, derailing freight cars and halting traffic
Russia.summary: Meduza reports a span of a railway bridge collapsed in the Arkhangelsk region and several passenger trains were delayed. NEXTA reports several freight cars derailed after a section of the bridge over the Viled River collapsed between Cheryomukha and Viled and rail traffic on the section was suspended. Posts on X claim sabotage, but no official cause has been established.
Russia.status: Traffic halted on the section; at least eight passenger trains delayed per reports; cause under investigation; sabotage claims unverified; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kyiv Independent says Russian attacks killed 10 and injured 40 across Ukraine over the past day; ballistic and Zircon missiles plus 123 drones launched overnight
Russia.location: Kirovohrad, Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says air defenses neutralized 135 of 162 Russian drones, 70 of them jet-powered, and that Russia also launched an Iskander-M ballistic missile. It says hits were recorded in 19 locations and debris fell in nine more. It reports critical infrastructure in the Kirovohrad region was attacked, with two people injured, and that a business in Dnipro caught fire. Ukrainska Pravda and Ukrinform carry the same figures.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone hits a commuter train at Sumy railway station; no casualties reported
Russia.summary: The head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, Oleh Hryhorov, says a Russian drone deliberately struck a commuter train at the Sumy railway station on Tuesday morning. He says there were no passengers on board, the crew was in a shelter and there were no casualties. Ukrainska Pravda and RBC-Ukraine also report the attack on the train.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) statement; no casualties; damage to rolling stock; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drones kill two in Ladyzhyn, Vinnytsia region; energy facilities and a civilian enterprise hit; three days of mourning
Russia.summary: Ukrainska Pravda reports that Russian forces attacked a civilian enterprise in Vinnytsia region, killing two people. The type of enterprise and the extent of the damage were not given in the post.
Russia.status: Reported by Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda; energy damage extent not given; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drones target military aircraft repair plant in Russia's Novgorod region; explosions reported near Staraya Russa
Russia.location: Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, Russia; Crimea
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, citing Telegram monitoring channels, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea. No damage assessment or official Russian or Ukrainian statement was found. RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.
Russia.status: Early reports; Ukrainian outlets citing media and monitoring channels; damage not officially confirmed on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Centrenergo warns of 'extremely serious' consequences after Russian strike on Trypillia Thermal Power Plant
Russia.summary: Russian forces struck the Trypillia Thermal Power Plant, the Kyiv Independent reports. Centrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned generating company, said the impact appears significant, but the extent of the damage is not yet clear and needs further inspection.
Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Responsibility is not established in the posts found.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (IAEA, via Kyiv Independent); carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

IAEA: ZNPP employee killed in drone attack today

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Houthi-run Saba says seven Saudi airstrikes hit northern Sanaa before dawn Tuesday; no coalition statement
Middle East.location: Sanaa, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Yemeni accounts citing local residents report a series of heavy airstrikes on Houthi-held sites in Sanaa around 6:10 AM local time on Nov. 17 (about 10:10 PM ET Nov. 16), with explosions heard across the city and warplanes flying low. Houthi-aligned commentator Hussain al-Bukhaiti says there were three Saudi airstrikes on the capital. A situation-map account says the reports cite unnamed Arab sources with no official confirmation.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; no Saudi-led coalition or Houthi official statement, targets or casualty figures found in posts checked; Nov. 17, about 1:40 AM ET: Houthi-run Saba news agency, relayed by Al Mayadeen, says seven Saudi airstrikes destroyed a textile and shoe factory belonging to an orphans' development foundation in al-Nahda, northern Sanaa, and separately reports four Saudi strikes in al-Misrakh district, Taiz. No Saudi-led coalition statement or casualty figures found; target descriptions are Houthi claims

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC claims it captured a ninth US MQM-170 drone intact south of Qeshm Island
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, south of Qeshm Island, Iran
Middle East.summary: Citing Iran's state Press TV, accounts report the IRGC Aerospace Force says it used electronic warfare to seize another American MQM-170 drone over waters south of Qeshm Island and land it undamaged, which it says makes nine captured. This is an Iranian state claim.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only; no US confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: Middle East Prime on X (citing Press TV)

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Palestinian woman killed and 10 wounded by what Palestinian TV calls Israeli settler gunfire in Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho
Middle East.location: Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, West Bank
Middle East.summary: Reuters reports Palestinian official television said a Palestinian woman was killed and 10 others wounded by what it described as gunfire from Israeli settlers in Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho. Haaretz reports the Palestinian account alongside the IDF's report of the attack on Israelis in the same area earlier Monday.
Middle East.status: Palestinian official account reported by Reuters and Haaretz; no IDF statement on the shooting found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: the IDF says that on the outskirts of Jericho, attackers rammed an Israeli vehicle, then got out with weapons and attacked the occupants; rocks were thrown and the Israelis fired 'to remove the threat,' with Israeli and Palestinian casualties. Forces are pursuing suspects and setting up roadblocks. i24NEWS reports two Israelis injured in a suspected terror attack outside Jericho and a Palestinian woman shot dead. The accounts conflict: Palestinian sources describe settler gunfire, while the IDF describes a ramming attack; Nov. 17, about 1:40 AM ET: Reuters reports a Palestinian woman killed and 10 wounded in settler gunfire, citing official Palestinian TV

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: CENTCOM confirms the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group is operating in the Middle East, giving the US three carriers in the region
Middle East.location: US Central Command area of responsibility (Middle East)
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English and Kuwait's state news agency KUNA report that US Central Command confirmed the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt is operating in the Middle East as part of a scheduled deployment. Xinhua and Antiwar.com say this brings the number of US carrier strike groups in the region to three, though the Roosevelt is expected to replace the USS George Washington at an unannounced time.
Middle East.status: Officially announced deployment (CENTCOM, as reported by Al Jazeera and KUNA); escalation signal amid Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Hormuz shipping; no new US strikes on Iran reported; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: KUNA on X (Kuwait state news agency)

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 208-26: tanker attacked 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz; vessel disabled with an engine-room fire
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16 evening: NDTV reports the Khasab tanker attack citing UKMTO; vessel still not identified and no responsibility claim found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Suspected car-ramming and axe attack near Jericho wounds two Israelis; IDF investigating
Middle East.location: Jericho area, Jordan Valley, West Bank
Middle East.summary: The IDF said it was investigating a suspected terror attack in the Jericho area and dispatched troops and set up roadblocks, Israel Red Alert reports. Initial reports say two people were injured in a suspected vehicle-ramming; Intel24News, citing Ynet, says a Palestinian vehicle deliberately struck an Israeli vehicle and its occupants were attacked with axes. NewsinIsraelUK says two Israelis were wounded near a Jericho outpost. Reports that assailants were shot are not confirmed by an official post checked.
Middle East.status: Developing; IDF investigating; injuries reported as two; assailants' fate unconfirmed officially; Nov. 16 night: Ynet News says two 18-year-old Israelis were hospitalized after assailants allegedly rammed their vehicle and attacked them with clubs and axes near Jericho; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Iraq orders forces into Kataib Hezbollah's Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold with a deadline after an oil-smuggling probe; the Iran-backed militia vows to keep its weapons
Middle East.location: Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), Babil province, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Rudaw reports Iraqi government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi said Iraqi forces are preparing to enter the militia-held town of Jurf al-Sakhar, with Baghdad setting a deadline for the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah. Al Jazeera English says forces were ordered in following oil-smuggling allegations, which the group denies, calling the crackdown an attempt to seize its weapons. Kataib Hezbollah posted that its weapons 'will remain in the hands of our Mujahideen' with photos of fighters setting up drones (Rudaw). Kurdistan24 and a Rudaw journalist report a tense Coordination Framework meeting, with Prime Minister al-Zaidi walking out over the dispute.
Middle East.status: Official Iraqi government statements reported by Rudaw and Al Jazeera; no clashes reported in posts checked; standoff developing; Nov. 16 night: The New Arab quotes Iraqi security expert Hashim al-Saadi saying Kataib Hezbollah and its allies are unlikely to give up Jurf al-Sakhar easily; no clashes or entry by government forces reported in posts checked; Nov. 16 night: Iran International, citing Al Arabiya sources, says an Iranian delegation arrived in Baghdad for talks to defuse the Iraqi government–Kataib Hezbollah standoff over Jurf al-Sakhar. Some Coordination Framework leaders have proposed replacing Kataib Hezbollah fighters with shrine-affiliated PMF units as a compromise. No clashes reported in posts checked; Nov. 17 early: The New Arab says Kataib Hezbollah denies involvement in oil smuggling from Jurf al-Sakhar; Channel8, citing sources, says the group opposes bloodshed and that mediation is under way. No clashes reported in posts checked

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi health officials say Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Omran province killed three, including a child
Middle East.location: Sanaa and Harf Sufian (Omran province), Yemen
Middle East.summary: The Tectonic, citing the AP, says a Houthi health ministry spokesman reported that a drone strike on a house in Sanaa's al-Sarar quarter killed a child and wounded seven, and that airstrikes on a private fuel station in Harf Sufian district killed two and wounded eight. The spokesman blamed Saudi Arabia, and Riyadh did not immediately comment.

The motive has not been established and no arrests have been made; Yfm reports a manhunt is under way and SABC says the Gauteng police commissioner is at the scene.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; comes hours after the separate Sweetwaters (KZN) shooting that killed eight; Nov. 16: Channels TV says police put the toll from the Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters shootings at 17; Newzroom Afrika and Sowetan carry Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni saying one of the nine victims was a person of interest in a December 2025 mass shooting and linking the case to the Saulsville shooting; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: WPLG says at least 17 were killed in the two mass shootings about 330 miles apart and police have not established motives; Pretoria News says SAPS is probing a possible retaliation motive after confirming one victim was a person of interest in the Saulsville case (also EWN); eNCA reports Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi's condolences; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: Reuters, NBC News, Al Jazeera and BBC report at least 17 dead in two weekend mass shootings: nine in the shack near Pretoria and eight men found in a bullet-riddled vehicle near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal; police say motives not yet established and no arrests reported; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight people shot dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters outside Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.location: Mabane Section, Sweetwaters, Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says KwaZulu-Natal police are investigating the murder of eight people who were allegedly shot and killed inside a vehicle along the road at Mabane Section in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg. Daily News reports the eight men were killed on Sunday evening and that a murder investigation is under way. No motive or arrests have been announced.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Peter Obi condemns a reported attack on Kwankwaso's NDC convoy in Bichi, Kano State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Opposition presidential candidate Peter Obi says he is saddened by reports of an attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area. He calls for an immediate investigation and arrests. Kwankwaso had been commissioning NDC offices across Kano State on Sunday.
Africa.status: Early reports; party-side statement only; no police statement, casualty count or damage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya opens probe into violent protests at the Dadaab refugee complex
Africa.location: Hagadera camp, Dadaab, Garissa County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Anadolu reports that Kenyan authorities have opened an investigation after protesters opposing a planned market in Hagadera camp damaged government offices, stole equipment and broke into nearby businesses during clashes.
Africa.status: Single wire report citing authorities; casualty figures not reported; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. It cites Caasimada Online as saying forces loyal to a former South West state leader took Golweyn.
Africa.status: Single-source early report citing Caasimada Online; no official statement or claim of responsibility found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: JNIM reportedly overruns a national police detachment at Balga, near Fada N'Gourma, eastern Burkina Faso
Africa.location: Balga, about 25 km from Fada N’Gourma, Est region, Burkina Faso
Africa.summary: A Sahel-focused account reports that a JNIM attack on the morning of Nov. 15 targeted the National Police detachment at Balga, sacking and burning it, and that many officers were killed and several are missing. It adds that the attackers took all weapons, ammunition and vehicles.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no official Burkinabe statement or casualty figure found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill a Zamfara governor's aide in a dawn attack in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits attacked worshippers at dawn prayer in Kaura Namoda on Sunday, Nov. 15, killing Nasiru Sani Kaura and abducting several others, according to the security platform Bakatsine (via Africa_lix). Nigerians_New reports he was an aide to Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal.
Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Several villages were burned and residents fled, and the RSF sent reinforcements to separate the two sides.
Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Al-Shabaab reported to seize Coomaad in Somalia's Hiiraan region and advance toward Matabaan
Africa.summary: Baidoa Online reports al-Shabaab militants took control of Coomaad in Hiiraan after clashes with local forces early Sunday. It says the area is about 31 km from Matabaan district and the group is reportedly advancing toward it.
Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; Nov. 15: Sudan Tribune reports intensive army drone strikes on RSF positions as the army advances on Al-Nuhud, with thousands of civilians fleeing toward Darfur; the Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights says the RSF moved all detainees, including civilians, from Al-Nuhud to Nyala; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed
Africa.location: Mundri East / Mundri West counties, Western Equatoria, South Sudan
Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eritrea's Information Ministry says its army is ready to answer an Ethiopian "invasion"; viral claim that Eritrea announced an actual invasion lacks a primary source

A widely shared post claims Eritrea's government announced that Ethiopia has invaded, but another account says the ministry accused Ethiopia of "preparing aggression." Africa.status: Early reports; contested framing; no Ethiopian government response or independent confirmation found in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A confrontation broke out on Wednesday (Nov. 11) between personnel of Ghana's National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents and suspected illegal miners as the task force removed seized excavators at Manso Keniago. NAIMOS, as reported by TV3/3News, says two of its personnel were shot and injured by an armed mob. Death tolls in reports range from two to four; Citi FM's latest report says four dead and 15 injured.
Africa.status: Casualty figures differ between outlets (two, three, then four dead); circumstances, including who fired the fatal shots, not established in posts checked; NAIMOS statement covers its two injured personnel; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.location: Hagarsu, Arabia Road, Mandera County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, reports eight people — two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver — were killed Tuesday in northeast Kenya near the Somali border in an attack by suspected al-Shabaab militants. Kahawa Tungu and Nairobi News, citing police, place the ambush at Hagarsu along Arabia Road in Mandera County, targeting workers on the Arabia–Lafey road construction project. Africa.title: CONTINUATION: UNHCR says nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year
Africa.summary: Reuters reports nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for neighbouring Niger this year, escaping attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to the UN refugee agency. It says the arrivals add to mounting humanitarian needs in Niger.
Africa.status: UN agency figure via Reuters; ongoing displacement; carried forward from 12:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: UN News reports UNICEF's James Elder said 15 power stations were hit in October alone as long-range drone strikes and drought threaten survival in Sudan. Wasl News reports an RSF drone attack killed nine civilians in a Blue Nile village on Tuesday; that toll is not independently confirmed.

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somali Guardian says al-Shabaab attacks are slowing Uganda's troop withdrawal from Somalia; casualty claims unconfirmed
Africa.location: Mogadishu to Barawe corridor, Lower Shabelle, Somalia
Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Claims circulating on X that 11 Ugandan soldiers were killed in IED blasts have not been confirmed by the Ugandan military or major outlets.

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people
Africa.summary: Voice of Horn reports Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan says clashes around Ethiopia's Moyale area have displaced more than 50,000 people, many into northern Kenya, with shortages of food, shelter and bedding. The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. America.title: UPDATE: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized; Nov. 16, about 9:45 PM ET: DHS posts Secretary Mullin saying "I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyberattack...nothing points to it being connected" about the FAA ground stop and other recent tech problems. Stabilized; monitoring can scale back

Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Middle East.location: US Central Command area of responsibility (Middle East)

Middle East.status: Officially announced deployment (CENTCOM, as reported by Al Jazeera and KUNA); escalation signal amid Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Hormuz shipping; no new US strikes on Iran reported; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Middle East.location: Jericho area, Jordan Valley, West Bank

Middle East.location: Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), Babil province, Iraq

Middle East.status: Early reports from Al Jazeera and local accounts; Israeli official comment not seen in posts checked; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sirik and Kong, Hormozgan province, and in Shahriyar near Tehran; cause unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran

Middle East.summary: Iranian state media IRNA reported explosions heard in the port city of Jask near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday evening, with further reports from Bandar Abbas. Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Two weekend mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 17 dead — nine in Jeffsville near Pretoria and eight in a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg
Africa.location: Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa
Africa.summary: The South African Police Service says nine people, six men and three women, were found shot dead inside a four-roomed shack in Jeffsville informal settlement. Police say the shooting is reported to have happened between 10 and 11 p.m. on Nov. 15 and that they were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Nov. 16. The motive has not been established and no arrests have been made; Yfm reports a manhunt is under way and SABC says the Gauteng police commissioner is at the scene.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (SAPS); suspects at large; motive unknown; comes hours after the separate Sweetwaters (KZN) shooting that killed eight; Nov. 16: Channels TV says police put the toll from the Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters shootings at 17; Newzroom Afrika and Sowetan carry Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni saying one of the nine victims was a person of interest in a December 2025 mass shooting and linking the case to the Saulsville shooting; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: WPLG says at least 17 were killed in the two mass shootings about 330 miles apart and police have not established motives; Pretoria News says SAPS is probing a possible retaliation motive after confirming one victim was a person of interest in the Saulsville case (also EWN); eNCA reports Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi's condolences; no arrests reported in posts checked; Nov. 16: Reuters, NBC News, Al Jazeera and BBC report at least 17 dead in two weekend mass shootings: nine in the shack near Pretoria and eight men found in a bullet-riddled vehicle near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal; police say motives not yet established and no arrests reported; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

threats.title: UPDATE: Threat reporting: CNN, citing seven US officials, says new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon
threats.summary: This is threat reporting, not an attack. CNN reports (exclusive by Katie Bo Lillis, Zachary Cohen and colleagues) that new US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, D.C., which has prompted a flurry of contingency planning, even as officials debate whether Iran can or will attempt such a plot. Drop Site News, summarizing the CNN report, says the White House said there are "no credible threats to the homeland," that sources describe the planning as "options" rather than an imminent plot, and that Iran's UN mission called the chemical-weapons claims "fabricated." The report follows the Secret Service move of Treasury Secretary Bessent to a military base over Iranian threats and the US indictment of Iranian-backed operatives already in this log.
threats.status: Major-outlet report citing seven US officials (CNN); no attack has occurred; White House says no credible homeland threat (as relayed by outlets summarizing CNN); Iran's UN mission denies the chemical-weapons claims; no DHS/FBI public bulletin or NTAS change found in this sweep; Nov. 16, about 9:40 PM ET: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asked on Fox News' Hannity what he would tell Americans worried about national security, said "Well, breathe. The homeland is secure" (Fox News clip); no DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep. Accounts quoting the CNN report add that US intelligence picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials were stashed inside the US, that officials are divided on its credibility, and that officials broadly believe Iran could have pre-positioned nuclear or chemical materials; this detail is attributed to one CNN source and is not independently confirmed. No new CNN posts since the original report were found; this remains threat reporting, not an attack; Nov. 16, about 10:00 PM ET to midnight: no new CNN reporting, DHS/FBI bulletin, NTAS change or CISA advisory found in this sweep; coverage is now mostly outlets and accounts re-reporting CNN (TRT World notes Tehran denies the allegations). America.title: NEW: Supply-chain attack through Optimizely serves malware ("OPTIMJACK") to visitors of about 178 major organizations' websites
America.location: Global (websites of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, IKEA, Equifax, Ledger and others)

America.status: Confirmed by the vendor (Optimizely) and independent researchers; vendor says contained and the injected code removed; extent of victim losses and data theft not yet known

America.title: UPDATE: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; Nov. 16 night: Reuters says US air travel has largely returned to normal after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, though the recovery was briefly marred by the United technology outage. Stabilized

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet.
