America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Kyiv Post says guided aerial bombs hit the Dzherelo gymnasium and an underground shelter where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian aid, and that four people remain missing. NOEL Reports says emergency services confirmed the toll, with four hospitalized, and that Russia struck the town 11 more times during recovery work, including nine strikes on the rescue site.
Russia.status: Official toll (Interior Ministry and emergency services) relayed by several outlets; event dates to Nov. 2; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Ukraine strikes the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge again Monday night; Russian-installed Crimea head says traffic suspended
Russia.location: Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of occupied Crimea, says Ukrainian forces struck the bridge across the Kerch Strait overnight. He says vehicle traffic on the bridge is restricted until around midday. Al Arabiya and NEXTA carried the statement; the extent of any damage has not been described.
Russia.status: Statement by Russian-installed authorities, reported by several outlets; no Ukrainian military confirmation and no damage details found in posts checked; Nov. 16: aggregator Mario Nawfal repeats the Russian-installed governor's statement that traffic is restricted until midday and that he gave no damage details; no new official detail found; Nov. 16: iStories reports Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge sustained 'minor damage' and that drivers complained of communications outages; no fuller official damage assessment found; Nov. 16: WarTranslated says satellite imagery published by monitoring channels shows at least two damaged roadway sections and a deformed arch; Ukrainian Front reports the same; imagery not independently verified in posts checked; Nov. 16 afternoon: Special Kherson Cat (bayraktar_1love) says Russia's Transport Ministry reported that traffic on the Crimean Bridge has partially resumed in alternating one-way mode after the morning drone attack; Kakka (kakkamax), citing Echo FM reporting, says the bridge remained closed as of 16:00 local time after Aksyonov had earlier said it would stay closed until about midday, and that Peskov called the damage 'minor' while aggregators reported long backups. Accounts differ on when traffic actually resumed; Nov. 16 afternoon: NBC News says Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since 2022, with Moscow saying air defenses downed 1,336 drones across 16 regions; the New York Post headline says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge in the attack; Nov. 16 evening: Drop Site News, citing the Financial Times, says Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing 2,049 drones over 24 hours across 15 regions. A pro-Russian channel (SMO_VZ) says traffic resumed across the bridge in reversible mode by about 7 PM local time after a closure of almost 17 hours, with trains running without restrictions; not confirmed by an official post in this sweep; Nov. 16 night: Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov, as quoted by NatalkaKyiv, says the bridge was attacked again and traffic is suspended; Kyiv Independent says Ukrainian forces reportedly struck the bridge again after the Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's bridges; Anton Gerashchenko relays Russian Z-blogger claims that an arch was hit directly, which he says is unconfirmed; damage not officially detailed

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Oil depot reported on fire in Azov, Rostov region, after overnight Ukrainian drone attack
Russia.summary: Multiple accounts posted videos of a large fire and explosions at an oil depot in Azov in Russia's Rostov region early Monday local time, after a drone attack. Anton Gerashchenko says the depot is reportedly on fire, and LetsArmUKR places the blaze at the depot off Kondaurova Street. Thetect0nic, citing monitoring account AMK, says an oil depot may be among the targets and that cruise missiles were also reported.
Russia.status: Official statement issued: Rostov Governor Yury Slyusar says fires broke out at four industrial facilities in Azov after the overnight drone attack and three men were injured (Kyiv Post, LetsArmUKR); local residents and monitoring channels also report a fire at a gas distribution station; LetsArmUKR adds that Kuban authorities report a separate fire at an enterprise and that homes and a gas pipeline were damaged in Rogalik, Rostov region; extent of damage to the depot not officially stated; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow and other Russian regions Sunday night; Sobyanin reports dozens of drones downed
Russia.location: Moscow and Moscow Oblast, plus other western and southwestern Russian regions
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports several hundred Ukrainian mid- to long-range drones launched Sunday evening toward Moscow Oblast, neighbouring regions and southwestern Russia. TASS quotes Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin saying air defenses destroyed 15 more drones heading toward Moscow; other accounts citing Sobyanin put the total at about 60 in one hour and 80 in three hours, with emergency services working at crash sites. One account reports flight restrictions at Vnukovo airport.
Russia.status: Developing; official Russian figures relayed by TASS; damage and casualties not reported; airport restrictions single-source; Nov. 16: Russian state outlet RT cites the Russian Defence Ministry as saying 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight over more than a dozen regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, its highest overnight total; Vedomosti says the ministry reported 2,049 drones, four Flamingo cruise missiles and seven guided bombs destroyed over the past day; Vzglyad cites Sobyanin as saying 191 drones were downed approaching Moscow; Russian figures not independently verified; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck Russia's Akhtubinsk military airfield in Astrakhan region overnight
Russia.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Sunday that its forces struck the Akhtubinsk military airfield, home to the 929th State Flight Test Center and a Su-34 base, and a drone launch site at Tsymbulova in Oryol region overnight. Accounts relaying the claim report a strong secondary detonation at a missile-kit depot.
Russia.status: Ukrainian military claim relayed by several accounts; no Russian official confirmation or independent damage assessment found; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on an energy facility cuts power across much of Zaporizhzhia city and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region

Hromadske reports a significant number of customers in Zaporizhzhia city and region lost power, along with settlements in the Dniprovskyi and Kamianskyi districts. A post citing the regional military administration says Zaporizhzhia city is almost completely without electricity, with water and heating problems and hospitals on generators.
Russia.status: Energy Ministry statement relayed by Flash; Hromadske and 24 Kanal corroborate; customer counts not published in posts checked; 'almost completely without electricity' wording comes from a single relay; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: Ukrainian outlet Censor.net reports that an overnight Russian attack on the Zhytomyr region struck energy infrastructure and residential buildings. Casualty and outage figures were not given in the post checked.
Russia.status: Single outlet report; no regional administration or energy-company statement found in posts checked; Anton Gerashchenko separately reports drone strikes on the Zhytomyr and Cherniakhiv communities that damaged private houses and energy infrastructure; still no regional administration or outage figures found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian Geran-4 jet drones reported hitting a locomotive depot in Dnipro
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports Russian Geran-4 jet-powered drones attacked a locomotive depot in Dnipro overnight, with a fire visible after the attack. No casualty figures or official confirmation were available.
Russia.status: Single OSINT source; no Ukrainian Railways or regional official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Russian Geran-2 drone attack on Chornomorsk, Odesa region — large fire reported after impacts
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reported Saturday night that at least 22 Geran-2 drones were approaching Chornomorsk in two waves. Global Surveillance reported up to 30 drones heading to the Odesa region. No damage or casualty figures were available.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts; no Ukrainian Air Force tally, regional administration statement or damage reports found yet; AMK Mapping reports a large fire in Chornomorsk after the attack and says NASA FIRMS data shows a large fire at the impact area; it says a likely target was a freight-logistics company or the Chornomorsk Automobile Plant; still no official Ukrainian damage or casualty report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays a Russian Defense Ministry claim that the targets were a ferry terminal, the Chornomorsk port administration and a nearby electrical substation; this is a Russian military claim, not independently confirmed, and no official Ukrainian damage report found in posts checked; AMK Mapping relays Ukrainian energy company DTEK confirming a substation in Chornomorsk was hit by multiple drones, leaving about 41,000 homes without power; Gerashchenko and Flash report six people injured in Chornomorsk and damage to energy infrastructure, an administrative building, a gas pipeline and nearby homes; the same overnight wave injured six in Zaporizhzhia (12 strikes, per Flash) and three in a drone hit on a Kropyvnytskyi residential building; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Large Ukrainian drone raid on Russia — Rostov governor says a Taganrog substation engineer was killed and five injured; Nizhnekamsk petrochemical plant hit; Russian MoD claims 533 drones downed
Russia.location: Western and southern Russia (reports around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov)
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a large Ukrainian attack-drone raid into western Russia was under way Saturday night, with local channels reporting hundreds of drones heading toward targets deep in the Volga River basin. FAB87F relays Russian monitoring channels reporting widespread drone activity around Voronezh, Rostov, Volgograd and Saratov.
Russia.status: Early reports from OSINT accounts citing local channels; no Russian Defense Ministry tally, regional governor statement or confirmed damage found yet; AMK Mapping reports Ukrainian long-range drones attacking Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with a large fire at the impact site, likely the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plant; Exilenova+ relays locals reporting an attack on a city plant; AMK Mapping also says drones hit Taganrog, Rostov region, likely targeting the T-10 220 kV substation; still no official Russian or Tatarstan statement found in posts checked; OSINTdefender, Tendar and CYRIF report several large fires at the Tatarstan oil refining complex in Nizhnekamsk after the drone attack; Russian state outlet Vesti reports four people injured by falling drone debris on vehicles on a highway and at a gas station, with a section of the R-280 highway in Neklinovsky district damaged and a bridge closed; no official Tatarstan statement on the refinery found in posts checked; Novaya Gazeta Europe reports Rostov governor Yuri Slyusar said drones hit two electrical substations in Taganrog, one serving the railway, killing the substation's chief engineer and injuring five more; it cites ASTRA that the Nizhnekamskneftekhim (Sibur) petrochemical plant in Tatarstan was hit, with authorities reporting injuries. The Russian Defense Ministry says it downed 533 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and seas between 8 PM Nov 14 and 8 AM Nov 15 Moscow time, and SOTA and Charter 97 report Rosaviatsia restrictions at about 12 airports including Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Samara, Sochi and Volgograd. An unsourced viral claim that about 190 drones hit the Moscow region and the Kapotnya refinery was not corroborated by any credible source checked and is not included; NOEL Reports relays Governor Slyusar: two substations and a bridge on the R-280 highway were also damaged in Taganrog, disrupting rail and road traffic; WarTranslated reports early information that a Defense Ministry flight-test center in Akhtubinsk was also hit and that the Russian MoD claims 533 Ukrainian drones were downed; Belsat corroborates the Taganrog substation engineer's death and five injured; NOEL Reports video shows the Nizhnekamsk plant still burning Sunday morning; Akhtubinsk damage unconfirmed; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.status: Single pro-Russian source; no Ukrainian official or Poltava regional confirmation found on X; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian double-tap drone strike in Hlukhiv, Sumy region, wounds a grandmother, her grandson and a police officer
Russia.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential area in Hlukhiv on the morning of Nov. 14, wounding a woman; a second drone hit while police were evacuating her and her 9-year-old grandson. NOEL Reports names officers Mykola Savchenko and Ihor Voloshko and says Voloshko was wounded; Ukraine's United24 says the officer and the boy were both injured and all survived.
Russia.status: Reported by Ukrainian government fundraising account United24 and multiple Ukrainian outlets with bodycam footage; final casualty details not confirmed by Sumy regional officials on X; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone strike on a house in Proletarsky, Belgorod region, kills three, Russian regional officials say
Russia.location: Proletarsky, Rakitnoye district, Belgorod region, Russia

It also reports injuries from drone attacks in Shebekino and the village of Rzhevka.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Russian regional authorities, relayed); not independently verified; no Ukrainian comment found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone strike sets warehouses on fire in Vyshhorod, just north of Kyiv
Russia.summary: WarTranslated reports a large fire in Vyshhorod near Kyiv after a drone strike on Saturday morning. A second account reports warehouses are on fire after the strike as attacks continued into the morning.
Russia.status: Early reports; casualties and official Ukrainian regional statement not found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, injure more than 50, including eight children; a rescuer clearing rubble is killed
Russia.summary: A Russian strike on Friday damaged two five-storey apartment buildings in Zaporizhzhia, causing fires, and rescuers freed people trapped in their apartments. Ukraine's State Emergency Service says 30 people were injured, including six children. Kyiv Post reports Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed two people on Friday, including a 17-year-old boy.
Russia.status: Official figures issued (Ukraine's State Emergency Service, as relayed by United24); search-and-rescue reported completed; a CGTN Europe post citing Ukrainian reports puts the injured at 50, which is not confirmed; Kyiv Independent now reports 50 injured, including eight children, and says a Cobra emergency-service rescuer was killed when a concrete slab fell on him while clearing debris, citing local authorities; Euromaidan Press, citing the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration, says the Nov. 13 strikes killed two people and injured more than 50, and Anton Gerashchenko puts the dead at three including the rescuer; death counts differ slightly between sources; Ukraine Review reports 29 of those injured remain under medical care, six in serious condition, including six children aged 10 to 17; Angurintel, relaying the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration, reports a new Russian strike on the Voznesenivskyi district today injured 15 people, including two children, and damaged a residential building and nearby educational institution; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Ukrainian drone attacks hit Rostov region and the Samara oil pumping station; Rostov-on-Don declares an emergency regime
Russia.location: Rostov-on-Don and Aksay district (Rostov region); Samara region, Russia
Russia.summary: NEXTA reports more than 120 drones attacked Russia's Rostov region on the night of Nov. 13, sparking a fire at a 1,500-square-metre warehouse in Aksay district and setting an industrial facility and three cars on fire in Rostov-on-Don. Sota reports Rostov-on-Don's mayor declared an emergency regime on streets where homes were damaged, saying nine apartment buildings were damaged and 114 houses were left without heat. The Insider reports the Samara regional governor confirmed a drone attack on an industrial enterprise, which monitoring channels identify as the Transneft-operated Samara oil pumping station (LPDS).
Russia.status: Official regional statements reported (Rostov governor and mayor, Samara governor); extent of damage at the Samara station not confirmed; separate from the Volgograd refinery strike logged below; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones strike the Volgograd oil refinery, setting fires; governor says four killed and two injured
Russia.summary: Multiple posts with video, including Liveuamap, report a drone attack on the Lukoil-operated Volgograd oil refinery on the evening of Nov. 12, with fires on the plant's grounds; one post says the extent of damage remains unconfirmed. A separate post relays Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as saying more than 50 drones headed for Moscow were destroyed in about 90 minutes. Russian-source claims of 750 or more drones launched overall have not been verified.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car explodes while driving in southern Moscow, seriously injuring the driver; Russian media say the car belonged to commentator Sergey Zavorotny
Russia.location: Kirovogradskaya Street, Chertanovo district, Moscow, Russia
Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. It comes a day after a car bomb killed a Russian Air Force colonel in St. Petersburg.
Russia.status: Early reports; cause under investigation; one Russian outlet cited a preliminary suspicion of a gas-system malfunction; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; The Washington Post now describes it as a car bombing that seriously injured a former adviser to ex-Ukrainian PM Mykola Azarov who became a pro-Kremlin commentator in Russia; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; Nov. 16: CGTN Français says Russia announced the arrest of a Russian woman it accuses of involvement in the Moscow car bombing on behalf of Ukrainian special services (Russian official claim; not independently verified); carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Russian drone attack on Ukraine — 117 drones launched, strikes at 24 locations; at least two killed, medical facility hit in Kyiv
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russia launched 117 drones overnight, including 63 jet-powered drones; 80 were intercepted or suppressed, but strikes were recorded at 24 locations and at least two people were killed. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account

Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; Nov. 16 afternoon: journalist Christopher Miller says Mayor Boris Filatov reports about half of Dnipro, a city of about one million, is without power after Russian attacks on the energy system, calling it the sixth blackout in two weeks, with two people killed, 10 high-rise buildings damaged and the Bunge-owned Oleina plant hit a third time; UNIAN says the city was left completely without power after a series of attacks, with outages also in parts of the region; MAKS 26 quotes DTEK as saying Dnipro lost electricity entirely and that crews were first restoring power to water, heat and social facilities; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: A massed Russian drone attack on energy infrastructure left parts of Kryvyi Rih without power, according to city official Oleksandr Vilkul. Apartment buildings, schools and kindergartens were damaged. Water and sewage services are being stabilized with generators, but heating will be harder to restore. AMK Mapping says at least 16 Geran-2 drones were used and that the "Pivdenna" and "Hirnycha" 330 kV substations on the city's southern outskirts were hit.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (city official Oleksandr Vilkul); Reuters reports the outage; substation details from OSINT mapping account, not officially confirmed; casualty figures not reported; Reuters headline reconfirmed this window; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko said a fire broke out in the Ust-Luga port area during an overnight Ukrainian drone attack and that a substation in the port zone went into emergency shutdown. He said 146 drones were intercepted over the region as of 7:30 a.m. local time and that there was no information on casualties. Earlier OSINT footage showed the oil terminal burning.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Leningrad governor, relayed by OSINT/news accounts); no casualty information; extent of terminal damage unknown; tanker damage claims unconfirmed; NASA FIRMS satellite data shows multiple fires at and just off the port (OSINTdefender); Estonian public broadcaster ERR shows the fire visible from Estonia; Reuters carries the governor's account of the fire; Hromadske cites the governor on a substation shutdown and three injured workers; Meduza says two people were killed in the Smolensk region when officials say drone debris hit an apartment building; NOELreports says the Ust-Luga port terminal was still burning on Wednesday morning after the overnight attack; NOELreports cites OSINT channel Absreliable reporting fires at three 30,000-cubic-meter tanks and damage to processing equipment and a berth at Novatek; Russian sources cited by Osint613, OSINTdefender and NOELreports say two Ka-52 attack helicopters and an Mi-8 went down while responding to the drone attack, reportedly partly to friendly air defense, with one to three crews killed (Russian-source claims, unconfirmed by officials); Ukraine's SBU says the overnight operation struck port and oil infrastructure at Ust-Luga, damaging several petroleum storage tanks, and also hit the Buyan-M-class missile ship Naro-Fominsk; damage to the ship not established; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

SOTA, citing Bumaga, reports Rosneft stations in St. Petersburg have capped purchases since Nov. 8, and Novaya Gazeta Europe reports fuel limits returning in Leningrad region.

NEXTA reports several freight cars derailed after a section of the bridge over the Viled River collapsed between Cheryomukha and Viled and rail traffic on the section was suspended. Posts on X claim sabotage, but no official cause has been established.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kyiv Independent says Russian attacks killed 10 and injured 40 across Ukraine over the past day; ballistic and Zircon missiles plus 123 drones launched overnight
Russia.location: Kirovohrad, Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says air defenses neutralized 135 of 162 Russian drones, 70 of them jet-powered, and that Russia also launched an Iskander-M ballistic missile. He says there were no passengers on board, the crew was in a shelter and there were no casualties. Ukrainska Pravda and RBC-Ukraine also report the attack on the train.

Russia.status: Reported by Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda; energy damage extent not given; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.

Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Responsibility is not established in the posts found.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (IAEA, via Kyiv Independent); carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: UKMTO warning 208-26: tanker attacked 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz; vessel disabled with an engine-room fire
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, about 7 nm north of Khasab (Musandam), Oman
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 208-26. Accounts summarizing the warning say a third party reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab at 1900 UTC (2 PM ET) that disabled the vessel and caused an engine-room fire; the crew are reported safe, and damage and environmental impact are not yet known.
Middle East.status: Official maritime warning issued (UKMTO); vessel and attacker not identified in posts checked; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks

Middle East.title: NEW: Suspected car-ramming and axe attack near Jericho wounds two Israelis; IDF investigating
Middle East.location: Jericho area, Jordan Valley, West Bank
Middle East.summary: The IDF said it was investigating a suspected terror attack in the Jericho area and dispatched troops and set up roadblocks, Israel Red Alert reports. Initial reports say two people were injured in a suspected vehicle-ramming; Intel24News, citing Ynet, says a Palestinian vehicle deliberately struck an Israeli vehicle and its occupants were attacked with axes. NewsinIsraelUK says two Israelis were wounded near a Jericho outpost. Reports that assailants were shot are not confirmed by an official post checked.
Middle East.status: Developing; IDF investigating; injuries reported as two; assailants' fate unconfirmed officially

Middle East.title: NEW: Iraq orders forces into Kataib Hezbollah's Jurf al-Sakhar stronghold with a deadline after an oil-smuggling probe; the Iran-backed militia vows to keep its weapons
Middle East.location: Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), Babil province, Iraq
Middle East.summary: Rudaw reports Iraqi government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi said Iraqi forces are preparing to enter the militia-held town of Jurf al-Sakhar, with Baghdad setting a deadline for the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah. Al Jazeera English says forces were ordered in following oil-smuggling allegations, which the group denies, calling the crackdown an attempt to seize its weapons. Kataib Hezbollah posted that its weapons 'will remain in the hands of our Mujahideen' with photos of fighters setting up drones (Rudaw). Kurdistan24 and a Rudaw journalist report a tense Coordination Framework meeting, with Prime Minister al-Zaidi walking out over the dispute.
Middle East.status: Official Iraqi government statements reported by Rudaw and Al Jazeera; no clashes reported in posts checked; standoff developing

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi health officials say Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Omran province killed three, including a child
Middle East.location: Sanaa and Harf Sufian (Omran province), Yemen
Middle East.summary: The Tectonic, citing the AP, says a Houthi health ministry spokesman reported that a drone strike on a house in Sanaa's al-Sarar quarter killed a child and wounded seven, and that airstrikes on a private fuel station in Harf Sufian district killed two and wounded eight. The spokesman blamed Saudi Arabia, and Riyadh did not immediately comment.
Middle East.status: Houthi-run authority figures relayed via a single account citing AP; not independently verified; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Iranian media say air-defence systems were activated over Isfahan; no further official detail
Middle East.location: Isfahan, Iran
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English says air-defence systems were activated in Iran's central city of Isfahan, according to Mehr news agency, with no further details reported. Other accounts also cited Mehr and later claimed explosions or activations in Tehran and Khuzestan, which were not independently confirmed in posts checked.
Middle East.status: Single-agency report via Al Jazeera; cause of the activation unconfirmed; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Vehicle ramming in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, injures at least eight Palestinians, Al Jazeera reports
Middle East.location: Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, occupied West Bank
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English, citing local sources, says at least eight Palestinians were injured after an Israeli settler allegedly rammed a vehicle into them in the town of Tuqu, south of Bethlehem. Eye on Palestine reported the same account from southeast of Bethlehem.
Middle East.status: Early reports from Al Jazeera and local accounts; Israeli official comment not seen in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosion reported in Erbil province, Iraqi Kurdistan; Rudaw reportedly says an airstrike hit the Soran area
Middle East.location: Erbil province (Soran area), Kurdistan Region, Iraq
Middle East.summary: CGTN reports that an explosion was heard in Erbil, Iraq. Iran International Arabic, citing Kurdish broadcaster Rudaw, says an airstrike targeted the Soran area of Erbil province and a large explosion was heard. Casualties, damage and the party responsible were not given in the posts checked.
Middle East.status: Early reports; no official statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 207-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile while sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz; engine-room fire
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO issued attack warning 207-26 on Monday. Arab News and other outlets citing UKMTO say a tanker leaving the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile, setting its engine room on fire. Drop Site News, citing UKMTO, puts the strike at 05:58 UTC and says no casualties were reported and all crew are accounted for.
Middle East.status: Official warning issued (UKMTO); vessel name, flag and attacker not identified in posts checked; extent of damage being assessed; part of the continuing Hormuz shipping attacks; Nov. 16: aggregators repeat UKMTO's description of an engine-room fire and that all crew are accounted for; vessel still unnamed in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Rare overnight Israeli strike in Lebanon's eastern Beqaa Valley near the Syrian border
Middle East.location: Beqaa Valley near the Lebanon–Syria border
Middle East.summary: Lebanese media report an overnight Israeli Air Force strike near the Lebanon-Syria border in the eastern Beqaa Valley, the first in that area in several months. Times of Israel reporter Emanuel Fabian, citing Israeli security sources, says it was meant to stop a weapons shipment bound for Hezbollah. The IDF has not commented.
Middle East.status: Early reports; IDF has not commented; no casualty or damage figures found in posts checked; Nov. 16: JNS reports Israeli forces struck a Hezbollah-bound weapons shipment crossing from Syria; the Alma Center, citing Lebanese reports, places the strike at about 4:30 a.m. in the Al-Shaara–Janta area of the Nabi Chit barrens and says no casualties were officially reported; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: UPDATE: Yemeni government forces withdraw from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Reuters says Houthis in control
Middle East.location: Dhubab and Bab el-Mandeb area, Taiz/Lahj, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Reuters reported Sunday that forces fighting for Yemen's internationally recognized government withdrew from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. Yemen's armed forces told Al Arabiya the redeployment reflects reprioritized objectives and aims to break the siege of Taiz. Al Jazeera says the Houthi advance threatens one of the government's last strongholds and brings fighting closer to the shipping route.
Middle East.status: Confirmed by government forces' statements and Reuters; no attacks on shipping linked to the withdrawal found in posts checked; extent of Houthi control along the coast unclear; Nov. 16: Anadolu Arabic reports the army foiled a Houthi attack in Taiz, cites two rights groups documenting 319 civilians killed or injured since September, and notes Houthi accusations of Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Saada with no Riyadh comment; Houthi-aligned YNP reports Saudi strikes on Sabr district south of Taiz city for the first time in weeks after a Houthi advance there (partisan source); Nov. 16 evening: Al Jazeera English says the Houthis have claimed control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait; Houthi claim, extent of control not independently confirmed

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 206-26: tanker approached by possible mothership and armed skiff 430 nm east of Socotra
Middle East.location: Indian Ocean, 430 nm east of Socotra, Yemen
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says the master of a tanker reported being approached at 0330 UTC on Nov. 16 by a possible mothership and a skiff about 430 nautical miles east of Socotra. Four armed people and a ladder were seen on the skiff. Ships are advised to transit with caution.
Middle East.status: UKMTO warning issued; suspicious approach, no boarding reported; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Explosions reported in Sirik and Kong, Hormozgan province, and in Shahriyar near Tehran; cause unconfirmed
Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran
Middle East.summary: Several accounts reported explosions heard in Sirik in Iran's southern Hormozgan province on Sunday afternoon, citing Al Mihwar News and Iranian media. Other accounts said an explosion in Kong, also near the Strait of Hormuz, was linked to the targeting of an Iranian surface-to-air missile launcher. Separate reports describe an explosion in Shahriyar, west of Tehran.
Middle East.status: Early reports; claims that US forces struck air-defense launchers are speculation, and no official US or Iranian statement on a strike, damage or casualties was found; Nov. 15 evening: HormuzLetter and AI313_ say, citing only 'initial reports', that the US struck Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik; still no CENTCOM, Pentagon or Iranian official confirmation found, so the attribution remains unverified; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC Navy says two tankers hit naval mines on the 'unauthorized' southern Hormuz route Sunday and claims one supertanker sank
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: The IRGC Navy says two oil tankers that had switched off their tracking systems struck naval mines on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours, caught fire after large explosions, and that one, carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, sank. It released footage it says shows the explosions. The vessels have not been named, and it is unclear whether either is the tanker in UKMTO warning 205-26.
Middle East.status: IRGC claim only, relayed by Tehran Times, The Cradle, FirstSquawk and ME Observer; not independently confirmed in posts checked; earlier IRGC tanker-mine claims in this log also remain unverified; Nov. 15 night: the IRGC Navy now claims two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire, saying six tankers have caught fire or sunk since Saturday (Iran International citing Iranian state media; Press TV). No confirmation from UKMTO, CENTCOM or ship operators found; ship names not given, so the claim remains unverified; Nov. 16 afternoon: The Tectonic, citing IRIB, says Iranian naval forces claimed three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, that the IRGC Navy again said six tankers have caught fire or are sinking since Sunday, and that a claimed sinking video shows fire on the water with no clearly visible vessel; ship names still not given and the claims remain unverified; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Houthi missile attack near Aden kills at least five civilians, AFP reports
Middle East.location: Lahj governorate, near Aden, Yemen
Middle East.summary: AFP, citing four sources, reports that a Houthi missile attack near Aden on Sunday, Nov. 15 killed five people and wounded eight (via LBCI). A Rai al-Youm report citing AFP and Anadolu puts the toll at at least eight civilians killed and 12 wounded in Lahj.
Middle East.status: Early reports via wire services; tolls differ between reports (5 dead/8 hurt vs. at least 8 dead/12 hurt); carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.location: Southern Arabian Gulf, near the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says it is aware of a report from Indian shipping authorities of an attack on a tanker transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait of Hormuz. Middle East.title: UPDATE: Bahrain sounds sirens and issues threat alerts as IRGC claims a second-phase drone attack on a US radar at Riffa
Middle East.location: Bahrain (Riffa helicopter base area)
Middle East.summary: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a potential-threat alert early Sunday, urging residents to go to the nearest safe location; Bwabtek later reported the all-clear siren. The IRGC said six drones hit the radar of a US air-defense site at the Riffa helicopter base as the 'second phase' of its response and again declared the Strait of Hormuz closed. AMK Mapping describes a combined cruise missile and drone attack, and Al Hadath (Kuwait) reports Bahrain said air defenses intercepted an Iranian drone.
Middle East.status: Official Bahrain MOI alert issued, all-clear later reported; IRGC damage claims and the attack's size are unconfirmed; no CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Kuwait Times confirms the Interior Ministry's sirens and shelter instruction; Giovanni Staunovo relays that Bahrain says its air defenses intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones. Low-credibility accounts claiming an Iranian cruise missile hit Sitra Island are uncorroborated and not included; still no Bahraini damage report or CENTCOM statement on this attack found in posts checked; Hindustan Times reports the IRGC claims six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al Riffa helicopter base and that Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued a shelter alert, noting the Iranian strike claims remain unverified; Nov. 15: IRGC says six drones hit a US site in Bahrain, its second attack in a week; Bahrain says it intercepted several. Middle East.title: UPDATE: IRGC claims it shot down a US MQ-1 Predator drone over Qeshm Island for a second straight day

Middle East.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Saturday it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Diario de Centro América reports. IEW Latest News relays CBS News reporting that this is the second straight day Iran has made such a claim.
Middle East.status: Iranian claim relayed by media; no US military confirmation found in posts checked; Nov. 16 evening: Al Mayadeen reports the IRGC now claims it took control of a ninth US MQM-170 drone over Qeshm; IRGC claim only, no US confirmation found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli airstrike in Khan Younis kills senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis, Hamas sources tell Reuters
Middle East.location: Khan Younis, Gaza Strip
Middle East.summary: The Israeli military says it struck a senior Hamas commander in Khan Younis on Saturday evening. Hamas sources told Reuters that Samir Abu Younis, described as head of the Rafah Brigade of Hamas's Qassam Brigades, was killed. Other casualties were not stated.

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Jaramana car bomb near Damascus — Syrian Internal Security and state news agency SANA confirm a man and a young girl killed
Middle East.location: Jaramana, Rif Dimashq (Damascus countryside), Syria
Middle East.summary: An explosive device planted inside a car detonated in Jaramana, a mainly Druze and Christian suburb southeast of Damascus, on the evening of Nov. 14. Syria's Internal Security Forces and state news agency SANA say a man and a young girl were killed and another person injured; EFE reports two dead and two injured. America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Nine people shot dead inside a shack in Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, South Africa
Africa.location: Jeffsville informal settlement, Atteridgeville, Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Somalia: Buulo Mareer security chief reportedly killed by a mine in Lower Shabelle
Africa.summary: An Africa-focused account reports that Buulo Mareer security chief Cabdisalaan Qoobeey and some of his guards were killed on Sunday when a mine hit his vehicle as he led reinforcements to Golweyn. Africa.status: Early reports; police had not commented in posts checked; number abducted unknown; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 31 reported killed in Rizeigat–Habbaniyah clashes in Al-Sunta, South Darfur
Africa.summary: At least 31 people were killed in renewed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniyah groups in Al-Sunta locality, a tribal leader told Darfur24, according to a post relaying the report. Africa.status: Single-source report via a relay of Darfur24; casualty count from a tribal leader; not independently corroborated in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.status: Single regional outlet citing local reports; no Somali government or federal military statement found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six

Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)

America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; India Today reports more than 6,150 US flights cancelled and 7,300+ delayed on Saturday per FlightAware; it says the FAA traced the outage to a router installation by contractor L3Harris that affected 17 of 22 en route centers, and that operations were expected to largely normalize by late Sunday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday, Nov. 15 that flights will 'come back to normal today, fully normal tomorrow'; the situation appears to be stabilizing and may move to routine coverage; Nov. 15: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that, as the investigation unfolds, there is no evidence the ground stop was caused by a cyberattack; viral claims of a foreign cyberattack have no official or primary-source support; Nov. 16: Bloomberg, citing travel app Flighty, says the weekend US air traffic outage ranks as the worst in 35 years for flight cancellations caused by a technology issue, surpassing Southwest's 2022 meltdown; Nov. 16: Anadolu says US airlines are expected to resume full schedules Monday; investigators are examining whether faulty equipment or human error caused the outage, with no evidence of a cyberattack, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to seek new modernization funding; Nov. 16: Transportation Secretary Duffy tells CNBC the outage began at a remote facility in Arkansas and the government will review how it makes air traffic network upgrades; Delta CEO Ed Bastian tells Fortune there is no evidence a cyberattack or AI was involved; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. It comes a day after a car bomb killed a Russian Air Force colonel in St. Petersburg.
Russia.status: Early reports; cause under investigation; one Russian outlet cited a preliminary suspicion of a gas-system malfunction; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; The Washington Post now describes it as a car bombing that seriously injured a former adviser to ex-Ukrainian PM Mykola Azarov who became a pro-Kremlin commentator in Russia; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; Nov. 16: CGTN Français says Russia announced the arrest of a Russian woman it accuses of involvement in the Moscow car bombing on behalf of Ukrainian special services (Russian official claim; not independently verified); carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery
Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)
Russia.summary: Russian local channels and multiple OSINT and media accounts report a prolonged Ukrainian drone attack on Omsk on Nov. 11, with the Gazprom Neft refinery named as the target and air defense activity lasting more than two hours. NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a crowded market in Chornomorsk, Odesa region, kills three and injures 11
Russia.summary: A Russian strike hit a market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing three people and injuring 11, according to regional authorities cited by NOELreports and Ukrainian outlets. Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.
Russia.status: Regional authorities report; toll rose from one to three killed during the morning; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro kills three and injures four
Russia.summary: Suspilne, citing regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha, reports a Russian strike hit a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro, killing two people, injuring at least four and starting a fire. Hromadske Radio later reported the toll rose to three, with businesses and a private home also damaged and four men hospitalized, two in serious condition. CGTN Europe, citing Ukraine's health service, reports three killed and five injured across Dnipropetrovsk region during the day.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) figures relayed by Ukrainian outlets; emergency services at the scene; facility not named; carried forward from 2:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine

Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.

Middle East.title: NEW: Houthi health officials say Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Omran province killed three, including a child
Middle East.location: Sanaa and Harf Sufian (Omran province), Yemen
Middle East.summary: The Tectonic, citing the AP, says a Houthi health ministry spokesman reported that a drone strike on a house in Sanaa's al-Sarar quarter killed a child and wounded seven, and that airstrikes on a private fuel station in Harf Sufian district killed two and wounded eight. Middle East.location: Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, occupied West Bank
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English, citing local sources, says at least eight Palestinians were injured after an Israeli settler allegedly rammed a vehicle into them in the town of Tuqu, south of Bethlehem. Eye on Palestine reported the same account from southeast of Bethlehem.

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO warning 207-26: tanker struck by an unknown projectile while sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz; engine-room fire
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz

Middle East.location: Sirik and Kong (Hormozgan province) and Shahriyar (Tehran province), Iran
Middle East.summary: Several accounts reported explosions heard in Sirik in Iran's southern Hormozgan province on Sunday afternoon, citing Al Mihwar News and Iranian media.
